articleTitle: Optimal Design of Differential Sensor Array for Interference Elimination of Noninvasive Multicore Cable Current Measurement
Integrated Carbon Nanotubes for MEMS Applications
abstract: Controlled synthesis and adjustment of carbon nanotubes on Microelectromechanical Systems (MEMS), and number of their applications are presented. These top-down followed by bottom-up integration process is performed on fully fabricated MEMS structures to enhance the functionalities of existing MEMS and/or to develop novel sensor and actuator applications. The demonstrated microdevices include micromechanical switches with enhanced lifetime, reversible and continuous latch mechanisms, displacement sensors with high sensitivity, inertial sensors, gas sensors et al. All of the devices were batch-processed for cost-effective manufacturing.

articleTitle: Force Myography Sensors for Gait Phase Detection
abstract: In human-machine interaction, muscle activity serves as an indicator of the human motion intent and is mostly assessed using electromyography (EMG). EMG requires special skin preparation, accurate electrode placement, and is affected by sweating. In contrast, force myography (FMG) measures the mechanical muscle contraction, thereby promising reliable long-term acquisition for gait phase detection. With one individual piezoelectric sensor patch per muscle, reduced cross-talk around the limb circumference is expected compared to state-of-the-art elastic straps comprising several sensors linked together. In this work, seven physically unimpaired participants wore four 3D-printed, highly sensitive ferroelectret sensors along with four EMG electrodes on the lower limbs while walking on an instrumented treadmill at normal walking speed. Tibialis anterior (TA) and vastus medialis (VM) are best suited for heel strike and toe-off detection with the FMG sensors to discriminate between swing and stance phases. The signal variability across all strides is exceptionally low. The characteristic FMG peaks differ from the ground reaction force reference by 3.6% ± 2.0% of the stride time for TA and 1.2% ± 1.2% for VM. Using the customizable ferroelectret sensors, this FMG system provides a substitute or supplement in sensor fusion for conventional EMG.

articleTitle: Wearable Ballistocardiography for Unobtrusive Respiratory and Heart Rate Monitoring
abstract: Respiratory and heart rate are accessible physiological signatures of human vitality. Unobtrusive insole ballistocardiography using highly sensitive piezoelectric sensors promises a wearable measurement system to monitor health throughout the day. In this work, the 3D-printed ferroelectret insole is worn by three participants while standing in upright posture. The beat-to-beat detection implements a continuous wavelet transform to filter the main frequency bands (6 to 8 Hz) in the time-frequency domain, offering accurate heartbeat timings. Amplitude and frequency variabilities in the heartbeat signal are evaluated separately to reveal the underlying respiration. Both instantaneous characteristics can be fused to obtain a robust breath-to-breath measurement, mitigating body movements and non-respiratory arrhythmia. The measured heart rate aligns well with the reference from a commercial chest strap, and the heart rate variability with ± 4 beats per minute is consistent with the literature values of respiratory sinus arrhythmia. In conclusion, the wearable insole concept with the presented signal processing chain qualifies for remote health monitoring.

articleTitle: Force Sensor for Versatile Single-Step Sensor Integration in 3D-Printed Parts
abstract: Fused filament fabrication enables low-cost and highly adaptable production for industrial applications and the consumer market. Sensor integration requires individual development and production steps, increasing cost and limiting accessibility. 3D-printed sensors offer a low-cost alternative. Available approaches either adapt conventional sensors for additive manufacturing or offer individual solutions for every application. We present a universal force sensor that is directly integrated and encapsulated during the printing process. The design consists of two measurement grids based on the piezoresistive effect, in a half-bridge configuration. Only commercially available conductive filament is used. The sensor geometry includes electrical connections and contact interfaces, thus, enabling a full encapsulation inside the target body. The function is examined by measurements on various test bodies, exhibiting a small linearity error of 3.6 % and the ability to compensate temperature influences. We demonstrate the capa-bilities in a customized robotic gripper, where the sensor is able to detect whether the grasping operation was successful through contact force measurements. Our approach offers a straightforward solution for integrating force sensing capabilities into 3D-printed parts by simplifying the design process to a drag-and-drop operation in any design software.

articleTitle: Integration of EMG Electrodes by Disruptive 3D Printing Into a Mandibular Brace
abstract: Electromyography (EMG) is a crucial technique for measuring muscle activity and is regularly used in motion detection and diagnostics. When applied to small muscles and integrated into devices such as prostheses or force measurement systems, conventional electrodes often fail to meet space and usability requirements. While conductive filaments have been successfully used to additively manufacture electrodes in previous work, these are typically large and not integrated into complex geometries. This work introduces a process employing additive manufacturing with both conductive and non-conductive materials to create integrated, customizable medical sensors with embedded EMG electrodes placed on flexible beams to assess otherwise inaccessible muscles. The process involves a disruption during 3D printing to insert a PCB with a preamplifier, which is then connected by the conductive filament, forming a functional EMG electrode. These EMG electrodes are exemplarily integrated into a mandibular brace for simultaneous measurement of human jaw opening forces and the respective suprahyoid muscle activity. After filtering, an EMG activity with an SNR of 11.6 dB and a correlation coefficient with the jaw opening force of 0.93 was found, validating the working principle of the sensors. This technology holds the potential for application in more complex devices, streamlining their production and eliminating the requirement for manual electrode placement on the patient for each use.

articleTitle: Transmit Beamforming for Phased Array Radars Under Uncertain Occupancy Grid Map Information
abstract: We consider phased array radars for target detection to support automotive driving applications. The detection performance of these radars can be enhanced by adapting the beams at the transmitter to the occupancy grid map. In practice, the occupancy grid map available at the radar differs from the true map due to pose errors. In this paper, we design transmit beams to exploit the side information available from the estimated occupancy grid map while being robust to pose estimation errors. Simulation results for automotive driving indicate that our method achieves enhanced detection over conventional quasi-omnidirectional beamforming even under pose estimation errors.

articleTitle: Investigation of Environmental Influences on Radar Measurements in the W- and D-Band
abstract: In modern automobiles, the installation of sensors, particularly radar sensors for obstacle detection, is becoming in-creasingly common. These sensors are designed to enhance safety when driving by providing the driver with reliable information about the surrounding environment. However, the sensors must also be able to function effectively in a wide range of weather conditions to ensure the driver's safety. This paper aims to investigate the influence of different weather conditions on radar measurements in the W-band from 68 GHz to 92 GHz and in the D-band from 122 GHz to 169 GHz. The difference between sunny weather, rain, fog, and snow will be investigated.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of a Skin Conformable Polymer-based Flexible Temperature Sensor
abstract: In today's modern age, there is a growing need for temperature sensors that can conform to the skin and monitor body temperature continuously. Achieving this requires the miniaturization of the sensor and careful selection of the active layer stacking. Further, it is important to check the effect of the active layer stacking on the sensor performance. In this context, we present the performance evaluation results for a polymer-based flexible temperature sensor designed to conform to the skin. This sensor utilizes PEDOT:PSS + GO composition as the temperature-sensitive material developed on top of a flexible PET substrate. The experimental results demonstrate that the performance of the sensor is dependent on the active layer stacking and electrode separation. An impressive sensor sensitivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.205 \%/^\circ\mathrm{C}$</tex> was achieved through sensor miniaturization and a single active layer stacking. This shows the performance tuning of a temperature sensor using active layer stacking.

articleTitle: Reliable Setup for Contact Separation Mode Measurements of Triboelectric Materials and TENGs
abstract: Triboelectric charge separation has received a recent and significant attention with the development of so-called triboelectric nanogenerators (TEN Gs), to harvest electrical energy from mechanical energy invested into the relative motion of triboelectric materials against each other. This research has shown that a large range of experimental conditions - like contact force, contact formation and separation speed, temperature and humidity - does influence the amount of triboelectric charge separation, together with the composition, geometry, bulk and surface morphology and chemical surface properties of the mating surfaces. This wide parameter space is relevant for the design of optimal triboelectric generators, but mostly not addressed in their design and operation today, as measurement equipment for its exploitation is widely missing. As a result, the testing and operation conditions of many different TENGs are not given in literature, not precisely known and not comparable, as are the results from different basic studies on triboelectric materials. To address these issues we have designed, built and initially tested a measurement system for the characterization of triboelectric materials in contact separation-mode under controlled conditions. A model system of Cu vs PTFE (Teflon) was used to demonstrate and repeatably proof the influence of varying measurement conditions on the recorded output voltage from the material pair. These results show the importance of controlled and well-known conditions for the characterization of triboelectric material pairs, offer a possible standardized method for material characterization and give hints on the optimal design of triboelectric generators.

articleTitle: A High-Precision Capacitive Absolute Angle Position Sensor with Improved Temperature Performance
abstract: A high-precision capacitive absolute angle sensor with improved temperature performance is presented. The proposed sensor comprises a rotor and a stator. Two opposing excitation signals are applied to the excitation electrodes of the stator. The contour of the sensitive structures is designed and optimized in order to ensure that the DC values of the obtained capacitance signals are as close to zero as possible. Consequently, the utilization of the capacitance cancel array, which would introduce temperature instability, is avoided. The full-temperature performance tests are conducted on the prototype. The result reveals that the resolution is and the maximum measurement error over the full range is under -45°C~+65 °C, showing the potential of the proposed prototype to achieve high-precision measurement over the full temperature range.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting Strategies for Plant Microbial Fuel Cells in Sustainable IoT Applications
abstract: Battery-free Internet of Things devices and sensors are gaining momentum, making energy harvesting an essential component of self-powered systems. Conventional energy harvesting techniques use well-established methods to track the maximum power point during conversion. This approach is not strictly applicable to emerging, more sustainable power sources like Plant Microbial Fuel Cells (PMFCs). This paper addresses the challenge of maximizing power and energy extraction from PMFCs without compromising long-term performance. Maximizing power is complicated by the slow dynamics of the cells and the vulnerability of the biofilm to excessive current extraction. In contrast, maximizing energy is facilitated by cell unloading periods, as constant loading can deteriorate their durability. Electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) conducted on the cell electrodes provides valuable feedback to determine the most appropriate loading strategy. This approach optimizes PMFC durability and peak power production, while opening up exciting prospects for bio-sensing applications.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Sensing for Enhanced Surface Roughness Prediction in CNC Machining Using an Intelligent Vise
abstract: This study showcases the utilization of an intelligent vise equipped with integrated cutting force and audio sensors to predict surface roughness during the milling process. Specifically, a piezoelectric PZT-based force sensor and a MEMS microphone are embedded within the vise jaw, enabling the acquisition of cutting force and audio signals in close proximity to the workpiece without interference. The collected data is then used to train predictive models for estimating surface roughness. The results demonstrate a root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.038, which outperforms the use of either force or audio data alone, which have RMSE values of 0.072 µm and 0.103 µm, respectively.

articleTitle: Recent Progress of Flexible Optical Sensor for Biomedical Sensing
abstract: Optical bio-imaging is a non-invasive method to measure biological information from outside of the body, such as fluorescent probes, photoacoustic imaging, and near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) have been widely used as medical devices. In recent years, along with the development of semiconductor technology, the miniaturization of these imaging devices has been progressing. In particular, organic optical devices have featured characteristics such as high efficiency, flexibility, and lightweight, and are being actively applied to healthcare by integrating them into wearable devices. In this talk, I will review recent progress in flexible organic optical sensors for applications in biomedical sensing and next-generation healthcare devices, addressing challenges and outlining the prospects of flexible optical sensors.

articleTitle: Dynamic Compensation of Quasi-Static Magnetic Field for Array Optically Pumped Magnetometers
abstract: The technology of optically pumped magnetometers (OPM) operating in the spin exchange relaxation free (SERF) range has rapidly advanced in recent years. To operate in the SERF state, it is crucial to maintain a near zero magnetic field operating condition. Therefore, dynamic compensation of the magnetic field fluctuation is desired. This paper presents a method of suppression the magnetic field fluctuations by utilizing array OPMs that are oriented to different directions. The outputs of the sensors are split into different channels, namely: one channel for the alternating signal measurement and the other one for the closed-loop control to cancel the quasi-static magnetic field with frequency lower than 1.5 Hz. To mitigate the effects of coil non-uniformity and magnetic field inhomogeneity, two coils are employed to generate the compensation field, including the internal Helmholtz coil within the sensor and external tri-axial coils. Experimental results show that this method can suppress the quasi-static magnetic field fluctuations in-situ by over a hundredfold and achieve a magnetic field suppression level of approximately 300 fT/Hz.

articleTitle: Moisture-Induced Energy Harvesting Devices with Biocompatible Albumin-MXene Composites
abstract: Amidgrowing concerns over global warming and rising energy demands, researchers urgently seek to develop green, sustainable energy from renewable and environmentally friendly sources. Moisture electricity generation (MEG) is one of the emerging technologies that convert the chemical energy of moisture into electricity. In this work, a biocompatible and biodegradable device using a chicken egg albumin-MXene composite. The devices can harvest up to 6.6 μw/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of electric power. The albumin-MXene composite-based devices exhibit enhanced performance compared to pure albumin-based devices. Our findings introduce a novel clean power generation concept using protein films. Additionally, MXene incorporation enhanced the performance of the energy harvesting devices.

articleTitle: High-performance and Low-power VOCs Monitoring System with Temperature and UV Light Modulation Enhanced MEMS Gas Sensors
abstract: As the demand for air quality detection increases, there is a pressing need for performance improvement and operational efficiency in gas detection. A high-performance volatile organic compounds (VOCs) monitoring system has been developed, which integrates homemade MEMS sensors with ultraviolet (UV) micro-LEDs, allowing for the modulation of both the operating temperature and light source intensity. Furthermore, the Bluetooth Low Energy module enables wireless communication with mobile phones, allowing for real-time data acquisition under multifunctional conditions. A combination of temperature and UV light co-modulation can significantly enhance sensor response performance while reducing operating temperature (from 300°C to 100 °C) and energy consumption (less than 1/6 of the original). Our work presents novel insights and methodologies for constructing high-performance, low-power VOCs sensing systems.

articleTitle: High Quality Factor Surface Acoustic Wave Temperature Sensor with Impedance Adjustment
abstract: High quality factor and impedance-matched surface acoustic wave sensors play a crucial role in temperature measurements in harsh environments such as aircraft engines. The quality factor affects the measurement accuracy of SAW sensors, whereas impedance influences the transmission efficiency of the sensor. This paper presents a SAW temperature sensor with an enhanced quality factor through the precise control of composite film electrode thickness to achieve impedance matching. Compared to conventional sensors, the impedance-optimized SAW temperature sensor exhibits a significantly improved Q factor, increasing from 6915 to 25363, and a matching impedance of 51 Ω and -16°. The error of the SAW temperature sensor ranging from 70 to 1000°C is less than 1%, ensuring reliable performance under extreme conditions.

articleTitle: Structure Deformation Measurement Based on Magnetoelectric Effect
abstract: The small deformation of structural parts in precision instruments has a significant impact on its performance, while traditional structural deformation measurement methods have disadvantages such as environmental sensitivity, high cost, and difficulty in integration. In response to these problems, this paper developed a novel precision structure deformation measurement method based on magnetoelectric position sensor. First, the principle of the magnetoelectric position sensor for deflection measurement and the influence of attractive force inside the sensor are studied. Then a position sensor prototype based on Terfenol-D/PZT composites is produced, and the performance of the developed deflection measurement method is tested. When the initial air gap of the position sensor is 8 mm, the measurement sensitivity is 1.77 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathbf{V}/\mu \mathbf{m}$</tex>, and the range is 0.404 mm. The results indicate that the developed structure deformation measurement system based on magnetoelectric effect has sub-micron precision, good linearity and reproducibility.

articleTitle: Uncertainty-Based Semi-Supervised Object Detection in Autonomous Driving Environment
abstract: In real-world traffic scenarios, due to the lack of actual labels, it is necessary to introduce a semi-supervised object detection (SSOD) algorithm, which can greatly reduce costs and improve model performance by mining a large amount of unlabeled data and a small amount of labeled data. The improvement of most existing SSOD algorithms relies on the previous semi-supervised classification tasks, ignoring the impact of the regression on the accuracy and robustness of the model, especially in complex autonomous driving environments. Hence, to solve this problem, we propose an uncertainty-based SSOD algorithm framework for the first time, which can quantify uncertainty by self-learning for teacher-student model optimization. And the uncertainty fusion mechanism is used to update the fuzzy labels generated by multiple iterations to improve their quality and ensure the stability of the training process. Finally, exhaustive experiments using state-of-the-art algorithms demonstrate that our proposed algorithm performs best in general object detection settings as well as autonomous driving settings.

articleTitle: Flexible Conducting Wire Based on Liquid Metal and Carbon Nanotubes
abstract: A flexible conducting composite material based on liquid metal and Carbon Nanotubes (CNTs) is introduced in this paper. The conducting wire is composed of PMDS and Liquid Metal (LM) Galinstan, with CNTs added to regulate its rheology and increase its conductivity. The flexible conducting material is sintered by mechanical sintering to break the oxide film on the surface of the liquid metal particles, release the unoxidized liquid metal, bond the liquid metal particles to form a conducting wire, and sinter the liquid metal wire. The test results show that the flexible conducting wire can maintain the conductivity when stretched or bent, and realize the transmission and control of electrical signals. These results indicate that it has a good application prospects in mechanical manufacturing, human-computer interaction, especially as a electronic components for electronic skin.

articleTitle: Estimating Suture Needle Size via Selective Detuning of Chipless RFID Tags
abstract: The time spent on cleaning and preparation in the operating room accounts for up to 23% of the average procedure time. Reducing these times could decrease cost and optimize care. Preparation time includes surgical instrument counting (SC) to prevent the problem of retained surgical instruments (RSI), which can cost hospitals over $200K per incident. Current SC methods are inadequate for smaller tools like surgical needles (SN). This study explores the use of a high-resolution circular chipless RFID tag for automatically differentiating suture needle sizes. The change in the signal response of the chipless RFID tag, affected by an overlaid SN, is used as a feature set to train a random forest classifier. We demonstrate that the system achieves a classification accuracy of 98.55%, effectively distinguishing between three needle sizes. These findings validate the potential of chipless RFID technology combined with machine learning as a viable tool for automated SC. Future research directions are also discussed.

articleTitle: Sparsity-Aware Occupancy Grid Mapping for Automotive Driving Using Radar-LiDAR Fusion
abstract: We tackle the problem of estimating a binary occupancy grid map by fusing point cloud data from LiDAR and radar sensors for automotive driving perception. To this end, we introduce two sparsity measurement models for fusion, formulating occupancy mapping as a sparse binary vector reconstruction problem. The first model jointly estimates a common map from all measurements, while the second assumes a shared map and an innovation component for each modality's measurements. We use the pattern-coupled sparse Bayesian learning algorithm to recover maps, leveraging the inherent sparsity and spatial dependencies in automotive occupancy maps. Numerical experiments on the RADIATE public dataset show that our fusion-based approach improves mapping accuracy compared to single-modality and high-level fusion mapping algorithms.

articleTitle: Dwell Time Allocation for Decentralized Phased Array Radar Sensing Networks with Target Tracking
abstract: This paper proposes a parallel strategy-based dwell time allocation method for a decentralized phased array radar sensing network (PA-RSN) for target tracking. Firstly, the dwell time allocation of PA-RSN is formulated as an optimization problem that aims to maximize the overall tracking utility. To make the solution applicable to PA-RSN, the utility function is approximated as a linear combination of multiple local utility functions, allowing for the update of them at each radar without fusion center. Upon reaching a consensus through a sufficient number of iterations, a global solution to the optimization problem is achieved. Numerical simulations verify the effectiveness of the proposed approach in a decentralized PA-RSN.

articleTitle: Multi-modal Photo-responsive Planar Microwave Resonant-based Colorimetric Analysis of Liquid-Color Compound for Biomedical Applications
abstract: Contactless sensing and monitoring have gained increasing popularity due to their versatile applications in various industries and scientific research. This work presents a photo-responsive microwave split ring resonator (SRR) sensor for the concurrent detection and characterization of the colorimetric and dielectric properties of materials in the liquid phase. This unique implementation enabled light-insensitive microwave SRRs to utilize the optical properties of materials, resulting in enhanced sensitivity and selectivity in their performance. The sensor core was mainly based on two coupled SRRs with one photoresistor in each ring and a light source of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\lambda=630\ \text{nm})$</tex> at 20 cm illuminating the photoresistors. The sensor's response was influenced by both the dielectric properties of the liquids contained within a cuvette and the light absorption characteristics of the sample with the SRRs operating at ~2.2 GHz, allowing for a comprehensive analysis of the liquid's properties. The sensor demonstrated an enhancement by over 112 % variation in the resonant amplitude when comparing the light-activated state to the inactivated state for the same liquid samples. This sensor has the potential to enhance the sensitivity of microwave planar sensors in biomedical applications, where variations in dielectric properties are coupled with optical changes in the media, facilitating early detection and monitoring.

articleTitle: Broadband MEMS Microphone Arrays with Reduced Aperture Through 3D-Printed Waveguides
abstract: In this paper we present a passive and cost-effective method for increasing the frequency range of ultrasound MEMS microphone arrays when using beamforming techniques. By applying a 3D-printed construction that reduces the acoustic aperture of the MEMS microphones we can create a regularly spaced microphone array layout with much smaller inter-element spacing than could be accomplished on a printed circuit board due to the physical size of the MEMS elements. This method allows the use of ultrasound sensors incorporating microphone arrays in combination with beamforming techniques without aliases due to grating lobes in applications such as sound source localization or the emulation of bat HRTFs.

articleTitle: A Planar Architecture with Polarity-Reversible Solenoid for High Power Density of MEMS Vibration Energy Harvester
abstract: A novel high-permeability closed magnetic circuit with polarity-reversible mechanism is developed and integrated inside a micro-solenoid, which could not only enlarge the magnetic intensity by concentrating magnetic flux initially diffused in open space, but also enhance the flux variation rate through the polarity-reversible of magnetic circuit, and thus achieves the significant increased electromechanical coupling at micro scale. Furthermore, this high-efficiency micro-solenoid is integrated with a bi-stable oscillator adopting magnetic and mechanical nonlinearity for high-performance energy harvesting spectrum, characterized as ultra-wide inter-well oscillation and high power output at low-level excitation. Moreover, with the unique advantages of planar architecture, the proposed device could be implemented through batch-fabrication process. The prototype shows normalized power density of 31.9 mWcm-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>g-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and inter-well oscillation of 61.5 Hz at acceleration of 0.7 g, showing high power-output within wide bandwidth below 100 Hz, which has great potential for powering commercial sensor.

articleTitle: Surface-Potential-Driven Sensing of Interfacial Configuration in Functionalized Suspended Graphene for Ionic Solutions
abstract: The surface potential is a crucial characteristic of solid-liquid interfaces that can influence the interfacial arrangement. However, previous research has largely neglected the surface potential impact of substrate effect on sensing performance. This work reports an experimental investigation of suspended/supported oxygen-modified graphene field-effect transistors in different ionic concentrations. According to the results, surface potential markedly influences interfacial characteristics, and this effect becomes more pronounced in solutions with varying ionic concentrations. Simultaneously, low-damage oxygen-modified graphene exhibits higher sensitivity to ionic solutions. This paves the way for low-damage modified graphene to expand its applications in the sensing field.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Aided Wireless Sensor Networks with Harvest-Then-Transmit Protocol
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the use of reconfigurable intelligent surfaces (RIS) to enhance the multiple access and energy harvesting capabilities of wireless sensor networks (WSNs) with the harvest-then-transmit (HTT) protocol. Specifically, we utilize a random/opportunistic beamforming concept to adjust the phase-shift configurations of RIS elements. Sensor nodes can then opportunistically select favorable RIS settings that improve channel conditions for both energy harvesting and data transmission without requiring complicated channel estimation, extensive information exchange, or centralized control. Simulation results demonstrate that this approach effectively increases the network's achievable rate and the amount of energy harvested by the sensor nodes.

articleTitle: Gas Sensing Kinetic Analysis: A Theoretical Approach Towards Multiple Gas Discrimination
abstract: Often, the chemiresistive gas sensor(s) are responsive towards multiple gases or volatile organic compounds (VOCs), thereby trailing in the aspect of selectivity. The paper presents an approach to address the concern of selectivity in chemiresistive gas sensors by applying gas sensing kinetic analysis. Herein, we employed an array of sensors comprising different metal nanoparticles decorated metal-oxide based sensing materials. Different types of VOCs were tested using an array of sensors that presented a distinct sensing pattern in terms of response magnitude. The Eley-Rideal process was adopted to carry out theoretical modeling and further kinetic analysis. The extraction of various kinetic parameters explains the order of response among VOCs and subsequently assists the discrimination. The kinetic parameters were incorporated as distinctive features for principal component analysis (PCA), resulting in effective recognition of tested VOCs.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Automatic Irrigation System for Regulating Intrapelvic Pressure During Instrument Insertion and Removal for Flexible Ureteroscopy
abstract: To maintain clear visibility and a wide surgical field during flexible ureteroscopy, adequate irrigation flow is necessary. However, if the irrigation flow is excessive, intrapelvic pressure (IPP) may increase, which can increase the risk of severe postoperative urinary tract infection and sepsis. The authors previously proposed an automatic regulation system for maintaining safe IPP levels. A custom-developed ultra-miniature fiber-optic pressure sensor (package diameter: 250 µm) is used to measure IPP and proportional-integral-derivative control is used to control the rotation speed of the irrigation roller pump based on the measured IPP. In this study, the effectiveness of this system was evaluated during instrument insertion and removal, which affect IPP. It was found that when the rotation speed was constant or manually adjusted, there was an unintended change in IPP due to instrument insertion or removal. With the automatic irrigation control system, the change in IPP was only temporary. Thus, it was possible to automatically maintain the desired IPP without surgeon intervention.

articleTitle: Extraction of Voluntary Muscle Contraction Based on PCA Reconstruction Error with a Reference of Skin Deformation at Passive Movement
abstract: Extraction of voluntary muscle contraction is important in assessing motor function in patients with severe upper-limb impairments. In this study, we proposed an extraction method of voluntary muscle contraction based on reconstruction error of principle component analysis (PCA), referencing skin deformation at passive movement. Skin deformations of the upper arm were collected on nine conditions of elbow joint movement, including passive, voluntary isotonic, and voluntary isometric. Experimental results indicate that the reconstruction error using the first principle component extracts muscle contraction at the level of 20% of maximum voluntary force (MVF) or more.

articleTitle: Critical Buckling Voltage Shift-Based Resonant Vacuum Pressure Micro-Sensor
abstract: In this work, a new pressure-sensing approach is presenting based on measuring the critical buckling voltage shift of an in-plane heated buckled microbeam with the presence of air pressure. The results show excellent linearity in the wide range of pressure from 2 to 100 Torr. Moreover, the proposed miniature pressure sensor shows a high sensitivity of 11.98 mV/Torr at its resonant frequency of 4 kHz and ambient temperature. The low power consumption, repeatability, and simplicity in design make the proposed sensor promising to realize high performance high-vacuum sensing applications.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Temperature Test of a Multi-Physics Coupling MEMS Sensor Chip
abstract: A multi-physics coupling MEMS sensor chip is put forward in this paper. The chip integrates Fabry-Pérot (F-P) cavity pressure sensing unit, AlN piezoelectric film and Pt thermistor. The fabrication begins with a silicon wafer and a BF33 glass wafer. Magnetron sputtering and lift-off process on silicon wafer are applied to realize multilayer films and patterning, AlN film and Pt film included. The lower electrode of piezoelectric module is exposed by ICP etching. Bottom reflectivity and thickness of F-P cavity are respectively controlled by deposited Al-SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> film and prepared SU-8 photoresist on glass wafer. The temperature test is applied after 3 hours' annealing at 300°C. The wire bonding package and three-wire bridge test scheme is adopted. The temperature coefficient of resistance is 1844 ppm/°C. The sensitivity is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.2822}\ \mathbf{\Omega}/^{\circ} \mathbf{C}$</tex>. The linearity is 1.65%. The resistance at 0 °C is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{153.1}\ \mathbf{\Omega}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Intrusion Detection of Accelerator Pedal Sensor Using a Scalable Data-Based Diagnostic Concept
abstract: Due to the rapidly growing number of functions and sensors or actuators required for this, the vehicle is increasingly developing into a software defined vehicle (SDV). However, the information network of the individual components harbors points of attack for intrusions. The objective is therefore to design a detection system for these intrusions, which is analyzed within the paper on the basis of the accelerator pedal sensor. The focus here is on the symbiosis of fault diagnosis and intrusion detection in order to be able to generate a comprehensive image of the SDV for the secure use of the vehicle and intelligent sensors.

articleTitle: Toward Continuous Monitoring of Concrete Health Via PVDF Receiver
abstract: Concrete structures, vital for modern infrastructure, face degradation due to environmental factors and aging, raising safety concerns in South Korea amidst economic challenges and regulatory pressures. Ultrasonic-based inspection methods, particularly ultrasonic tomography and pulse velocity methods have been effective for non-destructive evaluation. However, continuous monitoring remains difficult due to bulky transducers. This study explores the use of polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF)-based ultrasonic transducers for concrete inspection. PVDF transducers, with smaller dimensions and a flat frequency response, enable detailed analysis of scattered ultrasound related to concrete quality. Experimental results demonstrate that PVDF transducers provide enhanced detection of non-linear ultrasound components, facilitating better assessment of concrete integrity.

articleTitle: Ground-Engineered Planar CSRR-Array for Real-Time Nutrient Monitoring in Precision Agriculture
abstract: This study presents a novel microwave sensor designed for real-time monitoring of nitrogen levels, specifically through ammonium chloride (NH4CI) concentration in aqueous solutions. Simulations and experiments reveal that the proposed sensor design, which integrates multiple split-ring resonators (SRRs) and complementary split-ring resonators to operate at 1 GHz, significantly enhances sensitivity and specificity. The proposed sensor achieves a dynamic range of 42.7 dB as the nitrogen concentration in water increases from 0 ppm to 3500 ppm, highlighting the potential of the sensor in high concentration monitoring. This sensor addresses the limitations of conventional methods by providing a compact, inexpensive, and highly accurate solution. It is designed for real-time, in-field smart agriculture and environmental monitoring, eliminating the need for extensive human involvement in sample collection and laboratory analysis for nutrient monitoring.

articleTitle: A Novel High-Performance Miniaturized MEMS Gyroscope North Finding System Utilizing Rotation Modulation Technique
abstract: The current study reports on the development of a novel, high-performance miniaturized MEMS gyroscope north finding system, which employs the rotation modulation technique. The system features a compact design with a volume of approximately <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$31\text{cm}^{3}$</tex>, a weight of less than 100g, and a power consumption of under 1.5W. Notably, it achieves a remarkable heading angle precision of better than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.3^{0}(1\sigma)$</tex> within 5 minutes. This advancement holds significant potential as a critical reference for both scientific research and industrial applications.

articleTitle: Application of Super Fine Inkjet for Sensor Technology Adding Diversity with Micro Droplets
abstract: Super inkjet can dispense droplets 1/1000 of the volume of conventional inkjet technology. It can also print submicron dots and lines using nanometal, organic, inorganic, and bio-chemical materials. In other words, by simply placing a small volume of gas-sensitive material on top of a general-purpose Si sensor, it can be transformed into a specific sensor device, making it possible to create a variety of gas sensors from a single general-purpose Si sensor chip. The presentation will discuss the application of superfine inkjet to sensor technology.

articleTitle: Quality Factor Engineering in NIR Optical Metasurfaces Using Ge2Sb2Te5 and Graphene
abstract: This study presents a novel method for enhancing the performance of near-infrared (NIR) optical metasurfaces by integrating Ge<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Te5 (GST) phase-change materials with graphene plasmonic properties. By leveraging local graphene heaters, the phase of incident light is precisely controlled, dy-namically adjusting the crystallization levels of GST and altering the metasurface's optical behavior. This approach utilizes surface plasmon polaritons to achieve improved absorption rates and a dynamic phase modulation range of 0° to 300° for reflected waves at a wavelength of 1.55 Finite element method (FEM) simulations validate the effectiveness of the proposed design, demonstrating significant potential for applications in beam steering, LiDAR systems, and reconfigurable optical devices. Key parameters such as resonance frequency, quality factor, and reflection coefficient are meticulously engineered, highlighting the versatility and efficiency of GST-based metasurfaces in advanced photonic technologies.

articleTitle: Shape Sensing Stretchable Sensor Grid Towards Camera-Less Motion Capture
abstract: Stretchable electronics and conformal sensors are valuable for applications in soft robotics and wearable devices. Here, we demonstrate a stretchable sensor sheet with integrated readout for measuring strain and orientation across the sheet. Conductive liquid metal wires encased in silicone measure multi-axis strain. These strain sensors, paired with precision 9-axis IMUs mounted on PCBs embedded in the silicone, enable a shape-sensing, stretchable sensor grid. A prototype is presented first with a single strain sensor and IMU pair, which is charac-terized and calibrated for higher accuracy. Then, a larger scale stretchable grid with 24 strain sensors and 16 IMUs is presented. A four-wire liquid metal bus delivers power to the system and serves as a data communication bus. Long-term, our approach may enable motion capture and shape reconstruction without the need for external cameras or instrumented environments.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimization of Multi-terraced-Plate Electrostatic Actuator
abstract: This paper, for the first time, optimizes multi-terraced-plate electrostatic actuator (MTPEA) theoretically, in order to improve its driving ability. A theoretical model of pull-in angle of MTPEA is proposed, followed by extracting a structure index from it. This structure index is merely related to the ratio of step length to electrode length and the ratio of step height to electrode gap, and is positively associated with pull-in angle. Parameter sweeping is conducted to maximize this structure index, which reveals that the maximum pull-in angle of one-, two- and three-terraced-plate electrostatic actuator is about 25.8%, 42.5% and 53.9% larger than that of parallel-plate electrostatic actuator (PPEA) respectively. Besides, the principle of structure optimization is generalized. Finally, example analysis is conducted to verify the accuracy of the developed theoretical model, and to demonstrate the process of design of MTPEA based on actual situation.

articleTitle: Increasing the Diversity in RGB-to-Thermal Image Translation for Automotive Applications
abstract: Thermal imaging in Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) improves road safety with superior perception in low-light and harsh weather conditions compared to traditional RGB cameras. However, research in this area faces challenges due to limited dataset availability and poor representation in driving simulators. RGB-to-thermal image translation offers a potential solution, but existing methods focus on one-to-one mappings. We propose a one-to-many mapping using a multimodal translation framework enhanced with our Componentaware Adaptive Instance Normalization (CoAdaIN). Unlike the original AdaIN, which applies styles globally, CoAdaIN adapts styles to different image components individually. The result, as we show, is more realistic and diverse thermal image translations.

articleTitle: A Method to Boost the Sensitivity in Transmission-Mode Phase-Variation Planar Microwave Sensors
abstract: A highly sensitive permittivity sensor operating at microwaves is presented. The sensor is a two-port structure consisting of a shunt connected sensing element (a quarter-wavelength grounded stub) sandwiched between two cascades of impedance inverters in a mirrored (symmetric) configuration. It is shown that by alternating the impedance of the inverters above and below the reference impedance of the ports <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{Z}_{0})$</tex>, the sensitivity in the limit of small variations of the dielectric constant of the material under test (MUT) in the vicinity of the reference (REF) value can be significantly enhanced. To illustrate the potential of the approach, a prototype device is designed and validated through simulation and experimentally. The achieved maximum sensitivity is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$S_{\max}=-163.84^{\circ}$</tex> per unit of dielectric constant variation, and the figure of merit, defined as the maximum sensitivity divided by the area of the sensing region expressed in squared wavelengths, is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{FoM}=3257^{\circ}/\lambda^{2}$</tex>, competitive values.

articleTitle: Low Complexity Dynamic Obstacle Detection for Intelligent Road Infrastructure
abstract: We present a new lightweight algorithm for detecting the points related to dynamic obstacles within LIDAR point clouds. Thanks to its low complexity, the algorithm can be used either to enable near-sensor embedded functionalities or to enhance the capabilities of intelligent infrastructure in the C-ITS context. Experimental results on the real-world TUMTraf Intersection Dataset show that the proposed approach can run in real-time on an ARM Cortex A9 CPU while still reaching a detection precision of 69.1 %, which is consistent with state of the art performance of deep neural network-based approaches.

articleTitle: Analysis of Effects of Sensor Error Factors on Attitude and Heading Errors for Inertial/Magnetic Sensor-based Stationary Alignment
abstract: Attitude and heading reference system (AHRS) plays an important role in a variety of application fields. In the AHRS, stationary alignment is performed to determine the initial orientation of the sensor frame with respect to the navigation frame based on inertial/magnetic sensor signals. In this study, we analyze the effects of sensor error factors of accelerometer and magnetometer on attitude and heading accuracy for stationary alignment in undisturbed conditions. This study compared the attitude and heading errors by sensor error factors including noise, bias, nonorthogonality, and misalignment. Simulation results showed that sensor noise with a constant noise density made attitude/heading errors converge to specific RMSEs regardless of sensor orientations, while nonorthogonality and misalignment caused large deviations in attitude/heading errors depending on sensor orientations.

articleTitle: Environmental Variation or Instrumental Drift? A Probabilistic Approach to Gas Sensor Drift Modeling and Evaluation
abstract: Drift is a significant issue that undermines the reliability of gas sensors. This paper introduces a probabilistic model to distinguish between environmental variation and instrumental drift, using low-cost non-dispersive infrared (NDIR) CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensors as a case study. Data from a long-term field experiment is analyzed to evaluate both sensor performance and environmental changes over time. Our approach employs importance sampling to isolate instrumental drift from environmental variation, providing a more accurate assessment of sensor performance. The results show that failing to account for environmental variation can significantly affect the evaluation of sensor drift, leading to improper calibration processes.

articleTitle: Proof of Principle: Full 6D Point-to-Point Motion Tracking with Magnetoelectric Sensors
abstract: Magnetic motion tracking offers advantages in applications where other established methods are constrained due to limited mobility, non-line-of-sight conditions, or missing long-term stability. This contribution combines previous work on a hardware setup and a real-time magnetic signal preprocessing pipeline with a revised algorithm for position and orientation estimation. Finally, we demonstrate full 6D tracking with an early-stage triaxial array demonstrator of the magnetoelectric (ME) sensing principle. Therefore, we track relative movements toward a coil and validate the results against an optical motion capturing system. While moving the sensor at ranges of up to 50 cm, we obtained average errors of 1.4 cm for distance, 6.4 cm for position, and 27° for orientation.

articleTitle: High-Q Surface Acoustic Wave Humidity Sensors Based on Tunable Fano Resonance
abstract: Fano resonance, known for its narrow linewidth and high-quality (Q) factor characteristics, finds extensive applications in biological sensors, chemical sensors, switches, photodetectors, filters, and other fields. This paper proposes a high-Q surface acoustic wave (SAW) resonator for detecting humidity changes. The Butterworth-Van Dyke (BVD) equivalent circuit model of SAW resonators depicts the interference between the electrical and acoustic branch, analogous to the superposition of continuous background and discrete energy levels. This results in a typical Fano resonance phenomenon. Shunting an external capacitor at the interdigital electrodes (IDEs) port of SAW resonators could enhance the Fano line shape and increase the Q factor of the resonator, thereby improving the detection resolution. Compared to devices without the external shunt capacitor, the simple yet effective approach has achieved an impressive increase in the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{Q}$</tex> factor under various humidity conditions, especially at 30% RH, resulting in a three-fold increase in the Q factor to 4897 and has maintained good sensitivity. Leveraging the principle of Fano resonance, the design effectively improves sensor resolution and is adaptable to a broad array of applications.

articleTitle: Decoding Brain Age: A Self-Supervised Graph Neural Network Framework for EEG Analysis
abstract: Electroencephalogram (EEG) recordings are valuable for capturing neuro-physiological states, with brain age prediction providing key insights into brain health. To scale this diagnostic technique, we propose a computer-aided system using self-supervised learning (SSL) and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) for EEG analysis. SSL reduces the need for fully labeled data by pre-training models on large unlabeled EEG datasets. We tackle temporal-spectral feature learning challenges with GNNs, employing graph-based representations of EEG data to depict the brain's interconnectedness and extract meaningful features. Furthermore, we enhance the explainability of brain age predictions by visualizing channel-wise maps, highlighting critical EEG channels Influencing the model's decisions.

articleTitle: Toward Large-scale Application of a Bio-Inspired MEMS Optical Hair Flow Sensor Array
abstract: Bio-inspired artificial hair cell (AHC) sensors, mimicking the functionality of biological hair cells found in nature, have demonstrated versatility in sensing air flow, acceleration detection, and position tracking. Conventional AHC sensors including piezoresistive, piezoelectric, and capacitive types all require metal electrodes, which limit the implementation of large-scale arrays. In this study, we report an optical AHC sensor array that translates air flow into optical signals, thereby eliminating the requirements for electrodes, which makes it possible for future large-scale implementation of flow sensing. Preliminary experiments have established a correlation between the sensor output and flow velocity. Moreover, utilizing this sensor, we measured the frequency of the Karman vortex street at varying flow velocities. Additional testing over 1000 cycles with an error margin of less than 1% further validated the sensor's reliability. In the future, we plan to employ this sensor array to measure the boundary layer separation point on Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) wings.

articleTitle: Modular Sensor Network for Historic Buildings Structural Health Monitoring
abstract: This paper presents the implementation of an IoT-based modular sensor network for structural health monitoring in historic buildings, specifically applied to the Palace of Monser-rate, Portugal. The system aids in preserving cultural heritage through continuous data collection. It comprises four abstraction layers: Cloud, Network, Node, and Sensor. A Raspberry Pi-based solution leverages the existing Wi-Fi network, with each node consisting of a Raspberry Pi 3A+ running Python scripts to interface the sensor and upload data to Google Drive. Data uploads occur every 10 minutes to a designated drive, with alert emails triggered by drastic changes in acceleration or seismic activity. Sensor data, including temperature, relative humidity, ambient light, barometric pressure, sound noise, eTVOC, eCO2, vibration, and seismic intensity, can be collected. The paper details the system architecture, and in-situ testing results over seven days in Spring 2024 using Omron's 2JCIE-BU Environment Sensors. The proposed approach is cost-effective and versatile promoting proactive maintenance of historic structures and enhancing response strategies in emergencies, thereby contributing to the preservation and safety of cultural heritage sites.

articleTitle: A Simple Cascaded Fiber-Optic Fabry Perot Interferometer System with Vernier Effect for Sensitivity Enhanced Strain Measurements
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a sensitivity-enhanced optical fiber strain sensor based on cascaded FPIs that can be built from three off-the-shelf fiber Bragg gratings. Experimental results show that the proposed structure can provide strain sensitivity up to 23.6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{pm}/\mu\epsilon$</tex>, which is approximately 16 times higher than the sensitivity of the single-sensing FPI, which is 1.44 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{pm}/\mu\epsilon$</tex>. This configuration is straightforward to implement and features a simple design.

articleTitle: High Conductivity Graphene-Based Composite EMI Shielding for RF Device Protection
abstract: A high conductivity graphene-based ink was developed using reduced graphene oxide, poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS), diethylene glycol. The graphene ink is capable of being deposited at ambient conditions using an additive printing process on polymer substrate with post process of calendering and intercalation which resulted in an excellent electrical conductivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3.5}\times \mathbf{10}^{\mathbf{5}}\ \mathbf{S}/\mathbf{m}$</tex> and electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding efficiency of 62 dB across 8–18 GHz. Due to the high conductivity, the developed graphene ink can be used in the application of the EMI shielding for RF device protection.

articleTitle: A Disposable Sensor for PM2.5 and PM10 Based on Wireless Magnetoelastic Resonators
abstract: With the increasing awareness of the negative health impacts of airborne particulate matter (PM) on population health, there is a strong need for the development of low-cost PM sensors for citizens to monitor PM2.5 and PM10 exposure. A plastic chip measuring <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{22} \times \mathbf{14}\ \mathbf{mm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> is reported; it is comprised of two stages, for PM2.5 and PM10, each incorporating an impactor and a magnetoelastic resonator. The resonators are wirelessly interrogated by planar coils incorporated into an underlying PCB. Experimental test results show sensitivity levels of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.117} \mathbf{Hz}/(\mathbf{min}\times\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{g}/\mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{3}})$</tex> for PM2.5 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.056}\ \mathbf{Hz}/(\mathbf{min}\times\boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{g}/\mathbf{m}^{\mathbf{3}})$</tex> for the larger particles contained in PM10. Accelerated tests show a projected service lifetime exceeding 416 days in the designated operation mode and environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Hybrid Technique for Sensor Fault Diagnosis in Natural-Gas Pipelines
abstract: Sensor fault diagnosis is crucial for the safe and reliable monitoring of natural gas pipelines. Even though model-based techniques have remarkable performance, they still face significant challenges such as non-linearity and external dis-turbances. In contrast, data-driven methods struggle to deal with unknown disturbances and uncertainties. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid fault diagnostic scheme that leverages the benefits of both model-based and data-driven techniques. First, it introduces a model-based fault estimation technique based on a partial-distributed ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF). It reduces the computational complexity by separating the non-linear computation from the distributed architecture. Furthermore, a data-driven method is developed to detect and isolate sensor faults based on the Gaussian mixture model (GMM). Experimental results considering different sensor fault conditions confirm the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Nanostructured Sensors with P-N Heterojunctions on Metal Foil for Ionic Solution Detection
abstract: Metal-oxide-semiconductors (MOSs) are promising materials as chemiresistive sensors for ion detection in human body fluids. In this paper, we report on the ion sensing performance of the MOS nanostructured sensors with P-N heterojunctions fabricated by a simple technique. N-SnOx nanoparticles/P-NiO particles sensors were fabricated by heating the Sn foil as a substrate and drop-casting a colloidal solution containing Ni(OH)2. The SnOx/NiO sensor was more sensitive to chlorine and sodium ions, compared to SnOx-only sensor. Furthermore, the good sensing performance of the SnOx/NiO sensor for ions in glucose solution was demonstrated. The proposed fabrication technique will contribute to the practical application of MOS-based ion sensors with high performance.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive and Highly Specific Biomedical Sensing Device Development for Lung Cancer Tumor Marker
abstract: This article utilizes the Extended Gate Field-effect Transistor (EGFET) as the sensing element for detecting lung cancer biomarkers (NSE/CYFRA21-1). The EGFET sensing area is fabricated with a conical 3D structure using KOH anisotropic etching to increase the sensing surface area. High dielectric constant materials HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> are used as the EGFET gate dielectric layer to enhance gate capacitance and improve sensing sensitivity. Both gate dielectric structures exhibit high sensitivity, linearity, specificity, and low detection limits for detecting NSE and CYFRA21-1. The ZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gate sensing chip achieves the highest sensitivity of 0.051 V·(ng/ml)-1 for NSE and 0.210 V·(ng/ml)-1 for CYFRA21-1, while the HfO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gate sensing chip achieves the highest sensitivity of 0.061 V·(ng/ml)-1 for NSE and 0.243 V·(ng/ml)-1 for CYFRA21-1. Both NSE/CYFRA21-1 sensing chips demonstrate excellent specificity for CEA and CA15-3.

articleTitle: Preliminary Evaluation of Multi-Angle Spatial Compound Imaging with pMUTs
abstract: This work investigates the feasibility of a multi-angle image compounding scheme using a linear array of pMUTs towards clutter attenuation and speckle artifact suppression. This is the first time that spatial image compounding is deployed together with pMUTs. The proposed methodology is validated experimentally demonstrating an impressive performance with significant SNR gains of up to 20dB and highly accurate reflector localization considering a 3mm-diameter reflector highlighting its suitability for medical imaging and industrial applications.

articleTitle: Aptamer Assisted Simultaneous Detection of Lead and Arsenic in Water Using a Handheld System
abstract: Lead and arsenic contamination in water bodies poses a significant environmental and public health concern, requiring sensitive and rapid detection methods. This study presents a conveyable and facile approach for the simultaneous detection of lead and arsenic in lake water using an aptamer-assisted nano-biosensor in conjunction with a handheld sensing system integrated with a smartphone application. The fine-pitched inter-digitated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu$</tex>-electrodes sensor surface decorated with aptamer sequence exhibits distinct specificity towards the targeted metal, dissenting other interfering ions. The limit of detection (LOD) obtained for lead and arsenic is 1.3 ng/L and 3.8 ng/L, respectively. The presence of lead or arsenic ions induces a change in the aptamer structure, resulting in the shift of sensor current proportional to the concentration of the ions. The reader circuit interfaced with an Android application captures this current as a sensing parameter for analysis enabling the in-situ applicability of the assay.

articleTitle: Analysis of Uptake and Release of Explosive Analyte from PDMS Films Using UV-vis Absorption Spectroscopy
abstract: The accurate in-field detection of explosives is a continuing challenge for homeland security and defence personnel around the world. [1]-[3] While there are established methods for identifying bulk quantities there are fewer that are readily available for trace detection, particularly for explosives that have low vapor pressures. Pre-concentrator materials are specifically designed to absorb and subsequently release analyte vapors as a concentrated packet into a detector, thereby amplifying or even enabling the detection of trace amounts of analytes by sensor systems. [4], [5] This study describes the use of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) films of varying thicknesses as pre-concentrators for explosives by analyzing the kinetics of the uptake and release of p-nitrotoluene (pNT) vapor using UV-vis absorption spectroscopy. A crucial component of this study was to design the UV-vis measurement set-up to ensure quick exposure of PDMS films to the analyte vapor. Finally, the PDMS film fabrication process was optimized for optical clarity, and the pre-concentrator kinetic parameters were quantified.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Piezoresistive Tactile Sensor Based on Mechanical Metamaterial with Negative Poisson's Ratio
abstract: This work proposes a piezoresistive tactile sensor based on a metamaterial with a negative Poisson's ratio, utilizing a more cost-effective and straightforward method compared to previous processes for fabricating microstructures. To demonstrate the impact of negative Poisson's ratio on piezoresistive sensor performance, comparison structures with a positive Poisson's ratio are designed, manufactured, and tested. The metamaterial-based sensor exhibits a high sensitivity at low pressures, which is 2.8 times higher than that of a body-centered cubic structure and 10 times higher than a simple cubic structure. Additionally, the fabricated sensor demonstrates excellent flexibility and minimal physical interference due to the integration of flexible electrodes and substrates. The sensor shows potential for various applications, including wearable devices, which have recently gained significant attention.

articleTitle: Stabilized Adaptive Steering for 3D Sonar Microphone Arrays with IMU Sensor Fusion
abstract: This paper presents a novel software-based approach to stabilizing the acoustic images for in-air 3D sonars. Due to uneven terrain, traditional static beamforming techniques can be misaligned, causing inaccurate measurements and imaging artifacts. Furthermore, mechanical stabilization can be more costly and prone to failure. We propose using an adaptive conventional beamforming approach by fusing it with real-time IMU data to adjust the sonar array's steering matrix dynamically based on the elevation tilt angle caused by the uneven ground. Additionally, we propose gaining compensation to offset emission energy loss due to the transducer's directivity pattern and validate our approach through various experiments, which show significant improvements in temporal consistency in the acoustic images. We implemented a GPU-accelerated software system that operates in real-time with an average execution time of 210ms, meeting autonomous navigation requirements.

articleTitle: Long-term Durability Evaluation of Hetero-core Optical Fiber Hydrogen Sensor Composed of Palladium Nanoparticles and Poly-L-lysine
abstract: In this paper, a hetero-core fiber optic hydrogen sensor with alternating layers of poly-L-lysine and palladium nanoparticles is proposed and experimentally demonstrated to suppress degradation over time. The results suggest that stable performance can be maintained even four weeks after sensor fabrication, highlighting the potential utility of this technology in hydrogen sensors.

articleTitle: In Situ Linker of Protein for the Immobilization on the Carbon-Based Sensor Materials
abstract: Carbon-based nanomaterials such as graphene and carbon nanotube exhibit high electrical conductivity when used as sensors. By integrating carbon-based nanomaterials with biomaterials such as receptors and antibodies, it is possible to develop a nanobiosensor that combines the high sensitivity of carbon nanomaterials with the high selectivity of biomaterials. Achieving this requires effective immobilization technology between carbon-based materials and biomaterials, commonly utilizing linker-based methods such as pyrene-based linkers or surface modification of carbon-based materials. In this study, we developed an amino acid tag that can be immobilized on carbon-based nanomaterials without the need for a linker, utilizing the amino acid tag inherent in the biological material itself. The developed amino acid tag demonstrated strong binding affinity to carbon-based nanomaterials without compromising the productivity of the biomaterials. Additionally, single-chain variable fragment (scFv) antibodies containing an amino acid tag for immobilization were effectively bound to the surface of graphene sheets without significantly impeding productivity.

articleTitle: Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy Platform for Label-Free Characterization of Spheroid Viability
abstract: Industrial anti-cancer drug screening processes require label-free and high-throughput methods to characterize drug effects on in vitro 3D cellular models, such as spheroids. However, conventional characterization methods are either invasive or have limited throughput. In this study, we assessed the feasibility of using electrical impedance spectroscopy as a label-free method to evaluate spheroid viability. We developed an easy-to-fabricate flow-through impedance sensor with facing electrodes for improved sensitivity and simultaneous imaging. By exposing liver cancer spheroids to varying concentrations of a toxic compound, we demonstrate that impedance spectroscopy can be successfully used to measure spheroid viability with high sensitivity. We benchmarked our results against conventional viability assays, including ATP assays.

articleTitle: Numerical Temperature Analysis of the Double-Side Photonic Thermal Sensor System with Janus Radiation Cooler
abstract: In this study, we design a double-side photonic thermal sensor system to simulate continuous internal heating in an enclosed box using the Janus radiation cooler as an upper cover. The Janus radiative cooler is composed of a selective emitter in the upper part and a broadband emitter in the bottom part. A selective emitter is based on a polymer and metal thin film, which utilizes the dispersion relation of spoof surface plasmon polaritons to achieve a nearly ideal selective emitting surface. The finite element method is used to simulate the local temperature distributions inside the structures under steady-state operation. The temperatures changes are measured at the top and the bottom of the Janus radiative cooler, and the middle and the bottom of the thermal sensor system. The structure top radiates the absorbed heat into outer space, while the structure bottom absorbs thermal energy in the mid-to-far infrared spectrum. The excellent cooling performance of the double-side photon thermal sensor system is demonstrated by using two- dimensional thermal simulations. The proposed device is effective in developing advanced passive thermal systems that can operate simultaneously for the surface and vacancy.

articleTitle: MXene-based Planar Microwave Sensor for Acetone Gas Detection
abstract: Sensing properties enhancement of microwave-based gas sensor is a substantial challenge for trace acetone detection in many vital applications. MXene is employed on the high-field distribution area of the microwave resonator to enhance sensing performance. While the interdigital structure of the proposed sensor is considered as core part because the finger gap and width of the resonator are coupled with the transmission line above substrate, enhancing the coupling and field distribution. Deployment of MXene film on the microwave sensor for the exposure of acetone concentration ranging from 1–500 ppm exhibited a strong correlation between the resonant frequency and amplitude with high sensitivity of 8.23 kHz/ppm and 2.1 mdB/ppm, respectively. The proposed MXene based microwave gas sensor demonstrated an extremely effective route to enhance the sensing sensitivity by introducing microwave resonate structure and functional materials.

articleTitle: Source Number Estimation Based on the Pressure and Particle Velocity Combined Processing for Acoustic Vector-Sensor Arrays
abstract: This paper aims to achieve accurate source number estimation (SNE) using the acoustic vector-sensor (AVS) arrays, which are crucial for array-based detection and sensing applications. To fully exploit the advantages of the AVS arrays, we integrates SNE into the pressure and particle velocity combined processing (P&PV-CP) framework. This innovative approach leverages the uncorrelated noise between pressure and particle velocity channels to enhance the effective signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). We introduce a novel method for constructing the cross-covariance matrix within this framework, addressing challenges where signals from specific directions may be attenuated due to spatial filtering induced by fixed observation angles. Theoretical analysis and simulations demonstrate that the proposed P&PV-CP framework, along with the new covariance matrix construction method, significantly enhances processing gain.

Author Keywords: pressure and particle velocity combined processing (P&PV-CP)

articleTitle: Robust Centroid and Apparent Diameter Extraction via Convex Optimization for Optical Spacecraft Navigation
abstract: A robust optimization-based ellipse fitting procedure for planet/moon-relative optical spacecraft navigation is considered. Ellipse fitting is a classic problem in computer vision and pattern recognition. Methods ranging from simple linear least squares to nonlinear optimization techniques have been applied to solve it to varying degrees of accuracy. An important consideration is the presence of large outliers in the detected edge points from images. Sampling-based techniques such as random sample consensus (RANSAC) and M-estimator sample consensus (MSAC) have been used to tackle this problem. We present a technique that, to an extent, preserves the simplicity of linear least squares techniques and adds significant outlier robustness. We demonstrate our approach using synthetic and real images by adding a known level of outliers for comparative purposes. Standard and robust approaches in the literature are considered for comparison. Due to its generality, the proposed method can be used for similar applications where pattern recognition is utilized.

articleTitle: A Methodology for Developing and Evaluating FBG-Based Smart 3D-Printed Prosthetics
abstract: Lower limb amputation can greatly impact mobility and overall well-being. While recent advancements in 3D printing offer affordable and customizable prosthetics, maintaining structural integrity, performance, and accurate pressure measurements is essential. This study explores the use of Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors in 3D-printed prosthetics for real-time deformation monitoring. After modeling the prosthetic, Finite Element Analysis (FEA) was used to identify critical stress areas. These areas were then segmented and modeled, including a U-shaped segment for the metatarsal region and two linear segments at varying depths (0.4mm and 0.8mm). Our results show that the 0.8mm deep sensor demonstrated superior weight tolerance and response consistency compared to the 0.4mm deep sensor. This depth enabled more effective strain monitoring, enhancing response, recovery, and the reliability of the prosthetic. As for the U-shaped segments, both horizontally and vertically positioned sensors displayed rapid recovery and could bear maximum weight before reaching potential failure points.

articleTitle: Sixteen-micromachined-gyroscopes Array Beyond Accuracy Limit By 1.9 Times Without Bandwidth Reduction
abstract: How to break through theoretical accuracy limit of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sqrt{N}$</tex> times based on micromachined-gyroscopes array without bandwidth reduction is currently important challenge. To solve above challenge, a novel expectation cluster interval fusion method based on non-Kalman filter theory is for the first time proposed by dynamically adjusting weighted coefficients of the array samples with high-dispersion characteristics to cluster these samples into special refined interval, which is initially formed based on minimum variance theory representing accuracy limit of the array fusion method. The experimental results show that the accuracy of array-based microgyroscope reaches <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.57\times 10^{-20}/\mathrm{s}$</tex> in this work, which is improved by 1.9 times compared with theoretical accuracy limit value of sixteen-micromachined-gyroscope array of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.06\times 10^{-20}/\mathrm{s}$</tex>. Further, amplitude of angular rate has no reduction when the bandwidth reaches 50Hz. This work paves a solid path to apply the array-based gyroscope in actual engineering.

articleTitle: Simulating Next-Gen Automotive Sensors: Physics Meets AI
abstract: Current automotive perception systems fall short of providing level 5 anywhere-anytime autonomy because they lack robustness in long-tail scenarios (extreme weather, challenging lighting). Upcoming technologies like quantum dot short-wave infrared (SWIR) have the potential to address some of these failure cases, but are slow to break through because of the long and expensive testing and validation campaigns necessary to integrate them. Simulation can expedite the adoption of such new technologies, if it can bridge two gaps: from traditional to next-gen sensor models, and from simple baseline environments to realistic, complex corner case scenarios. In this talk, we investigate how AI can achieve this and augment existing datasets and simulation software with novel sensor data streams.

articleTitle: A Low Speed Sampling Method Applicable to IoT Data Analysis
abstract: Accumulation for Real-time Serial-to-parallel converter (ARS) is a period analysis method that provides high resolution in the low-frequency domain. However, the problem is that the resolution of period estimation is limited by the sampling period. To improve the resolution, the sampling frequency must be increased, which causes an increase in power consumption and waste of data volume. This paper proposes a new method to solve the above problems. Computer simulations and experiments were conducted to evaluate the performance of the proposed method. The results show that periodic analysis can be performed with high accuracy even when the sampling frequency is reduced while keeping low computational complexity compared with FFT.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Non-Contact Vital Sign Monitoring on Multiple Moving Targets for Daily In-Home Healthcare with a Single Fmcw Radar
abstract: Simultaneous non-contact breath and heart beat monitoring on multiple moving targets remains a significant challenge in the radar-based in-home healthcare field because of the severe motion artifacts and harsh propagation environment. To achieve it, a novel framework is designed for clutter removal and motion rejection vital sign detection.
