Fusing the extracted doppler characters with map features generated from the FMCW radar, it allows for distinguishing the multiple targets from environment and estimating the targets' motions for artifact suppression with only a single commercial radar, free from modifying any hardware or pre-training model. Experimental results demonstrated a significant artifact suppression, enhancing the accuracy of heartrate and breath rate estimation beyond 90% across subjects, when compared to Photoplethysmogram (PPG) sensors and pressure sensors on the belts. Furthermore, the accuracy of the extracted heartbeat waveform is validated through the Bland-Altman test, demonstrating potential applications in long-term in-home remote Heart Rate Variability (HRV) monitoring.

articleTitle: Oxygen Plasma Treated RGO Based Resistive Sensor: A Step Towards NH3 Detection from Human Breath
abstract: This report presents the impact of oxygen-plasma treatment on reduced graphene oxide (rGO) for ammonia (NH3) sensing ability. Raman and FTIR characterization suggest induction of defects and oxygen functional groups on rGO following the treatment of Oxygen-plasma. Using the material as channel, a two terminal resistive sensor is developed. The sensing response indicates high selectivity towards NH3 and water vapour. In case of water vapour there is recovery of base current along with higher response. Unlike the water vapour, NH3 reduced the current and response is relatively lower. Due to such distinctive features in the sensor response, the selective detection of ammonia through this sensor is proposed. Moreover, this sensor is found to be able to sense low concentration (1–5 ppm) of ammonia, comparable to concentrations observed in human exhaled breath, suggesting its possible implementation in medical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Sensitivity-Enhanced Non-Invasive Glucose Sensor Using Interdigital Capacitors
abstract: Microwave technology is one of the mainstream directions in the current research field of non-invasive monitoring of blood glucose levels (BGL). Based on the devices by grounded coplanar waveguides (GCPW), this paper reports a new structure using interdigital capacitors (IDCs) to improve the measuring sensitivity for the first time. The design and simulation have been performed by HFSS software. The results show that the electric field coupling effect of the interdigital structure is enhanced effectively. After fabricated on FR-4 substrate, the microwave performance of the sensor was tested by vector network analyzer (VNA) when the concentration of the solution varied to 8 mg/ml. The preliminary experimental results indicate that the sensitivity has been improved about 70 times compared to the traditional device.

articleTitle: A Novel MEMS Sensor with a Floating Cover Plate for Wall-Shear Stress Measurement in the Harsh Supersonic Flow
abstract: This work presents a novel capacitance MEMS sensor with a floating cover plate for robust wall-shear stress measurements in the harsh environment of supersonic flow field. Based on a Dual Silicon-On-Insulator (DSOI) wafer, the specific microfabrication technology is developed to achieve the combination of the floating cover plate and sensing structure, which features the accurate etching, anodic bonding, and backside TGVs' lead wire. A two-dimensional Poiseuille channel was established to carry out the sensor calibration. Moreover, the enormous reduction of damaging possibilities of the sensor in practical applications is experimentally verified. Wall-shear stress measuring experiments were performed at a Mach 2.0 supersonic wind-tunnel facility. The entire period of the supersonic flow from beginning and stabilization to end was observed by the proposed sensor, where shear stress fluctuations caused by the near-wall flow field structure were acquired. Additionally, the experimental results matched the pattern of changes in the wall pressure, and indicated the agreement with the model predictions for fully developed boundary layers.

articleTitle: Reflectometry Architecture for Enhanced Fault Localization Based on Low PAPR Chirp-OMTDR
abstract: This paper presents a novel method for generating a Chirp-based Orthogonal Multi-Tone Time-Domain Reflectometry (Chirp-OMTDR) signal. The proposed approach effectively reduces the Peak-to-Average Power Ratio (PAPR) compared to conventional OMTDR signals, enabling increased transmission power in cables under test, and extending the cable analysis range. Additionally, the chirp structure exhibits sparsity properties in the time-frequency domain, making it well-suited for compressed sensing applications. This leads to enhanced spatial resolution and more precise fault localization, while also enabling the use of lower-frequency, less expensive, and less noisy Analog-to-Digital Converters (ADCs).

articleTitle: Detection of Hidden non-Metallic Objects Using Electromagnetic Field
abstract: A nondestructive object detection method using an antenna as a sensor with a localized electromagnetic field is proposed. The proposed method uses the traj ectories of the real and imaginary parts of the reflection factor. The proposed method can detect non-metallic objects such as the human body based on the distance between the antenna and target. Additionally, the information regarding whether a target is approaching the antenna source can be determined using the direction of the trajectory. Therefore, the proposed method can detect hidden non-metallic objects even without any information on them.

articleTitle: Design of an Ultra Low-Power Glass-Based Micro-Hotplate with Thermal Isolation Structure
abstract: The development and optimization of micro-hotplates play a critical role in the advancement of thermal emitter, gas sensors and other micro-electro-mechanical systems. This study explores the thermal performance of a novel micro-hotplates based on glass substrate with enhanced thermal efficiency by thermal isolation gaps integration. It significantly reduces power consumption and enhances temperature uniformity. The power consumption is only 11.7 mW at 300°C with a huge decrease of 30.2 % compared to the device without thermal isolation gaps while the heating area is 340 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 340\mu \mathrm{m}^{2}$</tex>. And the temperature variation within the effective heating area is only 0.18 °C <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$/\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. Furthermore, the mechanical stability of the micro-hotplates is maintained, making it a promising candidate for low-power, high-efficiency MEMS applications.

articleTitle: AC-Driven Aptamer-Decorated Graphene FET for Cortisol Detection
abstract: Accurately measuring cortisol levels is crucial for diagnosing and managing stress-related conditions. Among all biofluids containing cortisol, Interstitial fluid (ISF) offers distinct advantages such as stable pH, continuous extraction, and minimal contamination risks. This study introduces a novel method utilizing an AC driven liquid-gate Graphene Field Effect Transistor (GFET) array device, decorated with a cortisol aptamer for precise cortisol detection from changes in GFETs' phase to address challenges encountered in DC measurements, including the Debye length screening effect and noise issues. Aptamers, selected for their compact size and ease of synthesis, serve as optimal recognition elements that also show capacitive changes. The proposed sensor demonstrates very strong linear detection ranges 1 nM to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1}\ \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{M}$</tex> with sensitivity of 3.34 mV/dec <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}=\mathbf{0.94})$</tex> for cortisol concentrations in 1XPBS. This effectively covers the physiological cortisol range in ISF, even in high ionic backgrounds. In this work, Graphene functionalization was validated using Raman spectroscopy and AFM-SNOM. The integration of AC voltage driven liquid-gate GFETs with aptamers shows promise for advancing 2D sensors in personalized healthcare technology. Keywords: GFET, graphene, aptamer, cortisol.

articleTitle: Optimising the Fabrication of Reduced Graphene Oxide Electrodes by Laser Reduction
abstract: In recent years, many studies have shown that graphene materials have the potential to play an important role as the electrode material in electrochemical sensor development although consistency in fabrication remains an issue. This study looks to develop a more reproducible approach to reduced graphene oxide manufacture utilizing a high-powered fiber laser. The fabricated sensors were characterized using cyclic voltammetry and Raman spectroscopy. Results demonstrate the produced graphene oxide had a significantly lower defect density compared to previous approaches with an improved and narrower spread in electrochemical performance.

articleTitle: Triaxial Force Plate with High Speed and Resolution Line Scan Camera for Sampling Moiré Method
abstract: This study reports on a force sensing method to enable high-time resolution triaxial measurement by analyzing line-scan camera images through a prism using the sampling moire method (SM). It is well-known that conventional SM accurately measures the in-plane displacement of grid pattern images. Recently, it was reported that by combining SM with a prism, a force sensor capable of triaxial measurement can be realized. However, in the case of area scan cameras, high-time resolution is usually a trade-off with the number of pixels, which determines accuracy. Here, we combined a line scan camera with a high frame rate of 26 kHz and a wide view in the horizontal direction with an inclined pattern to achieve high independence three axes measurement.

articleTitle: Integration of Single-Foot Impedance Plethysmography and Ballistocardiography on a Shoe Insole for Robust Heartbeat Detection
abstract: Smart insoles are a promising tool for monitoring population health status in ambulatory settings. However, obtaining heart rate in these systems remains a challenge, as the most common techniques for measuring heart rate require direct contact with the skin. Ballistocardiography (BCG) has recently been shown to be a good alternative to overcome this drawback, as it is a cardiac mechanical signal that can be measured with a piezoelectric sensor embedded in a shoe insole without skin contact. However, a limitation of BCG is that it is sensitive to motion artifacts, especially while standing. On the other hand, impedance plethysmography (IPG) is a technique that has been shown to be effective in detecting the heartbeat in the foot also in insoles with better performance when standing rather than sitting, even through socks, as the weight of the body when standing favors a better contact which improves the measurement. This study explores the integration of the two approaches, BCG and IPG, in a shoe insole to improve the robustness of heartbeat detection. The results indicate a 10% improvement in heartbeat detection accuracy for both BCG and IPG when the subject is standing, and a 4% improvement when seated, compared to the single best method, BCG.

articleTitle: Silk Fibroin-Based Flexible Bio-Piezoelectric Sensor for Nasal Flaring Monitoring
abstract: Nasal flaring is an abnormal movement of the nose that is often associated with symptoms of respiratory diseases such as difficulty breathing in medical research. The measurement of this movement has great potential applications, as it can not only assist doctors in quickly diagnosing the severity of lung damage in patients, but also serve as a reference for monitoring potential health issues during daily sleep. This paper productively proposes a piezoelectric flexible patch sensor based on silk fibroin for monitoring nasal flaring behavior. The first innovative use of glycine-chitosan doped in pure silk fibroin to modulate the secondary structure of silk fibroin, while excellent biocompatibility is maintained, and the piezoelectric properties of the silk fibroin are effectively enhanced. The sensitive layer obtained by the simple preparation process is only about 2μm thick, giving it a slim and lightweight profile. This allows for seamless integration into wearable devices, significantly enhancing the wearer's comfort. The sensor system demonstrates outstanding sensitivity (4.17 m V IkPa) and fast response, which can monitor different nasal flaring states, such as rapid expansion, stability, and large movements. With its excellent functionality, it offers a promising solution for real-time wearable monitoring, providing valuable alternative for assessing cardiorespiratory health.

articleTitle: Low-Cost Water Level Sensor with Improved Data Quality for Flash Flood Monitoring in Urban Areas
abstract: Flooding represents an unavoidable natural phenomenon that can result in significant loss of life and damage to infrastructure. Within urban environments, the presence of buildings, roads, and other man-made structures can disrupt natural drainage patterns, impede infiltration, and amplify surface runoff. Consequently, deploying many sensors holds potential for generating distributed runoff models capable of capturing fine-scale details necessary for early detection of flash floods. This study explores a capacitive based sensor approach to designing water level measurement stations using cost-effective measurement techniques, integrating a rigorous improvement of data quality prior to transmission to the smart city platform, thereby facilitating deployment in urban settings. The sensor structure and its sensing methodologies are comprehensively elucidated. Specifically, the sensor employs two distinct types of measuring methodologies to ascertain water level measurements, enhancing data validity through cross-verification based on differing well-known physical principles. Additionally, the study reports the sensor implementation, calibration, and resolution, providing empirical evidence to support the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed implementation strategy.

articleTitle: Incorporation of C-coated V2O5 Nanoballs with TiO2 Nanorod Arrays for Self-powered Electrochemical Broadband Photodetectors
abstract: This paper reported a self-powered broadband electrochemical photodetector (ECPD) based on V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nano-heterostructure. V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf> nanoballs (VNBs) an free-standing TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanorod arrays (TNRAs) were prepared using hydrothermal method, and an incorporation of SWCNTs-modified VNBs with TNRAs was conducted to form a SWCNT@VNBs/TNRAs heterostructure. The ECPD was assembled as ITO/electrolyte/SWCNTs@VNBs/TNRAs/FTO structure for experimental measurement. A thorough characterization for the materials and devices were performed. It is demonstrated that the photocurrent of ECPD can reach around 8 mA with a self-driving potential of 0.5 V. The interface electrochemical redox reaction at the SWCNT@V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</inf>/TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> heterostructure makes a high-efficient photoelectrical conversion without requirement of external bias.

articleTitle: Lateral Compression Enhanced Single-cell Microfluidic Cytometer for Tumor Cell Detection
abstract: The deformability of cells is critical indicator of their biomechanical properties and functional behaviors, particularly in cell heterogeneity and tumor cell detection. Conventional microfluidic-based mechanical detection has relatively low throughput, poor adaptability and insufficient cell resolution. Accordingly, we develop a high-throughput mechanical detection device based on microfluidic cytometer platform integrated with a laterally adjustable compression structure. The adjustable channel allows for the meticulous investigation of differences in cellular mechanical properties, thus facilitating the more precise detection of target tumor cells. The results demonstrated that tumor cells exhibited higher deformability compared to uroepithelial cells. Besides, the deformability of the nucleus was investigated by applying strong compression to the cells, and the clear differentiation between tumor cells and uroepithelial cells was achieved. In conclusion, the developed microfluidic platform offers a promising high-throughput method to detection the mechanical characteristics of cells, providing valuable insights into tumor cell biology.

articleTitle: Air-Coupled Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducers (PMUTs) for High-Resolution Distance Sensing
abstract: High-frequency airborne ultrasound enables high-resolution distance sensing for various applications, such as robotics, industrial automation, gesture control, and more. This paper presents a 1.5MHz, 12-element 2-D Piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT) array for high temporal and spatial resolution distance sensing in air. Electrical impedance analysis and measured electroacoustic frequency response of the air-coupled PMUT array showed a resonant frequency f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> of 1.5 MHz, an electromechanical coupling factor k<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</inf><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 4.5%, and a -3 dB fractional bandwidth of 5% centered at 1.5 MHz, with high transmit and receive sensitivities of 70 Pa/V and 0.16 mV/Pa, respectively. Distance measurement on a curved surface using two matched PMUT arrays in pulse-echo proved the feasibility of sensitive and accurate high-resolution distance sensing in demanding scenarios.

articleTitle: A Flexible and Self-Powered Chitosan-BaTiO3Composite Pressure Sensor for E-Skin Applications
abstract: Flexible, sensitive, and self-powered pressure sensors that can mimic tactile sensing of the human skin are the subject of research and development in various applications including electronic skin (e-skin), prosthetics, and soft-robotic applications. However, current state of the art pressure sensors are typically not fully conformable, requiring external power, and are generally limited in sensitivity. There is a critical need for innovative materials for the fabrication of self-powered pressure sensors that are high in sensitivity and mechanical flexibility. In this research, a piezoelectric nanocomposite-based pressure sensor fabricated using hybrid chitosan-BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>nanoparticles (NPs) is presented. The sensor exhibits high sensitivities of 238 mV/kPa and 1705 mV/Hz, excellent cyclic stability greater than 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> cycles, and superior biocompatibility. The results show that there is a significant enhancement in both pressure and frequency sensitivity of nearly 10-fold and 6-fold respectively, compared to pure chitosan film. This is due to the higher piezoelectric coefficient (d33=13 pC/N) of the composite, around double. This proposed hybrid organic-inorganic composite material lays a robust foundation for future development of high-performance sensors for next generation prosthetics and soft robotic applications.

articleTitle: Pd Decorated SiO2-TiO2 Nanocomposite for Low Temperature Hydrogen Sensing
abstract: This study explores development and application of Pd decorated SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanocomposite as an advanced material for hydrogen gas sensing operating at low temperatures. By combining the synergistic effects of Pd nanoparticles and SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>- TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanocomposite, the sensor has shown high sensitivity, fast response, and recovery time. Key mechanisms including enhanced electron-hole separation, increased carrier density, and efficient catalytic activity of Pd are investigated to understand their roles in improving the sensing performance. The study presents comprehensive experimental results, including the sensor's response to hydrogen with different concentrations (500–8000 ppm) at various temperatures (30 °C and 80 °C), demonstrating its potential for low-temperature hydrogen sensing in various industrial and environmental applications.

articleTitle: Multi Time-Over-Threshold System for Light Signal in a Liquid Xenon 3-Photon Compton Camera
abstract: This paper shows how multi-time-over-threshold (MTOT) method outperforms single-time-over-threshold (STOT) in precisely determining both the arrival time and the number of vacuum ultraviolet (VUV) photons detected by each PMT in a prototype <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3-\gamma$</tex> liquid xenon medical nuclear imaging system. Based on both experimental and simulated results, MTOT yields a 70% improvement in reconstructing the number of photoelectrons (PEs) and a 20–30% increase in arrival time precision as compared to STOT. These results pave the way for preliminary spatial localization of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\gamma$</tex> interaction helping reducing the imaging system's occupancy rate when imaged activity increases.

articleTitle: Phenomenological Model for a Light-Activated Gas Sensor
abstract: Light activation has been demonstrated as an effective alternative to heating for enhancing the gas response in semiconductor gas sensors. Despite two decades of research, the mechanisms behind their responses remain a topic of discussion. However, experiments have consistently shown trends in sensor responses to varying light conditions and gas concentrations. Building on these qualitative observations, we propose a phenomenological model that quantitatively predicts resistance changes in these devices. This prediction relies on a set of parameters that can be experimentally determined in advance. Our model includes effects such as photoconductivity, dynamic gas response, irradiance influence on sensitivity, and baseline drift. Validation with experimental data shows that the model accurately predicts sensor behavior over short and long timescales.

articleTitle: Generation of Microdroplet lens for Surface-Enhanced Raman Spectrometry Analysis for Sample Detection
abstract: In this conference presentation, we introduce a novel method for enhancing surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) signals using liquid-phase microdroplet lenses. By employing a contract deposition method, we create SERS substrates with a ~210 µm radius silver nanoparticle-coated region (SERS active site) on a hydrophobic porous silicon background. A water droplet is then positioned above the silver nanoparticle-coated region to serve as an optical lens, effectively focusing laser light and creating hotspots that amplify Raman signals. We evaluated three sample deposition methods-direct drying, pure water lens, and sample lens-using melamine samples at varying concentrations. Our results demonstrate that the sample lens method provides the highest Raman signal enhancement. This technique offers a rapid, simple, and highly sensitive approach to SERS analysis, with potential applications across various scientific and industrial fields.

articleTitle: Fabrication of Conductive Nanomaterial Patterns on Polymeric Substrates Using Laser and Adhesive Tape
abstract: This study introduces a technique for fabricating flexible devices using a combination of spraying carbon nanotubes (CNTs), laser patterning, and adhesive tape. The method involves depositing CNTs on polypropylene substrate by spray coating and utilizing selective laser treatment to create durable and embedded conductive patterns. This approach addresses the common issue of poor adhesion of conductive material to substrates in flexible electronics by partially melting the polymer to enhance CNTs integration. The fabricated sensors exhibit excellent durability and retain performance after multiple bending cycles. Chronoamperometry tests demonstrate the ability of the electrochemical sensors thus fabricated to detect hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) in buffer solutions, with a detection range from 0.1 to 900 ppm. The use of selective laser treatment and adhesive tape enables the removal of unpatterned areas and ensures high precision and flexibility in the design. This straightforward and versatile method can be applied to various conductive materials and polymers, and it can offer significant potential for advancements in flexible sensor technology and other electronic applications.

articleTitle: Finite Time Stabilization of Coupled Network by the Adaptive Event-Triggered Control
abstract: This paper studies finite time stabilization of coupled network by an adaptive event-triggered control protocol. Since the resource limitations, continuous control scheme is not valid in practical applications. Event triggered scheme can effectively reduce the cost of control. Unlike existing results, a novel adaptive event-triggered protocol is proposed. It largely reduces transmission times. Finite time stabilization of coupled network is achieved. The theoretical results are confirmed by numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Patchable Inkjet-Printed Wearable Sensors for Measuring Muscle Activities
abstract: In this paper, we present a patchable, non-invasive, inkjet-printed wearable electromyography sensor designed for unobtrusive, comfortable, and long-duration use. It will offer a compact, low-cost solution while maintaining high signal quality and resistance to body movement. As a first step toward creating practical, everyday wearable sensors, we conducted human-in-the-loop experiments with six participants, comparing the usability and performance of the proposed sensor against two existing commercial electromyography sensors during isometric and non- isometric contractions. We evaluated four key metrics—signal-to-noise ratio, signal-to-motion artifact ratio, drop in power density ratio, and power spectral density—against those of conventional sensors to assess the sensor's effectiveness and reliability. Additionally, user experience surveys were conducted to inform improvements in both the functional and emotional design aspects, with a focus on enhancing comfort and overall usability.

articleTitle: Event Intensity Decay with Event Cameras for Efficient Object Detection
abstract: In this paper, we explore the object detection challenge with event-cameras. We propose an event-frame representation with increased temporal information that improves the performance of off the shelf feed-forward object detectors significantly. We evaluate our method on the Gen1 [1] and 1 Mpx [2] dataset and show that it significantly outperforms existing feed forward implementations and compare it with the current state of the art.

articleTitle: A > 70dB Digital Readout Circuit Implemented in 65nm CMOS for 10 $\mu \mathrm{m}$ SWIR InGaAs Pixels
abstract: This paper presents a 10 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \text{mx}10\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> pixel readout interface for SWIR imagers implemented in a 65 nm CMOS technology. The pixel uses a pulse-frequency modulation ADC operating in two steps: a 5-bit coarse conversion and a 7-bit residue conversion. The residue conversion results to a non-uniform quantization that enables an area-efficient implemen-tation without a huge penalty to the system SNR. To improve analog readout performance, digital circuits inside the pixel were removed and transferred as an array mirroring the pixel array in the periphery. This allows for better analog circuitry that requires more area. Address-event representation is used for communication between the two arrays. The power consumption at the maximum expected input current is 0.188 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{W}$</tex> per pixel. With a full-well capacity of 59.24 ke-, the dynamic range is 74.56 dB, and the linearity error is 0.21 %.

articleTitle: A Novel Flexible Blood Pressure Sensor Based on Ultrathin Silicon for Continuous Monitoring
abstract: Continuous blood pressure (BP) monitoring is essential for the early detection and effective management of cardiovascular diseases. Conventional photoplethysmography (PPG) sensors are limited by their susceptibility to ambient light conditions and a low signal-to-noise ratio, whereas piezoelectric sensors often face challenges in achieving close skin conformity due to their inherent rigidity. This study introduces an innovative flexible BP sensor based on 5 µm ultrathin silicon, designed for continuous monitoring. Encapsulated in Eco-flex 0030 and reinforced with fiberglass, the sensor maintains high sensitivity and precision. Finite element analysis is employed to optimize the encapsulation materials and dimensions. When affixed to the wrist, the sensor proves to be non-burdensome and non-irritating to the skin, effectively detecting radial artery pulses. To estimate blood pressure, reflective pulse transit time (R-PTT) is utilized. Calibration against a standard sphygmomanometer indicates a high degree of concordance between the systolic and diastolic pressures estimated from the collected signals and the actual measured values, thereby validating its reliability for cardiovascular monitoring. The findings suggest that this BP sensor offers a promising improvement in continuous, non-invasive blood pressure monitoring technology.

articleTitle: Constant Envelope Orthogonal Frequency-Division Multiplexing with Selective Mapping
abstract: Constant envelope orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (CE-OFDM) employs phase modulation, yielding an exceptionally low peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR), thus positioning it as a highly promising candidate for future wireless communications, especially in the context of wireless sensor networks (WSNs). Nonetheless, phase modulation inherently introduces phase wrapping issues, which detrimentally impact the bit error rate (BER) performance of CE-OFDM. In this paper, we introduce the selective mapping (SLM) technique to address this challenge. By selecting sequences with the minimum number of phase jumps from a finite set of candidates, the BER performance is substantially enhanced. Simulation results substantiate that the integration of SLM effectively mitigates phase wrapping in CE-OFDM, achieving significant BER improvements while preserving the constant envelope property of CE-OFDM.

Author Keywords: Constant envelope orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (CE-OFDM)

articleTitle: TSeizNet: Triplet Loss Empowered Multi-Scale CNN for Superior EEG Seizure Detection
abstract: Automated seizure detection using electroencephalography (EEG) reduces the workload for neurologists and accelerates treatment planning for epilepsy. However, this approach faces challenges due to the imbalance between seizure and non-seizure events, as well as the complexity of EEG setups. To address these issues, we propose TSeizNet, a novel multi-scale convolutional network utilizing triplet loss for EEG-based epileptic seizure detection. We evaluate TSeizNet on the CHB-MIT dataset under both full-scalp and low-density EEG settings. Experimental results show that TSeizNet achieves higher accuracy and F1-score compared to baseline methods, while maintaining acceptable sensitivity and specificity in both settings. These findings confirm the superior performance of TSeizNet and highlight the ability of low-density EEG to capture seizure-related content comparably with full-scalp EEG. This study suggests potential for future research in channel-reduced EEG for home monitoring and wearable device implementation.

articleTitle: Banana Ripeness Estimation Using a Non-Destructive Approach Composed of an Array of Multimodal Sensors and Machine Learning
abstract: Ripeness is a crucial metric in the cultivation and sale of fruits. Current techniques for determining a fruit's ripeness rely on damaging, labour-intensive methods, providing only an approximation of crop-wide ripeness. A cost-effective, non-destructive ripeness detection method could provide instantaneous and accurate ripeness data whenever required, without generating wastage. This paper proposes a methodology for the measurement and estimation of banana ripeness using an array of low-cost sensing modalities. A 5-stage classification framework is proposed to classify bananas using a number of Machine Learning algorithms such as Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, K-Nearest Neighbours, Gradient Boosting Classifiers & Artificial Neural Networks. Datasets constructed from different combinations of sensor data were used for training and testing processes. The most accurate methods were Random Forest and Gradient Boosting Classifiers at 99.95 % each when using data from all available sensors.

articleTitle: Real-Time Monitoring of CaCO3 Precipitation Using Fiber Optics Scale Sensor Under High Temperature and Pressure Conditions
abstract: Monitoring and control of mineral formations are important tasks in several industries. A novel geothermal project called “Carbon Recycle CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> Geothermal Power Generation Technology,” currently under development in Japan, is expected to promote the introduction of geothermal power generation. Although part of the injected CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> can be stored as carbonate minerals underground, the mechanism by which the minerals precipitate under high temperature and pressure conditions, such as those in geothermal reservoirs, has not been clarified and a conventional measurement method is lacking. In this study, we experimentally monitored the phenomenon of calcium carbonate precipitation at high temperatures and pressures using optical fiber sensors based on attenuated total reflection. The transmittance was observed to decrease with increasing saturation index of the carbonate minerals.

articleTitle: Ultrasensitive Tilt Sensor Using Liquid Metal
abstract: We report an innovative liquid metal-based tilt sensor which shows orders of magnitude higher sensitivity than previous tilt sensors. This simple resistive sensor is designed to have a dense array of serpentine laser-induced graphene (LIG) electrode in a racetrack shape with linewidth in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100\sim 200\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. The key aspect of this tilt sensor is non-wetting lyophobic characteristics of the LIG electrode surface against gallium based liquid metal alloy. Due to high conductivity of liquid metal, this tilt sensor provides extremely high sensitivity of 8.9 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{k}\Omega/^{\circ}$</tex> in the tilt angle between −45° and 45°.

articleTitle: Cellytics: A Digital Inline Holography Platform for Single Cell Analysis in Biomedical and Environmental Applications
abstract: In this study, we explore the application of digital inline holography (DIH) and lens-free Shadow imaging technology (LSIT) for biosensing. LSIT offers a cost-effective and rapid method for cell analysis and real-time marine pollution monitoring without complex optical equipment. LSIT provides a cost-effective, rapid method for cell analysis and real-time marine pollution monitoring without complex optical equipment, offering a broad field of view. We analyzed human blood cells using parameters of the shadow images obtained using LSIT, which revealed significant differences and clear group separations. For polymer microspheres, contour algorithms were employed, revealing distinct group characteristics. Furthermore, using machine learning techniques, LSIT effectively tracked rotifer mobility in toxic environments with high accuracy. These results illustrate the potential of LSIT in biosensing, environmental monitoring, and clinical diagnostics.

articleTitle: Deep RL Based Obstacle Avoidance for UAVs with Time Varying Sensor Bias
abstract: Advancements in Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) have shown significant promise for the development of selfdirected Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs). Our research focuses on examining the impact of time-varying noise such as that present in Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) sensors on the efficacy of DRL-based waypoint navigation and obstacle avoidance in UAVs. Sensor noise affects localization and obstacle detection, and is assumed to follow a Gaussian probability distribution with an unknown non-zero time varying mean and variance. In this study, we consider environment with static obstacles where noise exhibits a time-varying bias, a characteristic commonly associated with IMU sensors. We evaluate the effectiveness of a DRL agent, trained using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) technique, in the presence of such noise.

articleTitle: ISAR Imaging of Near-Shore Maritime Vessels using a Low-Cost X-band Radar
abstract: This study presents a demonstration of using a low-cost off-the-shelf X-band radar system for ISAR imaging of maritime vessels. The system consisted of the CN0566 kit from Analog Devices, a WR-102 horn antenna, and a computer. The radar receiver consisted of an Analog Devices CN0566 X-band dual 8 element linear array of 98 mm aperture, while the transmitter antenna was a 15 dB gain horn. The radar bandwidth was 500 MHz resulting in an ISAR image resolution of 0.3 m in range and 0.66 m in cross-range. Data was collected on two boats passing by the radar. Images were focused using simple track estimation, and the resulting images were reasonable representations of the vessel dimensions.

articleTitle: A Perceptive Soft Finger for Shape and Texture Recognition
abstract: Touch is one of the main ways in which humans interact with each other and with the physical world. The ability to perceive the shape and surface topography of objects is crucial for robots to perform tasks safely and effectively in unstructured environments. In this paper, a perceptive soft finger (PSF) capable of shape and texture recognition via seamlessly integrated mutual inductance-based bending sensing and eddy-current effect-based force sensing at a fingertip is developed. The PSF can achieve a resolution of 1.29 mN for tactile sensing at the fingertip and 0.032° for bending angle sensing at the root. The experimental results show that the PSF can recognize small bumps that vary in size and height, as well as ridges with different shapes and pitches. Moreover, it has been demonstrated that the PSF can also reconstruct the 3D shape of a mouse by sliding on its top surface along different directions.

articleTitle: All-sky Near-infrared Star Identification
abstract: The atmospheric background light and the aerodynamic environment are the main challenges for star sensors utilizing visible light, which may cause missing stars or false stars. Additionally, high-speed maneuvering may result in star trailing, which reduces the accuracy of the star position. To address the issues above, an all-sky near-infrared (NIR) star identification method is proposed to handle position noise, false stars, and missing stars. Different from existing methods based on visible light, the proposed method employs NIR star angular distance to generate indexing, which is applied to build a database. The attitude is calculated and frequency is counted to match. In this work, the proposed method is validated in simulation. Compared with the state-of-the-art, the identification rate is improved by 6%-59.9%, and the solving time is reduced by 13.7%-89.5% under different disturbing.

articleTitle: Perfume Reproduction Analysis with Robustness Against Interference Using Improved NMF in Mass Spectrum Space
abstract: Performing odor reproduction analysis using commercially available odor samples such as perfumes is often compromised by the presence of odorless compounds called fixatives. It can lead to discrepancies when analyzing odors using instruments and human noses. Previously, we successfully separated the interference of fixatives in perfume samples in numerical analysis. In this study, we introduce an innovative method for odor reproduction analysis together with interference separation using the Nonnegative Matrix Factorization (NMF) technique with a predefined fixative matrix as a set of fixed basis vectors. We performed odor reproduction analysis using mass spectrometry (MS) data of 149 perfumes with proposed NMF. Here, the sensory test reveals our NMF method's capability to eliminate interference from odor reproduction in actual samples. Our study offers a new method for odor reproduction analysis amid the presence of interferences.

articleTitle: Advanced Integration of 3D Optomechanical Sensor Microsystems with Optical Fibers
abstract: The ever-increasing demand for affordable, compact, and integrated sensors necessitates innovations that outperform traditional, bulkier counterparts. This paper introduces an advanced integration of 3D optomechanical sensor microsystems with optical fibers, using a two-photon nanomachining process. This technique enables the fabrication of complex 3D structures, including dynamic and movable features, unattainable through conventional photolithography. We present sensor microsystems incorporating resonant and non-resonant cavities, demonstrating exceptional sensitivity and operational range. The resonant microsensors offer heightened sensitivity to environmental conditions, while the non-resonant counterparts use rotating reflective microblades for precise flow sensing. Utilizing optical fiber as the substrate, these sensors transmit detected information in real-time to remote locations with minimal loss, eliminating the need for additional packaging, amplifiers, signal processing, and data transmission components. This innovative integration promises a new generation of highly sensitive, compact, and versatile sensor systems, ideal for contemporary engineering applications.

articleTitle: A Closed-Loop Control System with Ultrafast Monitoring Based on a Photoelectric Sensor
abstract: Quantum information science using atomic, molecular, and optical systems relies on lasers to enable precise control of quantum states through light-matter interactions. However, laser intensity fluctuations can reduce fidelity of quantum operations. To address this issue, we develop a closed-loop system based on a photoelectric sensor for real-time monitoring and stabilization of laser intensity. The system uses a photoelectric sensor to detect the laser power and samples the photovoltage signal through an analog-to-digital converter. Communication and signal processing are implemented using FPGA. We use gigabit Ethernet technology to transmit data at a high speed to the host computer, enabling real-time display of the photovoltage signal in both the time and frequency domains. Additionally, the system can control the laser power in real-time to suppress laser intensity fluctuations. Our design is highly versatile and independent of lasers wavelength, and suitable for a variety of quantum information platforms. Experimental test results show that this system can significantly improve the stability and reliability of the lasers, facilitating various quantum information applications.

articleTitle: Channel Assessment for a Sensor System for Status Detection of Miniature Circuit Breakers
abstract: Status detection of miniature circuit breakers (MCBs) commonly requires side-coupled accessories using up valuable cabinet space. In space-restricted environments, breaker status detection using an AC test signal could be a promising alternative, but the highly varying electrical network would need to be used for signal transmission. In this study, the feasibility of relying on the electrical network as a transmission channel for an MCB status detection system is assessed across a frequency range of 0.1-100 MHz. Using simulations and measurements, the effects of different cable lengths, cable topologies and loads are investigated. Broad-and narrowband signal attenuations are observed, which for simple cable setups can be attributed to individual cable lengths and loads. For more complex cable topologies, typical for electrical installations in practice, the spectral location of these problematic signal attenuations cannot be predicted.

articleTitle: Smooth Speed Control for an Autonomous Vehicle and On-Road Verification
abstract: Current speed control systems in autonomous vehicles often lack the nuanced responsiveness of human drivers, resulting in abrupt deceleration or acceleration when encountering obstacles or hazardous situations, which can negatively impact both safety and ride comfort. To address this issue, this paper applies the quadratic programming approach for design of smooth speed control for an autonomous vehicle and on-road verification. The LiDAR SLAM is utilized for creating precise road maps, integrating it with a front of camera and YOLO network for obstacle detection. Next, the Pure Pursuit algorithm generates a reference steering angle based on planned route, obstacle positions, and vehicle data. Quadratic programming with hard constraints is then applied to estimate optimal smooth speed, guiding throttle and brake control. Integration of these components is achieved through the robot operating system (ROS) and Autoware, validated on a commercially available vehicle. The experiment results demonstrate an 81% improvement in ride comfort over traditional cruise control, meeting ISO-2631-1 standards, and significantly enhancing safety and comfort in autonomous driving.

articleTitle: UV Irradiated MoO3 thin film for Sensing of Dibutyl Sulfide: A Mustard Gas Simulant
abstract: A chemiresistive sensor with a UV-activated reactively sputtered MoO3 as the sensing layer has been explored for the sensing of dibutyl sulfide (DBS), a simulant of the chemical warfare agent (CWA) mustard gas. The sensor showed a maximum response of 15.15% towards 10 ppm DBS at 100°C with quick response time (18 s) and recovery time (34 s) in the presence of UV light. The developed sensor was also found to be selective to DBS and has the potential for the development of portable, low-cost sensors for mustard gas.

articleTitle: Sensing-Oriented ISAC with OTFS: Effective IRCI-free Target Range Reconstruction
abstract: Considering the potential of orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) signal in the development of integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) technology, the inter-range-cell interference (IRCI)-free range reconstruction method is re-designed to accommodate OTFS customization. Both single symbol's pulse compression and coherent pulse integration across the entire OTFS symbols are designed and executed for performance maximization. Subsequently, performance analysis regarding signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) function with respect to signal parameters is presented to readily give a benchmark for subsequent simulations and demonstrating a flexibility gain compared to the state-of-the-art. Finally, simulation results, including range reconstruction and comparisons with mainstream algorithms, highlight the effectiveness of the proposed schemes.

articleTitle: A Multi-Directional Pendulum-Based Energy Harvester for Self-Powered and Distributed Ocean Environment Monitoring
abstract: Ocean environment monitoring is essential to timely assess marine conditions and climate change, as well as promote the exploration of marine resources. However, the distributed ocean monitoring systems still face challenges in energy autonomy, as most of the systems are widely distributed and powered by batteries. To address the challenges of sustainable energy supply in distributed ocean environment monitoring systems, this paper proposes a multi-directional pendulum-based energy harvester to effectively harness low-frequency random ocean wave energy. This harvester consists of a fixed iron ball, a moving magnetic ball tethered by the fixed iron ball, and a multi-coil array to realize multi-directional harvesting of ocean wave energy. The fixed iron-ball and rolling magnetic ball configuration allows the magnetic ball rolling freely on the surface of the shell, avoiding complexity of using universal-joints. The developed energy harvesting device generates approximately 4.18 mW across a 220 Ω load under single-axis sinusoidal excitation at 3 Hz and 0.7 g. Under dual-axis excitation, it can charge a power management module with an 800 μF storage capacitor to 3.8 V within 60 seconds. This study provides a potential solution for the self-powered operation of distributed monitoring nodes in the Internet of Ocean Things.

articleTitle: Helios, a Contactless Optical Sensor for the Assessment of Transmission Line Conductors Peripheral Solar Absorptivity
abstract: Helios is the very first sensor to enable contactless assessment of peripheral solar absorptivity of transmission line conductors. This value, that typically ranges from 0.45 to 0.95 is ill documented in the literature so conservative assumptions are taken. Following in-lab measurements on 3D printed and field samples, and ray tracing simulations, a motorized prototype allowed the first ever reported field measurements of Aluminum Conductors Steel Reinforced (ACSRs) absorptivity. These measurements highlighted inherent variations around the perimeter of the conductors. Such sensor and associated knowledge are instrumental in supporting power utilities in enhancing transmission line capacity during warm summer months, while maintaining proper ground clearances.

articleTitle: Efficient Colorimetric Membrane pH Sensor Based on Electrospun PCL/PVP Immobilized with Anthocyanin Extract for Intelligent Food Packaging
abstract: The application of colorimetric pH sensors in intelligent food packaging has gained much attention in recent years. However, although the wettability of the sensor substrates influences the sensor performance, it has rarely been investigated. In this work, we utilize both hydrophobic and hydrophilic polymers as a matrix where anthocyanins are immobilized to fabricate colorimetric membrane pH sensors. In this manner, the wettability of the membrane sensor could be precisely controlled by adjusting the ratio of hydrophobic to hydrophilic polymers in the matrix. The effect of wettability on the pH-sensing performance, such as sensitivity and response rate, was investigated. In addition, the current membrane sensors provide excellent stability in extremely humid environments.

articleTitle: A Study of Low Power Infrared Sensor Using Ground Truth for Presence Detection Applications
abstract: In the era of Internet of Things (IoT) and smart home devices, there is a rise in demand for reliable, nonintrusive, low-cost, and low-power human occupancy sensing solutions. While traditional motion-based standards such as NEMA WD 7-2011 and IEC 63180:2020 test primarily motion based pyroelectric infrared (PIR) sensor systems, new human occupancy solutions based on infrared sensing technologies such as STMicroelectronics' STHS34PF80 require novel validation methods to evaluate precise benchmarking in static and dynamic scenarios. In this paper, we propose using the OptiTrack motion-capture system as a Ground Truth Reference System (GTRS) to benchmark the STHS34PF80's human presence detection beyond motion-centric standards and enabling in-depth analysis of sensing performance.

articleTitle: Visual and Inertial Sensor Fusion Approach for Visual Inertial Odometry Used in Vehicle Localization
abstract: Ego vehicle motion estimation is crucial for automotive navigation systems even in challenging environments where Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) based localization systems fail. This study explores Visual Inertial Odometry (VIO), which combines visual information from cameras with Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) data for precise motion estimation. Initially, our approach focuses on a conventional Visual Odometry (VO) pipeline and utilizes Epipolar and Perspective-n-Points for motion estimation along with a selection strategy. Our second approach implements VIO with Adaptive Extended Kalman filter to incorporate imu data with a newly added update rule, enhancing the overall accuracy by effectively utilizing the vehicle's longitudinal velocity. Our approaches are evaluated on the KITTI dataset, both demonstrating superior performance, but VIO shows a reduction in translation error by 92.66% and rotational error by 97.79<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, achieving better results compared to VO alone.

articleTitle: Compact Room Temperature-Operated Sensing System for Methanol and Ethanol Mixture Separation and Quantification
abstract: For practical olfactory sensing with a safe and low-power system, it is important to be able to operate easily at room temperature. However, this has not been a trivial task to achieve with existing conventional gas separation and sensing devices. In this study, a novel compact room temperature-operated sensing system is proposed to separate and quantify each component in a vapor mixture with simple operation. The sensing system consists of a portable and replaceable gas separation column and a sensing module containing a nanomechanical Membrane-type Surface stress Sensor, MSS. Proton transfer reaction time-of-flight mass spectrometry (PTR-TOF-MS) results show that the gas separation column can clearly separate methanol and ethanol in their mixtures. The sensing signals from the column-MSS system are consistent with the peaks measured by PTR-TOF-MS. For mixtures of methanol and ethanol with various ratios, a clear correspondence is observed between the output signals and the theoretically calculated vapor pressure ratios of each mixture. The developed compact room temperature-operated sensing system can discriminate and quantify different methanol and ethanol mixtures, paving the way for practical applications of olfactory sensing devices.

articleTitle: Unleashing Dynamic Range and Resolution in Unlimited Sensing Framework via Novel Hardware
abstract: Conventional digitization based on the Shannon-Nyquist method, implemented via analog-to-digital converters (ADCs), faces fundamental limitations. High-dynamic-range (HDR) signals often get clipped or saturated in practice. Given a fixed bit budget, one must choose between minimizing quantization noise or accommodating HDR inputs. The Unlimited Sensing Framework (USF) eliminates saturation by incorporating nonlinear folding in analog hardware, resulting in modulo signals. Quantizing or digitizing modulo signals enables low quantization noise as the modulo representation maps HDR signals into low-dynamic-range (LDR) samples. In the context of USF, the core innovation of this paper is a novel, low-cost, integrator-based efficient modulo ADC hardware implementation that imposes no restrictions on folding rates, enabling significantly HDR capture. The feasibility of this design is demonstrated by hardware experiments showcasing clear advantages across different quantitative performance metrics. These include capturing HDR signals with a 60-fold increase in dynamic range, achieving up to 5 Effective Number of Bits (ENOBs), and improving Signal-to-Noise and Distortion (SINAD) by 30 dB.

articleTitle: Zirconia-based Electrochemical Sensor Utilizing Au-based Electrodes for Rapid Hydrogen Detection
abstract: The explosive nature of hydrogen <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{H}_{2})$</tex> demands a sensing device that is not only sensitive and selective to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> but also capable of providing a very rapid response to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex>. This paper describes the development of a high performance electrochemical <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> sensor consisting of yttria-stabilized zirconia (YSZ) as a solid electrolyte and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Au}+\text{YSZ}$</tex> as a sensing electrode as well as Au as a counter electrode examined as potentiometric- and amperometric-type sensor. Under potentiometric mode, the sensor generated a highly sensitive and selective response to 200 ppm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> in air at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$550^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> with a 90% response time of 8 s • Meanwhile, under the amperometric pulse-potential mode, the developed sensor could generate a relatively sensitive and selective response to 200 ppm <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> in air with a significantly faster response time (< 0.002 s) under the same operating conditions. Different sensing mode evidently affected <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> selectivity and response time, where large discrepancies in response time suggest significant differences in reaction speed toward <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{H}_{2}$</tex> under different sensing mode.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Wearable Olfactory Interface for Locating Odor Source
abstract: We developed a human-machine collaborative experiment to localize sources of odor using the Wearable Olfactory Interface (WOI) system. This system aids human participants in tracing faint odor trails by translating detected odors into discernible vibrational cues on a wearable device. The experiment employed a 5% ethanol solution as the target odorant, which remains undetectable to the human olfactory senses. Eighteen participants were involved in a two-factor experimental design, incorporating three levels of tactile stimulus intensity and three angular positions. We collected and analyzed 90 data samples using a confusion matrix for multi-class classification, achieving an overall source localization accuracy of 54.44%. The findings indicate that the WOI system enhances the ability of participants to track airborne odor plumes by enabling them to perceive subtle spatial variations in odor concentration through vibrational cues at the waist.

articleTitle: Homo-Thermocouple Fabricated by Selective Laser Sintering and Melting of Semiconductor Nanoparticles
abstract: Selective laser sintering of micro and nanoparticles has become a prominent additive manufacturing technology for making engineered components and conformal circuits. The sintering and melting behaviors of polymer, metal, and ceramic powders in this context have been thoroughly studied. Compared to metals or insulating ceramics, semiconductor grains present more complexity due to grain coarsening, elemental diffusion, and seepage effects under photovoltaic and photothermal influences. These factors offer a broad spectrum of opportunities for property modification. Nevertheless, there is an existing research gap in the area of laser sintering of semiconductor nanoparticles. In this research, In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films were produced using varying sintering and melting regimes by adjusting the laser energy density and preheating temperature. The findings revealed that the In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, when in the melting regime, demonstrated significantly low carrier concentration and high carrier mobility due to adequate grain coarsening and weakened grain boundaries. Utilizing this unique melting regime, In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> homo-thermocouples with high Seebeck coefficients, reaching <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{133.7} \boldsymbol{\mu} \mathbf{V}/\mathbf{K}$</tex>, were developed. This was achieved by managing the extent of sintering/melting of the branched paths instead of altering the materials.

articleTitle: A MEMS Gravimeter with Buckling-Beam Nonlinear Springs for Enhanced Sensitivity and Dynamic Range
abstract: Accurate measurement of variations in local gravitational acceleration is crucial for geophysical research, natural hazard forecasting, and resource exploration. However, existing gravimeters are expensive, heavy, large, and power-hungry, motivating research on gravimeters based on micro-electromechanical systems. This paper introduces a buckling-based nonlinear spring mechanism. Through proper structural design, the buckling of two beams results in a significant reduction of the effective stiffness of the structure and, hence, improving sensitivity under the desired load. A prototype device was designed to demonstrate the working principle. The design demonstrated a remarkable drop in resonant frequency from ~110Hz to 30Hz in simulations, corresponding to a ~13×increase in sensitivity. On the other hand, the buckling of the support beams occurs gradually over a wide range of input forces, allowing the device to simultaneously achieve a high dynamic range. The designed prototype was fabricated through standard microfabrication processes and characterized. The device utilized an on-chip optical interferometer between an optical fiber and the proof mass sidewall to monitor displacements of proofmass due to input accelerations. The optical displacement sensitivity was 0.6 mV/nm with a displacement noise floor of 40 pm/√Hz at 2 Hz, The gravimeter demonstrated a sensitivity of 23,4 V/g and a dynamic range of 276 mg(1g ≈ 9,81 m/s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>).

articleTitle: Non-Invasive Real-Time Monitoring of Blood Lactate Using a Low-Power Microwave Sensor
abstract: This article presents the advancement of a low-power microwave sensor for real-time and non-invasive monitoring of blood lactate, an important biological marker in sports, clinical and agrifood settings. The sensor is presented in a proof of concept wearable form-factor, and is shown to provide adequate performance (0.6721 mmol/L 95% mean error). The sensor is currently able to provide a lactate measurement every 10s. Unlike sweat-based sensors, the microwave sensor exhibits no measurement latency. Further, the sensor eliminates single-use waste resulting from current commercial devices.

articleTitle: Single-Step 3D Printing of Flexible Ferroelectret Sensors with Large Air Cavities
abstract: Flexible sensors based on ferroelectrets can utilize the full potential of the widely adopted 3D printing process, capitalizing on its accessibility, freedom of design, and range of materials. However, 3D printing faces limitations in accuracy and poor surface quality for small dimensions, particularly constraining the ability to manufacture precise ferroelectrets as mechanical sensors that require complex structures with well-defined air cavities. In this work, we explore the printing process to overcome these limitations and present a complex structure printed in a single step with a large air cavity and adaptable surface quality. We present a complex structure printed in a single step with a large air cavity, while ensuring mechanical stability of the structure and its piezoelectric sensitivity as a ferroelectret sensor. We print two sample groups out of polypropylene with reduced material extrusion and demonstrate surfaces without defects and low surface roughness, measuring down to 4.9 µm. Mechanical tests reveal regions with linear bending stiffness of 0.48 N/mm for loads below 0.11 N and 2.47 N/mm for loads ranging from 0.17 N to 0.28 N, respectively. Treated as a ferroelectret sensor, the samples achieve a sensitivity of up to 5.71 nC/N, well within the range of comparable ferroelectrets. The ferroelectret sensor elements presented are well-suited for 3D printing sensor arrays, particularly in applications such as tactile interfaces, i.e. requiring measurements of small forces across large areas.

articleTitle: Loaded Re-Entrant Cavity Microwave Sensor for Dielectric Constant Measurement
abstract: This paper presents a novel microwave sensor combining a planar sensor with a 3D re-entrant cavity structure for measuring the permittivity of materials. The sensor is based on a re-entrant cavity loaded with a complementary split-ring resonator (CSRR). The proposed structure enhances electric field concentration at the top of cavity and excites the CSRR on the top layer. This configuration effectively couples the internal electric field of the re-entrant cavity through the CSRR and facilitates high-intensity electric fields outside the cavity for sensing material properties. The design leverages the low-loss characteristics of the cavity and provides the non-intrusive measurement advantages of the CSRR. Moreover, sensitivity for relative dielectric constants in the range of 2-10 is improved by 77.6% compared to the structure with top-open design.

articleTitle: Characterization of Damping and Stiffness Mismatch on a Dual Foucault Pendulum Structure Manufactured in 30-μm-Thick Epitaxial Polysilicon
abstract: This work presents the first characterization results in terms of aniso-damping and aniso-stiffness of Dual Foucault Pendulum (DFP) structures fabricated in a mass-market MEMS process, to be used as angle sensors. Devices are designed within (3.5 mm)2 and feature linear electrostatic driving and sensing combs, along with linear-tuning tapered combs. The modes are set at 29 kHz, with quality factors in the range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3\cdot 10^{5}$</tex>. Measured aniso-damping is in the 1.5% range, while aniso-stiffness causes <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 45$</tex> Hz mismatch dispersion. This value can be fully compensated by the tapered combs, to mode-match the modes within few ppm.

articleTitle: A Quantitative Microfluidic Flow Cytometer Based on Spaced Uniform Optical Fields
abstract: This study presented a quantitative microfluidic flow cytometer based on spaced uniform optical fields, which were constructed by adopting optical paths of conventional microscopy. Single cells with stained fluorescent probes travel through three uniform optical spots sequentially and leveraging calibration solutions under uniform excitation, nine types of proteins with arbitrary distributions at the single-cell level can be quantified. Characterization of the spaced uniform optical fields was conducted with corresponding geometrical parameters and uniform distributions confirmed. Based on this approach, calibration curves of nine-fluorescence channels were linearly correlated with the best detection limit of 10 molecule per cell at PE channel. Five-channel fluorescent signals of rainbow calibration microbeads were sampled by this platform and based on quantitative results these microbeads were classified into six subtypes. The developed microfluidic flow cytometry may provide a new perspective in the field of quantitative single-cell protein analysis.

articleTitle: An Individually Addressable Microneedle Array for Continuous Real-Time Monitoring of Glucose in Interstitial Fluid
abstract: Microneedle technology provides a minimally invasive, convenient and continuously monitorable way of glucose monitoring for diabetes management. As blood glucose monitoring needs to accommodate long-term and complex environment during daily activities, it brings multiple risks to sensor's continuous monitoring. In order to enhance the accuracy and stability of microneedle array sensors, this paper proposes a glucose sensor based on a flexible split-integrated microneedle array. We set up separate conduction pathways for different glucose sensitive microneedle electrodes, by means of one-to-one flexible monitoring circuit system achieving individual addressing and data processing of glucose microneedle electrodes. Multiple groups of data could be transmitted in real time by Bluetooth and proceed with data optimization and selection discarding problematic data to improve the accuracy and service life of sensors. The experimental results show that individually addressable microneedle array can improve the detection performance of the glucose sensor to some extent, the average absolute relative error is lower than 10%, and the microneedle array sensor remains stable within three weeks.

articleTitle: Stretchable Pulse Wave Sensor with a Laser-Induced Graphene-Formed Kirigami Structure
abstract: This paper reports on a stretchable laserinduced graphene (LIG) pulse-wave sensor based on a kirigami structure. The proposed sensor is fabricated by embedding a stretchable sensor element using the kirigami structure into an elastic material. The polyimide-based sensor element is formed by UV and CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> laser irradiation, and the stretchable LIG strain gauges detect skin vibrations caused by pulse waves with high sensitivity. The proposed sensor could be stretched by up to 7.5 mm, and the sensitivity increased 27 times in the stretched state. Furthermore, the fabricated sensor was able to measure the pulse waves. Therefore, the proposed sensor shows potential as a stretchable wearable sensor for measuring pulse waves with high sensitivity.

articleTitle: EmoHEAL: A Fusion-Based Framework for Emotion Recognition Using Wearable Sensors
abstract: Wearable sensor technology emerges significantly in sensing physiological data for real-time health monitoring, showing promise for early disease detection by continuously monitoring vital signs like body temperature, heart rate, and electrodermal activity. However, current emotion recognition methods are limited by high measurement noise in wearable health sensors, negatively impacting performance. Additionally, most classification models are too complex to be deployed on IoT devices for real-time performance. This paper presents EmoHeal<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup><sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>https://github.com/Oh-yk/EmoHEAL, a lightweight deep learning-based fusion architecture to process wrist sensor-based physiological sensor data for IoT devices. EmoHeal integrates data augmentation, attention mechanisms, Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCNs), and Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) for robust emotion classification. Each sensor's data is processed through a separate TCN block that extracts temporal features using dilated convolutions. These blocks are enhanced by channel and spatial attention mechanisms to emphasize significant features. The extracted features are then fused and fed into a bidirectional GRU, which captures long-term dependencies in the wrist sensor data. EmoHeal demonstrated excellent performance on the K-EmoCon dataset, achieving a mean accuracy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\approx 72\%$</tex> arousal for an edge-deployable emotion recognition model, surpassing state-of-the-art models. This research significantly benefits real-time mobile health sensing in Internet of Things (IoT) applications.

articleTitle: Design of Microfluidic Refractive Index Sensor Based on Phase Shift Grating
abstract: A optical fiber refractive index sensor based on phase shift grating is proposed and tested. In principle, the periodic linear relationship between the peak wavelength of the PS-FBG phase shift and the refractive index of the liquid in the gap is used to measure the refractive index of the liquid. The sensor is composed of two parts, the sensing module is cut off by the ordinary Bragg fiber grating in the center of the grid area, and then fixed with a ceramic ferrule. The microfluidic injection module used microfluidic chip technology. Assisted by temperature calibration work finished, the refractive index of a sensor measuring range more than 1.3330~1.3650, the sensitivity of 5.4 nm/RIU. The phase-shift grating refractive index sensor can be applied to real-time monitoring directions such as alcohol concentration measurement in industrial production.

articleTitle: A Binary Frequency Shift Keying Chipless RFID IoT Switch
abstract: This article introduces a Binary Frequency Shift Keying Chipless RFID IoT Switch (BFSK-CIS) as a low-cost and battery-less solution for a relocatable and reprogrammable solution. In this work, the information about the switch's status is encoded as a frequency shift in the frequency spectrum, eliminating the need for reference resonators necessary in the previous amplitude modulation-based approach. The implementation of the BFSK-CIS tag involves using a single-pole-double-throw (SPDT) switch placed between a transmission line and two spiral resonators (each has a unique resonant frequency). Depending on the switch's status, one of the resonators is coupled to the transmission line, thus shifting the resonant frequency of the tag. The BFSK-CIS is passive and designed using commercially available components and a standard PCB fabrication process. Measurement results show the BFSK-CIS tag toggles between two resonant frequencies (i.e.,1.2 and 1.23 GHz) depending on the status of the SPDT switch.

articleTitle: Mode Localized Piezoelectric Resonator Design and Implementation for Electrical Current Sensing
abstract: This study presents a piezoelectric MEMS resonant type current sensor developed through an in-house process. Leveraging the mode localization phenomenon in a weakly coupled system, we use the eigenstate rather than the eigenvalue as the output metric, which offers higher sensitivity. Using Joule heating as a sensing mechanism provides the advantage of a square term relationship between heating efficiency and sensing current, resulting in a larger output difference under the same current increase compared to a linear sensor. In open loop measurements with a 20Ω. sensing resistor, the changes in amplitude ratio (AR) for mode 1 and mode 2, when calibrated, exhibit coefficients of -11.015 and 6.373, respectively, corresponding to the square of the input current. Additionally, using AR as the output metric yields a 65 times enhancement of the calibrated index compared to frequency shift-based sensors under a 50mA input current. This work successfully verifies that employing mode localization together with Joule heating as a sensing mechanism is feasible for detecting electrical signals. This technique holds great potential for future applications.

articleTitle: Detection of Out-of-Plane Waviness in Carbon-Fibre Reinforced Plastics - Comparing different Non-Destructive Evaluation Modalities
abstract: The detection of fibre wrinkles (out-of-plane waviness) is investigated using Eddy Current (ECT), Ultrasonic Testing (UT) and X-ray and is compared on 9 Carbon Fibre Reinforced Plastic (CFRP) samples with varying wrinkle heights. All three Non-Destructive Evaluation (NDE) modalities demonstrated detection capabilities for wrinkle heights 0.13 - 1.31 mm, with UT being able to map the interior structure of the composite material, which was further used to measure the distortion of plies caused due to the presence of wrinkles using an image processing technique.

articleTitle: Riding Skill Visualizing System for Motorcycle Using Multiple Zigbee Communication Line
abstract: In this study, we report developing a wireless visual system that is the operating force exerted by a rider on the motorcycle and the state of the motorcycle. To detect the amount of operation by the rider and the state of the motorcycle, the number of sensors installed on the motorcycle was 27 and the sampling frequency was 100 Hz. In the system, we used wireless communication modules that conform to the Zigbee standard and communicated using four pairs of wireless communication modules to ensure sufficient communication speed. Experimental results, the system has a performance of a throughput was over 49.6kbps, and it is able to visualize the status of the motorcycle on a monitor.

articleTitle: A Mode-Localized DC Electric Field Microsensor with 0.4 V/ m Resolution
abstract: This paper reports a high-resolution DC electric field microsensor based on mode localization of three weakly coupled resonators (WCRs). We propose an innovative electric field input structure capable of generating a larger electrostatic negative stiffness to the WCRs. Consequently, this results in a larger amplitude ratio output from the WCRs. Furthermore, a theoretical analysis reveals that the square root of the amplitude ratio corresponds proportionally to the measured electric field. The device was fabricated and tested. The results show that the sensitivity is 36.235 ppm/(V /m), which is 2013 times greater than that based on mode frequency (0.018 ppm/(V 1m).
