The resolution is 0.4 V/m, roughly two orders of magnitude higher compared to that of the reported microsensors based on field mill principle and mode localization.

articleTitle: A Dual Input Five Output Solar Energy Harvester with 93.46% Peak Efficiency for Heterogeneous Wireless Sensor Node Applications
abstract: A Single Inductor Dual Input Five Output (SIDIFO) energy harvesting system is introduced in this work for heterogeneous WSN-based applications. The proposed system harvests energy from solar cell and drives multiple loads of 1.8 V, 1.2 V, 1.0 V, and 0.8 V. The surplus energy after driving the loads is stored in a battery backup with a battery or a super-capacitor. In a situation of less harvested energy, the pre-harvested energy is reused to handle the needs of the multiple loads. The proposed system performs all these tasks without hampering the MPPT process of the input source. The novel switching technique employed helps in removing one nMOS Low Side (LS) switch which is typically mandatory in such systems. Low power consumption is achieved by the usage of the shared comparator for load regulation due to the optimal clocking techniques proposed. The complete system is implemented in a standard 180 nm CMOS technology and it consumes 1.2 μW of quiescent power. The simulation results exhibit 93.46% of peak efficiency with less than 4% of worst-case ripple.

articleTitle: Effective Compensation of the Piezo-Hall Effect in CMOS-integrated 3D Hall Sensors
abstract: A highly effective method based on half-blind calibration is demonstrated for the dynamic compensation of the mechanical stress cross-sensitivity of a CMOS-integrated 3D Hall sensor system caused by the piezo-Hall effect. The system combines a Hall plate with two orthogonal vertical Hall sensors. For the first time, the use of dedicated stress sensors is avoided by exploiting a piezoresistive signal from the Hall plate. The combination of this signal with the output signals of the three Hall sensors in respective polynomial sensor response models allows to infer the three corresponding magnetic induction components largely cleared of the piezo-Hall effect due to an in-plane uniaxial normal stress. Model parameters are extracted at 25°C by simultaneously applying stress between 0 MPa and -90 MPa and 3D magnetic inductions up to 30 mT. As a result, the residual angular resolution of the system is reduced from about 4° to below 0.10 in the investigated stress range.

articleTitle: Pheromone Receptor-Based Olfactory Sensors Using Resonant Diamond Membranes
abstract: In this work, we present a fabrication technology and characterization of a diamond membrane-based sensor targeted for pheromone detection. Circular membrane with diameter of 850 μm and thickness of diamond in the range of 3566 nm to 4964 nm were successfully fabricated with integrated piezoresistive gauges for embedded electrical measurement. Calculation and simulation results aligned closely with experimental results of membrane resonance frequency. Values of resonance frequency in the air and in DI were measured to be 153.5 kHz - 254.0 kHz and 34.4 kHz - 65.3 kHz, respectively. Our ultimate goal is to functionalize this mechanical transducer with pheromone receptors in order to detect traces of pheromones and thus specific pest insects in the field through resonance frequency readout.

articleTitle: Rapid and Field Portable Water Quality Monitoring Using Lens-Free Shadow Imaging Technology and Machine Learning
abstract: Over the past few decades, advancements in industry and technology have increased the registration and distribution of new chemicals, posing substantial risks to ecosystems and human health. Traditional chemical analysis methods are insufficient for rapid and accurate water quality assessment. This study introduces Cellytics, an innovative image processing-based machine learning platform for rapid water quality assessment. By combining lens-free shadow imaging technology (LSIT) with YOLOv9 and ResNET-50 algorithms to track and classify Brachionus plicatilis (a standard test species for marine water quality), Cellytics significantly improved analysis time and accuracy compared to traditional methods. Cellytics demonstrated significant improvements over conventional methods, reducing analysis time from 24 h to 10 min while maintaining high accuracy. Object tracking achieved a mean average precision (mAP) of 0.934 with precision and recall rates of 92.5% and 94.1%, respectively. However, due to the limited dataset, the accuracy of classifying rotifer movement paths was 76%, highlighting the need for larger datasets to prevent underfitting. This study highlights the potential of Cellytics to revolutionize water pollution evaluation, offering a swift, precise, and cost-effective tool for environmental conservation and ecosystem sustainability. Further development of this platform could enable rapid pollution detection, significantly contributing to environmental conservation and ecosystem sustainability.

articleTitle: Multiarray Gas Sensors Based on Nanoporous Layers Produced à la carte by Spark Ablation Using Metal Oxides, Binary and Ternary Alloys
abstract: Chemiresistive gas sensing layers were produced by the generation of nanomaterials by spark ablation technique and subsequently deposition by inertial impaction. Spark ablation is a dry-nanomaterial fabrication approach that allows to mix multiple materials in an aerosol, and deposit them as nanoporous layers (NPL) on sensor structures. This highly flexible technology was employed to realize gas sensor multiarray based on pure metal oxides (MOx) layers (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SnO}_{2}$</tex> and NiO), binary alloys (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SnO}_{2}-\text{Ag}$</tex>, NiO-Ag, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SnO}_{2}-\text{NiO}$</tex>), and a ternary alloy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{SnO}_{2}-\text{NiO}-\text{Ag})$</tex>. The multi sensor array was used to detect the toxic gas formaldehyde in a concentration range from 0.1 ppm up to 10 ppm. The unique versatility of the spark ablation technology to deposit different sensing layers on multiarray sensor configurations, enables a very efficient engineering of the NPL. Key figures of merits like responsivity and dynamic range can be controlled by the NPL composition. For instance, the addition of the Ag catalyst to the pure MOx drastically increased the response to formaldehyde for 0.1 ppm concentration, for higher concentration of 10 ppm the response saturates. The ternary alloy has a lower response in the whole concentration range but exhibits no response saturation. While the present work is focused on the response and detectable range towards formaldehyde molecules, the spark ablation technique can be extended to a variety of other materials and target molecules. Therefore, this work is setting a highly promising basis for development of the next-generation chemiresistive sensor devices based on nanostructured materials.

articleTitle: Controllable Starching Treatment for High-Performance Strain Sensors and EMG Electrodes in Smart Garments
abstract: This study introduces a novel pretreatment strategy using starching agent to control ink-textile interactions for smart garments with integrated textile-based sensors. By modulating ink penetration, we tailored the functionality of printed conductive patterns, achieving significant improvements in their sensing performance. Sodium carboxymethyl cellulose was found to enhance strain sensitivity and flexibility, suitable for precise health monitoring applications. In contrast, ethyl cellulose provided moderate responsiveness, and polyurethane acrylate offered high durability under mechanical stress. In addition, starching with ethyl cellulose reduce the skin-electrode impedance of printed double-sided textile electredes. The application of these techniques was demonstrated through the integration of a printed wrist pulse sensor and EMG electrodes into a smart garment, showing enhanced performance for both cardiovascular monitoring and motion detection.

articleTitle: A Normative Way to Implement ISO/IEC 23005 Between Olfactory Capturing and Displaying Device Applicable to Bio-Digital Convergence Technology
abstract: This paper proposes a practical design how to implement olfactory capturing device in compliance with the standard ISO/lEC 23005 and data transferred to an olfactory displaying device applicable to bio-digital convergence technology.

articleTitle: Quantum Sensing of Phonons and Nuclear Spins in an Electromechanical Resonator
abstract: Here, the quantum sensing of phonons in an elec-tromechanical resonator and its application to detect nuclear spins is discussed. A quantum dot defined in semiconductor heterostructures is highly sensitive to changes in its surrounding electric field environment. Using quantum dots as sensors for the piezoelectric field associated with the mechanical motion of the resonator, thermal phonon states at millikelvin temperatures, corresponding to a mechanical amplitude at the level of a femtometer, were detected. Next, the detection of nuclear spins using an electromechanical resonator is discussed. When mechanical oscillations were strongly excited while measuring the nuclear magnetic resonance of nuclear spins contained in the resonator, a blue shift in the nuclear magnetic resonance frequency with increasing mechanical amplitude was observed. This blue shift can be accounted for by the strain-mediated quadrupole interaction between the electromechanical phonons and the nuclear spins. Based on this discovery, a new scheme to detect nuclear spins using an electromechanical resonator is proposed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Vibration Energy Harvester with Replaceable Ortho-planar Springs
abstract: This paper proposes and investigates a novel electro-magnetic vibration energy harvester using ortho-planar springs. Addressing the limited output power of previously reported designs, the proposed harvester targets milliwatt level power outputs to be relevant for practical sensing and IoT applications. The proposed design employs an optimized pickup unit with Halbach array configuration and an optimized ortho-planar spring, which are integrated in a 3D-printed housing. During experimental evaluations, the harvester demonstrates an output power of up to 5.26mW and a normalized power density of 133.05 µW/(cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>*g<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>), exceeding the performance of previously reported harvesters with ortho-planar springs. Moreover, exploiting the versatility of ortho-planar spring designs, it is shown that the harvester's frequency response can easily be adjusted to different application conditions.

articleTitle: Onion Spoilage Detection Using PEDOT Coated Paper Based Sensor
abstract: The postharvest onion losses pose a serious challenge to the government in maintaining adequate supply and price. One of the causes of onion deterioration and wastage during storage is rotting, which is brought on by natural decay and bacterial pathogenic infections. Certain volatile organic compounds (VOCs) emitted by onions have been reported to be useful in differentiating between fresh and spoilt onions. This paper reports a chemiresistive based PEDOT sensor to detect onion spoilage with an appreciable sensing response of 30 % with good repeatability and reproducibility.

articleTitle: Self-Referencing MEMS Resonator with Dual Mechanical Modes for Temperature-Independent Environmental Sensing
abstract: Microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) resonators are ideal for low-power, compact, and cost-effective sensing due to their small size and low power consumption. In this study, dual-mode Aluminum Nitride (AlN) transduced MEMS resonators were designed and characterized over a broad temperature range from -200°C to +200 °C. A systematic study was conducted to evaluate the influence of a silicon oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{SiO}_{2})$</tex> thin film on the MEMS resonators' quality factors (Q-factors) and temperature coefficient of frequency (TCF). The two adjacent mechanical modes consistently shifted together across the entire temperature range, enabling temperature-independent self-referencing for enhanced environmental sensing. The addition of the oxide film increased the quality factor of the resonators by more than 500%, significantly improving their sensitivity to various environmental phenomena.

articleTitle: PDMS Micro-Patterning on Wafer Based on EtchBack Lift-Off for Microsystems Fabrication
abstract: In this study, we presented an etch-back lift-off method (EBLO) for Micro-patterning of PDMS on wafer. This method utilizes a photoresist mold to form PDMS patterns, followed by reactive ion etching (RIE) to precisely control the pattern dimensions and film thickness. Our experimental results show that this method can successfully produce PDMS patterns with dimensions ranging from 4 to 20 μm. The PDMS patterns exhibit clear edges, extremely vertical sidewalls, and flat surfaces with acceptable adhesion. However, a high aspect ratio (greater than 2.8) increases the risk of pattern collapse. The stability of the RIE etching rate, measured at 1.2 μm/min, allowing for precise control over the PDMS film thickness. This developed method for wafer fabrication offers a robust and reliable approach for creating micrometer resolution of PDMS patterns suitable for MEMS and microfluidic applications.

articleTitle: Environmentally-Aware Wireless Sensor Network Optimization for Improved Target Localization
abstract: This paper presents a method of improving target localization given a wireless sensor network (WSN) by optimizing additional sensors that consider environmental impedance in their line-of-sight (LOS). Commonly, sensors are optimized to minimize target position estimation variance by maximizing the determinant of the Fisher information matrix. Existing work, however, largely ignores how this optimization may induce deleterious sensor-environmental effects, like an impeded LOS. Thus, we present a problem formulation that considers these effects to improve target localization. We also demonstrate a novel use of the pre-existing DIRECT optimization algorithm by utilizing it for WSN optimization, where we show an average 50% reduction in ellipse uncertainty compared to current methods.

articleTitle: Research on the Metal 3D Printing Heat Exchanger for the Graphene Nanofluids
abstract: This research uses metal 3D printing to integrate the pulsating heat pipe (PHP) and wavy fins. We use the graphene nanofluids for the PHP. The graphene nanofluids increase the thermal conductivity, reduce thermal resistance on the PHP and improve the thermal energy conversion efficiency. Moreover, graphene nanofluids lets the PHP to be activated in a lower temperature environment, so that PHPs can be used more widely.

articleTitle: Bolt Type Force Sensor with Improved Wiring for Force Measurement in Sport Climbing
abstract: This paper proposes a new bolt type force sensor that can be used as a bolt to fix an object and can also measure the force applied to the fixed object. The intended application of this sensor is force measurement in sport climbing. Climbing holds are generally fixed by a steel bolt. Four strain gauges are installed to the shaft of the bolt to detect forces applied during sport climbing. This proposed sensor allows force measurement without the need to modify climbing holds or distance them from the wall to install force sensors. Additionally, the wiring comes out from the threaded side of the bolt, and when installed, the wiring comes out from behind the wall. Therefore, it does not interfere with the movement of sport climbing. In this paper, the structure of the sensor is firstly introduced. Next, the calibration method using 6-axis force sensor is shown. Finally, force measurement experiments are conducted, and it is confirmed that the sensor is able to achieve force estimation in practical situations.

articleTitle: Target Isolation and Enhancement Through Coherent Multi-View Vital-Doppler Detection
abstract: Doppler Radar has long been considered for use in biomedical applications due to its ability to detect um-scale displacements. In these cases, a common concern is the ambiguity introduced in vital sign detection caused by clutters, both moving and stationary. This work proposes using multiple radars with coherent multi-view detection to reduce the impact of moving clutter and other factors, such as fundamental harmonics, on vital sign detection.

articleTitle: Functionalized Graphene Sensors for Selective and Sensitive Gas Detection in Real air at Room Temperature
abstract: While graphene excels at single-molecule detection due to its high surface area and signal-to-noise ratio, its inherent non-selectivity and atmospheric doping hinder its use in real-world applications like environmental monitoring and medical diagnostics. This research addresses this limitation by functionalizing graphene channels with porous activated carbon, and metal nanoparticles (NPs). Notably, nanopored activated carbon demonstrates both ammonia selectivity and the ability to passivate graphene in air, achieving a remarkable 500 ppt ammonia sensitivity with a 3-second response time. Similarly, 1 nm tin NPs on graphene field-effect transistors (GFETs) exhibit high sensitivity and selectivity for ethanol and ammonia in real-world air, detecting ethanol as low as 100 ppb at room temperature. Likewise, 1 nm aluminum NPs functionalized graphene shows high ammonia selectivity in air at room temperature.

articleTitle: A 40-KS/s In-Plane Stress Sensing ΔΣ Frontend Integrated into a 2×48 Needle-Shaped Array
abstract: This work presents a densely packed sensor array for high speed localized mechanical stress measurement. A direct digitization approach is used, which embeds shear (S) and normal (N) stress sensitive transistors into the input stage of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1^{\mathrm{s}\mathrm{t}}$</tex> -order two-step continuous-time incremental Delta-Sigma <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Delta\Sigma)$</tex> modulator. A prototype ASIC with 48 dual (S/N) sensor sites is fabricated in a 180 nm process, with a unit cell area of 70 μm x 109 μm and a power consumption of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$19.24 \ \mu \mathrm{W}/\text{sensor}$</tex>. The proposed readout achieves a resolution of 11 Bit at a bandwidth of 20 kHz and over a full-scale of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{F S}_\mathbf{\sigma}= \pm \mathbf{3 3 0} \mathbf{M P a}(\mathbf{S}$</tex> ) and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\pm 161 \mathbf{MPa}\ (\mathbf{N})$</tex>. The circuit achieves <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{2}$</tex> values of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.9997 }(\mathbf{S})$</tex> and 0.9987 (N), respectively.

articleTitle: Design and Test of Mems Resonant Pressure Sensor with A Novel Membrane Structure
abstract: The limitations of quartz resonant pressure sensors are due to random errors caused by structural complexity and frequency temperature drift induced by thermal stress. This paper proposes an integrated metal-based pressure sensor structure with a sensitive membrane featuring thermal stress-isolation grooves. The innovative design reduces the temperature drift of the sensor's output frequency due to thermal stress, improves the stability of the sensor, and makes it suitable for high-precision applications.

articleTitle: An Efficient Wrist Photoplethysmogram Quality Assessment Method Based on Wristwatches
abstract: Photoplethysmogram (PPG) is widely used to provide information about the cardiovascular system. However, PPG is very susceptible to various noises, especially wrist PPG. Highly noisy PPG could not provide sufficient information to reflect cardiovascular conditions. This study proposed an efficient signal quality assessment solution for wearable wrist PPG using only 10 time-domain features. Data from 170 participants were involved to evaluate the proposed solution. Proposed features were validated with the LightGBM model. The results show that the proposed solution achieves 0.93 in F1 score, which is higher than traditional methods. For each PPG segment, computing proposed features on the C++ platform consumes only 73.17±12.26 microseconds. Finally, the proposed method is deployed to an edge computing platform and realizes real-time PPG quality assessment.

articleTitle: Integrating LSPR and SERS for Rapid and Effective Visualization and Identification of Volatile Organic Compounds Distribution
abstract: Microbial volatile organic compounds (MVOCs) can serve as a diagnostic tool for assessing the respiratory status of microorganisms. Localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) sensors are noted for their rapid response and straightforward operation; however, they often struggle to provide specific information about the detected substances and to differentiate between gas types. In contrast, gas sensors utilizing surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) technology offer excellent selectivity and can generate unique “fingerprint” signals, enabling easy identification and distinction of various gas molecules. Integrating these two technologies promises to enhance the visualization of volatile organic compound distributions both more effectively and expeditiously.

articleTitle: Opto-Microfluidic Lab-on-a-Chip Characterization of Yeast Suspension Using Monte Carlo Method-Based Light Extinction Model
abstract: We propose a PDMS-based photonic lab-on-a-chip system for precise detection of yeast radius and concentration with tiny amounts of the suspension. A Monte Carlo method-based light extinction model has been presented to statistically examine photon destinations and extinction characteristics of the yeast suspensions by tracing all underlying rays in detail. Meanwhile, a series of extinction spectrum measurements are designed and performed. Thereafter, the optimized genetic algorithm is broached to calculate the simultaneous inversion of the radius and concentration of the yeast suspension based on the extinction spectrum. The inversion results indicate that the miscalculation for the yeast radius is less than 5%. The proposed device is suitable for any spectrophotometric detection as a particle measurement platform in an advanced photonic lab-on-a-chip system.

articleTitle: A New Frontier in CO2 Sensing: A Comparative Study of Thermal and Light Activation in Na:In2O3 Nanostructured Materials
abstract: Carbon dioxide emissions are a major contributor to climate change. To effectively map these levels and restrict carbon footprint, we need reliable and affordable CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensors that address main limitations of conventional technologies developed until now. Our recent research has demonstrated the highly CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensing capabilities of a new chemoresistive gas sensor based on sodium-doped indium oxide operating at 250 °C. The present work aimed to further exploit the properties of this semiconductor in order to make it even more sustainable and effective. One promising approach involves using UV or visible light for sensor activation at room temperature. Then, this study explored the chemoresistive properties of sodium-doped indium oxide nanostructured films towards CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> under both thermal and light activation (using 385 nm UV-LED). Three different sodium-doped samples were prepared and comprehensively characterized. These films exhibited a high sensitivity and selectivity to CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> over a very broad concentration range (250-5000 ppm), which covers most indoor and outdoor applications, further with a negligible influence of environmental humidity variations. Advanced operando diffuse reflectance infrared Fourier transform spectroscopy was exploited to achieve a deeper understanding on the sensing mechanism in thermo- and UV-light activated conditions.

articleTitle: Doppler Radar-Based Recognition and Prediction of Cycling Behaviors
abstract: To develop a detection system of cycling movements including abnormal riding, this study presents the Doppler radar-based classification and prediction of four cycling behaviors: riding, stopping, turning, and wobbling. We used a convolutional neural network (CNN) whose inputs were time-velocity (spectrogram) images measured by Doppler radar. Furthermore, preliminary movements immediately before the motion were also measured in the same way to evaluate the feasibility of prediction of the cyclist behaviors. Experimental results demonstrate that the accuracy of cyclist behavior classification is 99% and the prediction accuracy is over 60%. Thus, the applicability of the method for detecting cycling behaviors including wobbling movements was confirmed.

articleTitle: Self-Heating SnO2 Gas Sensors for Low-Power Intelligent Olfactory Diagnosis
abstract: Olfactory diagnosis presents a promising non-invasive approach to lifelong chronic disease monitoring. Metal oxide gas sensors without external heaters prove effective in meeting the requirements of miniaturization and low power consumption in smart healthcare. In this work, we designed a sensitivity-computable self-heating gas sensor featuring a suspended thin lines array structure made of SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> as the sensing element and Pt interdigitated electrodes. Experimental results showed the comparative advantages of gas sensitivity and the self-heating efficiency of the sensor over previous methods. The joule heating of sensors with various essential parameters, such as the width of the thin line, pairs of electrodes, and spacing between each line, were investigated numerically using COMSOL Multiphysics. With a 10 V DC bias voltage, the steady-state temperature of 283.35 °C was achieved on the surface of the sensing element. A higher surface-to-volume ratio of the thin lines array structure was found to decrease the maximum surface temperature of the designed SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sell-heating gas sensor.

articleTitle: Sensing and Localization of Multiple Defects in Pipes with Pulse-echo Mode Torsional Guided Wave Ultrasonics
abstract: We demonstrate localization of multiple damages in steel pipes utilizing the pulse-echo technique combined with synthetic focusing of torsional guided waves on a custom-designed FPGA-based smart structural health monitoring (SHM) system. Torsional modes were utilized for damage detection and were excited using a ring of PZT transducers that serve as both transmitters and receivers. Finite element (FE) simulations and experiments were conducted with notches placed at various locations, and the resulting data analysis shows excellent performance for localization of multiple defects. The results demonstrate the utility of the proposed method for accurately assessing the condition of pipelines in real-time.

articleTitle: A Plug-in OCT Module for in Situ Live Monitoring of Laser Processing
abstract: This paper presents a novel design of an Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) module that is pluggable into all kinds of existing laser heads in industrial applications. The current method of coupling OCT with a laser head needs customized light-splitting optics inside the laser head, which bounds the OCT and laser head manufacturers, hence hindering a wider application of OCT in the monitoring of laser processing. For the existing laser heads in service that need to add the function of OCT monitoring, one needs to open up the laser head, install the dichroic mirror, and tune the optics, which is time-consuming and runs the risk of damaging the laser head. In addition, the existing OCT coupling method shoots the probe beam through the thick focus lens for high power laser beam, which degrades the signal strength and introduces dispersion issue. To address these issues, we propose a laser head-independent OCT module that functions as a plug-in component, which avoids interference with the laser head and works fully independent. The test demonstrates the feasibility of the plug-and-play solution for new independent OCT products and updating the existing laser head with OCT function with seamless integration and un-degraded performance.

articleTitle: Empowering Energy-Aware Task Operations and Timekeeping with Intermittent Sensor Systems
abstract: Varying energy requirements and timekeeping issues faced by intermittent sensor systems are addressed by an Energy and Time Management Unit (ETMU) introduced in this work. This ETMU allows dynamic energy storage size and operating voltage adjustment to meet task energy requirements and startup times. It also includes an ultra-low power real-time clock (RTC) for accurate timekeeping. The ETMU is integrated into an intermittent sensor system for ultrasonic water flow measurements, using three energy harvesters and the LoRaWAN protocol for data transmission and time synchronization. Experimental results show efficient energy management of LoRaWAN communications, e.g. improved startup and charging time for LoRaWAN communication task, and precise timekeeping for data collection.

articleTitle: Modular Wireless Inertial Motion Capture System with Self-Calibration
abstract: Wearable inertial motion capture systems enable movement analysis outside the laboratory, thereby promising valuable data collection in natural environments. We present an open-source motion capture system consisting of a variable number of wireless IMU sensor modules and a modular software framework providing OpenSim compatibility. System calibration is achieved by automatic sensor-to-segment alignment (S2SA) using a weighted least squares approach, enabling self-calibration based on arbitrary movements and ongoing recalibration. The S2SA approach is evaluated in a simulation and a proof-of-concept walking experiment with a human participant. Both in the simulation and in the experiment, all initializations converge, demonstrating the robustness of the automatic S2SA approach. Position and orientation deviations are below 0.09 m and 1.28/spl degree/, respectively. Lower limb joint angles exhibit root mean square errors ranging from 2.1/spl degree/ to 7.2/spl degree/ compared to a state-of-the-art S2SA method, while Pearson correlation coefficients are larger than 0.91 for all joints. Altogether, the results demonstrate the potential of self-calibration based on arbitrary movements, thereby enhancing the motion capture system's usability and paving the way towards clinical applicability.

articleTitle: Liquid Metal Flexible Pressure Sensor Based on Femtosecond Laser Direct Writing Microchannel
abstract: The rapid development of flexible pressure sensors stems from their extensive applications in wearable electronic products, biomedical devices, and human-machine interfaces. This paper presents a novel approach to fabricate flexible pressure sensors by utilizing femtosecond laser direct writing technology to manufacture complex microfluidic channels for injecting liquid metal. The performance of the manufactured flexible sensors is characterized through comprehensive mechanical and electrical testing, demonstrating high sensitivity, short response time, and good stability. Overall, this study showcases the potential of femtosecond laser direct writing based manufacturing techniques in developing flexible pressure sensors with outstanding performance characteristics, thus driving advancements in the fields of flexible electronics and sensor technology.

articleTitle: NiO-Doped Laser-Induced Graphene: A High-Performance Flexible Temperature Sensor
abstract: This study introduces a high-performance flexible temperature sensor prepared using laser-induced graphene (LIG) doped with nickel oxide (NiO) nanoparticles (NPs). Unlike conventional LIG surface doping methods, we developed a nickel oxide-doped LIG flexible temperature sensor by introducing NiO NPs into a polyimide (PI) precursor solution cured into a film followed by ultraviolet (UV) laser treatment. This approach achieves a more stable and uniform doping process while further improving the sensing performance of LIG-based temperature sensors. Over a prospective temperature detection range (30–100 °C), the sensitivity of the NiO-doped LIG temperature sensor is significantly improved from -0.064% °C-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> to -0.079% °C-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>, an improvement of 19.3%, compared to that of the intrinsic LIG temperature sensor, while maintaining high linearity (R2 = 0.999) as well as excellent temperature stability and reliability. This research not only enhances the performance of flexible temperature sensors based on LIG but also paves new pathways for its industrial production in various application fields.

articleTitle: Airflow Optimization for Olfactory Display Using Inkjet Device
abstract: This study presents a novel multichannel olfactory display that utilizes an electroosmotic (EO) pump combined with an inkjet device to dispense odor components. The inkjet device's ability to release tiny liquid amounts (picolitres) significantly improves the dynamic range of odor blending. To ensure proper aroma delivery, a micro-ceramic heater was incorporated to evaporate the droplets ejected from the inkjet device. Additionally, the study examines the role of airflow in dispersing the evaporated samples, utilizing a DC fan to optimize airflow for uniform and consistent aroma distribution. A fan in front of the inkjet device showed stability better than that placed at the back side of the device.

articleTitle: Active Sensing Based Quaternary Mixture Odor Quantification Using Viscous Coated QCM Sensor Array with Multiple Harmonic Responses
abstract: This paper proposes an active sensing based odor record system which can quantify each component in quaternary gas mixture. The system consists of an odor blender and a gas sensor array with four quartz crystal microbalance (QCM) sensors coated with viscous films. In the measurement process, this system records the response pattern of the sensor array to the target odor. Then it uses the odor blender to generate a gas mixture and modify the recipe successively to make the response pattern of generated mixture approach the target one with the use of linear quadratic regulator (LQR). The quantification result is the recipe of the generated gas mixture whose response pattern is close to target odor. The result of the experiments indicates that the proposed system can measure the concentration of each component in quaternary gas mixture after introducing time-varying gain matrix into the system.

articleTitle: Fibre Optic Interrogated Palpation Sensor for Mechanical Tissue Assessment in Minimally Invasive Surgery
abstract: The advantages robotic assisted surgery offers compared with conventional laparoscopic surgery has led to increased use in recent years. However, a limiting factor is the lack of physical feedback information for the surgeon. For example, a characteristic marker for cancer location is the stiffness of the soft tissue. Typically, cancerous tissue has a higher stiffness than the surrounding healthy tissue. In this paper, we propose a design for an optical fibre interrogated palpation probe that can be used within minimally invasive robotic assisted surgery. The probe measures the force and displacement applied to the tissue via a flexible membrane. Initial tests have been carried out to measure the stiffness of silicone phantoms. In future, this can be expanded to more complex phantoms with stiff inclusions, and ex-vivo tissue samples.

articleTitle: A Phonocardiogram Quality Assessment Method Using Multi-Domain Feature
abstract: Phonocardiogram (PCG) is a direct response to the mechanical activity of the heart and carries a wealth of physiological and pathological information. However, reliable information reflecting cardiac activity is not available from high-noise PCG. Therefore, this study proposes a multi-domain feature quality assessment method using morphological, timedomain, and frequency-domain features to screen noisy interfering PCG segments. Data from 170 participants were involved to evaluate the proposed solution. Proposed features were validated with the LightGBM model. Also, this study compares the inter-beat-interval (IBI) of Photoplethysmogram (PPG) and PCG to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method. The results show that the proposed solution achieves 0.90 in AUC, higher than traditional methods. After the PCG quality assessment, the root mean square error (RMSE) of IBI was reduced to 10.23 microseconds. Finally, the model was deployed on an edge computing device to realize real-time PCG quality assessment.

articleTitle: Integrated Acoustic-Optic-Magnetic Sensing: Enabling Telemetry via Submarine Cables
abstract: Communication is crucial for underwater telemetry with autonomous underwater vehicles (AUVs). Traditional seabed-station-based communication methods face challenges due to high costs and limited range. Utilizing distributed acoustic sensing (DAS) and quantum sensing technologies, we propose a novel solution for bidirectional communication via submarine cables. AUVs can transmit data through existing submarine cables without surfacing or additional seabed stations. Sea trials show that our solution achieves an uplink rate of approximately 1117 bps and a downlink rate of approximately 7.2 bps. The integrated acoustic-optic-magnetic sensing solution enables AUVs to perform telemetry through submarine cables, expanding their operational scenarios.

articleTitle: Investigation of Long-Term Embedded RFID Sensors for Structural Health Monitoring
abstract: Ensuring the health of civil engineering structures is crucial for the safety and longevity of the built environment. In this direction, structural health monitoring (SHM) has been increasingly employed, providing insight into the structural behavior, based on sensor data representing structural responses. This paper investigates the plausibility of embedding sensors into concrete structures for SHM, leveraging radio frequency identification (RFID) technology, in an attempt to enable the passive operation of sensors without continuous power supply and to reduce potential sources of interference. In contrast to conventional SHM sensors, the uninterrupted operation of embedded sensors must be ensured because post-installation interventions are either impractical or impossible. RFID technology enables wireless data acquisition and energy transmission without mechanical impact on civil engineering structures, although it may be challenging when RFID sensors are embedded in concrete. This study presents a durable passive embedded RFID sensor system (i.e., a system without batteries), including the selection of components, such as housing and cable materials, suitable for withstanding the aggressive environment of concrete without damaging the sensitive electronics or contaminating the data recorded by the sensors. The proposed sensor system is validated in laboratory tests, the results of which provide insights into the influence of each component and are intended to advance the implementation of embedded sensor systems.

articleTitle: Wearable Textile Sensor Using Hetero-Core Optical Fiber for Blood Pressure Measurement
abstract: This paper described a novel use of textile sensors incorporating single-mode hetero-core optical fiber for blood pressure estimation. The textile sensors were designed by weaving hetero-core optical fibers together with wool yarn. The sensor detecting the applied pressure can be integrated into a garment. Textiles, which are fabrics like clothing, are innovative sensors that do not cause stress to the subject. In this paper, pulse wave detection was performed using smart textiles, and pulse waveforms were acquired at the wrist and elbow. We estimated blood pressure for two subjects using the Pulse Transit Time (PTT) method and found that the results were comparable to those of a reference sphygmomanometer. With this smart textile, sensor functions can be embedded in clothing, making it possible to measure blood pressure.

articleTitle: Impact of Al Content on the Photoresponse Characteristics of Ultrasonic Spray Pyrolytically Deposited (AlxGa1-x)2O3 Solar-Blind Photodetectors
abstract: In this work, (Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">x</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1-x</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ultraviolet photodetectors (PDs) with Al/Ga mole fractions of 0.1/0.9, 0.2/0.8, and 0.4/0.6 were fabricated using ultrasonic spray pyrolysis deposition (USPD) system. The material analyses revealed that oxygen vacancies are strongly dependent on the aluminum content. As the Al content increased, the number of oxygen vacancies that act as charge carriers also increased. PDs using Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.4</inf>Ga<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0.6</inf>O thin films as active layers showed the best performance, demonstrating a simple method to improve device performance by controlling the number of oxygen vacancies in Aluminum Gallium Oxide (AGO) through Al content.

articleTitle: Smart Cell with Internal Sensors to Limit Lithium Plating During Fast-Charge at Low Temperature
abstract: In order to improve the performance, safety and durability of the cells, monitoring the internal parameters of the lithium-ion battery with sensors is a critical issue. In this article, we present a comparative study between a smart cell with internal sensors and a control cell during an ageing test with fast charge and WLTP discharge protocol at 0°C. Two internal sensors, a reference electrode and an optical fiber temperature sensor, were inserted within the cell to monitor the electrode potential and internal temperature respectively. By using the reference electrode sensor that gives access to the value of the negative electrode potential, one of the cells is monitored during the fast charge to limit the risk of lithium plating. We observe that the degradation of the control cell is very fast compared to the smart cell. These results demonstrate the interest of the internal sensor to limit cell degradation during fast charging at low temperature.

articleTitle: Evaluating 3D Depth Sensors: A Study and an Open Source Data Set of Logistic Scenarios*
abstract: In logistic environments, diverse applications, reaching from robotics to monitoring and quality assess-ment, benefit from depth information processing. In addition, multiple depth image cameras have been introduced to the market which differ widely in the used imaging technology, quality and price. In this paper, an open source data set is presented, containing calibrated and timely synchronized real world data from seven different depth imaging sensors, including a quantitative evaluation of the quality of each used sensor, in multiple logistic scenarios.

articleTitle: Skin-Interfaced Wearable Biosensors
abstract: An overview of recent efforts in developing wearable biosensors for non-invasive molecular analysis is given.

articleTitle: Flexible Sensing Skin for Simultaneous Measurement of Wall Shear Stress, Flow Direction and Dynamic Pressure
abstract: A flexible sensing skin has been developed for aircraft surfaces to enable the simultaneous measurement of wall shear stress, flow direction, and dynamic pressure. Three types of sensitive unit structures are designed based on the measurement mechanisms and manufactured using microelectro-mechanical system processes. All sensitive units are flexible and distributed on the surface, enhancing sensitivity and frequency response. Gold is used to create the wall shear stress and flow direction sensitive units, achieving errors of less than 0.4 Pa within the wall shear stress range of 0 to 17 Pa, and directional errors of less than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3^{\circ}$</tex>. Polyvinylidene fluoride film is positioned above the chamber to effectively respond to dynamic pressure within the frequency range of 230 Hz to 7800 Hz, covering typical flow characteristics and indicating high sensitivity. The development of the flexible sensing skin provides a novel approach for flow sensing and monitoring on aircraft surfaces.

articleTitle: Flexible Stretch-Free, Liquid-Sealed Packaging Method for Ultra-Thin Silicon-Based Bending Sensor
abstract: Thin-film-like bending sensors possess significant application potential in wearable electronics, robotics, and biomedical sensing. Conventional packaging methods are inadequate in mitigating the effects of external forces, particularly tensile stress, which can compromise sensor performance and even result in structural damage. Here, we develop a flexible stretch-free, liquid-sealed (FSFLS) packaging method for ultra-thin silicon-based bending sensors, aimed at applications in robotic precision control. Comprehensive research was conducted on structure, mechanism, material, performance measurement, and practical application. The key feature of the packaging structure is the ability to eliminate the influence of external tensile forces. It ensures conformity with the measured object while independently facilitating pure bending, thereby guaranteeing measurement accuracy. Under the packaging method, the bending sensor achieved large curvature radius measurements (radius < 2 mm), high linearity (Coefficient of Determination > 0.999), and high accuracy and precision in dynamic testing. Furthermore, it effectively shielded the sensor from external environmental influences and has been successfully implemented to the precise grasping operations of robotic hands.

articleTitle: Frequency Measurement Using Frequency Control to Improve Distance Resolution of FMCW LiDAR
abstract: Frequency modulation continuous wave (FMCW) LiDAR is valued for its robustness in harsh environments like rain, snow, and fog. It measures distance by detecting interference frequencies between transmitted and received beams, typically using Fast Fourier Transform(FFT). However, FFT is slow in achieving high-resolution frequency measurements. This study proposes using a frequency-to-voltage converter (FVC) for faster measurement through one-shot conversion. Despite its speed, FVC introduces ripple noise, reducing resolution. To mitigate this noise, a frequency control technique shifts the frequency to minimize ripple noise, indirectly measuring the interference frequency. The paper provides mathematical analysis and experimental validation of this method.

articleTitle: Design of Micro-Security Device Based on Three-Stage Electric-Thermal Mechanism
abstract: In response to the current trend of integration and miniaturization of weapons and equipment, the size of its combat unit is getting smaller and smaller, in order to adapt to the small size of the combat part and at the same time leave more space to accommodate the gunpowder, a micro-security device based on three-stage electro-thermal mechanism is proposed, in which the micro-partition chip is prepared by SOI silicon wafers, and the cover plate is prepared by alumina ceramics. In order to increase the output displacement of the electrothermal mechanism, a lever mechanism is designed. The theoretical analysis and experimental verification of the designed three-stage electric-thermal mechanism show that its output displacement meets the needs of releasing the insurance at 9V voltage, and its response time is within 20ms, and the fire transmission channel is 2.1-3.5mm through the fire transfer test, which can not only ensure that the flame is isolated when the electric heating mechanism is not opened, but also ensure that the flame is transmitted to the ignition powder when the electric heating mechanism is opened.

articleTitle: Contactless Electrical Impedance Tomography with Deep Learning for Lung Monitoring: Phantom Study
abstract: This study proposes the application of contactless electrical impedance tomography (CEIT) for lung imaging, which is a crucial tool for respiratory disease diagnosis and monitoring. By employing the contactless measurement approach, CEIT not only avoids the contact impedance of traditional EIT but also has the potential to reduce discomfort for users, such as avoiding pressure on the chest caused by traditional EIT electrode belts. This study designed a phantom experiment to investigate the feasibility of CEIT in monitoring lung respiration. The deformations of the lung simulators are monitored through the difference in magnitude and phase angle of the measured impedance data. An image reconstruction algorithm combining the Landweber iteration and neural network was proposed. The method comprehensively utilized impedance magnitude and phase angle information, significantly improving the quality of CEIT's image reconstruction. With the proposed image reconstruction method, our CEIT can effectively achieve ventilation monitoring. It is a significant advancement for CEIT in the field of lung monitoring.

articleTitle: A 1.25 μm 59.3 Mpixel 60 fps CIS with 2×1 Multi-Directional Phase-Detection Pixels
abstract: This paper presents a 59.3 Mpixel 60 fps back-illuminated stacked CMOS image sensor (CIS), which is designed for immersive visual content production. To ensure high-speed signal readout with a small pixel pitch and low power consumption, a six-fold column parallel single slope analog-to-digital converter array with a hybrid counter is installed. Additionally, a multi-directional phase detection (PD) function is incorporated by stacking a 2×1 on-chip lens and metal shield, allowing for PD across diverse objects with minimal pixel defects. Our CIS demonstrates full-frame readout with power consumption of less than 2.5 W and random noise of 2.56 e-rms, representing superior performance relative to sensor size compared to recent high-resolution sensors.

articleTitle: Simulation and Validation of Automotive Radar Performance with Water Spray Over Radome
abstract: Accurate environmental perception is essential for advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). Vision-based sensors underperform in bad weather, while radar, which performs well in adverse weather, can be affected by spray over its radome, reducing detection capabilities. Simulations reduce real-world validation efforts but must match real scenarios, necessitating validation. Current ADAS simulation software lacks realistic radar models due to computational challenges. This paper measures radar performance with water spray and saline solution, proposing an attenuation model. Results show a significant performance deterioration, emphasizing the need for accurate environmental modeling and simulation. The physically presented model matches the reality adequately.

articleTitle: Facile and Scalable Fabrication of Micro-Dome Structure Array Based on Liquid Metal and its Application for High-Performance Flexible Pressure Sensors
abstract: Artificial somatosensory systems in humanoid robots are essential to building physical interactions with objects and environments. Specifically, bioinspired sensors mimicking dome-like wrinkled structures underneath the epidermis play an important role in achieving high sensitivity and wide-range pressure detection. This study introduces a novel fabrication technique to create a high-resolution and high-density micro-dome structure array based on liquid metal by utilizing hybrid lithography (photolithography-soft lithography) and the selective wetting characteristic of the liquid metal. The micro-dome structures based on liquid metal can be scaled from sub-um to mm and formed over 70,000 patterns in a 1 area with a diameter of 10 with 10 spacing. The fabricated micro-dome structure arrays were utilized to create deformable and micro-dome-structured pressure-sensitive layers for flexible capacitive pressure sensors. The pressure sensing performance of the fabricated pressure sensors with different diameters and spacing of the dome structures was conducted and verified through simulations and experiments. The design parameters with larger spacing and smaller diameters showed high sensitivity in a small pressure range <10 kPa. Furthermore, the flexible pressure sensors maintained consistent performance under repetitive mechanical testing. The proposed fabrication technique allows the creation of multiscale micropatterns designed to meet specific performance requirements, such as sensor size, sensitivity, and sensing range. The proposed fabrication technique is expected to be applied to tailored pressure sensors requiring various performance levels.

articleTitle: Cantilever-Plate Piezoelectric Micromachined Ultrasonic Transducer (PMUT) for Airborne Applications with Enhanced Output and Linear Working Range
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducer (PMUT) for airborne object detection, which provides high sensitivity compared to the conventional round-shaped PMUT structure. This paper reports the concepts, fabrication and characterization of the new structure. The proposed structure shows a 13.3% improvement in transmitting (TX) sensitivity compared to the conventional one.

articleTitle: Simulation Methods for Lock-In Pixels Considering Gating Driver's Response
abstract: This paper presents two simulation methods for lock-in pixels incorporating driver response. The first method (sim1) replicates chip evaluation but requires longer simulation times. The second method is the cross-correlation method (sim2), which estimates modulation characteristics by calculating of cross-correlation of the photocurrent response and driver response. By conducting these simulations individually, this approach significantly reduces simulation time. Both simulation methods were conducted 3-tap lock-in pixel and the results show good agreement with measurement data, demonstrating their effectiveness.

articleTitle: A Droplet Screening System for Discovery of Slow-Growing Microbes from Environment Through Long-Term Culture
abstract: The exploration of new microbes and the establishment of a comprehensive microbial library are fundamental to broadening our understanding of ecological diversity and laying the groundwork for development in various industrial and pharmaceutical fields. Conventionally, agar plates to isolate microbes are widely used, but this traditional method is not appropriate to discover new, slow-growing microbes due to their drying out during long-term cultures. This approach has also limited the discovery of slow-growing microbes because they can be inhibited by faster-growing species that have already been identified. In this study, a droplet screening system was developed to discover novel, slow-growing microbes by providing long-term culture and iterative analysis capabilities, which overcomes the limitation in the conventional isolation method. The developed screening system comprises droplet generation with single microbe encapsulation, culture, growth detection and sorting, followed by cell extraction from the sorted droplets. This system allowed for stable on-chip cell culture and signal detection (growth analysis) over extended periods, more than 4 weeks. 20,000 microbes collected from environment were encapsulated into individual droplets with single cell and cultured in the screening system. After one week of culture, the microbial growth of individual droplets was measured, and only droplets showing higher growth than an isolation criterion were sorted. Microbes were then extracted from the separated droplets for further analysis. Droplets showing lower growth, considered as slow-growing microbes were collected to the screening system and re-cultured for another week. This whole screening process was repeated for 4 weeks to discover new, slow-growing microbes from environment samples. The microbes recovered from the weekly screening assays were analyzed using Next Generation Sequencing (NGS), and their DNA sequences were compared to a known microbes' sequence library. Through the droplet screening and further off-chip analysis, 1,081 new microbes were discovered. The developed screening system can offer new technology that allows for the discovery of difficult-to-culture microbes and overcomes the limitations of traditional screening methods.

articleTitle: Bridge Vibration Measurements from Very High-Resolution Spaceborne SAR
abstract: Structural health monitoring (SHM) using vibrometry is a key technique for the maintenance of bridges and other infrastructure. Conventional methods require in-situ placement of sensors which can be costly and inconvenient. This paper presents a remote monitoring method for extracting vibrational information from very high-resolution SAR data. This was achieved using a combination of a modified back-projection algorithm, spectrogram, and cadence-frequency analysis, which was applied to SAR data of a bridge. The extracted vibrations were validated against synchronous in-situ ground truth measurements.

articleTitle: UWB-Visual-Inertial Fusion Localization with Fast and Robust UWB Extrinsic Calibration
abstract: In order to realize the lightweight and low-drift localization of the autonomous robot system under the condition of satellite rejection, the extended Kalman filter can be used to fuse UWB, camera and IMU. The accuracy of UWB extrinsic estimation influences the accuracy of system positioning. Therefore, this paper proposes an automatic UWB extrinsic calibration method, which includes two steps: initialization and online update. First, we establish an UWB-Visual-Inertial fusion localization system based on extended Kalman filter, and use UWB external parameters as state variables to realize online update, so as to effectively suppress UWB extrinsic noise distur-bance. Then, we propose an initialization method to obtain a good initial value of the UWB extrinsic. The method is based on the data of VIO and UWB to obtain the initial value by optimization, avoiding the cumbersome steps of manually calibrating the initial value. Finally, we do simulation experiments based on the public dataset to verify that the proposed method improves the localization accuracy and robustness of the system.

articleTitle: Three-Dimensional Shape Optimized Seesaw-Type Force Sensor Fabricated with a Micro-Scale 3D Printer
abstract: This paper proposes a force sensor that utilizes three-dimensional (3D) shape optimization and 3D printing technology. Introduction of micro-scale 3D printing technology have simplified the fabrication processes of microdevices with complex geometries. At the same time, there have also been advancements in the optimization of 3D structures to achieve desirable performances. This study combined these two technologies to develop a force sensor for measuring the force of a soft actuator. The force sensor combines a typical probe geometry with a laser displacement sensor. Due to the millimeter-order scale of the sensor, the low rigidity of the resin material causes undesired torsional deformation. Through 3D shape optimization, a beam design with more than 70 % torsional displacement reduction was achieved without changes in spring constant. Furthermore, a beam printed by a micro-scale 3D printer showed elasticity. The relationship between the input force and laser displacement sensor output showed linear characteristics, indicating its suitability as a force sensor.

articleTitle: Verilog-A Modelling of Electrochemical Sensors for Combined Simulation of Biosensors and Interfaces
abstract: The ability to accurately model and simulate the behaviour of test devices is essential for effective design of sensor interface circuits. Electrochemical sensors are becoming increasingly popular for environmental and biosensing applications, generating a demand for high-performance and low-power sensor interfaces. Such sensors exhibit non-linear behaviour with non-negligible memory effects, and hence are difficult to model using standard electronic components in circuit simulation frameworks. Working toward overcoming this limitation, a Verilog-A-based model of a typical three-electrode electrochemical sensor has been developed and is presented. The model simulates electrochemical kinetics and mass transport effects in the time domain, outputting a redox current as a response to a provided electrode potential.

articleTitle: Speed-invariant Texture Discrimination using an Optical Tactile Sensor Array (LiVec Finger)
abstract: Providing robotic fingers with tactile sensation can enable better performance of dexterous manipulation. Identifying a texture by touch can further the ability of grippers to adjust their grip to the object being contacted. This work presents a non-camera-based optical tactile sensor array capable of dis-criminating between textures. The texture discrimination method uses sensor waveform amplitude, morphological, and spectral features. We show that an array of sensing units helps achieve high classification accuracy. Using the phase difference between sensing unit signals as a feature allows for good classification regardless of the scanning speed.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Open-Cavity Fiber Mach-Zehnder Interferometer Sensor Based on Beveled No-Core Fibers
abstract: An open-cavity fiber Mach-Zehnder interferometer (MZI) sensor is proposed by sandwiching a hollow-core fiber (HCF) between two beveled no-core fibers (NCFs). Due to the beveled fiber endface, there exists an opening in the MZI cavity at each splicing point, which can help the analyte to flow into the cavity for sensing. The measured RI sensitivity of our proposed open-cavity fiber MZI sensor is shown as high as 2851.86 nm/RIU. Meanwhile, very low temperature cross-sensitivity of 7×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-6</sup>RIU/oC is demonstrated, which makes our sensor avoid temperature disturbance during RI sensing.

articleTitle: Polymer-Free Batch Production and Application of Metal Foil-Based Thin-Film Strain Gauges
abstract: In the monitoring of mechanical components for lifetime prediction and detection of critical load conditions, especially strain gauges play a major role. They can be integrated into components to measure strain in the components themselves. This places special demands on the sensors used because of higher temperatures in the manufacturing phase of the components like additive manufacturing. This is why the sensors need to be polymer-free and cannot be applied with an adhesive. For this, directly deposited polymer-free sensors have been developed. In this article, the advantages of conventional polymer-foil based strain gauges (batch production) and directly deposited sensors (polymer-free) are combined by depositing the sensors on a metal foil and applying them polymer-free to metal specimens. This enables the batch production of strain gauges for use in harsh environments. Therefore, steel and aluminum foils were used as sensor carrier materials with aluminum oxide insulation layers and Platinum and NiCr sensor layers on the front side. On the back side, a tin layer was applied to enable thermocompressive bonding on the specimens leading to maximum tensile shear strengths of 10.7 MPa. After application, the sensors showed a k-factor of about 3.6 for the platinum sensors and about 2.4 for the NiCr sensors proving the functionality of the sensor concept.

articleTitle: Nanozyme-Assisted Quantitative Estimation of Cholesterol Using Ultrathin Silver Nanosheet
abstract: The severity of change in blood cholesterol standard concentration is a significant concern for all individuals. Developing a highly sensitive, low-cost, self-usable and long-durable blood cholesterol detection sensor is the utmost priority of all experts. Enzymatic detection kits used widely are comparable to high cost and require specific storage criteria. So, in this work, we have developed a highly sensitive electrochemical cholesterol sensor that will be able to detect human blood cholesterol levels, including high and low blood cholesterol levels. A very ultrathin silver Nano sheet was synthesized using a galvanic replacement reaction. It was examined using various electrochemical and physical characterization methods to explore its suitability for replacing the enzyme in an electrochemical sensor. After developing a silver nanosheet-modified screen-printed carbon electrode (SPCEI Ag nanosheet/Chox), it was implemented to detect the cholesterol concentrations covering low to high blood cholesterol levels. The modified electrode was found to be highly sensitive with LOD 50mg/dL and sensitivity O.1411A mg: IdL.

articleTitle: Four-Channel NFC System for Electrochemical Sensing of Fluids
abstract: Electrochemical analysis systems are increasingly important for applications like Point-of-Care diagnostics and Lab-on-Package sensing. Herein, we propose a system composed of four passive NFC (Near Field Communication) microchips capable of performing open circuit potentiometry through interactions with commercial smartphones. The multi-chip NFC system can be used to quantify four chemical quantities within a unique liquid sample thanks to a microfluidic circuit which feeds four ad-hoc screen-printed electrodes. In this contribution, preliminary calibration on four analytes is reported. The four target quantities considered in this paper are sodium, potassium, calcium, and pH. The sensing matrix will be human blood and fluids derived from food spoilage Thanks to further implementation with microfluidic channels currently under development, the NFC chemical analyses can facilitate domestic monitoring of patients and rapid, on-site test of pieces of food to check food quality and prevent foodborne illnesses.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Relation Between Shoulder Joint Angle and Bioelectrical Impedance on Deltoid Muscle
abstract: Electrical stimulation based on biological signals is effective in stroke paraplegics. However, functional electrical stimulation based on electromyography is challenging to apply to muscle groups with complex coordination, such as the periarthrodial muscles of the shoulder joint. This research aims to identify suitable measurement frequencies and electrode arrangements for measuring the bioelectrical impedance of the deltoid muscle to electrically stimulate based on bioelectrical signals generated from shoulder joint movement and muscle activity. Experiments were conducted under three different measurement frequencies and two electrode configurations measuring bioelectrical impedance and shoulder joint angle during forward-reaching and repositioning. The results showed that the correlation between bioelectrical impedance and shoulder joint angle of the deltoid muscle was higher when the measurement frequency was 40 kHz, and the electrode arrangement was parallel to the muscle fibers.

articleTitle: Monocular Camera and IMU Integration for Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction
abstract: This paper develops a pedestrian trajectory prediction model based on monocular camera and inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensor. By combining object detection and tracking with time series prediction deep learning techniques, the model predicts the future trajectories of pedestrians in road environments. This allows for earlier warnings to drivers, enhancing the effectiveness of modern advanced driver assistance systems (ADAS). The model records the past trajectories of pedestrians through object detection and tracking models, and then predicts future trajectories using a pedestrian trajectory prediction model built with gated recurrent unit (GRU). The proposed model was evaluated on the PIE dataset captured by onboard cameras and IMUsensor. The pedestrian trajectory prediction model proposed in this paper outperforms previous models, with 14.90% improvement in average distance error (ADE) and 22.20% improvement in final displacement error (FDE).

articleTitle: Battery-Powered Portable Multiplexed RT - PCR for HIV-1 and HIV-2 Viral Load Testing at LIMIC
abstract: HIV is a major health issue in LMICs, necessitating precise viral load (VL) monitoring for effective management. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) has made HIV manageable, underscoring the need for effective VL testing to achieve the 95-95-95 targets. The diversity of HIV subtypes in LMICs calls for innovative diagnostic solutions. Here, we demonstrate a portable multiplex RT-PCR device designed for fast and cost-effective testing of HIV-1 and HIV-2 using finger-prick blood in LMICs. It features on-site RNA extraction and real-time multiplex RT-PCR targeting HIV-1, HIV-2, and an internal process control of RNase P. The cost per test is approximately $10, based on laboratory-scale material costs. The device offers a sample-to-answer turnaround time of less than 70 minutes. Our internally controlled device exhibited 100% sensitivity and specificity against HIV-1, and 100% sensitivity and 90.91 % specificity against HIV-2.

articleTitle: Microacoustic Shear Horizontal Lithium Niobate Leaky SAWs for Harsh Environment Sensing
abstract: This paper investigates a novel microacoustic Shear Horizontal Leaky Surface Acoustic Wave (SH0 LSAW) resonator on X-cut Lithium Niobate (LN) for harsh environment sensing. Using optimized bulk LSAWs with highly resistant electrodes (gold and tungsten), the device demonstrates significant electromechanical coupling (≥ 40%), mechanical quality factors (≥1,000), with Figure of Merit (FOM) of approximately 300. The resonator maintains functionality under exposure to direct flame at 900 °C, with good power handling up to 20 dBm. A proof-of-concept application as a viscosimeter shows the sensor's capability in consistently monitoring fluid viscosity under high temperatures, with a temperature coefficient of frequency (TCF) of -65 ppm/K.

articleTitle: On-chip Integration of Acoustic Streaming Tweezers and Coulter Counter for Simultaneously Particles Focusing and Sensing
abstract: Microfluidic impedance flow cytometry is widely used for cell and particle analysis. However, position-sensitivity due to the nonuniform electric field produced by the coplanar electrodes is an unreliable factor in electrical impedance detection. Herein, a microfluidic impedance flow cytometry integrated with solid mounted bulk acoustic wave resonator (SMR) was developed. Particles were 3D focused via acoustic streaming tweezers triggered by GHz bulk acoustic waves. The coefficient of variation of the electrical diameters of the particles reaches 3.68%, 2.59%, and 1.68% for 3.5, 5, and 10 particles, without any sheath flow. It shows a significant improvement in the accuracy and precision of particles electrical impedance measurement.

articleTitle: DMGAN: Bridging AI and Chemistry with Enhanced GC-MS Data Generation
abstract: Data from gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) represent significant deviations between the large peak values of a particular substance and the small peak values of other components. Such deviations have many limitations for applying traditional deep learning techniques. Our proposed Dynamic Modulation Generative Adversarial Network (DMGAN) provides a solution to these limitations and generates a variety of synthetic data that enable real experiments to be efficient. We compare it with various models using pearson correlations, a representative metric that measures the similarity of chromatographic data, with DMGAN showing a quality exceeding 0.99. Furthermore, we show how it can be used for models in the existing AI-chemistry field using the generated synthetic data, showing a performance improvement of over 50%. This paper highlights the possibility that DMGAN can establish a strong connection between AI and chemistry.

articleTitle: Thin Film Reconfigurable Intelligent Surface Assisted Device-Free Fall Detection
abstract: Fall detection is essential for safeguarding vulnera-ble populations, such as the elderly. We design and implement a low-complexity reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted fall detection system. The manufactured thin film <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 1$</tex> RIS can effectively control the scattering of the dominant harmonics of the captured radio frequency (RF) carrier wave by steering their beams to a desired direction ranging from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$230^{\circ}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$310^{\circ}$</tex> in elevation. With beam steering, the RIS enables device-free fall detection by conducting dynamic elevation beam-scanning in an indoor space and analyzing variations in received signal strength (RSS) caused by human presence and motion, without requiring the person to carry any sensors or electronic devices. We design a posture recognition-based fall detection algorithm. Experimental results show that using a simple support vector ma-chine (SVM) classifier can achieve 92.50% accuracy in significant posture recognition that includes standing, sitting, and lying. Five voluntary participants were used for cross-validation. Compared with a conventional sensor node pair-based solution with a static beam, our proposed dynamic beam scanning technique improves accuracy by 11.83% using SVM. The results indicate that the RIS and the proposed algorithm have the potential to facilitate fall detection applications for assisted living.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal EIT Imaging Using Lensfree and Flexible Impedance Sensor
abstract: The low spatial resolution is one of the primary limitations of Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT), making it challenging to reconstruct images with accurate structural information in practical applications, such as tissue or cellular imaging. An effective solution is to incorporate images from other imaging modalities, thereby introducing additional structural information. In this paper, we introduce a multi-modal imaging system combining EIT and Lens-Free Imaging (LFI). We design a series of flexible soft EIT sensors of varying sizes for EIT imaging with a large field-of-view (FOV) LFI platform. We apply the Hologram-Guided Group Sparsity (HGGS) algorithm with a hologram captured by LFI for multi-modal EIT imaging. The effectiveness of our multi-modal imaging system is demonstrated through real-world experiments, which showcase the reconstruction of high-quality conductivity distributions with improved structural accuracy.

articleTitle: A Bias-Tunable Dual Band Photodetector for Plastic Material classification
abstract: This work introduces a novel technique for efficient and accurate classification of plastic materials in recycling process. The approach is based on a voltage-tunable Germanium on Silicon photodetector that operates within the 400 nm - 1600 nm spectral range. Utilizing a lab bench setup with a broad-spectrum light source and standard components, material properties are analyzed through photocurrent measurements. By employing the K-Nearest Neighbors algorithm, the analysis achieved a high accuracy of 94.6% for classifying 6 different types of plastics. This work underscores the critical role of advanced photo detection techniques in enhancing the efficiency and accuracy of classification for plastic recycling, contributing to more effective waste management and environmental sustainability.

articleTitle: Anchor-Free Relative 3D Pose Estimation Using Ultra-Wideband and Inertial Data Fusion
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to relative 3D pose estimation using Ultra-Wideband (UWB) Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) technology and Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU) data fusion. Unlike previous methods requiring multiple UWB sensors, our approach achieves accurate pose estimation with a single UWB tag per device, simplifying system setup. We integrate IMU data using an Error State Kalman Filter (ESKF) to enhance robustness and accuracy, particularly in Non-Line-of-Sight (NLOS) conditions. Experimental results demonstrate our method's effectiveness, achieving an average translation error of 9.5 centimeters and a rotation error of 9.3 degrees. This fusion of UWB and IMU data provides a reliable solution for applications requiring precise device-to-device spatial awareness.

articleTitle: A MXene@Pt Nanocomposite-based Wearable Epidermal Patch for Real-time Glucose and pH Monitoring
abstract: An electrochemical epidermal patch based on the MXene@Pt nanocomposite and platinum nanoparticles (PtNPs) functionalized laser-induced graphene (LIG) electrode was newly developed for real-time and continuous glucose and pH monitoring. The MXene@Pt nanocomposite coated on the working electrode exhibited excellent conductivity, biocompatibility, and hydrophilic properties, and its layered structure significantly increased the electrochemical surface area. It also adhered effectively to the electroplated PtNPs for improving their stability and glucose sensitivity. Within the physiological sweat range (0–2 mM), the fabricated glucose sensor showed an excellent sensitivity of 86.46 μAmM<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−1</sup>cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup> while the polyaniline-based pH sensor showed a near Nernstian sensitivity of -53.072 mV/pH over a pH range of 4–9 with excellent regression coefficient value (R2 = 0.99996).
