The combination of MXene@Pt nanocomposite and PtNPs much enhances the sensitivity of glucose detection and offers great potentials for various electrochemical sensors applications.

articleTitle: Microbial Fuel Cell (MFC)-Based in-Situ Water Toxicity Biosensor for Monitoring Heavy Metals and BTEX
abstract: As the electricity is produced by exoelectrogenic bacteria in an microbial fuel cell (MFC), monitoring electrical signals from MFCs can provide a novel way of real-time health monitoring of many engineered systems and processes such as anaerobic digester systems. The purpose of this study was to investigate the potential of the MFC process as a water toxicity sensor for detecting toxins such as heavy metals and BTEX in the water. Cu<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, Hg<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2+</sup>, benzene, and xylene were selected as the representative toxicants and the toxicity response of the MFC biosensor was evaluated based on the inhibition ratio, indicative of the voltage changes when the toxicants were exposed to the anodic biofilm. It was found that the inhibition ratios were proportional to the concentrations of spiked toxicants. The toxicity responses toward heavy metals demonstrated an excellent linear relationship between the inhibition ratio and the toxicant concentration. Overall, this study demonstrated the potential of MFC technology as a water toxicity biosensor for real-time health monitoring.

articleTitle: Colorimetric/Electrical Sensing of Chemical Warfare Agent Surrogates with Polydiacetylenes
abstract: Colorimetric sensing arrays (CSAs) are frequently explored for detecting chemical agents but often face challenges such as low sensitivity, delayed response times, or the need for various materials/chemicals, some of which can be hazardous themselves. Consequently, there is a growing interest in developing better materials for defense applications. Diacetylene (DA) monomers, which have a functional headgroup and an aliphatic tail with two adjacent carbon-carbon triple bonds, can be polymerized into polydiacetylenes (PDAs) that exhibit a visible blue color. When exposed to chemical liquids or vapors, the structured arrangement of PDAs is disrupted due to interactions between headgroups, leading to a change in both the visible color to red and the semiconductivity of the material. The degree and reversibility of this color shift depend on the headgroup type, DA chain length, and the nature of the stimulus. Our focus is on employing a collection of these materials to create an innovative design platform for detecting and, ideally, identifying chemical warfare agent (CWA) surrogates (e.g. organophosphates versus mustards) by observing quantitative changes in colorimetric and electrical responses. These changes are monitored through red-green-blue (RGB) values and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) measurements, respectively.

articleTitle: Fully-Printed Sensor Based Extended Gate Field Effect Transistors for Wireless Monitoring of Potassium and Ammonium Ions
abstract: This paper presents an extended gate field effect transistor based ion sensing platform utilizing flexible printed ion selective electrodes. A custom-printed circuit board with a Bluetooth-enabled microcontroller module enables wireless monitoring of the transistor's transfer characteristics modulated by the ion concentration in the target solution. The utilization of printing techniques such as inkjet printing and direct 3D writing provide the scope for facile and cost-effective fabrication. The system has been utilized for remote monitoring of Potassium and Ammonium ions with ideal Nernstian response, high sensitivity, and selectivity. This work provides a promising path for real-time and continuous ion monitoring which has crucial implications for health, industry, and environmental applications.

articleTitle: Magnetoelastic Torque Sensor with GaAs Hall Plates for E-Bikes
abstract: Typical e-bikes magnetoelastic torque sensors employ bulky fluxgate magnetometers to resolve few <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathbf{T} / \mathbf{N m}$</tex>. Instead, we propose the use of a miniaturized gradiometric arrangement of GaAs Hall plates sensitive to the radial magnetic field and a design approach that reduces the impact of axial misalignment. The proposed architecture provides comparable performance to commercial solutions, with reduced sizing and simplified magnetization requirements. Experiments conducted on a prototype with a full-scale (FS) upper limit of 200 Nm show a resolution of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7 \text{mNm}/\sqrt{\mathrm{H}\mathrm{z}}$</tex> with a combined standard error of 1.85%FS.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a Rotational Energy Harvester with a Dynamically Changing Potential Energy Function
abstract: This paper details the design, theoretical analysis, and experimental implementation of a rotational energy harvester using PZT (Lead Zirconate Titanate) piezoelectric material. The system includes a spinning host with magnets and a beam magnet that generates attraction and repulsion forces to drive a PZT transducer at the beam's end. Vibration from the host, powered by a DC motor, activates the beam. The PZT transducer converts mechanical energy into electrical energy. The study includes theoretical analysis, simulations for performance forecasting, and experimental validation in a laboratory, showing consistent simulated and real-world results. The research highlights optimization strategies for enhancing the reliability and efficiency of piezoelectric energy harvesters, demonstrating feasibility for low-speed rotating applications. The system also features a dynamically changing potential energy function as part of the rotational energy harvester.

articleTitle: Joint Outdoor Ozone and Carbon Monoxide Prediction with a Carbon Nanotube Sensor Array Calibrated Using a Bayesian Framework
abstract: While carbon nanotube sensor arrays are highly sensitive to multiple gases, they typically have moderate selectivity, major interferents and significant measurement noise. This makes the calibration of such systems deployed in uncontrolled environments a challenging task. This paper presents a Bayesian framework that addresses these difficulties. It is used to demon-strate the joint ozone and carbon monoxide prediction capability of a fully integrated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10\mathrm{x}2$</tex> carbon nanotube-based chemistor array deployed for several weeks in outdoor conditions. For ozone, mean absolute error (MAE) was found to be 4ppb over the range 15 to 83 ppb with a detection limit at 5.1 ppb; for carbon monoxide, 22 ppb MAE over the range 7 to 8 ppm with a detection limit at 2 ppm.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Microstructured and Capillary Optical Fibers for Refractive Index Measurement from 1.316 to 1.425 RIU
abstract: We experimentally investigate the potential of two types of optical fibers for refractive index (RI) measurement from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.316 < RI < 1.425$</tex>, which is a range of interest to detect low to very low concentrations of target gas typically found in the natural environment or in aquatic environments. The first fiber is a microstructured optical fiber (MOF) with a ring of air-holes arranged at the outer periphery of the fiber. The second investigated fiber is the capillary fiber (CF). To simulate the varying RI of the surrounding medium, a glycerolpure water mixture is used. A 5-cm fiber length is utilized as the sensing element to monitor RI changes for the two fiber types and performances are compared with MMF-based refractometer. MOF achieved a sensitivity 95 times greater than that of the MMF, and a resolution of ~ 1.01 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−4</sup> RIU. The CF demonstrates promising results, increasing the sensitivity up to 321 times of that of the MMF and three times that of the MOF over the RI range of 1.316 to 1.425.

articleTitle: A High Resolution Phase Shift Detection System for a Differential Multimode Fiber Refractometer
abstract: In this work, we present a phase shift detection system to instrument a differential multimode fiber (MMF) refractometer designed for methane (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>) detection in aqueous environments. The concentration of CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> can typically be directly obtained by observing the variation of the transmitted optical power along a functionalized MMF using a sensitised polymeric thin film compared to a reference MMF. Here, using a lock-in amplifier and modulating the laser drive current, we propose to indirectly monitor this concentration variation via phase shift measurement of a second order filter implemented using the photo diode parasitic capacitance. We show that the sensitivity of the system can be amplified by the quality factor of the circuit compared to a first order filter. Simulations show that refractive index (RI) change down to 20 nRIU can be detected. In addition, a closed-loop approach based on delay locked-loop is designed to improve both the linearity and dynamic range.

articleTitle: On the Cramér-Rao Bound for Bacterial Sensors
abstract: Bacteria-based biosensors are relevant due to their potential for highly specific and sensitive detection of various chemical signals. The use of bacterial cells as components in biosensors mandates the consideration of noise effects inherent in biochemical systems. The molecular nature of the dynamics governing the sensor mechanism has implications for the theoretical limits for estimating a chemical signal concentration with a bacterial sensor. In this paper, we derive the Cramer-Rao lower bound for the corresponding estimation problem. We find that the bound increases with the signal concentration of interest.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Photothermal Parasitic Effect on an Optomechanical Antenna
abstract: In this paper, we investigate the parasitic opto- thermo-mechanical transduction in nano-optomechanical an-tenna, focusing on its impact on the performance of a previously designed structure. This study encompasses both experimental and computational analyses to model the parasitic effects that overlap with the intended opto-electromechanical responses. Uti-lizing COMSOL Multiphysics, we simulate the thermal, optical, and mechanical interactions within the optomechanical structure. Our findings indicate that the parasitic opto-thermo-mechanical effect significantly influences the device's mechanical deflection, driven primarily by localized heating at the microcantilever's free end. Experimental validation aligns well with simulation results, showcasing the parasitic response's dominance over the intended functionality. This research contributes to the broader understanding and optimization of our nano optomechanical devices for advanced applications in radiation detection and sets the future efforts to mitigate these parasitic effects.

articleTitle: Vertical-Axis Rotary Triboelectric Nanogenerator with a Dual-Shaft Design for Enhanced Performance
abstract: Triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) offer a promising avenue for renewable energy generation, particularly from wind sources. In this study, we present a structural modification approach to enhance the output performance of rotary-type wind-driven TENGs by introducing a dual-shaft mechanism. This design modification significantly improves energy harvesting efficiency and reliability across a wide range of wind speeds, especially under low wind speed conditions. Our dual-shaft TENG (DS-TENG) nearly doubles the frequency of contact-separation events compared to conventional configurations, resulting in substantially higher electrical output. Experimental results demonstrate that the DS-TENG consistently outperforms traditional designs across all wind speed ranges, with notable improvements in RMS voltage (108.72%) and current (119.82%). Fast Fourier Transform analysis further highlights the potential of the DS-TENG for reliable low wind speed anemometry. The versatility of the dual-shaft design enables its application in various rotary-type energy harvesters, offering a promising solution for sustainable energy harvesting in diverse environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Under Display Ambient Light Sensor for non-Invasive Vital Signs Monitoring
abstract: This research details the cutting-edge application of an Ambient Light Sensor (ALS) placed behind an Organic Light Emitting Diode (OLED) display for obtaining biomedical optical signals, leveraging the display's inherent light emission. It is the first instance of an ALS sensor being strategically placed behind a display to measure vital signs, capturing the light from the display as it reflects off the body. This method is designed to simplify integration, reducing both costs and the size of such technology in devices with displays. Performance was quantified by calculating the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and estimating heart rate (HR) to benchmark against the gold standard. Initial tests demonstrated an average SNR of 12.88 dB and a root mean square error (RMSE) in HR measurement of 2.65 bpm compared to the gold standard.

articleTitle: Microwave Filtering Sensor for Simultaneous Materials Characterization and Wireless Communication
abstract: In this paper, a dual functional component integrated with bandpass filter (BPF) and material sensing function is proposed, at the first time. By applying two dual mode ring resonators with defected ground structure, the dielectric properties of loaded materials under test (MUTs) can be detected based on the frequency drift of the transmission poles and zero, without affecting the bandpass filtering response for communication. To verify this design method, a demonstrated dual functional component integrated with bandpass filtering for 5GHz Wi-Fi channel and sensor for detecting the permittivity is implemented. Measured results are in good agreement with the simulated ones, indicating the feasibility of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Terahertz Quasi-MIM Absorber for Integrating with Thin-film MEMS Bolometers
abstract: We present a novel terahertz (THz) absorber with a quasi-metal-insulator-metal (MIM) structure for improving the THz absorption coefficient of a SOI MEMS bolometer. The quasi-MIM structure is fabricated by etching the silicon substrate to create a groove structure, followed by metal deposition on both the etched and non-etched parts of the substrate. Silicon is used as the dielectric structure, approximately sandwiched between two metal layers. Consequently, this quasi-MIM structure offers a notable advantage over conventional MIM structures due to its reduced thickness, eliminating the need for multiple additional layers atop the substrate and making it suitable for integration with MEMS bolometers. Simulation results have indicated that the absorber features absorption levels of up to 98%, and the absorption frequency can be greatly tuned from 1–10 THz by modulating the size of the groove structure, demonstrating this quasi-MIM absorber as a promising option for realizing high THz absorption in MEMS bolometers.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Interstitial Cystitis with Single-chip Multiplexed Biosensing Array of Urine Biomarkers at the Point-of-Care
abstract: Interstitial cystitis is a chronic condition causing bladder pain, bladder pressure, and sometimes accompanied by pelvic pain and other symptoms overlapping with similar diseases. Urine biomarkers including cytokines and growth factors play a crucial role in the diagnostic criteria of interstitial cystitis. We report a multiplexed biosensor for simultaneous detection of interleukin-1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> and vascular endothelial growth factor on the same chip exhibiting rapid and accurate sensing capabilities at point-of-care. These two urine biomarkers showcased a significant increase in patients with interstitial cystitis compared to healthy controls. The developed biosensor detected and monitored interleukin-1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\alpha$</tex> and vascular endothelial growth factor simultaneously in a linear detection range of 0.01 to 100 pg/mL and 1 to 1000 pg/mL, and a detection limit of 1 fg/mL and 10 fg/mL, respectively. In addition, high sensitivity, high selectivity, and reproducible performance of the fabricated multiplexed sensor manifest a huge potential in the real-time determination and clinical analysis of interstitial cystitis.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Wideband MEMS Energy Harvester Using Graph Neural Network
abstract: Piezoelectric microelectromechanical system (MEMS) vibration energy harvesters commonly experience frequency incompetence in real-world applications. Operating at higher frequencies is often insufficient due to the low-frequency nature of ambient vibrations. The operational frequency range, so-called bandwidth, is a crucial characteristic especially under the unpredictable or uncontrollable ambient vibration conditions. In this study, we propose an innovative design methodology for piezoelectric MEMS energy harvesters that incorporate multiple cantilevers and masses to convert vibration to electricity as a power source. To achieve optimal performance, we employ a machine learning approach by using a graph neural network (GNN) model trained with finite element method (FEM) simulation data. Along with the trained model, we focus on optimizing the geometry sizes of the proposed structure to reach the largest harvested voltages and the frequency metrics by using a genetic algorithm. The optimized harvester exhibits six low resonant frequencies from 91.17 Hz to 102.54 Hz, featuring advantageous wideband nature, in addition to significant voltage outputs.

articleTitle: A Novel Phase Error Quantitative Characterization Method for Whole-Angle Micro Hemispherical Resonant Gyroscope
abstract: This article studies the effect of the control circuit phase errors on the micro-hemispherical resonant gyroscope (µHRG) under whole-angle (WA) mode. The causes of the phase error in WA µ HRG are first analyzed. Then, a WA dynamic model containing phase error is established, and the impact of the phase error in WA mode is analyzed. The analysis demonstrates that the phase error induces the coupling between the orthogonal control loop and the angle detection loop. Based on the coupling relationship of the self-precession control voltage to the orthogonal control voltage, a novel phase error quantitative characterization method is proposed, and the phase error is characterized. The characterization result shows a phase delay error of 13.44° in the WA µHRG control circuits. The phase error calibration is conducted using the characterization result. The results show that after calibration, the WA µHRG's angular velocity drift error reduced from 2.0016°/s to 0.38°/s, reduced by 81%; the zero bias instability reduced from 0.605°/h to 0.438°/h, reduced by 27.6%. The results validate the validity of the presented phase error characterization and calibration method.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Enhanced EMG Armband with an Interactive Game for Effective Wrist Rehabilitation
abstract: Wrist rehabilitation is essential for patients recovering from injuries or surgeries to regain mobility and strength. This study introduces a novel approach using a deep learning-enhanced electromyography (EMG)-based armband integrated with an interactive game. The custom-designed armband captures EMG signals from wrist muscles and processes them with an advanced deep learning model to interpret five wrist movements: power grip, extension, flexion, radial deviation, and ulnar deviation. These movements are translated into game actions, creating an engaging and motivating rehabilitation experience. The game adapts to the patient's progress, offering personalized challenges to promote continuous improvement. Our system achieved classification accuracies of 94.48% for subject-dependent and 91.18% for subject-independent approaches, demonstrating its effectiveness in wrist rehabilitation.

articleTitle: Lightweight Object Detection Model for a CMOS Image Sensor with Binary Feature Extraction
abstract: For the coming IoT age, we propose an object detection system using a CMOS image sensor capable of extracting binary feature data in order to reduce the power consumption of recognition systems. First, a lightweight deep neural network (DNN) for feature data is verified based on YOLOv7. The presented model is comparable to the YOLOv7-tiny in the number of parameters and FLOPs, but improves the object recognition accuracy of large objects AP<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> 50 by 6.6%. Additionally, the presented model for the feature data reduces GPU power consumption by 39.2% compared to the original YOLOv7 that processes RGB color images. Secondly, an on-chip signal processing technique for the CMOS image sensor is proposed to extract binary feature data. The simulation results demonstrate that the size of 1-bit feature data is reduced by 96.0% at the cost of a image classification accuracy degradation of 8.3% compared to the 1-bit RGB color image.

articleTitle: Event-Based Real-Time Fall Detection Using YOLOv8 and LSTM
abstract: Addressing the critical issue of fall detection among the elderly as global aging intensifies, this study develops an innovative system that integrates event cameras with advanced object detection and Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTM) to accurately identify fall incidents. The research methodology involves the utilization of these technologies to capture dynamic changes in the environment and analyze data through machine learning algorithms, ensuring the system operates effectively even in low-light and privacy-sensitive environments. The experiments conducted on the URFall and Le2i datasets demonstrate a 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> accuracy rate in fall detection, proving the system's efficacy in real-world scenarios. These findings indicate that the proposed system not only significantly improves the safety of elderly populations by providing timely and accurate fall detection but also pushes forward the boundaries of computer vision technology in health care applications.

articleTitle: Integrated Silicon-On-Insulator Based Mesh Membrane for Continuous Monitoring in Organs-on-a-chip
abstract: Porous membranes play a crucial role in organ-on-chip (OOC) models mimicking barrier functions like e.g., brain, intestine, and lungs. These membranes act as basement membranes for cell growth and communication via their pores, while also serving as physical barriers between chip compartments. Integrating electrodes close to the cells will allow continuous cell culture monitoring, but direct integration into the membrane presents challenges. Moreover, while natural extracellular matrix protein-based membranes are beneficial over synthetic ones, electrode integration onto such biological membranes is challenging ifnot possible at all. To address these challenges, we present the silicon-on-insulator (SOI)-based mesh membrane (SMM) as a support for a biologically relevant collagen-based membrane for the cell culture. The SOl material of our SMM allows for electrode integration, thus facilitating the impedance monitoring of the cell culture. Here we integrated the SMM into well plates, Transwells, and OOC devices highlighting its versatile applicability across different in vitro setups. We demonstrate its biocompatibility by modeling vasculature utilizing human-induced pluripotent stem cell-derived endothelial cells. In the future, the electrical impedance of the cell culture will be monitored providing non-invasive measurement of the cell layer development in real time.

articleTitle: System Integration of an Implantable Drug Delivery Device for Long-Term In-Vivo Experiments
abstract: The Nanochannel Delivery System (nDS) is a remotely-controlled active drug delivery device intended to treat chronic diseases. This work is focused on system integration and characterization towards long-term in-vivo experiments on sustained drug release. The design included a wireless charging system, improved release control system, and the introduction of temperature sensing. The engineering process prioritized compactness and energy efficiency, and its results, concerning improved functionality, energetic efficiency, and communication performance indicated compliance with biocompatibility and functional requirements set by chronic experiments lasting years.

articleTitle: Direct Estimation vs. Indirect Metrics: Machine Learning Techniques for Cardiac Output Estimation
abstract: Cardiac Output (CO) is crucial for assessing health, ensuring optimal blood pressure (BP) for oxygen delivery. Non-invasive CO (NICO) monitoring is promising for pre-hospital emergencies, and traditional monitors are impractical. Leveraging AI, this work explores NICO estimation for mobile health monitoring. We compare techniques, including direct CO, BP-based, and Stroke Volume-Heart Rate (SV-HR) based CO Estimation, and examine body weight's impact on CO estimation. Due to a lack of public CO datasets, we curated data from 43 subjects, including electrocardiography (ECG) and photoplethysmography (PPG). CO computation involves extracting features from ECG and PPG, using similarity measures (Euclidean, Manhattan, and Chebyshev distances) and a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to estimate CO/SV. CO via BP uses the estimated BP values fed to CNN. Experimental results show superior CO estimation through SV and HR, outperforming direct and BP-based methods by 4.85% and 4.57% for R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, 23.17% and 22.29% for RMSE, and 22.93% and 27.07% for MAE, respectively. However, BP-based CO performs comparably to SV-HR method, indicating potential for an efficient, BP integrated NICO monitoring system.

articleTitle: Radioluminescent Nuclear Battery for the Application of Self-Powered Sensors
abstract: The sensors applied for harsh environments have an urgent need for high power density, long-life, and maintenance-free power sources. The radioluminescent nuclear batteries (RLNBs) stand out for its high reliability and high-power output when using high energy beta-emitting sources. However, it is necessary to improve the energy conversion efficiency (ECE) for practical application. In this study, the optimal designs for two kinds of highly efficient scintillating materials were proposed for enhancing their energy coupling efficiency at structure interfaces, respectively. In comparison with the conventional RLNBs, the integrated structures reduced the photon loss by improving the photon transport structure and enhancing the coupling of radioisotopes with scintillators, resulting in an increase of 38.2% in output power of RLNB based on ZnS:Cu, Al phosphor and an increase of 285% in luminescent intensity of RLNB based on GAGG:Ce scintillator, respectively. Both optimal structures are cost-efficient and feasible for practical applications.

articleTitle: Microfluidic Sensor for Label-Free Corrosion and Biofilm Monitoring Using Electrical Impedance Spectroscopy
abstract: Microbiologically induced corrosion (MIC) is a major issue in several industrial settings, such as in the oil and gas industry, marine industry, as well as civil infrastructures. Measuring and monitoring of MIC is of high interest; however, traditional techniques only show average corrosion, are limited in resolution, and often require bulky instruments. In this study, we develop a microfluidic sensor using electrical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) for label-free continuous monitoring of metal corrosion as well as biofilm formation in parallel with high accuracy and high sensitivity. Two pairs of interdigitated electrodes (IDE) are integrated in each sensor. One pair is made of two different metal fingers, corrosion-resistant gold electrode finger on one side and an opposing electrode finger made of corrosion-susceptible metal of interest, for corrosion monitoring. The other pair is made of only gold electrode fingers, thus non-corrosive, to monitor biofilm formation. Corrosion-associated microorganisms were cultured in the sensors, and corrosion and biofilm formation were monitored based on impedance change for 4 days. As the corrosive metal corroded and the biofilm was formed on the IDE over time, the electrical impedance changed, allowing monitoring and measuring of real-time metal corrosion and biofilm formation. We developed a compact, easy-to use, and low-cost impedance-based sensor and successfully demonstrated that it can be used for continuous corrosion and biofilm formation monitoring with high sensitivity, accuracy, and high-throughput fashion.

articleTitle: Can QR Codes be used to readout Colorimetric Gas Sensors? A Back-Compatible Color QR Code with an Embedded CO2 Sensor Dye
abstract: Colorimetric dye readout devices have been explored extensively, with many approaches relying on complex hardware setups that stabilize the illuminant and capture conditions, typically involving attachments to smartphones or other digital cameras. In this work, we introduce a cost-effective sensor fabrication pipeline to embed a colorimetric dye in a QR Code, enabling readout by any standard smartphone without the need for specialized equipment. QR Codes, as established machine- readable patterns, offer a robust platform for integrating gasometric active dyes. Our approach ensures the preservation of QR Code data integrity by employing a novel method for maintaining back-compatibility throughout the pattern creation process, avoiding the limitations of dye placement solely in the center or outside the QR Code. We demonstrate this concept by embedding a CO2 sensor dye in a QR Code, while the QR Code presents a link to our website and a traceability ID. The dye is based on a pH-sensitive dye that changes color in the presence of CO2, focused on Modified Atmosphere Packaging (MAP) applications.

articleTitle: Optodevice-in-Sphere for Biaxial Tilt Sensing
abstract: A compact dual-axis tilt sensor utilizing chip-scale GaN optoelectronics is presented. The sensor comprises a cross-shaped optoelectronic device enclosed in a glass sphere, employing mineral oil as a liquid pendulum. The device integrates a light emitter and four independent detectors, designed to detect changes in the air-oil interface induced by dual-axis angular tilts. The sensor exhibits a linear response to an angle range of ±80° on both X- and Y-axes, with sensitivities of 40 nA/° and 37 nA/° respectively. It also demonstrates negligible inter-axis crosstalk, a resolution of up to 0.10, fast response, and high stability. Owing to its compact dimensions, the sensor facilitates integration into detection targets, rendering it an ideal candidate for real-time monitoring applications.

articleTitle: Resolution Upscaling of 3D Time-of-Flight Sensor by Fusion with RGB Camera
abstract: 3D time-of-flight (3D ToF) cameras enable depth perception but typically suffer from low resolution. To increase the resolution of the 3D ToF depth map, a fusion approach with a high-resolution RGB camera featuring a new power efficient edge extrapolation algorithm is proposed, implemented and benchmarked here. Despite the presence of artifacts in the output, the resulting high-resolution depth maps exhibit very clean edges when compared to other state-of-the-art spatial upscaling methods. The new algorithm first interpolates the depth map of the 3D ToF camera and combines it with an RGB image to extract an edge map. The blurred edges of the depth map are then replaced by an extrapolation from neighboring pixels for the final high-resolution depth map. A custom 3D ToF and RGB fusion hardware is used to create a new 3D ToF dataset for evaluating the image quality of the upscaling approach. In addition, the algorithm is benchmarked using the Middlebury 2005 stereo vision dataset. The proposed algorithm typically results in a perceived effective upscaling factor in the order of two or more in both the x and y directions.

articleTitle: Single-Step Laser Fabrication of 3D Free-Standing Origami MEMS Thermal Sensor
abstract: This paper presents a facile fabrication approach for micro-electro-mechanical systems (MEMS) thermal sensors, utilizing laser ablation and origami techniques to create a 3D free-standing structure. A single-step fabrication for a micromachined metal structure was demonstrated using a fiber laser. Thin nichrome sensing structures as small as 45.1 ¼m width were fabricated, with an electrical resistance of up to 6 Ω and a TCR of 390.39 ppm/°C. Thermal analysis via infrared thermography revealed that the free-standing structure exhibits a diminished thermal mass. The voltage response for airflow demonstrates the sensing ability of the fabricated structure, showcasing its potential for airflow sensing applications.

articleTitle: A Self-Biased Strontium Ferrite-Nickel Ferrite Compostite and PZT Bilayer for Magnetic Field Sensors
abstract: Magnetoelectric (ME) composites are promising materials for use as magnetic sensors and arrays for applications such as medical imaging. The search for ME composites with high sensitivity and self-magnetic-biasing to eliminate the need for external bias is in progress for several years. Here we report on a novel approach to obtain strong ME coupling without the need for a dc magnetic field. We have used a bilayer composite obtained by attaching vendor supplied PZT and a piezomagnetic composite comprising of M-type Sr-ferrite, a hard ferrite, and spinel NiFe204, a soft ferrite. We carried out a systematic study of structural, compositional, magnetic and magnetostrictive properties of the synthesized ferrite composites at room temperature. We use the lock-in technique to measure ME voltage coefficient of the bilayer composites formed by the ferrite composites and PZT shows a value of ~26 mV/cmOe at room temperature. We attribute the zero-bias ME strengths to the large bias provided by the magneto-crystalline anisotropy associated with the ferrite composites.

articleTitle: Electrolyte-Gated Field-Effect Transistor-Based Sensor for Nanoplastic Detection: A Sensitivity Investigation of Two Nanoplastic Models
abstract: Nanoplastics (NPs) accumulating in the environment pose a severe environmental threat, harming both animals and humans. This urgently calls for reliable, fast and easy to use sensing methods. In this work we investigated the use of an electrolyte-gated field-effect-transistor (EG-FET) based sensor with a carbon nanotube (CNT) semiconducting channel (EG-CNTFET) for the detection of NPs in aquatic environments. A variety of NP models, made from different materials and with different surface modifications, are nowadays available. Here, we compared the EG-CNTFET sensitivity using two NP models: polystyrene NPs with both non-functionalized and carboxylated surface. The EG-CNTFET devices presented a sensitivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$22.6 \mu A/(1mg/ml)$</tex> for non-functionalized NPs, and of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$20.9 \mu A/(1mg/ml)$</tex> for carboxylated NPs. This sensitivity is attributed to the hydrophobic interaction between CNTs and the NPs. Indeed, through atomic force microscopy, NPs were observed on the CNTs network. This study offers a starting point for future use of EG-FET-based sensors for detection of environmentally relevant NPs.

articleTitle: A Magnetofluidic Nucleic Acid Cartridge for Multiplexed Detection of Respiratory Pathogens
abstract: Multiple, rapid, and inexpensive on-site nucleic acid tests for respiratory pathogens have become an important development direction in the point-of-care testing (POCT) field in recent years. Magnetofluidic control is a branch of various microfluidic methods that is simple to operate and does not involve pumps or valves. However, detecting multiple targets through this technique is often difficult. In this work, six targets in the cartridge were detected in parallel through ultrasonically resuspending magnetic beads and evenly dividing the magnetic beads in a uniform magnetic field. The cartridge constructed in this paper was applied for the detection of respiratory influenza A, influenza B, and SARS-CoV-2, and a detection sensitivity of up to 1 copy/μL was achieved; thus, the cartridge demonstrates great potential for on-site detection of respiratory pathogens.

articleTitle: System for Measuring Material Properties and Surface Roughness of Objects from Microscopic Images
abstract: The present paper introduces a method for non-contact estimation of the type of material and the surface rough-ness for objects using images obtained by an optical microscope. The experimental results verified that the maximum surface roughness could be measured as the distance between the initial focal point and the final focal point as a microscope camera is moved towards an object. The type of material and the surface roughness can be used to estimate the friction coefficient which provides important tactile information for grasping and manipulating an object by robot hand systems.

articleTitle: ME-Net: A Network for Scale-Variant Objects in Harsh Underwater Detection Scenes
abstract: Underwater object recognition is a key technology in the field of underwater exploration. However, current under-water imaging tasks often face significant object scale variation under severe quality degradation. This paper proposes ME-Net, a salient object detection network that fuses information from multi-scale effective receptive fields (ERF) for scale-variant objects in underwater scenes. Specifically, we design an ERF-Server module to dynamically adjust ERF in the fusion phase, enabling enhanced multi-scale features across multi-resolution semantics interactions. Our network with refined ERF and resolution features utilizes both global and local information more comprehensively and better adapts to scale variations of underwater objects. Experiments on underwater image datasets UFO-120 and MAS3K demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other state-of-the-art underwater image methods.

articleTitle: Dual-Coupling Induced Singularities and Ultra-Sensitivity in Non-Hermitian Electromagnetic Systems
abstract: We herein introduce a new type of non-Hermitian sensing system respecting the parity-time (PT) symmetry, which is established by a dual-coupling (i.e., inductive and capacitive coupling at the same time) scheme. We demonstrate that this dual-coupled structure can not only exhibit the spectral degeneracy-exceptional point (EP)-but also an additional divergent point (DP). Further, the occurrence of this DP can be engineered as will by manipulating the strength of two types of coupling, which may even make the DP coalesce with the EP. Beyond the EP, we show that the existence of DP may greatly enhance the eigenfrequencies bifurcation, rendering an unprecedented sensitivity. We also provide experimental validations by practical measurements of temperature and relative humidity, which agree well with our theoretical analysis. Our work may open new paradigms for investigating PT-symmetric electronic sensors.

articleTitle: A Miniature Self-Decoupled Multiaxis Force Sensor via 3D Orthogonal Configuration
abstract: Multiaxis force sensors can provide crucial physical contact information for intelligent robots, surgical tools, biomedical instruments, and teleoperation systems. In particular, miniature multiaxis force sensors can be easily integrated into scenarios with limited dimensions. In this paper, we present a miniature self-decoupled multiaxis force sensor (SD-MFS) that utilizes disk-shaped coils in a 3D orthogonal configuration to detect the multiaxis movements of the conductive film based on the eddy-current effect. Benefiting from the 3D orthogonal configuration, the SD-MFS has a self-decoupled multiaxis force sensing output. By adopting the folding mechanism in the electronics design, a signal conditioning circuit is also embedded in the inner frame. The fully integrated sensor prototype has an overall dimension of only <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10\times 10\times 10\text{mm}^{3}$</tex>. The prototype achieved a force measurement resolution of 0.3 mN in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$x-$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y-$</tex> axes, 1.9 mN in the z-axis, with a low cross-talk of 2.5% and 1.6% in the x- and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$y-$</tex> axes. The SD-MFS shows promise for being readily implemented in application systems ranging from robotic hands to biomedical instruments.

articleTitle: Wireless Readout System for Pressure Monitoring Using FFF-Printed Mold Fabricated Flexible Piezoresistive Sensors
abstract: Flexible piezoresistive pressure sensors are critical components in wearable technology, extensively utilized in domains such as healthcare and sports analytics. However, achieving optimal sensitivity for different applications across diverse pressure ranges remains challenging. This paper presents a novel approach to fabricating these sensors using a synthesized graphene-polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) ink and fused filament fabrication (FFF) printed molds, which allows precise control over sensor layer thickness. The innovative combination of the PDMS-graphene ink with the FFF-printed molds results in customizable sensor performance tailored to diverse pressure ranges. Additionally, a compact, portable data acquisition system built on a printed circuit board (PCB) is introduced. This wireless PCB efficiently collects and transmits data from the fabricated sensors, showcasing a scalable, cost-effective solution for comprehensive pressure monitoring across various applications.

articleTitle: Using Triple Reverse-trapezoid Cantilevers and Unique Driving Method to Extend the Bandwidth of MEMS Microspeaker
abstract: This study demonstrates a piezoelectric MEMS microspeaker containing triple reverse-trapezoid cantilever membranes. A unique driving method is also presented. The design features: (1) reverse-trapezoid cantilever membranes providing better electro-acoustic efficiency, (2) two additional reverse-trapezoid units in higher frequencies expanding the overall bandwidth, (3) a unique driving method, which named the enhanced terminated driving method can solve the SPL response issue by suppressing the unwanted motion, (4) the center anchor design can enhance the fault tolerance of the fabrication and decrease the disturbance among membranes. The proposed microspeaker shows SPL (Sound-Pressure-Level) above 80 dB within the frequency range of 1.0 kHz ~ 8.0 kHz when actuated by 0.707 Vrms+7 V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">DC</inf> and above 70 dB from 1.0 kHz ~ 14.1 kHz. The proposed design could be integrated with common dynamic drivers to compensate the insufficient SPL at higher frequencies.

articleTitle: Single-Shot Efficient Depth Imaging Based on Time-Compressive CMOS Image Sensor
abstract: We propose an efficient depth imaging with temporal compressive sensing. Using a charge-domain coded shutter sensor based on an indirect ToF sensor, we can achieve robust observation against multi-path interference (MPI) similar to direct ToF. We achieve low cost and accurate depth estimation from coded shutter images without recovering the complete temporal response of the scene.

articleTitle: High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Detection: Towards Multiplex Point-of-Care Detection of HPV Using an Easy-to-use Device
abstract: This study demonstrates the use of degenerate primers in combination with CRISPR-based detection for high selectivity measurements of high-risk HPV types. We found that the E6 genes are more suitable for this purpose than the L1 gene, and the lbCas12a performs better than AsCas12a in differentiating between HPV types. Initial steps toward integrating this method into an easy-to-use device have been taken, with future research focusing on incorporating the entire process, including DNA extraction, target amplification, and target detection, into a single device. This advancement aims to make primary HPV screening feasible in low-resource settings, improving accessibility and early detection capabilities.

articleTitle: Human Presence and Attention Detection Through Stand-Alone Low Resolution Time-of-Flight Sensor
abstract: A novel approach to human presence and attention detection using stand-alone low resolution Time-of-Flight (ToF) sensor is introduced. Compared to traditional camera based methods, it significantly reduces power consumption and algorithmic complexity, and meanwhile it enhances user privacy. Alongside the description of the implementation, accuracy under various use case definitions are also evaluated. Optimization for storage space and computational complexity is also analyzed.

articleTitle: An Integrated Triple Sensing Electrode Design for Biochemical Applications
abstract: In recent years, the demand for Internet of Things (IoT) and Point of Care (PoC) technologies has been increasing rapidly. Integrating multiple sensing functions and mechanisms into a single device has gained attention to reduce construction costs, achieve simultaneous detection of multiple variables in complex environments, and enhance the performance of the biosensor for medical applications. In this study, we utilized a simple and rapid thermal dewetting process to generate a layer of gold nanoisland (AuNI) structures on indium tin oxide (ITO), achieving a multifunctional sensing device capable of electrical, electrochemical, and optical sensing. In the electrical sensing mode, the device functions as an extended-gate field-effect transistor (EG-FET), demonstrating a sensitivity of 41.03 mV/pH for ion concentration detection. In the electrochemical sensing mode, the device serves as a working electrode for electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) analysis, fitting well with the Randle circuit model with a constant phase element. Moreover, the Kramers-Kronig (KK) validity test showed an error value of less than 0.5%, confirming the device's suitability as an electrochemical system. In the optical sensing mode, the device exhibited a sensitivity of 66.96 nm/RIU for environmental refractive index detection due to the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect. This multifunctional sensing device holds significant potential for applications in the IoT market and serves as a biosensing platform capable of multimodal biomolecule detection for PoC use.

articleTitle: A 0.45°/h Lissajous Frequency-Modulated MEMS Gyroscope
abstract: This paper reports the test results of a DISK gyro working in the Lissajous frequency-modulated (LFM) mode based on dual digital phase-locked loops (PLLs), which track the resonance frequencies of the two vibrating modes of the gyroscope with direct frequency reading, thus avoiding the use of specific frequency converting circuit. Furthermore, automatic gain control (AGC) using parametric excitation is implemented to mitigate the impact of the driving force misalignment angle on gyroscope output. The temperature coefficient for the gyroscope scale factor in LFM mode is 48ppm/°C and the maximum vibration of zero offset is 0.0694°/s over the temperature range from −30°C to 60°C, which is due to the relatively large mismatch of electromechanical conversion coefficients of two vibration modes. The bias instability (BI) improves from 0.6°/h to 0.45°/h after driving force misalignment angle suppression using parametric excitation, and the angle random walk is 0.14°/√h, which is the best result reported for the LFM gyroscope as a result of the relatively large mechanical sensitivity of the sensor.

articleTitle: Flexible, Non-Invasive, and Wearable Fish Heart Rate Monitoring Tag for Guiding Aquaculture in Marine Ranching
abstract: The welfare of farmed fish has emerged as a significant concern. Behavioral and physiological stress responses in fish are widely recognized indicators of compromised welfare. Heart rate and heart rate variability in response to various stimuli have been utilized to gauge stress levels. Implanted heart rate tags can cause non-circadian heart rates post-surgery, impacting the normal activities of farmed fish and potentially leading to abnormal mortality. In response, we proposed a flexible wearable fish heart rate monitoring tag for marine ranched farmed fish. This system is lightweight, harmless, and biocompatible, allowing seamless integration with the fish body without impeding natural movement or behavior, thereby providing precise guidance for scientific aquaculture in marine ranching.

articleTitle: An Ultra-light and Flexible sEMG Active Probe for Patch-like Muscle Activity Monitoring
abstract: Surface ElectroMyoGraphy (sEMG) constitutes a valid tool for monitoring muscle activity in sports, rehabilitation, control of Human-Machine Interfaces (HMIs), and telemonitoring. To extend its applicability beyond clinical settings, the wearability of acquisition systems is a key factor, allowing for reduced discomfort during use, acquiring signals without hindering movement, and reducing the risk of detachment during the acquisition. This paper proposes a flexible, lightweight (0.81 g), and extremely compact active probe, measuring 30 mm x 10 mm x 3 mm, produced using rigid-flex PCB technology. The experimental tests, conducted on five subjects, each one performing six dynamic movements, show that the developed probe is capable of acquiring good quality sEMG signals, with a median Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) of 10.9 dB. Additionally, the minimal power consumption of the active probe, amounting only to 0.732 mW, makes the probe suitable for battery-powered applications, e.g., activities of daily living long-term recordings.

articleTitle: Portable Intelligent Multi-Channel Electrochemical Analytical System with Self-Reconstruction Strategy and Edge Computing
abstract: Electrochemical sensors are of critical importance in a number of domains, including environmental monitoring, energy conversion, and biosensing. There is a clear trend toward miniaturization, intelligence, and wearability. Nevertheless, the versatility of these devices is frequently constrained by their bulkiness and cumbersomeness. In response to this challenge, this study developed a portable and intelligent multi-channel electrochemical analytical system equipped with chronoamperometry and cyclic voltammetry capabilities. A supplementary PCB adapter board connected by an FPC cable enables the support of up to eight independent channels. A software application has also been developed to enable real-time curve plotting, state control, and parameter adjustment. Additionally, the system employs self-reconstruction technology for automatic wide-range current measurement and incorporates edge computing for onboard anomaly detection. The proposed measurement system and data processing method highlight its extensive application prospects in the development of reliable and intelligent electrochemical devices.

articleTitle: AI-Driven rPPG Heart Rate Detection for In-Vehicle Monitoring
abstract: Road accidents are frequently attributed to driver conditions such as stress, fatigue, and drowsiness, all of which can be detected by heart rate (HR) monitoring. Remote photoplethysmography (rPPG) emerges as a promising non-invasive method that leverages standard camera technology to estimate HR by analyzing subtle skin color changes. In this article, we present a deep learning (DL) model capable of extracting HR from the rPPG temporal structure found in the public UBFC-rPPG dataset. The knowledge gained from analyzing this dataset, along with the absence of a database that reflects the dynamic conditions within a vehicle, prompted the creation of a novel Infrared (IR) dataset.

articleTitle: Flexible Coils Localization Using Optically Pumped Magnetometers for Biomedical Applications
abstract: Optically pumped magnetometers represent a breakthrough in magnetic measurements, enabling new applications across various fields including medicine. In this paper, we propose a novel electromagnetic tracking approach using optically pumped magnetometers to detect ac magnetic fields generated by small, thin, and flexible coils with sub-nanotesla noise levels. This approach could facilitate tasks such as catheter localization, monitoring of endoscopic capsules, and capturing object shapes without a line of sight. This first proof-of-concept demonstrates a position error of less than 3 mm in two dimensions. In addition, we investigated the impact of coil bending on tracking error, which is crucial for applications where the coil deforms during tracking. While similar tracking performance was observed up to 60° of bending, larger curvatures resulted in a significant rise in the tracking error.

articleTitle: Temperature Dependence of Accuracy of Thermal Conductivity Hydrogen Sensor
abstract: In this study, we developed a high-precision thermal conductivity H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> microsensor using a high-temperature micro-hotplate. When interfering gases are mixed with N<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, the measured H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas concentration is lower than the actual H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration, affecting the accuracy of the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor. The accuracy of the H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor was improved by increasing the temperature of the heater because the sensitivity to CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, which is an interfering gas that decreases H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor accuracy, significantly decreased. The accuracy of H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor was improved by a factor of 2.6 times by operating at 342°C compared with operation at 92°C. Notably, operation at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 450^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>, where CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensitivity is predicted to be zero, will eliminate the influence of interfering gases. Because thermal conductivity H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensors are known for their long lifespan property, this high-precision thermal conductivity H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor is the best candidate for applications that require both long lifespan and high H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-sensing accuracy.

articleTitle: Impedance Flow Cytometer Tailored to the Real-Time Detection and Characterization of Microorganisms
abstract: Impedance flow cytometry is a powerful tool for real-time, label-free investigation of individual cells based on their electrical properties. It is therefore a promising approach for providing insight into bacterial extracellular electron transfer and enabling microbial fingerprinting. However, obtaining sufficient signal to noise with bacteria having micron or sub-micron dimensions remains a challenge. The geometric parameters of the electrofluidic cell were therefore optimized on the basis of a model that takes into account both the impedance detection pathway and the microorganism. For realization of the device, a microfabrication technique was developed. Finally, validation experiments were performed using fluorescent polystyrene beads, latex beads and priesta megaterium bacteria. The results show that the electrofluidic cell is capable of detecting all tested microparticles and microorganisms. In addition, the detected phase change shows the capacitive behavior of the priesta megaterium membrane, which can thus be used as a fingerprint for this microorganism.

articleTitle: Characterization of Vibration Sensitivity of One-Port and Two-Port MEMS Microphones
abstract: Micro-electromechanical system (MEMS) microphones (mics) with two ports are receiving considerable interest in both industry and academia, with the prospect of achieving higher directional sensitivity than their one port counterpart. However, two-port mics measures the pressure differences that exists inside the soundwave itself to record sound, which is fundamentally smaller than the absolute pressure measured in typical one-port mics. This typically commands the use of softer sensing element that are potentially more prone to interference from external vibrations. This work derives a universal expression for microphone sensitivity to vibration and validates it experimentally for two emerging two-port mics. We find that the acoustically-referred vibration sensitivity of two-port MEMS mics, in unit of measured acoustic pressure per external acceleration (i.e., Pascals per g), does not depend on the sensing element stiffness nor on its natural frequency. The vibration sensitivity of two-port MEMS mics is also shown to be inversely proportional to frequency as opposed to the frequency independent behavior observed in one-port MEMS mics.

articleTitle: A Smart, Energy-Efficient, and Low Cost Portable Device for Continuous Breath Analysis
abstract: The detection of breathing patterns and inferring one's state (physical, mental, or social well-being) remains a difficult task in the current research community. Moreover, early recognition of abnormal respiratory patterns can aid the clinician in early intervention to prevent further deterioration of the patient's condition [1]. In this work, we present a smart and low-cost portable medical device designed for continuous breath monitoring. Our system leverages advanced sensor technology combined with novel signal processing algorithms to achieve high sensitivity and accuracy in detecting breath patterns.

articleTitle: Flexible Tactile Sensing Using PDMS/TiO2 Based Capacitor with MOSFET Structure
abstract: In this paper, we present a flexible capacitive tactile sensor based on a polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) elastomer, which is well-suited for a wide range of applications. The sensor incorporates an n-channel depletion-mode MOSFET to achieve an extended gate architecture. To enhance the sensing performance, TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles are incorporated as nanofillers, resulting in an improved dielectric material ideal for highly sensitive capacitive pressure and tactile sensors. The 99PDMS-01TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanocomposite (comprising 99 wt % PDMS and 1 wt % TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is utilized for promising flexible tactile sensor applications due to the synergistic effects between the PDMS matrix and TiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanoparticles, which enhance both the mechanical and sensing properties of the composite. The fabricated sensor exhibits a sensitivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{30} \boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{A}/\mathbf{kPa}$</tex> within the range of 0-10.5 kPa and a sensitivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{9} \boldsymbol{\mu}\mathbf{A}/\mathbf{kPa}$</tex> in the range of 10.5-30 kPa.

articleTitle: GaN Monolithic Chips for Rapid Temperature Sensing
abstract: In this work, a monolithically integrated GaN-based chip for rapid temperature measurement is fabricated and characterized. The monolithic design enables the compact integration of an array of light emitters and a detector on a chip-scale GaN-based platform. Its operation eliminates the reliance on external components, offering enhanced operational simplicity and cost-effectiveness. Notably, the developed chip exhibits a highly linear response to temperature variations, spanning from 25°C to 100°C, with its dynamic response to temperature fluctuations being verified. Moreover, the ability to track and distinguish the respiratory state of volunteers, including the amplitude and rate of exhalation and inhalation, holds immense practical significance, presenting its potential for rapid measurement ability in practical applications.

articleTitle: Estimation of Stress Distribution at Adhesive Edge by Inverse Analysis of Deformed Shape Data
abstract: This study has developed a method to estimate the stress distribution at the adhesive edge by applying an inverse analysis to deformed shapes of adherends. The deformed shape of the adherend is measured using strain sensors and laser displacement meters, and the stress distribution at the adhesive edge was estimated by the inverse analysis of the measured deformed shape. The Tikhonov regularization parameter is found to be optimal when the sum of the estimated interfacial stresses is close to the actual load value at delamination. Comparison with the results of the direct analysis using the conventional finite element method confirmed the validity of the method., as the stress singularity index and intensity of singular stress field of the stress distribution showed good estimation results.

articleTitle: Effect of Metallic Ion Implantation on Dark Current Distributions of Silicon-Based CMOS Image Sensors
abstract: Accidental metallic contamination is known to have a deleterious impact on the dark current characteristics of silicon-based CMOS image sensors (CIS), especially when metallic species are present in the depletion region of the photodiode. Solving a contamination issue requires a clear identification of the contaminant signature on the sensor response. In this study, different metallic species were voluntarily introduced in the photodiode region of Si-based CIS wafers, using ion implantation at relatively low doses. The dark current spectroscopy (DCS) technique is used to quantify the influence of each of these metallic species on the sensor performance. The results presented herein could aid in their identification after accidental contamination in a clean room environment, particularly in the cases of Pd, Mn and Nb, for which the references in the literature are scarce.

articleTitle: Compact GaN-based Optical Force Sensors with Hemispherical Reflectors
abstract: In this work, a compact GaN-based optoelectronic chip with a hemispherical reflector for force sensing is demonstrated. The GaN chip integrates one light-emitting diode (LED) and four photodetectors (PDs) on the sapphire substrate. The polydimethylsiloxane is mixed with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CaCO}_{3}$</tex> powders to form a reflective layer through a cost-effective molding method. This deformable layer can respond to the applied force, thereby modulating the intensity of light captured by the on-chip PDs. Validated through a series of experimental tests, the developed sensor with a size of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4\times 4\times 1.9 \text{mm}^{3}$</tex> is capable of detecting normal and shear forces ranging from 0 N to 0.8 N, achieves a low detection limit of 0.01 N, and maintains high stability over 4200 cycles. The significant advantages, including a small footprint, high stability, and low detection limit, make the sensor suitable for a wide range of applications that require precise force detection.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of MEMS Vibration Sensors for Throat Microphones
abstract: This study demonstrates the development of miniaturized throat microphones using MEMS-based vibration sensors and a voice conversion algorithm. A MEMS-based accelerometer, attached to the throat along with an audio microphone, records the throat vibrations and sound wave data from the TMHINT Mandarin Chinese script, consisting of 320 sentences. The recorded vibration signals are processed to match the microphone signals by an artificial neural network and evaluated using objective metrics such as the Mean Opinion Score (MOS) and Short-Time Objective Intelligibility (STOI). The converted results show that a MEMS vibration sensor with a bandwidth of 2.4 kHz is sufficient for the purpose of voice recovery.

articleTitle: Ultra Miniaturized Absolute Rotary Encoder Integrated into Hinge Joint
abstract: In minimally invasive endoscopy systems, traditional optical tracking solutions commonly employed in computer-assisted surgeries are not applicable due to the lack of line-of-sight. Electromagnetic tracking (EMT), in contrast, has been used as an alternative, but it is limited by its susceptibility to interference from metal objects. The accuracy achieved with EMT is often inadequate for many applications. To address this limitation, for endoscopes based on rotational joints, we propose a novel solution: a miniature absolute rotary encoder integrated into a hinge joint. Our system characterization reveals excellent performance, with a precision of 0.0009° (corresponding to a resolution of 13 bit over a range of 45°) and an accuracy of ±0.2°. These results are achieved within a compact footprint of 2 × 1.5 × 1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, making it suitable for integration into minimally invasive endoscopy systems.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Biosensor Using Methylene Blue as an Electrochemical Mediator Coupling with DNA Aptamer
abstract: Methylene blue (MB) is known as a redox mediator as well as a DNA intercalator. We evaluated the electrochemical impedance dependent with the MB concentration with a fixed concentration of a redox mediator <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{K}_{4}[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_{6}]/\mathrm{K}_{3}[\text{Fe}(\text{CN})_{6}]$</tex>. The results showed that charge transfer resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}_{\text{ct}})$</tex> decreased with increasing the MB concentration, which indicated that charge transfer was enhanced. We designed to develop new electrochemical biosensor using above characteristics of MB. DNA aptamer coupling with MB was synthesized and coated on Au electrode. We demonstrated the sensing property of this newly sensing system to measure thrombin, which is one of serine protease. The results showed that trace amounts of thrombin could be detected. This method enables early detection of cancer and other diseases.

articleTitle: Optimal Growth Conditions for Human Endometrial Stromal Cells in a Bidirectional OoC with Porous Membrane
abstract: Human Endometrial Stromal Cells (hESCs) undergo a differentiation process with dramatic changes in cell functions during the menstrual cycle, which is called decidualization. This is an important event for implantation of the embryo for successful pregnancy. Defective decidualization can cause implantation failure, miscarriage, and unexplained infertility. Decidualization can be recapitulated in vitro by culturing primary hESCs with medroxyprogesterone acetate (MPA) or cAMP[1]. This study will find the optimal culture parameters for in vitro decidualization through the surface design of the porous membrane in the bidirectional microfluidic chip. Furthermore, the physiology of hESCs under culture would be analyzed in the bidirectional organoid chip.

articleTitle: Monolithic Integration of Audio Filters for Frequency Response and THD Modulation in MEMS Microspeaker
abstract: This study presents a design to monolithically integrate audio filters in piezoelectric MEMS microspeaker to modulate frequency response and total harmonic distortion (THD). The proposed design has two major features: (1) leverage the advantages afforded by micromachining technology to integrate audio filters composed of passive (electronic) components and piezoelectric microspeaker onto a single chip; (2) the two-stage filter is implemented on the commonly ineffectively utilized anchor area of MEMS microspeaker to achieve selectable low-pass filtering effect that adequately modulate the bandwidth and reduce the THD. Measurements conducted using the standard ear simulator demonstrate that with the 1st stage filter, the upper limit of 85±5dB bandwidth of the microspeaker is extended from 2.2kHz to 2.9kHz, with 21.7% improvement in THD at subharmonic frequency and a 4.1% reduction at resonant frequency. With the 2nd stage filter, flat bandwidth is further extended to 3.7kHz. THD is improved by 38.3% at subharmonic and 4.9% at resonant frequency.

articleTitle: MEMS Based Rain Sensor
abstract: We report a novel sensing principle for disdrometer (rain sensor) based on a resonant scanning micromirror featuring high-speed detection in kHz range, accurate estimations of droplet rate, distribution, velocity, trajectory and two-dimensional (2D) shape. This high-speed ID MEMS scanner en-ables fast detection and compactness. We introduce a calibration technique to convert temporal information of passing objects, recorded on a high-speed point detector, into spatial information. Measurements of free-falling steel balls achieve a maximum error of 5 %. Raindrop distribution and velocity measurements show good agreement with theoretical values.

articleTitle: Synthetic Electrochemical Biosensor Data with Conditional Variational Autoencoders for Enhanced Predictive Modeling
abstract: Electrochemical biosensors (EB) have revolutionized various domains with their rapid and sensitive analyte detection capabilities. However, as EBs advance to tackle more challenging targets, the complexity of post hoc analysis intensifies, posing a significant bottleneck. Integrating AI with biosensing devices offers a promising solution, yet widespread adoption faces hurdles such as limited data availability. This study introduces a novel approach leveraging Conditional Variational Autoencoders to generate synthetic electrochemical data for augmenting training datasets. This approach aims to address the specific issue of data scarcity in the post hoc analysis of electrochemical biosensing data. Evaluation experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of incorporating synthetic data in enhancing prediction model performance, reducing the MRE by 41.16%, and achieving similar performance to a model trained with the full dataset by using only 50% of the training data supplemented with synthetic data. This work highlights a critical advancement, bridging the gap between AI and electrochemical biosensing, ultimately improving the efficiency and accuracy of post hoc analysis in this vital field.

articleTitle: Analyzing and Overcoming Strain-Rate Dependence for Triboelectric Self-Powered Pressure Sensors
abstract: Flexible pressure sensors have a wide range of applications, including health monitoring and wearable devices. Recent work has focused on developing pressure sensors that excel at measuring pressure in the ultrasensitive and low ranges, but often these sensors require a power supply. While recent works in triboelectric transduction schemes provide a solution to the power requirement, these approaches have largely ignored the strain rate dependence of their measurement technique. We explore this dependence using a low-cost, flexible, self-powered pressure sensor. The sensor consists of two interdigitated electrodes encapsulated in polyimide for stability. A polydimethylsiloxane dielectric friction layer is coupled to the electrodes, and pressure is measured via the generated voltage during sliding induced by uniaxial compression. The sensor was characterized at two strain rates, 50% s-1 and 100% s-1. While the maximum generated voltage was found to be different for each strain rate even at similar pressures, we found that the voltage integral over time provides a direct measure of pressure irrespective of strain rate. As a result, the sensor operates in a range of up to 5.5 MPa with an average sensitivity of 19.27 m V -ms kPa-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>•

articleTitle: Optical Long Base Hydrostatic Tiltmeter for Slow Earthquake Detection
abstract: We present an optical long base hydrostatic tiltmeter (OLBT) designed to be able to detect slow earthquakes in this work. Interrogation is carried out by a high precision fiber-based Fabry-Perot interferometer that detects variations of the surface liquid level in a hydrostatic leveling vessel. Field results from a 41 m long OLBT installed along the Gulf of Corinth, Greece, near the Psathopyrgos fault since mid-February 2024 demonstrate a tilt resolution of 0.2 nanorad and a stability of better than 0.15 µrad per month. This can potentially enable the instrument to be employed for detecting and monitoring slow slip events over the long term in earthquake precursor research.

articleTitle: Bimodal Surface Acoustic Wave Sensor Based on Vanadium-Doped Zinc Oxide Film for High-Precise Pressure Measurement Enabled with Temperature Compensation
abstract: In this work, a bimodal surface acoustic wave (SAW) sensor employing a vanadium-doped zinc oxide (VZO) thin film is presented for high precise pressure measurement. The sensor is designed with multilayer waveguide structure to operate on both Rayleigh and Lamb modes to achieve temperature compensation. A 3-mask process platform on a SOI wafer based on MEMS technology is used for the development of the sensor. The influence of the oxygen/argon ratio during RF magnetron sputtering of VZO films are studied. Thepiezoelectric coefficient of the VZO film can reach to 120.3 pm/V,indicating high piezoresponse. The Rayleigh mode resonating at 312.5 MHz and the Lamb mode oscillating at 448.3 MHz of the presented sensor are observed. Calibrations of the pressure at different temperatures ranging from 25°C to 170°C have been conducted. The compensated pressure measurement error is demonstrated to be no more than 2.1%, showing a promising application prospects in high precision pressure measurements.

articleTitle: Development of Unit Functions of Electrowetting-on-dielectric Digital Microfluidics
abstract: This paper presents the development of various unit functionalities of electrowetting on dielectric (EWOD) digital microfluidics (DMF). To build systems such as micro total analysis system and high throughput drug discovery and screening system, multiple unit functions of microfluidics need to be integrated monolithically. For the seamless integration, this paper focuses on EWOD DMF as the main microfluidic tool and demonstrates successful unit functions of; i) microextraction for sample preparation, ii) ion-selective sensor array for high-throughput chemical sensing, iii) 3-dimensional cell-based assay, and iv) high-throughput organic chemical reactions.

articleTitle: Remote Gait Behavior Monitoring System for Older People Based on Wearable Sensor
abstract: Gait describes moving the body in a specific direction. Gait analysis, as an effective tool to monitor humans in daily life, can provide technical support for reducing the risk of falls by studying the gait characteristics of older people. In the last decade, the increasing health challenges posed by population aging and chronic noncommunicable diseases have generated significant interest in wearable physiological measurement devices. Wearable sensors have the characteristics of small size and portability, which have great potential in human health care. They can play a crucial role in monitoring human gait in health-related issues and have advantages in gait data collection and processing. In this study, a portable and wearable gait recognition system based on a wireless body area network was designed to solve the problems of single data signal collection and poor portability of the collection equipment in the existing gait recognition system. Based on the wearable acquisition node, the system can collect, transmit, process, and analyze the human body's plantar pressure signal and posture signal in real time, which can realize the effective recognition of human gait and remote data transmission and monitoring. The gait recognition system is used for data collection, feature extraction, and classification, and the classification accuracy can reach more than 90%, which provides a reliable basis for elderly gait behavior monitoring.

articleTitle: Soft Capacitive Sensor and Wearable Sleeve Towards Measuring Fluid Retention
abstract: Measuring fluid retention, or edema, is essential in clinical diagnosis and treatment of disorders. We demonstrate a soft, passively shielded capacitive strain sensor and sleeve worn over the upper arm to detect arm swelling during exercise. In a human subject study, the sensor captured an increase of approximately 7 pF pre- to post-exercise, which corresponded to circumference measurement increase of 0.7 cm. This work has applications to soft and wearable robotic systems for the continuous monitoring of persistent edema with minimal discomfort.

articleTitle: High Sensitivity Lateral Hall Device in Silicon on Insulator (SOI) Platform
abstract: In this work, a novel lateral Hall device (LHD) with deep trench fingers is designed and fabricated in the O.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> silicon-on-insulator (SOI) platform.
