The deep trench finger serves to regulate the path of bias current in the magnetic-sensitive well, thereby rendering current-related sensitivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{S}_{\mathbf{I}})$</tex> I insensitive to the size of the signal electrode. The proposed LHD presents a Slover 1000V / AT with an offset lower than 2.5m V. In addition, the proposed LHD presents high stability in temperature from 25°C to 225°C.

articleTitle: Copolymerized Ion-Gel for Dimethyl Methylphosphonate Sensing: from Material to Multi-type Sensor Applications
abstract: Ionic gel (Ion-Gel), prepared through the polymerization of ionic liquids and polymers under specific conditions, typically exhibits strong surface polarity, allowing it to adsorb molecules and potentially function as gas-sensing materials. In this study, we present Ion-Gel material designed for Dimethyl Methylphosphonate (DMMP) detection, which is prepared through in-situ copolymerization of ion liquid, polymer monomer and DMMP sensitive molecules. The paper showcases the detailed and universal applications method of the Ion-Gel sensing material in three different types of gas sensors (surface acoustic wave type, flexible capacitor/resistor type, and field effect transistor type), respectively. All of the sensors work at room temperature. The low limit of detection can be reached to 100 ppb, which has a response time of less than 30 s.

articleTitle: A Novel TimesNet Based Electronic Nose Data Recovery Method
abstract: During the process of electronic nose detection/monitoring, factors such as sudden sensor failures and unstable systems often lead to a large number of missing values in the data. To address the issue of missing data in electronic nose system, this paper proposes a novel method for data recovery based on TimesNet. An improved TimesNet network is designed to transform the electronic nose data from one-dimensional (1D) to two-dimensional (2D), embedding adjacent data and cross-period data of the sensor array into a 2D tensor. Features are then extracted by three convolution kernels of the same scale, and then fused to enhance the representation ability of the input data. A batch data at loss rates of 10%, 20%, 30% and 40% acquired from an electronic nose composed of an array of 10 sensors are processed and recovered. Compared with the typical methods, the mean square errors are reduced by at least 10 orders of magnitude, showing a big enhancement.

articleTitle: Development of a Portable Optical Sensor for Low-Concentration Copper Sulfate Detection in Water
abstract: Currently, spectrophotometry is the dominant detection method in semiconductor industrial manufacturing and environmental pollution investigation. However, the complex design of the optical structure in existing water quality systems makes these machines bulky and requires large sample volumes, preventing the widespread adoption of lowconcentration solution detection. To address this issue, an optical sensor with a chip-based Micro-Spectrometer was designed for water quality detection in this study, specifically for copper sulfate detection. The developed device can detect concentrations ranging from 2.5% to 0.04%, covering the human lethal dose (500 ppm). Experimental results show that the R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of the detection line is higher than 0.98, and the CV value is less than 5%, indicating that the device is suitable for detecting low concentrations of copper sulfate.

articleTitle: Influence of Scallops in Deep Reactive Ion Etching on Vertical Comb-Based Sensors/Actuators
abstract: The Bosch deep reactive ion etching (DRIE) is a critical bulk-silicon-micromachining (BSM) processing for vertical comb-based (VC-based) sensor/actuator fabrication. However, scallop in the Bosch process leads to undesirable VC gap varying. Herein, influence of scallops on performance of VC-based sensors/actuator is presented. Firstly, mathematical modeling of scallop distribution on VC sidewall is established. From this, capacitance of VCs and electrostatic force of VC-drive (VCD) actuators are derived, including for rotating and piston types. Then, finite element analysis (FEA) is used as modeling verification. Results indicate that the varying amplitude and period of VC capacitance are attributing to depth and period of scallops, respectively. Moreover, limitation of VCD actuators' positioning accuracy due to scallop is given.

articleTitle: Leveraging Large Language Models and Fuzzy Clustering for EEG Report Analysis
abstract: In this paper, we explore the application of large language models (LLMs) to analyze Electroencephalogram (EEG) reports by clustering them into normal or abnormal classes. We employed fuzzy clustering techniques, leveraging Clinical-BERT, Meditron 7B, and Biomistral to extract robust features from clinical text. To address the high dimensionality of these embeddings, we used Principal Component Analysis (PCA) for dimensionality reduction while retaining critical information. The processed embeddings were subsequently clustered using Fuzzy C-Means (FCM) and Fuzzy J-Means (FJM) algorithms. Our methodology demonstrated flexibility in clustering, effectively handling the inherent noise and variability in medical data. The results indicated that FCM, although consistent, required more computational time as dimensionality increased. Conversely, FJM exhibited faster performance and was effective in avoiding local minima, albeit with some variability in clustering quality. These findings highlight the potential of specialized models and advanced clustering techniques in enhancing the analysis of medical reports.

articleTitle: Towards a Portable Multi-Gas Sensor for Environmental Gases with Miniaturized Photoacoustic Cells and Mid-Infrared Quantum Cascade Lasers
abstract: Current issues on air pollution monitoring or greenhouse gases emissions rely on the sparse use of expensive gas sensors. We target to develop a portable miniaturized sensor with the capacity of being gas-specific, lightweight and autonomous. We present here results obtained with our newly packaged Photoacoustique Module. We also present the development of its dedicated electronic companion system.

articleTitle: Online Non-Myopic Route Planning for Airborne Sensor Networks with Multi-Target Tracking
abstract: This paper introduces an online route planning strategy for airborne sensor networks (ASN) with the task of multitarget tracking within a non-myopic strategy. Leveraging a distributed covariance intersection rule for tracking processing serves to fuse the tracking data from ASN nodes. The posterior Cramér-Rao lower bound (PCRLB) regarding sensor's velocity and course is derived as the tracking performance metric to guide the route planning. Employing the MinMax criterion (i.e., minimizing the PCRLB of the target with the worst predicted tracking accuracy over a future time horizon), the non-myopic route planning problem for ASN is formulated. To address this high-dimensional optimization problem, a sequential particle swarm optimization algorithm is proposed. Numerical results validate the superior performance of the proposed non-myopic route planning strategy.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Low-Complexity Circuit for Event-Based Feature Extraction from sEMG
abstract: This paper presents an analog circuit for calibration-free event-driven myoelectric control of sEMG-based applications. The proposed solution is to be installed downstream of the conditioning chain of an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>EMG sensor and consists of a Sallen-Key filter, acting as a differentiator in the main sEMG frequency band, and a voltage comparator. The output of the circuit is a quasi-digital signal, in which the muscle activity is mapped onto the time distribution of digital events. The design phase focused on noise robustness, and a prototype was tested during in-vivo experiments on both upper and lower limbs. Among the obtained results, besides a current consumption of only 12.92 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu \mathrm{A}$</tex>, a median increase in the number of events of more than 25 % was achieved by varying the exerted muscle force in steps of 20 % MVC.

articleTitle: Fully Printed Low-Cost Ammonia Gas Sensor on Paper Substrate
abstract: Fabricating affordable, biocompatible, and biodegradable gas sensors presents challenges due to complex and costly traditional methods. Despite advancements, most paper-based gas sensors remain time-consuming and environmentally unfriendly. This study introduces a novel approach utilizing PEDOT, known for its biocompatibility and biodegradability, as both sensing and electrode material. PEDOT was deposited using dispense printing and spray coating techniques. The active layer was characterized for ammonia (NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) detection, evaluating passive (25°C) and active (60°C) recovery methods within the 10-50 ppm range. The sensor exhibits a linear sensitivity of 0.15%/ppm at 25°C and 0.10%/ppm at 60°C, with high reproducibility (standard deviation ≤ 0.5) and transient dissolution noted in citric acid over 7 days. Notably, active recovery enhances sensitivity by 50% compared to passive recovery. Optimal sensor performance was observed at 30% RH, demonstrating minimal variability. This flexible and biocompatible sensor shows promise for NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> sensing in delicate applications such as plant and health wearables, suggesting potential for eco-friendly applications in green electronics.

articleTitle: Laws of Long-Term-Drift Performance for a Highly Sensitive MEMS Gravimeter Over 500 Days
abstract: This paper reports a MEMS gravimeter that has been working continuously over 500 days, which demonstrates the long-term drift properties of MEMS gravimeters for the first time. The results reveal that the long-term drift features a logarithmic model, which seriously conflicts with the linear model widely used for removing drift in relative gravimeters. In addition, the proposed MEMS gravimeter exhibits an ultra-low self-noise floor of less than 1 µGal/√Hz, comparable to commercial quartz spring gravimeters. This work represents a crucial progress that promotes MEMS gravimeters from laboratory research towards engineering applications.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Dual Point Photoplethysmography Device for Assessing Impact of Diabetes on Arterial Stiffness
abstract: Arterial stiffness is a condition that results from the thickening and loss of elasticity in arterial walls, commonly observed in subjects with peripheral arterial disease (PAD). The paper aims to examine the variation in arterial stiffness at two different points, point A (3 cm above the foot on the posterior tibial artery (PTA)) and point B (on the foot) to facilitate early detection and monitoring of PAD in people with diabetes. A novel non-invasive photoplethysmography (PPG) device was developed to acquire signals from the PTA using optical sensors, a microcontroller, and an analog-to-digital converter. Signals were collected from three categories: ‘Healthy and Young (< 40 years, N=20)’, ‘Age matched controls (AMC) (> 40 years, N=20)’, and 'Diabetic and Aged (> 40 years, N=20)‘. The study found consistent pulse wave patterns in healthy subjects but distinct variations in those with diabetes and PAD. In subjects with diabetes, the stiffness index increased from point A to point B. By evaluating pulse signals at multiple points, the study captured arterial property variations at point B caused by PAD, which might not have been evident in single-point analyses. This approach improves the thoroughness of the detection and emphasizes the significance of acquiring signals from multiple points to evaluate arterial health accurately.

articleTitle: A Fast Start Method for Whole-Angle Micro-Shell Resonator Gyroscope
abstract: This paper reports a fast start method for the Micro-Shell Resonator Gyroscope (MSRG) working on the whole-angle mode. The micro-shell resonator has a high Q factor of about 1,000,000 to achieve high performance, while its narrow mechanical bandwidth makes the start characteristic sensitive to the initial frequency accuracy of the digital phase-locked loop (DPLL). In this paper, the start method based on self-exciting and frequency-tracking is proposed and the control strategies and parameters during start-up are designed. Experimental results verify that this method can correct the frequency within 0.3 seconds even under an initial frequency misalignment of over 500Hz. The starting performance of MSRG achieves a start time of below 2 seconds under a wide temperature range of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-40\sim 60^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. Benefiting from the fast and reliable start-up process, MSRG can have greater potential for mass production and practical application.

articleTitle: Topology Reconstruction Approach for Distributed Blind Equalization Over Sensor Network
abstract: Distributed blind equalization in wireless sensor networks (WSNs) attracts much attention in the field of in-network processing since the data signal can be recovered without the training signal and the desired output at the receiver. Therefore, it has a wide range of applications in various fields such as science, medicine, and agriculture. However, the performance of the distributed blind equalization is susceptible to the transmission channel conditions, especially for the ill-channel conditions. To overcome this problem, we propose a topology reconstruction approach to discard the affect of the ill-channel condition based on the analysis of the received signal for all sensors in each local sensor network (LSN). In addition, the weights of each sensor node are re-designed in order to further improve the prediction accuracy of blind equalization. In the computer simulations, average mean square error (a-MSE) and average symbol error rate (a-SER) are used to evaluate the performance of the conventional and proposed methods. Compared with the conventional (state-of-the-art and non-cooperative) methods for distributed blind equalization, the proposed method achieves better a-MSE and a-SER.

articleTitle: Sensor System for Water Stress Detection Using In-Plant Transmitted Signal Amplitude Evaluation
abstract: Environmental sustainability has become a significant topic, especially in recent years. Extreme natural phenomena and food insecurity related to the rising world population have highlighted the need for a new approach to agriculture. Smart Agriculture solutions may represent a viable answer to boost productivity, reduce emissions, and optimize human labor through the utilization of several new technologies and techniques in the climate-change scenario. From this perspective, the following paper proposes a sensor system capable of evaluating the plant's health status based on stem electrical impedance from a local and global point of view. In particular, the receiving system is able to sense the global stem impedance, monitoring the amplitude of a signal transmitted inside the plant itself. The system injects a square wave into the plant, and thanks to the proposed sensor, it is possible to read a frequency proportional to the amplitude of this signal collected from another point of the stem. The developed system has been tested on a tobacco plant, showing correlations of 0.94 and -0.97, respectively, for the local sensor and global sensor with respect to the soil water potential.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning-Based Pork Freshness Classification with a Batteryless Sensor Tag
abstract: This study presents a battery-free system for classifying pork freshness using ensemble learning. Our system uses a 915 MHz RF energy harvester to power sensor tags with a 3D Quasi Yagi antenna. These tags monitor carbon dioxide (C02), total volatile organic compounds (TVOC), and temperature emissions from pork during storage. We collect these emissions every five minutes over five days to train our machine learning model. Pork freshness is classified into three states: fresh, semi-fresh, and rotten. The ensemble learning model combines five primary learners-Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional LSTM (Bi-LSTM), and One-Dimensional Convolutional Neural Network (1D-CNN)-with a 1D-CNN meta-learner. The system achieved 96.944% accuracy, 96.957% precision, 96.944% recall, and a 96.951 % F1-score in detecting pork spoilage. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of our battery-free sensor system for real-time pork freshness monitoring, providing a non-invasive, sustainable solution for food safety and quality control.

articleTitle: Investigation of Hydrogen Spatial Distribution During Smoldering Fire in Capacitive MEMS Hydrogen Sensor Using Pt Thin Film
abstract: This paper describes a capacitive MEMS hydrogen sensor that is the first to utilize the change in film stress due to metal oxide reduction. Pt thin film is used as a hydrogen-sensing film in which tensile stress increases when the Pt oxide of the film surface is reduced by hydrogen. Since oxidation of Pt in air and reduction of Pt oxide by hydrogen occur simultaneously and cancel each other out, a SiO2 oxygen barrier was applied to control the oxidation to ensure high sensitivity. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis showed that hydrogen penetrated the SiO2 barrier, and the reduction of Pt oxide proceeded. The capacitance of the capacitive MEMS hydrogen sensor decreased as the Pt oxide was reduced by hydrogen, with the response depending on the hydrogen concentration. A fire experiment was performed to evaluate the spatial distribution of hydrogen produced by a smoldering fire, and it was shown for the first time that hydrogen remains near the ceiling.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Sensing of the Colorectal Cancer BRAF p.V600E Mutation Using a Lab-on-Chip Integrated DNA Amplification Analysis Method
abstract: Despite the increasing occurrence and high mortal-ity rate of colorectal cancer (CRC) in low resource settings, the lack of reliable point-of-care (POC) devices remains a critical issue in its diagnosis. Recent advancements in the miniaturisation of biosensors have contributed to the progression of lab-on-chip (LoC) technology for cancer diagnostics, where this study proves the feasibility of detecting the BRAF p. V600E mutation, one of the major CRC biomarkers, through loop-mediated isothermal amplification (LAMP) reactions conducted on integrated ion-sensitive field-effect transistor (ISFET) sensors. Our findings reveal that LAMP reactions conducted in a qPCR machine and on the LoC device are allele-specific and produce comparable output yields, with a limit of detection (LOD) of 500 copies/μL and time-to-positive (TTP) under 15 minutes. Preliminary results suggest that specific, non-specific and control reactions that have been conducted in parallel produce distinct trends in their output signals. A signal processing methodology was developed to quickly distinguish between positive and negative outputs using simple data manipulation and analysis techniques. The LoC system has proven to be a robust method for detecting cancer mutations and has the potential to be adapted for multi-reaction sensing. This research is an essential step towards creating a practical multigene cancer panel for POC testing, which would be a game-changer in cancer diagnostics.

articleTitle: Creep Property of Polyvinylidene Fluoride in Water When Used as Binder for Battery Electrodes
abstract: Although polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is one of polymer materials and has excellent mechanical properties, PVDF has viscoelastic properties and occurs easily creep deformation even at room temperature. In this study, creep tests in air and water were performed on PVDF and electrode materials using PVDF as a binder to investigate the creep properties of PVDF when immersed in water. The results show that PVDF, both alone and as a binder, appears to be affected by long-term immersion in water. Compared to air, the creep transition region became longer, and the strain increased in water due to softening of PVDF.

articleTitle: Temperature Sensor Fabricated via Direct Laser Writing on Copper Nanoparticles Coated Paper Substrates
abstract: Measuring temperature is crucial, as it affects biological, chemical, and physical processes, impacting climate control, healthcare, and industrial operations. This work introduces a novel flexible and fully printed temperature sensor, based on copper nanoparticle electrodes direct laser written and coated with a screen-printed film of Poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) on a paper substrate. The sensor shows a linear response with a sensitivity of -0.15 %/°C in the 30-50°C temperature range. Hysteresis evaluation at different humidity levels (30% RH, 50% RH, and 80% RH) reveals the lowest average hysteresis at 50 % RH, indicating the most stable and reliable performance at these conditions. Our sensor platform combines the advantages of biocompatible nanomaterials and paper substrates, offering a scalable and ecofriendly solution for temperature sensing, potentially applicable in plant wearable scenarios in precision agriculture.

articleTitle: Edge AI Algorithm for FBG-Based E-Skin Touch Localization on Embedded Electronics
abstract: The field of collaborative robotics is constantly growing given the central role that safe human-robot interactions are gaining in the current era of Industry 4.0. To act and interact, robotic systems are increasingly being either natively equipped with or adapted to house sensing devices. In this scenario, tactile sensors are fundamental to detect impacts, accurately manipulate objects and enable learning from demonstration strategies. The development of such systems requires technological efforts in terms of both design, for their seamless integration in robots, and software programming, for achieving reliable and prompt reactions to relevant events. In this study, an edge AI algorithm deployed on an embedded device for the recognition of contacts on an FBG (Fiber Bragg Grating)-based e-skin is presented. A Convolutional Neural Network has been trained offline to localize touch events occurred on the e-skin. The performance of the algorithm assessed on the test set reached a mean absolute error on the three cartesian coordinates of less than 4 mm. The algorithm has been then ported to a microcontroller board for real-time testing of both simulated and concurrent contacts. The achievements of this work pave the way to new opportunities for collaborative robotics applications through intelligent FBG-based artificial tactile skins.

articleTitle: Multi-Sensor Integration in Orthopedic Implants for Total Knee Arthroplasty
abstract: In this work, we introduce the design and fabrication of an innovative multi-sensor system integrated into a knee implant, aimed at the early detection of postoperative complications. This system incorporates pH and temperature sensors for infection detection, accelerometers for measuring flexion angles, and force and moment sensors to identify postoperative complications, particularly mechanical issues. A 13.56 MHz RFID-based system was employed for power and data transmission. Collaborative efforts with clinicians and project partners were crucial in designing, testing, and validating the prototype, with initial experiments conducted on cadaveric specimens.

articleTitle: Exploring pH Sensing in MoS2-Based ISFETs with 2D-3D Gate Oxide Stacks
abstract: In this work, we present a theoretical investigation of the application of 2D oxides in 2D channel material-based ISFETs for pH sensing applications. The investigation involved a stack of 2D oxide and 3D oxide in the front gate of ISFET, where the 2D oxide has an interface with the 2D channel material. To perform the proposed study, a combination of a calibrated TCAD setup and a compact model validated against experimental data are used. The proposed study compares the performance of the 2D-oxide-based 2D channel material with purely 3D oxide-based 2D channel material ISFET. In the 3D oxide-based 2D channel material ISFET, the interface trap charges at the oxide/channel interface are accounted for to calculate sensitivity. The calculated current sensitivity and transconductance to drain current ratio sensitivity is 29 nA/pH and 0.651 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}^{1} \text{PH}^{-1}$</tex> respectively with the density of interface traps at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1\mathrm{x}10^{12}\text{cm}^{-2} \mathrm{V}^{-1}$</tex>. A current sensitivity of 36.36 nA/pH and transconductance to drain current ratio sensitivity of 0.338 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}^{1} \text{pH}^{-1}$</tex> is achieved using 2D-3D gate oxide stack in a 2D material-based ISFET. The proposed ISFET can be utilised to develop highly sensitive next-generation pH sensors.

articleTitle: Characterization of Graphene-based Flexible One- Side-Coil NFC Tag for Temperature Sensing
abstract: This paper proposes a flexible one-sided coil NFC (Near Field Communication) tag integrated with a temperature sensor, enabling real-time and battery-less temperature monitoring. The flexible tag antenna and temperature sensing circuit are made of graphene-based conductive materials and PET substrate, ensuring the necessary flexibility to conform to different structures of items. The incorporation of a temperature sensor (NTC thermistor) with the NFC tag allows for continuous monitoring of the temperature, enabling early detection of any deviations from the desired temperature. Experimental results show that the tag performs well in monitoring temperatures across a wide range from 3°C to 60°C, covering cold, room, and hot temperature, indicating its suitability for various temperature monitoring applications. The temperature sensing application has been verified in food temperature monitoring, where the tag can be detected in the range of 1 to 2 cm while attached to various food structures and storage temperatures, proving the flexibility and reliability of the NFC tag.

articleTitle: Development of a 2–4 Double Arbiter PUF Design on FPGA with Enhanced Performance
abstract: Implementation of delay-based Physical Unclonable Functions (PUFs) on FPGAs poses significant challenges due to high requirements, such as the generation of unique and reliable keys. These requirements must be fulfilled, especially when using PUFs in security applications, otherwise security cannot be guaranteed. In addition, it must be ensured that physical disturbances such as fluctuations in the ambient temperature do not have a major impact on the performance of the PUF and therefore on security. In this paper, the implementation and evaluation of a novel 56-bit 2–4 Double Arbiter PUF (DAPUF) is presented. For performance analysis, the proposed 2–4 DAPUF is investigated with 20 Digilent Nexys-3 (AMD-Xilinx Spartan-6 FPGA) boards and a large data set of 30 million challenges under varying ambient temperature in the range from 0°C to 50°C. Our experimental results show that the proposed 2–4 DAPUF is resistant to temperature fluctuations. Here, the maximum change in reliability amounts to 1.18 %. For randomness and uniqueness, the changes are less than 0.50 %. Furthermore, our results show that performance can be significantly improved by combining PUFs with XOR operations.

articleTitle: Free Space Detection Using Automotive Radar
abstract: This paper proposes a novel free space detection method based on Occupancy Grid Map (OGM) with automotive radars. Because radar sensors on commercial vehicles provide sparse detections, the limitations of radar sensors become clearly apparent in existing OGM generation methods. For generating high-quality OGM with automotive radars, we augment additional radar detections using radar attributes such as Doppler velocity and bounding boxes and use them as inputs of a deep learning-based OGM generation model. We also apply a Bayesian framework to enable OGM generation that considers the dynamic changes in the driving environment. The performance of the proposed method is verified through experiments using real driving data, demonstrating significantly improved performance compared to the result with sparse radar detections.

articleTitle: Wireless, Fully soft, Pressure and Temperature Sensors for Sensitive and Robust Diabetic Foot Ulcer Monitoring
abstract: This study introduces a wireless, fully soft sensor for the sensitive and robust monitoring of foot pressure and temperature, advancing the prevention and diagnostics of diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs). The sensing system leverages parity-time (PT) and PT-reciprocal scaling (PTX) symmetry, creating an exceptional point (EP) that induces rapid frequency shifts in response to sensing parameters, demonstrating high sensitivity. Additionally, the system's eigenfrequencies generate a pair of balanced resonant dips in the reflection spectra, enabling the accurate retrieval of pressure- and temperature-induced resistive perturbations by measuring the resistance of the reader, independent of reader-sensor alignment. The results indicate that the proposed sensing system can robustly monitor pressure (0–400 kPa) and temperature (25–50 °C) with various reader-sensor distances, effectively addressing the longstanding issue linked with inductively coupled passive sensors. Moreover, by integrating a custom-made resistive pressure transducer, the proposed sensor remains fully flexible and soft, showcasing significant potential for DFU management and a broad spectrum of wearable healthcare applications.

articleTitle: Effects of Annealing Temperature on Morphology and LSPR Sensing Performance of Au Nanostructures
abstract: Localized Surface Plasmon Resonance (LSPR) stands out as a powerful sensing method, where nanostructures can be formed by depositing a thin layer of metal onto a substrate followed by Rapid Thermal Annealing (RTA). This study investigates the influence of annealing temperature on the morphology, optical properties, and sensitivity of gold nanostructures fabricated on glass substrates. Utilizing thermal annealing, gold thin films were treated at temperatures ranging from 550°C to 850°C to create distinct nanostructures, which were evaluated using scanning electron microscopy (SEM) and extinction spectra measurements. The analysis revealed a significant impact of annealing temperature on the LSPR characteristics, including a blue shift in the LSPR peak and changes in the full width at half maximum (FWHM) as nanostructure uniformity improved. Finally, we conducted measurements on different chips using glycerol-water solutions of various concentrations, observing that the sensitivity decreased with the annealing temperature. This research offers critical insights into the enhancement of LSPR-based sensors through precise manipulation of nanostructure formation, highlighting the pivotal role of temperature control.

articleTitle: Humidity Detection Based on Inorganic Topological Insulator Bi2Se3-Organic PEO Composite Film
abstract: Inorganic Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-organic PEO composites were prepared via a combined treatment of liquid exfoliation and mechanical blending for humidity detection at room temperature in this work. The experimental results show that the sensing performance is greatly improved after PEO introduction including the humidity detection range and sensor response. Typically, the Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>-PEO-3 sensor delivers a large response of 443 % and quick response/recovery speeds of ~11/2 s toward 75%RH. In addition, benign repeatability, hysteresis and selectivity are demonstrated. The humidity-sensing features are primarily originated from swelling behavior of hydrophilic PEO that distances the conduction pathways when adsorbing water molecules. This work exhibits an excellent application potential of Bi<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>Se<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> as a representative of topological insulators in the field of next-generation humidity sensors.

articleTitle: Flexible Electrochemical Biosensor with Graphene and Gold Nanoparticle Modification for Enhanced e-ELISA Point-of-Care Biomarker Detection
abstract: Point-of-Care (POC) devices used for medical applications such as disease detection, monitoring, and treatment, require certain levels of accuracy, efficiency, reliability, and accessibility. In order to meet these requirements, this study presents the development of a flexible electrochemical biosensor with a novel design and fabrication technique. This biosensor utilizes cost-effective and available materials, while incorporating surface modification techniques using graphene and gold nanoparticles to enhance sensitivity. The improved performance of the developed device is demonstrated through a comprehensive set of optical and electrochemical experiments, showing enhanced sensitivity, durability, repeatability, and limit-of-detection for electrochemical enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (e-ELISA) targets. The findings of this study highlight the potential of our biosensor to be utilized in wearable applications, thereby improving patient outcomes, and reducing healthcare costs.

articleTitle: Theory and Design of Tunable Localized Plasmonic Biosensors Using Au-Ag Bimetallic Alloy Nanoparticles
abstract: This study explores the potential of Au-Ag bimetallic alloy nanoparticles for LSPR-based biosensors. We present a theoretical framework that models analyte attachment to nanoparticles by considering the evolution of the analyte's refractive index relative to its concentration. Using glucose as a benchmark analyte, we calculate its refractive index and assess the performance of LSPR biosensors with varying molar fractions of Au-Ag alloys. Our findings demonstrate that Au-Ag alloy nanoparticles offer enhanced LSPR intensity and tunable chemical stability due to the molar fraction of Au, with the ability to precisely adjust the LSPR wavelength by modifying the alloy composition. This tunability provides significant advantages in sensitivity and specificity, advancing the application of Au-Ag alloy nanoparticles in biosensing technologies.

articleTitle: Understanding Electrostatic Sensing with Graphene: A Miniature and Versatile Alternative to Standard Technologies
abstract: Electric field measurement is becoming of primary importance in various domains, for both civil and military applications, such as early prediction of lightning or prevention of electrostatic discharges on satellites. Here, we propose a physical model of a highly sensitive electric field sensor based on a graphene field effect transistor, with a floating gate acting as an antenna. This model, based on the combination of the so-called graphene's transistor effect and the laws describing the potential of a floating conductor, is demonstrated using transistors made of graphene (grown by chemical vapor deposition) on a SiO2/Si substrate.

articleTitle: Electrochemical Fingerprinting for Discrimination of $\mathrm{A}\beta_{3-16}, \mathrm{A}\beta_{11-16}$ and their Pyroglutamate Counterparts, Related to Alzheimer's Disease
abstract: The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-amyloid <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{A}\beta)$</tex> peptides are believed to be crucial for Alzheimer's disease (AD) by forming toxic oligomers in the brain, which cause neuronal death. Consequently, these peptides serve as biomarkers of AD. Various forms of AP have been identified so far, and their levels vary between healthy and afflicted individuals. Moreover, forms naturally modified through pyroglutamylation at the amino terminus are characterized by higher toxicity and resistance to proteolytic degradation. The current methods focus exclusively on the determination of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}\beta_{1-42}/\mathrm{A}\beta_{1-40}$</tex> ratio, losing information on the broad spectrum of other forms, which could be at least as important as the routinely determined AP peptides. In this work, we proposed a novel detection strategy of short analogs of AP peptides: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}\beta_{3-16}$</tex>, APll-16, and their pyroglutamate counterparts related to Alzheimer's disease. The proposed approach is based on the chemometric analysis of voltammetric signals recorded in solutions of Cu(II)-A <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> complexes for generating and extracting characteristic fingerprints of the different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{A}\beta$</tex> analogs for their further discrimination.

articleTitle: MEMS Gas Sensor with On-chip Electrospun Ru-SnO2 Nanospheres Patterned by Photolithography
abstract: Over the decades, many high-performance gas-sensing materials have been developed, but integrating these materials with MEMS devices still faces challenges. In this paper, to address this challenge, we propose a method based on electrospinning and photolithography techniques, using photoresist to provide the required polymers and solvents in the electrospinning precursor. This precursor is then used for on-chip electrospinning, followed by patterning and calcination, to achieve on-chip growth of patterned gas-sensing materials. Using this method, we successfully obtained on-chip patterned Ru-doped SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanospheres. The sensors based on these materials exhibited excellent sensitivity, repeatability, and selectivity to acetone, demonstrating the potential of this method for practical applications.

articleTitle: Towards Wearable Acute Stress Detection and Mitigation via Real-Time Photoplethysmogram Feature Detection
abstract: Acute stress has been linked to an increased risk for adverse cardiac events, necessitating the development of techniques for continuous stress monitoring and regulation. Wearable sensing can be used to continuously monitor cardiovascular signals relevant to acute stress. However, to enable real-time stress mitigation techniques in a wearable system, both cardiac and vascular features of acute stress need to be extracted from these signals in real-time. We have developed an efficient algorithm capable of accurately extracting heart rate (HR) and photoplethysmogram (PPG) amplitude (PPGamp) from PPG signals on resource-constrained wearable devices. This algorithm was deployed on a custom-designed wearable device and was compared against a reference electrocardiogram and standard signal processing techniques in a protocol involving acute stressors. The device consumed an average of 113 mA during the protocol. Through correlation and Bland-Altman analyses, we found that the features extracted using our algorithm were significantly <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(p < 0.001)$</tex> correlated (HR: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r=0.919$</tex>, PPGamp: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I {=0.993}$</tex>) and strongly agreed with (HR: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 5$</tex> beats per minute difference, PPGamp: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 5\%$</tex> difference at 95% limits of agreement) those derived using the benchtop devices and post-processing algorithms. These results demonstrate our algorithm's ability to extract both the cardiac and vascular effects of acute stress in real-time, enabling future work in the area of wearable closed-loop stress detection and mitigation.

articleTitle: Defense Method Against Adversarial Example Attacks using Thermal Noise of a CMOS Image Sensor
abstract: With the development of IoT technology, edge AI has attracted widespread attention. However, edge AI shows vulnerability to adversarial example (AE) attacks, where invisible small perturbations can cause a convolutional neural network (CNN) to misclassify input images. Defense methods that add disturbance noise to the input images have been proposed as a solution to AE attacks on edge AI. In this paper, we first show that the defense method using disturbance noise is less effective when the noise generated (e.g., with an arithmetic algorithm) is predictable. Therefore, we propose a defense method using unpredictable noise based on thermal noise generated by an image sensor, along with a post-processing method for the thermal noise. An image sensor was utilized to generate 5-bit disturbance noise for defense against AE attacks based on thermal noise. Using the NIST 800–22 random number test, all items passed with high probability, indicating high randomness. It is also confirmed that the defense performance was improved by 24% when using the proposed post-processing approach.

articleTitle: Multispectral Imaging for Preliminary Burn Depth Evaluation in Mice with Tissue Section Analysis
abstract: This work presents a system that uses multispectral imaging (MSI) for burn depth evaluation. The system emits 880 nm and 660 nm light onto burn area and captures the reflected light from burns. Using the images captured by the system, the oxygenation indices, including the concentration of total hemoglobin, deoxygenated hemoglobin, oxygenated hemoglobin, and tissue oxygenated saturation can be calculated by modified Beer-Lambert law and then used to evaluate the burn severity. An animal experiment was conducted to verify the system ability of assessing burn severity. The result shows that burn severity can be determined by observing the levels of the oxygenation indices at 72 hours after burning.

articleTitle: Improving the Reliability of Wireless Pressure Sensors by Optimizing the Fabrication Process
abstract: Smart stents equipped with LC wireless pressure sensors are currently a hot topic of research, designed to aid in diagnosing in-stent restenosis. The LC wireless pressure sensors, fabricated from SU-8 photoresist, offer exceptional biocompatibility and flexibility, making them suitable for implantation in the human body. However, the softness and heat-induced deformation of photosensitive polymers introduce significant performance variability in the fabricated LC wireless pressure sensors. This variability manifests as differences in initial resonance frequencies, sensitivities, and other performance metrics, which constrain the practical application of this technology. Our study addresses these challenges by implementing air elimination techniques, incorporating open windows, and enlarging capacitor plates. These modifications successfully reduced performance variability to 2.1% in initial resonance frequency and 6.4% in pressure response sensitivity. Consequently, we have demonstrated the fabrication of LC wireless pressure sensors with stable and reliable performance, advancing the feasibility of their application in smart stents for cardiovascular patients

articleTitle: Utilizing Electropolymerized Polyaniline Films for Acetic Acid Detection: A Proof of Concept
abstract: In the present study screen printed carbon electrodes have been modified by electrodeposition of polyaniline to detect acetic acid. Volatile acetic acid content needs monitoring for the manufacturing of premium wines. This acid content is in very trace amounts and hence electrochemical detection can provide a cost-effective testing standard for quality monitoring purposes. Electrochemical deposition of polyaniline on carbon electrodes is an efficient method to increase the conductivity and sensitivity of the sensor. Further this method of synthesis of polymers is simple, cost-effective, and environment friendly. The current sensor shows high sensitivity for acetic acid with the lowest detected concentration of 0.01mM and a linear increase in peak current with an r-square value of 0.97. The proposed carbon electrode modified with polyaniline exhibits potential for applications in monitoring food quality and microbiological development.

articleTitle: Toward Automatic Cardiovascular and Respiratory Assessment Using Automatic 6-Minute Walking Test
abstract: The aim of this study was to investigate suitable cardiorespiratory features for automatic six minute walking test for home monitoring using inertial measurement units and electrocardiography by recognizing walking and standing, estimating the intensity of the walking and assessing the physi-ological response to the walking. The walking was recognized from gyroscope and accelerometer signals from a wrist with accuracy of 84% using XGBoost. To estimate the functional capacity, heart rate, heart rate recovery time and respiratory rate were calculated from electrocardiogram and accelerometer signal, respectively. To evaluate the physiological response to the exercise, several features to describe the walking intensity were calculated from the accelerometer signal from the chest. Feature that best correlated with the heart rate, heart rate recovery time and respiratory rate was walking frequency with R value of 0.65, 0.47 and 0.55, respectively and relative change of 31 %. This was a pilot study to show that motion sensors and electrocardiography could be used to perform an automatic six minute walking test which could be used for example in assessing functional capacity of heart failure patients.

articleTitle: Exploration of Flavor Sample for Odor Reproduction In Mass Spectrum Space
abstract: Olfaction is one of the important senses. In particular, we often sniff food smells. In this study, we used mass spectrometry data of food to search for approximating odor reproduction recipes for odor components. We used principal component analysis, Nonnegative Matrix Factorization and Non-negative Least Squares algorithms for the analysis of 100 food samples. In particular, we analyzed 20 component odor recipes, Through the experimental results, the 20 odor components recipe is able to approximate the target odor with appropriate accuracy.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive and Moisture-Resistant 3D DC Electric Field Meter Based on Microsensors
abstract: This paper reports a 3D DC electric field meter (EFM), whose core detection component is three identical 1D microsensors. We propose an innovative inner-convex packaging solution to amplify the sensitivity of the microsensor, thereby enhancing the sensitivity of the 3D EFM. To suppress the impact of ambient humidity on the 3D EFM's measurement accuracy, a unique anti-humidity design structure is proposed. The test results indicate that the proposed 3D EFM's sensitivity is at least 4.64 times superior to the highest sensitivity of previously reported MEMS 3D EFMs. Remarkably, even in high-humidity conditions, the EFM can maintain linearity within 1%. Finally, the maximum relative deviation recorded is a mere 2.2% for any rotation attitude.

articleTitle: High-Pressure Silicon Resonant Microsensor Based on Microbeam Arrays
abstract: Distinct from conventional pressure sensitive diaphragm sensors, this study presents a novel design of a high-pressure silicon resonant pressure microsensor employing a microbeam array. This sensor utilizes microbeam arrays to regulate the axial stress of resonators, allowing two distinct resonant beams to experience tensile and compressive stress respectively when the sensor as a whole is subjected to pressure. This configuration enables accurate pressure measurements within the range of 0.1 MPa to 100 MPa. Resonator I exhibits a sensitivity of -122.45 Hz/MPa Resonator II shows a sensitivity of 64.80Hz/MPa and the differential output at 20°C is 187.25Hz/MPa ppm/MPa). Performance characterization of the fabricated sensor was conducted within open-loop and closed-loop systems. Finally, the microsensor exhibited high accuracy in closed-loop testing, with a maximum fitting error of 1.49kPa (0.03% FS) within a range of 0–5 MPa and -20 to 60°C.

articleTitle: Nd Modified Bismuth Ferrite Perovskite for Efficient Subtle NO2 Monitoring
abstract: Now a days human health and well-being are greatly impacted by indoor and outdoor air quality, where contaminants like nitrogen dioxide (NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) which is a potent candidate of greenhouse (GHG) gas can pose serious concerns, even at low parts per billion (ppb) concentrations. In this paper, we explored the use of Nd-doped Bismuth Ferrite (BiFeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) perovskite as a new material for highly sensitive detection of NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> gas at ppb levels. The study was showed an extensive experimental investigation to detect NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> by maintaining a real time environment scenario, which gave us the remarkable sensitivity and selectivity of this material by compared with other toxic gases. In addition, we delved into its potential as a preliminary tool for greenhouse gas detection or screening, capitalising on the link between NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> exposure and its effect on human health as well as living species. The results of our study were emphasized the versatility of Nd-doped BiFeO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> perovskite by different material characterization processes (like XRD, FESEM etc.) as a sensing platform, and it also shows good response (1.5 times at 500 ppb NO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) and stability (70 days) in the presence of humidity. This study marks a noteworthy advancement in the pursuit of affordable and effective methods to enhance air quality and safeguard public health.

articleTitle: Development of Microfluidic Platform for Refractive Index Measurement of Liquid
abstract: Our new platform measures the refractive index of liquid by combining a near-infrared (NIR) interferometry with a silicon cavity. NIR interferometry is conducted perpendicular to the silicon membrane and the cavity following the injection of a liquid into the cavity through parallel fluidic ports. After conducting refractive index measurements on five different pure liquids, the concentration of NaCI in DI water is accurately evaluated through refractive index measurements. Measured refractive index have an accuracy of within 0.5% of the reported values in the NIR.

articleTitle: Multi-Modal Sensor Fusion in Latent Embedding Space for Robust Autonomous Navigation
abstract: In this paper, we present a framework for multi-modal data fusion in the latent embedding space to enhance the robustness of autonomous navigation. Autonomous vehicles often rely on cameras and LiDAR, which are susceptible to degraded optical conditions. To address this, we fuse data from LiDAR, radar, and sonar using a shared latent representation, generated via a phased training approach with transformer-based models. This fusion mitigates the limitations of individual sensors and facilitates robust generation of 2D LiDAR point clouds. Our approach demonstrates improved performance in SLAM tasks, particularly under sub-optimal optical conditions, and introduces an adaptive anomaly detection mechanism for sensor reliability.

articleTitle: SPECTRE: A Dataset for Spectral Reconstruction on Chip-Size Spectrometers with a Physics-Informed Augmentation Method
abstract: Reconstructing usable spectra from an array of optical filters has been central to miniature spectrometers for many years. However, as optical sensors become more suitable for low-cost applications by exploiting sub-par filter characteristics, creating high-quality reconstructions has become increasingly challenging. There has been growing interest in data-driven reconstruction methods within the scientific community to address this issue. The main obstacle to progress in this area is the lack of publicly available and comprehensive datasets for spectral reconstruction. In our research, we propose a physics-informed data augmentation technique to significantly increase the size of datasets for spectral reconstruction and make our augmented dataset, containing 10117 samples, publicly available. Furthermore, we demonstrate the potential performance improvements achieved by training complex neural networks for spectral reconstruction using the augmented dataset. Our short benchmark indicates a performance increase of up to four times over the baseline.

articleTitle: LIF-SAR: Local Interpolation Function based SAR Imaging for Irregular Scanning Geometries
abstract: This paper introduces an efficient Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) image reconstruction for irregular scanning geometries referred to as Local Interpolation Function for SAR Image Enhancement (LIF-SAR). Irregular scanning based SAR imaging is becoming a necessity of-late due to the prevalence of freehand radar imaging using handheld radar devices. Unlike conventional SAR imaging, irregular scanning techniques yield a diverse sampling scales, posing significant reconstruction challenges. Motivated by generalizability of implicit neural networks, LIF-SAR aims to achieve enhanced SAR image across various scales. Using Non-uniform Fast Fourier Transform (NUFFT) based Range Migration Algorithm (RMA), we obtain the initial noisy SAR images which are then enhanced using the LIF based implicit neural network. By mapping the noisy SAR image onto a 2D feature map and employing a decoder function, we predict enhanced SAR image values based on surrounding 2D feature space. Comparative evaluations demonstrate LIF-SAR's superior qualitative and quantitative performance, achieving close to a 5dB improvement in PSNR and a 0.4 increase in SSIM over the existing classical NUFFT-RMA.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive, Multiplexed, and Accessible Digital Protein Measurement with MagDroplex
abstract: Highly sensitive and multiplexed protein detection is crucial across various biological contexts. Although the digital enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (dELISA) has enabled 1000-fold increase in sensitivity over traditional immunoassays, it involves sophisticated microfluidic devices for single bead trapping, has limited multiplexing capability, and lacks broad accessibility. To address these challenges, we present MagDroplex, an innovative approach that integrates magnetic beads-based proximity extension assay and fluorescence-coding droplet digital polymerase chain reaction (ddPCR) to transform the detection of protein into the quantification of fluorescence-coded DNA molecules. By detecting DNA rather than enzyme labels, our approach eliminates precise bead control as required in dELISA, facilitates concurrent detection of multiple targets through PCR multiplexing, and leverages the widespread adoption of ddPCR technology for broader implementation. As a proof of principle, we apply MagDroplex towards an 8-plex detection targeting human cytokines. Our approach demonstrates exceptional sensitivities for all the targets, while operating only across 2 fluorescent channels.

articleTitle: Enhancing Sensitivity and Size Efficiency in CMOS Extended Gate FET Biosensors
abstract: Field-effect transistors (FETs) are widely considered as one of the most promising electronic devices for rapid, sensitive, and label-free bio-detection. In many studies, floating gates are connected to extended electrodes to gather electrical charges of detected biomolecules. However, while the sensitivity typically increases with electrode size, this trend gradually diminishes beyond a certain threshold. This issue of over-design is critical to address, particularly in the development of large-scale biosensing arrays. In this study, we investigated this phenomenon using a transistor design accompanied by five extended electrodes with areas of 5 to 50 times that of the transistor. We comprehensively tested these devices for the detection of DNA hybridization from 0.1 fM to 10 pM. The results indicated a decline in the rate of sensitivity increase beyond an area ratio of 20X.

articleTitle: Impact of Finger Contact Force on Aortic Waveform Parameters Derived from Finger Photoplethysmography Using a Transfer Function
abstract: Objective. Photoplethysmography (PPG) technology is the basis of most wearable cardiovascular health monitoring devices. PPG-based monitoring typically uses heart rate (HR) analysis. Cardiovascular pulse wave analysis (PWA) could enhance PPG-based monitoring. Applied finger pressure may alter the waveform, limiting potential for PPG-based PWA. This study investigates that potential limitation. Design and Method. Radial tonometry and fingertip infrared PPG measurements were performed at 10 different applied finger pressure levels in participants (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{n}=\mathbf{18},\ \mathbf{41}\pm \mathbf{16}$</tex> years, 8 female) under resting conditions. Aortic pressure waveforms were derived by applying a generalized transfer function (GTF) (radial and PPG measurements) and a selective transfer function (STF) (PPG measurements). Differences (mean±standard deviation) of PPG derived aortic waveform parameters from radial tonometry derived waveform parameters were calculated and statistically compared. Results. When using the STF applied to the PPG at all applied forces, central systolic blood pressure and central augmentation index corrected to a heart rate of 75 beats per minute were overestimated. The GTF applied to the PPG underestimated the same parameters. PPG derived aortic subendocardial viability ratio and ejection duration displayed minimal differences from radial derived parameters. Reduced variability tended to occur at higher contact forces. Conclusions. In the context of cardiovascular health monitoring, finger contact force on a PPG sensor should be taken into consideration as some aortic waveform features were impacted by the applied force.

articleTitle: High-Performance Microfluidic Chip Calorimeter for Biomedical Applications
abstract: MEMS-based chip calorimeters are characterized by high integration, miniaturization, high sensitivity, and fast response. However, the sensitivity still faces challenges among biomedical and many other tiny thermal effect detections. This paper presents a miniaturized, highly sensitive microfluidic chip calorimeter with low reactant consumption. It consists of 0.32 uL microfluidic chambers and polyimide(PI)-based thermal sensor. The thermal sensor comprises a high- performance Bi2Te3-Sb2Te3 thermopile suspending on PI substrate. This greatly eliminates the heat dissipation of the reaction chamber, contributing to a high sensitivity. As a result, the chip calorimeter exhibits a power sensitivity of 8.64 V/W, and a thermal detection resolution of 201 nW. Besides, it performs excellently in detecting exothermic ethanol-diluted and glucose oxidation reactions. Moreover, with the help of enzyme immobilization process, it successfully detected glucose from the aqueous solution. These results indicate the chip calorimeter owns a promising potential in biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Hetero-Core Fiber Optic Glucose Sensor Coated with Glucose Oxidase Immobilized in pH-Sensitive Polymer Multilayer of Poly-L-Lysine and Poly Acrylic Acid
abstract: In this study, we propose a hetero-core structured optical fiber based glucose sensor which can sense different concentrations of glucose solutions on reaction with Glucose Oxidase immobilized on a pH sensitive polymer multilayer, which causes a pH induced refractive index change of the multilayer, which is sensed by the sensor.

articleTitle: YOLO-ICP: Deep Learning Integrated Pose Estimation for Bin-Picking of Multiple Objects
abstract: In this paper, we present a novel deep learning-integrated pipeline called YOLO-ICP that aims to estimate the six degree of freedom (6-DoF) pose of objects using RGB-D sensors and does not require pose labels to train deep learning networks. YOLO-ICP integrates a real-time object detection algorithm with a point cloud registration method to estimate the pose of multiple objects. We evaluated our approach by quantitatively comparing it with baseline models on the OccludedLINEMOD dataset. Experimental results illustrate that our approach outperforms baseline models in challenging scenarios with textureless and occluded objects. In particular, our pipeline shows superior performance when dealing with small and symmetric objects in terms of the ADD(-S) metric.

articleTitle: Vapour Recognition Based on Deep-Convolutional Neural Network: Portable Impedance Analyzer
abstract: Gas detection technologies are essential tools in maintaining safety and environmental standards across various applications. Through advanced sensors and analytical techniques, these systems aim to quickly detect and classify molecular content in an environment, providing valuable insights for early warning and effective response to incidents. In this work, we present the development of miniaturized, multiplexed, and connected electronic nose (e-nose) based on impedance spectroscopy technology. Our platform has been tested and optimized to process electrical responses of 15 conductimetric cells, each cell is tuned using a drop-casted conducting polymer poly(3-hexylthiophene) and 14 different triflate salts. The recognition of various solvents vapor (acetone, methanol, isopropanol, water, ethanol and blends of the last two at various concentrations) relies on a Deep-Convolutional Neural Network based on a back propagation algorithm with two hidden layers of 64 and 32 neurons respectively. The achieved experimental results show an effective classification for the e-nose data to discriminate the alcoholic blends by type and composition, with high classification accuracy (∼96%).

articleTitle: An Ultra Sensitive Malaria Detection Platform Based on Magnetic Biosensors
abstract: This work reports a novel malaria detection method using Tunnelling Magnetoresistance sensors. Using the paramagnetic properties of malaria haemozoin, a magnetic sensing platform is established and verified by simulations. This portable device consists of a TMR sensor, magnetic flux concentrator and back-end circuits. An estimated sensitivity limit of 2 parasites/µl is calculated for state-of-art TMR sensors with detectivity of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.5 \text{pT}/\text{Hz}^{1/2}$</tex>. Finite element analysis is applied in simulation to observe the paramagnetic nanoparticles magnetization and magnetic flux concentration. This point-of-care system shows an excellent theoretical detection limit, making it a promising diagnostic method.

articleTitle: FERT: Real-Time Facial Expression Recognition with Short-Range FMCW Radar
abstract: This study proposes a novel approach for real-time facial expression recognition utilizing short-range Frequency-Modulated Continuous-Wave (FMCW) radar equipped with one transmit (Tx), and three receive (Rx) antennas. The system leverages four distinct modalities simultaneously: Range-Doppler images (RDIs), micro range-Doppler Images (micro-RDIs), range azimuth images (RAIs), and range elevation images (REIs). Our innovative architecture integrates feature extractor blocks, intermediate feature extractor blocks, and a ResNet block to accurately classify facial expressions into smile, anger, neutral, and no-face classes. Our model achieves an average classification accuracy of 98.91% on the dataset collected using a 60 GHz short-range FMCW radar. The proposed solution operates in real-time in a person-independent manner, which shows the potential use of low-cost FMCW radars for effective facial expression recognition in various applications.

articleTitle: Shielding of Eddy Current Displacement Sensors with a Single Backside Shield
abstract: Eddy current displacement sensors (ECDS) are essential for accurate position measurement in heavy industries. For instance, in steel plants, position sensor systems often need to measure large displacements and withstand high temperatures, dirt, and dust exposure. Various protective measures, such as metal shields or chain curtains, create a restricted environment for such sensors and cause interference. Shielding techniques must be used to reduce this interference. However, due to spatial restrictions, established shielding techniques cannot always be applied. This study presents a design approach for a single-coil ECDS that reduces the effects of metal objects on the measurement signal by using a single backside shield. The accuracy of the proposed measurement system is improved by integrating shielding measures and selecting a suitable measurement frequency. This improvement is demonstrated through the lab measurements. The measures provide a basis for reliable position measurement with ECDS in harsh environments.

articleTitle: An Underwater Multipath Channel Azimuth Estimation Method based on Sweep-Spread Carrier
abstract: Underwater acoustic localization plays an important role in marine explorations. However, the complex shallow-sea environment induces the multipath reflection which severely interfere the localization accuracy. To suppress the multipath reflection induced interference and improve the estimation ac-curacy, we propose a method which based on circular sensor array. By using a uniform circular receiving array, the method estimate the target's azimuth through sweep-spread carrier (S2C) algorithm. To mitigate azimuth estimation distortion caused by array arrangement errors, we employ an array calibration method. The lake experiment results have verified our proposed method, leading to an average 64.7% error reduction in the azimuth estimation when compared with traditional method.

articleTitle: Architecture and Doping Optimization For FSI SPAD In 55nm BCD Lite® Process
abstract: This paper presents a study of industrialized CMOS single-photon avalanche diodes utilizing GlobalFoundries 55nm BCDLite® technology. A family of 12μm SPADs was fabricated including one device without shallow trench isolation (No-STI SPAD) and the others with increasing STI width (STI-1, STI-2 and STI-3 SPADs) between cathode and anode. Dark count rate (DCR) measurements revealed that STI-3 (widest STI) SPADs have negligible lot-to-lot median DCR variability, because of less trap-assisted tunneling as compared to No-STI SPAD. With optimized doping profile, photon detection probability (PDP) of STI-3 SPAD is improved over a wide spectral range, achieving peak PDP of 42% at 580nm and 3.5% at 940nm, DCR 0.42 cps/µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>at 2 V excess bias.

articleTitle: Broadband Response Photodetectors Based on Lead-Free Perovskite Quantum Dots/Transfer-Free Green Graphene Heterojunctions
abstract: Lead-free perovskite ((NH4)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf>) quantum dots (QDs) are integrated with transfer-free green graphene derived from camphor (a sustainable and eco-friendly precursor) to create a heterostructure successfully for photodetection applications. The monolayer structure with high coverage (>90% in a 25 μm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> area) of transfer-free green graphene was confirmed by the Raman spectrum and mapping images, respectively. The I-V characteristics of (NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf> QDs/transfer-free green graphene-based photodetectors (PDs) were measured with/without white light illumination, showing a significantly higher photo-to-dark current ratio (PDCR) than pure (NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf> QDs -based PDs, indicating the improvement of carrier transport by graphene layers. Moreover, (NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>)<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>Sb<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</inf> QDs/transfer-free green graphene-based PDs show an operation speed as fast as ~ 0.7 ms (the rise time)/~ 1.5 ms (the fall time) and ultra-broadband photoresponse characteristics. These results support the lead-free perovskite QDs/transfer-free green graphene-based PDs for future imaging techniques, optical communications, and optoelectronic circuits.

articleTitle: Speech Enhancement in Extremely Noisy Environments Based on Time-Frequency Harmonic Mask with Throat Microphone
abstract: We propose a time-frequency harmonic mask (TFHM) utilizing a throat microphone (TM) signal for speech enhancement in extremely noisy environments. The TM captures low-frequency speech signal below 1 kHz without interference from ambient noise. We analyzed the harmonic characteristics of the low-frequency TM signal and replicated this harmonic structure to the high-frequency band up to 4 kHz to generate the TFHM. The TFHM represents the presence of speech as binary values in the time-frequency domain. It is applied to the noisy signal to extract speech accurately. The proposed method demonstrated superior performance over previous approaches through objective and subjective tests under various noise conditions.

articleTitle: Ultra-High Frequency Photoacoustic Sensor Design for Early Stage Melanoma Diagnosis
abstract: Photoacoustic imaging is an emerging imaging technique with application in early melanoma diagnosis, leveraging a laser pulse depositing a dose of energy into an optical absorber, such as melanin. This promising approach aims at detecting the morphological characteristics of a biological sample at depths that cannot be observed by conventional optical techniques. However, the technological immaturity of the sensor limits the spatial resolution, hence the performances of the system in early-stage melanoma diagnosis. In order to address this issue, this paper examines the scaling potential for Ultra-High Frequency Ultrasound PVDF-based sensors, which operate at (50–100 MHz) frequencies and which require a significant miniaturization as their acoustic performance depends on the ratio between their sizes and signal wavelength. The trade-offs between image quality, sensor channel directivity and system noise are discussed reporting simulation results for different um sensor sizes on imaging performance.

articleTitle: Broadband Terahertz Metamaterial Absorber Based on Laser Reduced Graphene Oxide Films
abstract: This article introduces a terahertz metamaterial broadband absorber, fabricated through the laser-induced reduction of graphene oxide. The absorber is composed of a tri-layered structure: a graphene oxide layer, a filter membrane, and a gold substrate. Graphene patterns are etched onto the graphene oxide film via femtosecond laser processing, culminating in the formation of the metamaterial absorber. Simulations conducted using CST software corroborated the experimental findings. The underlying absorption mechanism was elucidated through analysis of the simulation data.

articleTitle: Digital Model-Based Approach for Predicting Gearbox Remaining Useful Life Using Response Surface Methodology
abstract: Predicting the remaining useful life (RUL) of gears and bearings in rotating machinery is crucial for effective maintenance. Traditional methods are time-consuming and rely heavily on sensor signal analysis. This study introduces a digital model-based methodology incorporating gearbox design elements and external conditions. The model calculates per-second damage rates for bearings and gears based on ISO 281 and ISO 6336 standards. Using response surface methodology (RSM), damage profiles are transformed into high-order nonlinear fitting equations, improving computational efficiency and reducing memory usage. Integration with a LabVIEW interface enables real-time monitoring and visualization of the gearbox's RUL.

articleTitle: A Resonant MEMS Pressure Sensor Utilizing Higher-Order Mode Oscillation
abstract: This paper demonstrates a resonant MEMS pressure sensor utilizing second-order mode oscillation. Through differential drive and differential detection, the second-order frequencies of resonators can be read out effectively. Test results indicate that the pressure sensitivity of differential frequency can be enhanced from 316.964 Hz/kPa to 387.176 Hz/kPa, and the measurement range can be expanded by more than 100<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> by utilizing the second mode oscillation. Besides, closed-loop calibration tests were constructed and the second mode shown better accuracy (0.01% FS, 3.5 Pa of the maximum fitting error) than the first mode (0.02% FS, 5.2 Pa of the maximum fitting error), with the pressure range extended from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\sim 30\text{kPa}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5\sim 80\text{kPa}$</tex>. Moreover, given the higher Q factor of the second mode, the utilization of higher-order mode is also expected to improve the frequency stability.

articleTitle: A Practical Analysis of Persuasive and Dark Patterns for IIoT and Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems
abstract: Sensors and actuators are essential for monitoring and controlling industrial processes. Both kinds of devices are usually managed through Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) platforms and Industrial Cyber-Physical Systems (ICPS), whose cybersecurity is critical. This paper focuses on such cybersecurity by analyzing how a set of attacks known as Persuasive and Dark Patterns can affect user interaction with IIoT applications and ICPSs. By capturing data on how users interact with the system's interface elements, valuable insights are gained into the operator behavior within the industrial environment. Specifically, two versions of the same application are compared: one incorporating Dark Patterns and another one that makes use of Persuasive Patterns. The obtained results reveal significant differences in user behavior, highlighting the impact on user experience and navigation efficiency in an industrial scenario.

articleTitle: Harnessing the Fourth Dimension Through Nonlinear Damping in Optical Fiber Flow Sensing
abstract: In this study, nonlinear damping is introduced as a critical enhancement in the operation of a fiber tip optomechanical flow-sensor. The flow sensor, is integrated onto the cleaved face of an optical fiber and features a three-dimensional (3D) rotor fabricated using a two-photon nanomachining process. By infusing a polydimethylsiloxane hydrocarbon stabilizing agent via integrated microfluidic channels into the sensing element, the device achieves consistent periodic measurement of gaseous nitrogen flow rates between 10 and 20 LPM. This paper presents a comprehensive characterization of the fiber tip flow sensor and highlights the advantages of nonlinear damping in enhancing the sensitivity and reliability of flow measurements.

articleTitle: Semantic Landmark Detection & Classification Using Neural Networks For 3D In-Air Sonar
abstract: In challenging environments where traditional sensing modalities struggle, in-air sonar offers resilience to optical interference. Placing a priori known landmarks in these environments can eliminate accumulated errors in autonomous mobile systems such as Simultaneous Localization and Mapping (SLAM) and autonomous navigation. We present a novel approach using a convolutional neural network to detect and classify ten different reflector landmarks with varying radii using in-air 3D sonar. Additionally, the network predicts the orientation angle of the detected landmarks. The neural network is trained on cochleograms, representing echoes received by the sensor in a time-frequency domain. Experimental results in cluttered indoor settings show promising performance. The CNN achieves a 97.3% classification accuracy on the test dataset, accurately detecting both the presence and absence of landmarks. Moreover, the network predicts landmark orientation angles with an RMSE lower than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{\circ}$</tex>, enhancing the utility in SLAM and autonomous navigation applications.
