This advancement improves the robustness and accuracy of autonomous systems in challenging environments.

articleTitle: A Low Power Single-Cantilever Gas Sensor Cell with Remarkable Recognition Capability for Food Freshness Related Gases
abstract: This paper reports a single-cantilever gas sensor cell with four detection channels as well as low power consumption. Four pairs of detection electrodes with a common terminal and a microheater are integrated on a single cantilever extended out from the substrate. The total sensor cell was fabricated using typical 4-inch MEMS process and four types of metal- oxide (MOx) sensing layers were patterned by four times of UV lithography and lift-off processes. Based on the single-end fixed cantilever beam structure, there is a natural temperature gradient from the fixed end to the free end of the cantilever beam. Due to the self-temperature-modulation of the structure combined with four different sensing materials, the gas-specific responses of the sensor cell are improved. Four kinds of food freshness related gases (ammonia, sulfuretted hydrogen, ethanol, and trimethylamine) were tested with a low power consumption of 23.5 mW, and test results indicate that the sensor cell can clearly distinguish these gases.

articleTitle: Visible Light-Induced Organic Artificial Synaptic Transistors Based on Protein-Ag Nanoparticle Composite
abstract: Neuromorphic photonics system, inspired by the biological brain, is emerging as a potential solution to the limitations of the classical von Neumann computing architecture. Compared to traditional neuromorphic chips that rely on electronic synapses, photonic neuromorphic chips, which use light as the input signal, offer a promising alternative for next-generation artificial intelligence systems with high density and low power consumption. In this study, we developed a biocompatible organic field-effect transistor (OFET) using a protein-silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) composite as the active dielectric layer. When exposed to blue light (445 nm), the AgNPs generate photocarriers. These carriers decay slowly due to the surrounding gelatin layer. The synaptic transistor also consists of an aluminium oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{A}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3})$</tex> dielectric layer, enabling efficient low-voltage operation <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(< 2\mathrm{V})$</tex>. The device replicates various synaptic functions, such as, excitatory postsynaptic current (EPSC), short-term potentiation (STP), spike number-dependent plasticity (SNDP), spike-rate dependent plasticity (SRDP), etc. This work presents an innovative method for combining protein and nanoparticles to create biocompatible, low-voltage optoelectronic neuromorphic vision systems for a wide range of applications.

articleTitle: Design and Characterization of a Printed Circuit Board-Based Gas Chromatography Column for Greenhouse Gas Analysis
abstract: Herein we report the development of a printed circuit board-based gas chromatography column (PCB-GC), its characterization, and demonstrate its use for process or environmental monitoring of greenhouse gases. This type of device is desirable for prototyping or for implementation in low size, weight, or power systems. The PCB-GC device is comprised of two PCB boards metalized with gold for a solderable, inert column surface. The top layer houses the fluidic connections and built-in heater while the bottom layer has the rectangular channel (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.5 \text{mm }\mathrm{x}1.6 \text{mm} \mathrm{x}1$</tex> m) designed to be packed with particles for gas separation. The devices integrated heater supported rates as high as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50^{\mathrm{o}}\mathrm{C}/\min$</tex> at over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$100^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. Column efficiency found to be optimal between 10 and 20 mL/min. Using HayeSep D as the packing material, separation of methane and carbon dioxide from a greenhouse gas mixture near <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> was achieved. Initial cost metrics for research level manufacturing quantities was in the range of $200 per column.

articleTitle: Quadrature Compensation for a Frequency Modulated piezoMEMS Gyroscope
abstract: This paper introduces an effective way to improve the performance of a Lissajous frequency modulated piezoelectrical MEMS gyroscope by reducing the quadrature error of the sensor system. The effects of a quadrature error to the apparent modulated frequency are explained. To minimize the quadrature effects on sensor output, a cross-axis drive-to-sense-method was implemented on an FPGA-based control system. Experimental results confirm the effectiveness of the quadrature removal method, as the noise of the sensor was halved after applying the optimum compensation.

articleTitle: TFT-based Piezoelectret Sensor for Arterial Pulse Measurement
abstract: Mechano-sensors with the capability of monitoring real-time physiological signals are essential in health monitoring and medical diagnosis systems. Herein, a piezoelectret sensor based on thin film transistors (TFTs) is reported for arterial pulse measurement. The sensor properties are studied through simulation and experiment. Integrated with TFT, the output impedance of the piezoelectret sensor was tremendously reduced, making the sensor have better performance with higher sensitivity of 55.3 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{kPa}^{-1}$</tex>, and capability of detecting quasi-static forces. The developed TFT-based piezoelectret sensor can be used for arterial pulse measurement, and capture the pulse wave features, providing clinical information on cardiovascular dynamics.

articleTitle: Integration of Ballistocardiogram with PPG and ECG Using a CNN-LSTM Model for Cuff-Less Blood Pressure Estimation
abstract: Recent advancements in wearable technology have revolutionized the capability for continuous and non-invasive monitoring of vital signs, such as blood pressure. This paper presents a novel approach leveraging a hybrid Convolutional Neural Network-Long Short-Term Memory (CNN-LSTM) model to predict systolic and diastolic blood pressure (SBP and DBP) using data from wearable devices. Our model employs Photoplethysmography (PPG), Electrocardiography (ECG), and Ballistocardiography (BCG) signals, exploring their efficacy across different signal window sizes to optimize prediction accuracy. Through rigorous preprocessing, including advanced filtering and normalization techniques, we ensured data integrity for effective feature extraction. The model was evaluated against the rigorous standards set by IEEE and the Association for the Advancement of Medical Instrumentation (AAMI), demonstrating promising capability. These findings suggest the model's potential for integration into clinical workflows, offering a reliable alternative to traditional blood pressure monitoring methods. Further validation on a larger scale to confirm its efficacy and adaptability in diverse clinical scenarios is ongoing.

articleTitle: Self-Coupling Laser Sensor Using Triangular Wave Chirp Modulation and Signal Intensity Detection: Method for Improving Low-Frequency Range Operation of Self-Coupling Laser Sensor
abstract: This paper presents a method for improving the low-frequency operation of a self-coupling laser sensor using an algorithm based on triangular chirp modulation and signal intensity detection. The validation results of this method are discussed. A self-coupling laser sensor is a measurement device that uses an optical beat signal generated from the interference between the returned light from a target and the light in the active layer of a laser diode during laser irradiation. A self-coupling laser sensor with a modulation drive can be used to measure various parameters such as distance to the target, velocity, and direction of movement. However, when the signal frequency is low, a strong Doppler shift in the returned light due to the movement of the target may invert the signal frequency, resulting in measurement failure. As a countermeasure, we devised a signal processing method to detect signal frequency inversion and output accurate measurement values based on the positional relationship of multiple signal frequency spectral peaks and signal intensity generated by triangular wave chirp modulation. The distance and velocity measurements were verified in a strong Doppler shift environment, and accurate measurements were obtained, particularly when the signal frequency was inverted.

articleTitle: Performance Enhancement of Piezoelectric MEMS Microspeaker by Jointed and Separated Curved Cantilever Array with Phase Modulation Circuit
abstract: This study presents the piezoelectric MEMS microspeaker with an area under 5.3 mm for high-frequency applications. The multiple tweeter units together with the driving circuits are designed to extend the bandwidth from 5 kHz to 13 kHz. Features and merits of the design to modulate resonant frequencies of the tweeters to extend the bandwidth are: (1) curve slit: to modulate the cantilever resonant frequency under the same anchor and diaphragm area, (2) central joint: to connect part of the cantilevers to form different tweeter units, (3) driving circuits: to implement the gain and phase modulation driving signals to extend the SPL (Sound-Pressure-Level) in specific frequency ranges. Measurements under 1 Vpp with 8 Vdc driving voltage in the pressure field, the proposed design with phase modulation driving achieves over 80 dB from 5 kHz to 13 kHz. Moreover, THD (Total-Harmonic-Distortion) is below 3% at the same time.

articleTitle: High Performance Hydrogen Sensors Based on Tellurium Nanobelt Field-Effect Transistors
abstract: Tellurium (Te), a p-type semiconductor with high carrier mobility, is particularly advantageous for field-effect transistor (FET) applications. In this study, a high-performance FET-type hydrogen sensor utilizing Te nanobelts was developed. The sensor was fabricated with a palladium (Pd) gate, specifically chosen for its sensitivity to hydrogen, enhancing both selectivity and response. The results indicate a short response time of ~2 s to 4% H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, a detection limit as low as 50 ppm, and negligible cross-sensitivity at room temperature, highlighting the potential of Te in advancing gas sensor technology. Furthermore, the flexible FET design is expected to detect various gases, broadening the application potential of Te-based gas sensors.

articleTitle: Ultra-Sensitive Differential Sensor for Liquid Dielectric Characterization Using 1-Bit Coding in DGS
abstract: This paper introduces a kind of microwave sensors to characterize dielectric liquid sample. To enhance sensitivity and reduce the disturb of environment, differential method is applied in sensor design. The sensor based on defected ground structure (DGS) is optimized by adaptive genetic algorithm, and the sensing performance is improved by magnifying resonant frequency differences and enhancing electric field energy. The optimized sensor has a relative sensitivity of 0.076%, which is 1.52 times of the basic structure. The experimental results show that it is sensitive and has good robustness and quick response for liquid detection.

articleTitle: Self-Powered Component for High-G Sensing via Prestress Structured Triboelectric Transducer
abstract: High-g mechanical impacts are widely present in scenarios such as vehicle collisions, aircraft forced landings, and sports confrontations. The development of sensing components for high-g mechanical mpact is difficult, because it is necessary to take into account wide range and linearity, while also considering the impact resistance of the device itself and the power supply system in such extreme environments. In this work, we present a prestressed packaged single-electrode triboelectric nanogenerator (PS-TENG) for the first time, as a self-powered sensor for sensing high-g mechanical impacts over a wide range. We built a multi-physics theoretical model, then designed and verified it through finite element simulation and Machete hammer test. It is proven that the sensor has the advantages of large output signal, wide sensing range and good linearity, and it can provide strong technical support for low-power sensing applications in various high-g impact scenarios.

articleTitle: Ni3S2-HCSs Modified Polyaniline: Enhanced Ethanol Detection at Room Temperature
abstract: Gas sensing technology is crucial for safety and environmental monitoring. Our research focused on creating ethanol gas sensors using new composite materials and a cleaner approach to producing Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> nanostructures. These materials included trinickel disulfide (Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) supported on polyaniline (Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-PANI), hollow carbon spheres supported on P ANI (HCS/PANI), and a hybrid of both materials (Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-HCS/P ANI). Our study demonstrated significant improvements in ethanol sensing capabilities at room temperature. We addressed existing limitations associated with traditional sensors and enhanced the sensor performance of the hybrid sensor devices. The research highlights the potential of Ni<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>-HCS/P ANI composites as promising candidates for room-temperature, high-performance ethanol gas sensing applications. Further research in this area could lead to practical implementations and widespread adoption of these sensors.

articleTitle: High-Precision Fabrication of Graphene Nanoplatelet-Based Piezoresistive Strain Sensors Using PμSL 3D Printing Technology
abstract: This study presents the design and high-precision fabrication of 3D printed strain sensors, which feature graphene nanoplatelet based piezoresistive sensing elements. The strain sensor features fully encapsulated microfluidic inner channels, 500μm in diameter, created using Projection Micro Stereolithography (PμSL) 3D printing technology. A flexible printed strain sensor was achieved through the creation of a custom resin mixture. The strain gauges were printed in 20 μm layers, resulting in a dimensional printing error rate of less than 3%, and exhibited fine structural details and high resolution. Graphene nanoplatelet inks of three different concentrations (5%, 10%, and 20%) were used to form the piezoresistive sensing elements. The gauge factors (GFs) for the 10% and 20% strain sensors were determined to be 28 and 19, respectively. The strain sensor with the lowest concentration (5%) showed a high GF of 13.5 and 564 in the strain ranges 0% to 13% and 13% to 18.5%. These findings introduce PμSL 3D printing as a method to form flexible piezoresistive strain sensors and highlight the impact of nanomaterial concentration on piezoresistive performance, demonstrating a potential for applications in customized, high-performance strain sensors.

articleTitle: Singularity-Enhanced Deep Sub-Linewidth Mode Matching of the Disk Resonator Gyroscope
abstract: Precise mode-matching is one of the most important factors for achieving optimal performance in Coriolis gyroscopes. However, achieving sub-linewidth mode matching is a significant challenge, largely due to the limited spectral resolution. In this study, we employ a novel singularity physics in the phase-locked-loop-enabled steady states of the Coriolis gyroscope to precisely measure the natural frequency mismatch. Through this method, we can achieve deep sub-linewidth mode matching for a MEMS disk resonator gyroscope (DRG). Remarkably, our experimental results demonstrate an impressive level of mode-matching precision, exceeding the gyroscope's linewidth by a factor of over 160.

articleTitle: Average Capacity Analysis and Power Allocation for Data-Gathering Wireless Sensor Networks
abstract: This paper focuses on the average capacity analysis and power allocation (PA) for data-gathering wireless sensor networks (DAWSNs), in which single-antenna source nodes communicate with the low-cost quantized multiple-antennas sink. We derive a tractable analytical expression for the average capacity using the replica method, and based on it elaborately design the cooperative iterative water-filling (CIWF) PA algorithm to enhance capacity. It is shown that the obtained analytical results match well with Monte-Carlo simulations, and the developed CIWF algorithm can remarkably enhance the average capacity of DAWSNs with relatively low power consumption, thereby compensating for the loss caused by low-resolution quantization.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Intelligent Wearable System with Multi-Sensors and Lightweight Machine Learning Algorithm for Motion-Status Monitoring
abstract: Health monitoring enabled by wearable device aids in the early warning of potential health issues, but wearable devices still face technical bottlenecks in multiple physiology acquisition, low-power consumption, intelligent data processing. To address these challenges in a holistic manner, this paper proposes a multi-sensor, intelligent and low-power wearable system, integrating both multi-sensor data acquisition and lightweight machine learning algorithm into a computation-limited wearable device. A one-dimensional CNN model, with a motion status recognition accuracy of 99%, is constructed and optimized for lightweight deployment on the wearable device, used for real-time data processing of multi-channel foot pressure and 3-axis acceleration signals. To further reduce the system power consumption, an event-triggered mechanism is developed based on human motion characteristics. The system ultimately realizes the low-power intelligent perception of five motion states, achieving an optimized power consumption of 6.3 mA in the active mode and 652 µA in the low-power mode. This study provides a potential solution for real-time intelligent monitoring of remote personalized healthcare.

articleTitle: Dynamic Sensing of an Embedded Object Using Laser, Camera, and Collaborative Robot
abstract: This paper focuses on the application of a collaborative robot in dynamic sensing of embedded objects. Dynamic sensing is a way to characterize embedded objects using optical sensors and dynamically moving robots. Here, we use diffuse optical imaging techniques to determine the mechanical properties of an embedded object. The dynamic sensing is split into two phases. In the first phase, the location of the target is estimated. Then in the second phase, the embedded object's size and depth are estimated. The results of this paper demonstrate a dynamic sensing method that estimates location, size, and depth of embedded objects autonomously using a collaborative robot. The size and depth estimation yielded an error of 11.1 % and 90% respectively.

articleTitle: Paper-Based PEDOT:PSS Sensors for Cure Process Monitoring of Epoxy Resin
abstract: Novel, paper-based sensors with a sensitive layer of PEDOT:PSS, an organic semiconductor, are investigated for their suitability to monitor the curing process inside epoxy-based fiber composite materials. PEDOT:PSS shows a strong response toward temperature which appears to be increased by increasing humidity. At the same time, paper is expected to be an excellent substrate material for embedding in hybrid materials, as it is completely soaked by the resin that forms the matrix and thus adapts the material properties far better than conventional sensor substrates. Therefore, it is expected that the curing process can be monitored with these sensors directly inside the material layers offering improved process control, especially for thick composite parts.

articleTitle: Enhancing Maritime Situational Awareness through Monocular Vision
abstract: Situational awareness can be significantly enhanced through the application of novel perception technologies. Camera-based solutions are particularly well-suited for this purpose due to their effectiveness in object detection. We present a monocular camera system designed to detect and track multiple objects. An image tracker is employed to track detections within the image space. Specifically optimized for maritime scenarios, the data association process enables tracking of both slow-moving large and fast-moving small objects. To determine the object's location in vessel coordinates, we utilize a back projection method that accounts for vessel movements. A second tracker is used to track detections in world coordinates. We demonstrate this approach with an example involving two crossing vessels that are occluded for a short time. Our proposed method achieves accurate tracking of both vessels, with a relative range error of less than 10%. Overall, our approach enhances situational awareness and contributes to improved safety.

articleTitle: A Respiratory Disease Diagnosis Method of Electronic Nose Based on Pyramid Pooling and Self-Attention Mechanism
abstract: In order to address the challenges of insufficient sensitivity and specificity, sample diversity, and unbalanced distribution of electronic noses(E-nose), this study proposes an innovative approach that integrates pyramid pooling and one encoder utilizing self-attention mechanisms for analyzing response data of E-nose. Pyramid pooling aggregates features across scales to capture multi-level global information, while a single encoder with self-attention mechanisms captures feature relationships. To enhance interpretability in deep learning models, SHapley Additive exPlanations analysis tools are used to clarify model explanations, aiding in understanding prediction logic and feature contributions. Through 3-fold cross-validation, the model achieved 92.31% accuracy, 94.84% precision, and 93.95% recall. This study provides an insightful approach to the implementation of E-nose systems for respiratory disease diagnosis.

articleTitle: Signal Response Investigation of Skin Deformation and sEMG on the Biceps Brachii Muscle During Isometric Elbow Flexion
abstract: In this paper, we measured skin deformation and sEMG of the biceps brachii muscle during isometric elbow flexion to investigate the difference in response between both signals. The amplitude of skin deformation and sEMG were compared for each flexion force exerted. The ratio of mean amplitude between each flexion force and maximum voluntary force (MVF) of skin deformation was larger than that of IEMG from 20% to 40% of MVF. The ratio of skin deformation for the two subjects was also larger than that of IEMG in the range from 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> to 15<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> of MVF.

articleTitle: Graphene FET Biosensors with Surface-Charge Modulation
abstract: This study addresses the challenges of counteracting the negative surface charge of graphene by functionalizing it with positively charged compounds and demonstrated the detection of C-reactive protein (CRP) using surface-charge-modulated graphene FETs (SCM-GFETs). We integrated multiple SCM-GFETs with anti-CRP antibodies alongside nonfunctionalized GFETs within a single chip, and measured differentials to eliminate background changes, thereby enhancing measurement reliability. The devices exhibited a specific response to the adsorption of CRP. We also demonstrated detection of CRP in artificial saliva. Our findings indicate that these devices effectively mitigate nonlinear electrolytic screening, paving the way for further advancements in GFET-based biosensor technology.

articleTitle: Microneedle Array Patch as Biomedical Sensors in Collecting ISF and Subsequent Biomarker Analysis
abstract: To monitor and obtain the biological information of our body, a microneedle array patch (MAP) has attracted great attention as a new type of biosensor. At the same time, interstitial fluid (ISF) is being widely researched as an alternative analyte to blood as it has equivalent amount and kinds of biomarkers to blood. Thus, MAP enables the extraction of ISF from skin layers and the onsite diagnosis using various assay methods. In this study, we introduced MAPs as well as ISF, and several biomarkers that were diagnosed by using porous MAP biosensors. Along with the advantages acquired from MAPs, MAP biosensors are expected to be a promising medical device as a personal healthcare device for self-monitoring and diagnosis.

articleTitle: Passive Acoustic Temperature Sensor Characterization with Animal Tissue
abstract: In this work, we present first tests of a new implantable sensor concept based on acoustic metamaterials and ultrasound interrogation tested with animal tissue. The metamaterial sensor is passive and measures temperature with high sensitivity. The sensing performance is characterized in the [36], [42] °C physiological temperature range and it is also compared in presence of tissue mimicking materials (phantoms), as well as animal tissue. The high temperature sensitivity, observed without tissue (S= -3.3.10-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>K-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>), is almost unaffected by the presence of tissue (S= -3.5·10-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>K-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>). The temperature resolution degrades as expected in comparison to the experiment without tissue, but still reaches a value of 0.18 K. We also investigate two approaches to address challenges associated with sensor spatial localization under scattering tissue. A simple time-windowing approach is found to be lower in performances compared to a spectral approach in both ratio of positives (30.2% vs 65.80/0) and true positives (19.3%) detected values. This metamaterial-based sensing approach opens the way to a new class of passive temperature sensors for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: The Impact of Outgassing of Molding Compound on Graphene for Gas Sensing
abstract: Packaging is an indispensable part in microelectronics manufacturing industry, where transfer molding as an essential step is typically included for encapsulation. Recently, with the fruitful achievements of research on graphene in gas sensing, there is also urgent need for study on how the packaging process will affect the graphene, to develop compatible manufacture protocol for practical graphene-based gas sensor. In this work, we carried out experiments on how molding compound outgassing affects graphene for gas sensing. Our results show that although there is some impact on the electrical properties of the graphene, there is no change in the microstructure, and only a slight and manageable change in gas sensing abilities. This work suggests that graphene could maintain performances after epoxy molding packaging processes.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensor Nodes for Condition Based Maintenance in Railway Systems
abstract: Ensuring the reliability, safety, and efficiency of railway systems is increasingly critical in global transportation networks. This paper addresses the necessity for advanced monitoring systems by introducing a multivariate energy-efficient wireless sensor node designed for proactive maintenance in rail applications.

articleTitle: Fall Risk Prediction for Elderly Using Head-Mounted Inertial Sensors and Tree-Based Models
abstract: In recent years, with the increasing number of elderly people, falls have caused significant concerns and troubles in their daily lives. Therefore, the importance of fall prediction is indispensable. This work applies a head-mounted device with an inertial measurement unit, and tree-based models are used to predict the future fall risk of elderly individuals. Elderly participants were asked to stand in place with their eyes closed for 1 minute. A random forest and Morse fall scale were utilized to select features of acceleration and angular velocity from time-domain and frequency-domain. Because the decision tree is more lightweight than the random forest, the decision tree can be more suitable for use on edge devices. Therefore, a decision tree was utilized to classify the future fall risk of elderly individuals. With the optimal feature subsets, the 10-fold cross-validation results yield recall, precision, and F1-score of 0.818, 0.692, and 0.750, respectively.

articleTitle: Sideslip Angle Estimation Based on a Kinematics Model Using An Unscented Kalman Filter
abstract: Vehicle stability control is a crucial function for vehicle safety, requiring various dynamic parameters for effective control. Among these, the sideslip angle is particularly important for maintaining stability. However, due to cost considerations, directly measuring the sideslip angle in vehicles is challenging. This study proposes an estimation method based on a kinematic model, utilizing an Unscented Kalman Filter (UKF) to address the nonlinear estimation problem. The proposed method utilizes the inputs of yaw rate, longitudinal and lateral accelerations, and incorporates feedback correction using longitudinal velocity to estimate lateral velocity, accounting for the effects of process noise and measurement noise. The performance of the proposed sideslip angle estimator was evaluated in MATLAB/Simulink using CarSim under different road friction conditions. The results demonstrate the potential of the proposed sideslip angle estimator.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled hBN/AlGaN/GaN High Electron Mobility Transistor for Carbon Dioxide Monitoring
abstract: Monitoring carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) is critically prudent across various domains such as environmental surveillance, industrial processes, and space applications due to its considerable impact on climate change and human wellbeing. Conventional CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensors often have limitations of high response time, poor resolution, large size, and short operational lifetime. This work presents a CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor to address the challenges, exploiting an AlGaN/GaN High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT) functionalised with hexagonal boron nitride (hBN). This sensor leverages the high electron mobility of the two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) at the AlGaN/GaN interface and the selective adsorption properties of hBN. Characterisation results show the highest selectivity and sensitivity towards CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, with a tested detection range from 1 ppm to 100 ppm, a response of 56°/0 at 100 ppm, and a response time of about 120 seconds. The sensor was also integrated with an ESP32 IoT module for real-time monitoring and data transmission. The operational principle involves CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> adsorption on the hBN layer, leading to changes in the 2DEG conductivity and measurable variations in the sensor's electrical characteristics. The results underscore the potential of AlGaN/GaN HEMT-based sensors in environmental monitoring and industrial applications.

articleTitle: Polarized IrOx Enables Novel Referencing for Biocompatible L-Glutamate Sensors
abstract: Long-term monitoring of neurotransmitter levels in vivo is crucial for understanding the mechanisms behind neurological disorders. Electrochemical sensors offer advantages such as miniaturization and fast response times, but their biocompatibility is often overlooked. The widely used Ag/ AgCl wire pseudo-reference electrode, despite its stability, has poor biocompatibility and necessitates additional brain insertion, causing more damage. This work presents a polarized IrOx pseudo-reference integrated L-glutamate sensor for long-term neurotransmitter measurements. The on-probe IrOx thin film, electrochemically deposited, has been tested for stability and biocompatibility. Additionally, strategic polarization of IrOx is introduced to enhance stability. The polarized IrOx on-probe L-glutamate sensor significantly improves the biocompatibility of the electrochemical sensing platform, facilitating the investigation of neurological disorders through long-term neurotransmitter monitoring.

articleTitle: A Passive Wireless Quasi-Harmonic Strain Sensor for Eternal Structural Health Monitoring
abstract: This work presents a novel passive, wireless, strain-modulated quasi-harmonic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\varepsilon-\mathbf{qHT})$</tex> sensor aimed at continous, eternal structural health monitoring. The proposed system leverages a non-linear parametric oscillator coupled together with a MEMS piezoelectric resonator to generate an output frequency comb centered at half the interrogating RF signal. This approach minimizes clutter and reduces multi-path interference while maintaining long communicating distance. Strain-sensitivity is achieved by integrating a commercial off-the-shelf strain-gauge into the qHT architecture, which directly modulates the spacing between the output comb lines. As a proof of concept, a PCB-based <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon-\mathbf{qHT}$</tex> prototype, in-corporating in-house fabricated MEMS resonators is designed, assembled, and successfully tested in both wired and wireless configurations.

articleTitle: A Low-Cost RF Power Measurement System for Optimizing the Configuration of BLE Mesh Nodes
abstract: Nowadays, there is a significant occupancy of the 2.4 GHz Industrial, scientific and medical (ISM) band. Systems utilizing this band, such as wireless sensors based on the Bluetooth Mesh Protocol (BMP), must configure their parameters to enhance reliability, consumption, and delay. Given the abundance of interference, which is complex and continuously changing, selecting the optimal configuration parameters is not straightforward. Moreover, the standard does not propose any adaptive algorithm. This paper proposes a low-cost solution to adaptively determine the suitable transmit and scan channels and the appropriate number of retransmissions for Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) mesh nodes by combining Radio Frequency (RF) power measurements and traffic analysis.

articleTitle: Adaptive Filter to Remove Motion Artifacts from GSR Sensor Embedded on Handle Cane
abstract: Wearable devices capable of recording physiological variables such as pulse and electrodermal activity have become popular in the form of smart watches or bracelets. The measurement is affected by the relative movement of the device with respect to the skin, generating artifacts. An alternative to watches or bracelets that can improve adherence for population groups such as elderly people may be the integration of sensors into everyday objects, such as walking sticks. In this case, the challenge of motion artifacts is particularly difficult. This paper presents a strategy based on a Notch filter that adapts its center frequency from the reading of a force sensor placed under the GSR sensor. A noticeable reduction of the interference from motion artifacts is observed.

articleTitle: Field Evaluation of a High-Resolution NDIR Sensor System for Measurement of Methane in Water
abstract: A system for the measurement of methane concentration in water is presented. The system is a stand- alone device using a high-resolution NDIR (Non-Dispersive Infra-Red) gas sensor. The NDIR sensor is configured to measure methane, water vapor, and carbon dioxide in the air. It is mounted in a housing with a stabilized environment and includes cross-sensitivity compensation. An equilibrator is used to transfer the methane concentration from the water into a circulating gas flow that is analyzed by the NDIR gas sensor. The equilibrator consists of a vertical plastic tube filled with 2,000 glass marbles, where the water runs from top to bottom on the surface of the glass marbles, in contact with a circulating air flow, exchanging gas. The system is stand- alone, including power supply and logging features for 72 hours of operation. The system performance was evaluated in a field test, measuring the methane content of seawater at a fiber bank in Sundsvall, Sweden. This fiber bank consists of remaining waste from an old paper industry from before 1970 and is known to produce methane. The detection limit of the tested system is below 1.4 nmol/L in water, corresponding to 1 ppm methane concentration in the air. The settling time of the system in its current configuration, including the equilibrator and gas sensor housing, is 30 minutes.

articleTitle: Pulse Repetition Rate and Unwrapping Limits in OTDR Fiber Optic Sensing Systems
abstract: This study investigates the effect of pulse repetition rate (RR) on the accuracy of strain reconstruction in distributed acoustic sensing systems (DAS) using OTDR with heterodyne detection. Experimental evaluations at different values of RR reveal significant dependencies on the strain rate, which go beyond the simple dependence on bandwidth as already known from the Nyquist theorem. The findings underscore the necessity to optimize RR in order to guarantee the system's capacity to reconstruct dynamic strain signals and mitigate the constraints imposed by the phase unwrapping algorithm. Future research should focus on advancing phase unwrapping algorithms to improve performance at lower RR to ensure robust strain measurement capabilities in diverse industrial contexts.

articleTitle: Directionally Sensitive Active Helmholtz Resonator Metamaterials Enabled Through 3D-Printing
abstract: Controlling the absorption and diffusion of sound in the audible range is an exciting field of research. Achieving miniaturized acoustic systems able to operate at audio frequencies is one of the main challenges of acoustic engineering for many practical applications. One viable approach to tackle this challenge is by using meta materials such that deep subwavelength control can be achieved. This work investigates the fabrication and experimental characterization of membrane-coupled Helmholtz resonators as directional attenuators via 3D-printing, and introduces a 3D-printed piezoelectric component to transform acoustic attenuation to electrical outputs.

articleTitle: SensOL: Memory-Efficient Online Learning for Tiny MCUs
abstract: This paper introduces SensOL, an online learning replay-based approach for hardware-limited microcontroller units (MCUs). It addresses two major bottlenecks for continuous learning within tiny MCUs: the computational cost of learning a new task in real time and the memory requirements for storing task exemplars. Our proposal originally combines the TinyOL approach with a memory-efficient replay strategy to refresh old task information during the continuous training process. The memory footprint for storing task exemplars is optimized by saving the quantized outputs of the frozen model, which are subsequently compressed according to their sparsity level. We evaluated our approach on a realistic online incremental IMU-based transport mode learning scenario. The SensOL approach demonstrated a 115x lower memory footprint for storing the compressed task exemplars compared to storing them in their original format. Finally, we estimated the on-device training time to update the weights/biases and achieved a time of 1 ms within an STM32L476JGY microcontroller based on an Arm Cortex-M4 processor operating at 80 MHz.

articleTitle: Wirelessly Powered Buried Soil Moisture Sensor System
abstract: This work presents a wirelessly powered, buried soil moisture sensing system. The system is electrically charged by a low-frequency electrodynamic wireless power transmission scheme. A coin-cell secondary battery and battery management system provide an energy reservoir, which supplies power to a capacitive soil moisture sensor connected to an ESP-8266 Wi-Fi SoC for transmitting data. Buried at 30 cm from the wireless power transmitter, the 17 cm3, three-phase, rotating-magnet receiver produced an average power of 230 mW. The system demonstrated a time averaged energy transfer of 0.272 W-hr. The soil moisture data was transmitted to an IoT cloud platform for remote monitoring.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing of Multiple Gases Emitted from Industrial Plants by an Ultra-lightweight Gas Chromatograph Installed on a Drone
abstract: To quickly analyze multiple gases emitted from places of high altitudes, high temperatures, or emission of hazardous gases where humans cannot access, we installed an ultralight gas chromatograph using ball SAW sensor on a small drone. We detected four kinds of gases at the top of a chimney in 3 min. This method will open the door to remote in-situ analysis of industrial plants.

articleTitle: Dynamic Error Reduction in Soft Tactile Sensors by Optimum Material Selection
abstract: Emerging applications in the field of robotics require tactile sensors with low dynamic errors. Such sensors are often made of elastomers, which exhibit time-dependent drift and hysteresis, leading to lower sensing accuracy. In this work, we systematically study the dominant material-inherent sources for the dynamic error within a tactile sensor, based upon a diverse range of commercially available elastomers. We demonstrate that the initial error associated with the Mullins effect can be completely eliminated, that the residual transient force error related to viscoelastic drift is reduced by 57%, and that the hysteresis force error is reduced by 20% with an optimized selection of suitable elastomers.

articleTitle: Physically Accurate Lidar Simulation for Automotive Digital Twins
abstract: Recent advancements in real-time ray tracing show promise for creating digital twins in automotive applications. AI perception models can be validated and fine-tuned using digital twin sensor data, improving autonomous driving in edge cases. However, there is still a gap in the realism of these simulations. This paper addresses specifically the simulation of LiDAR by combining physics-based ray tracing from a graphics buffer with a database of real-world material properties captured in the infrared spectrum under various weather conditions. Compared to other approaches, our method synthesizes point clouds that match much closer those from commercial LiDAR scanners under similar conditions than pure geometry-based simulations (e.g. from CARLA). We demonstrate this through a performance study on pedestrian detection task, where a state-of-the-art model pre-trained on real data performs equally well on our synthesized data. Our digital twin LiDAR sensor works independently of existing simulation enviornments and can be used in single or multi-sensor simulations without additional tuning.

articleTitle: A Wearable ECG System with Printed Electrodes for Heart Health Monitoring and Diagnosis
abstract: The increasing prevalence of cardiovascular diseases worldwide has triggered the need for developing wearable Electrocardiogram (ECG) systems for routine use in daily life. Here, we report the development of a miniaturized wireless ECG monitoring system that is easy to use and low cost. Our innovative wearable ECG system comprises screen-printed ECG electrodes connected using snap connectors to an ECG readout. The screen-printed ECG electrodes comprises of silver nanowires as conductive layer, ECG electrode gel and a silicone adhesive printed on a flexible plastic substrate. The effect of the distance between the two printed electrodes in the form of an ECG strip (5 cm and 8 cm centre-to-centre) is tested by collecting ECG data from volunteers using our custom wearable ECG readout, operated through a generic app. The printed ECG electrodes demonstrated performance similar to commercial ECG electrodes, as confirmed by a cardiologist during a blinded review of the ECG data. Future developments involve testing the system in large populations (adults, kids, infants, and neonates) and validation with gold-standard ECG systems and electrodes.

articleTitle: Biocompatible, Dual-Purpose Electrochemical Aptamer Based Sensor for Real-Time Phenylalanine and pH Monitoring
abstract: Developing biosensors for real-time monitoring is crucial for understanding cell metabolism and improving quality control in biotechnology. This article presents a biocompatible, high frequency scanned, dual-purpose electrochemical aptamer based (EAB) sensor for real-time monitoring of pH and amino acid (phenylalanine) concentration. The sensor can measure phenylalanine concentrations ranging from 1 μM to 3 mM and pH. Additionally, a leakless reference electrode is integrated into the system to prevent Ag+ ion cytotoxicity in cell cultures, enhancing the sensor's biocompatibility. This sensor allows researchers to gain deeper insights into cellular pH and amino acid consumption, advancing fundamental research in biology and biotechnology.

articleTitle: A Microfluidic Platform Based on Magnetic Labels for Rapid Mixing, Trapping and Detection of Biomarkers
abstract: Early diagnosis of diseases, which usually relies on biomarker detection, can prevent the mass spread of infectious diseases and dramatically reduce mortality rates in patients with different diseases. However, traditional detection methods are limited by their complexity and long time spent associated with multiple handling and transfer steps. The development of simple and automated diagnostic devices for rapid and sensitive biomarker detection is significant. In this study, a fully integrated and automated microfluidic platform was proposed. A microfluidic chip with an active-passive mixing module, micro-coil, and functional sensing region was designed for rapid sample processing. A spin exchange relaxation-free (SERF) atomic magnetometer was used to scan the remanent field of magnetic labels. The detection limit of fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP), which was an early cardiovascular disease biomarker, reached 1.57 pg/mL. And the whole detection process can be finished in 25 minutes, which shows high potential for the early detection of diseases.

articleTitle: Gain and Distortion Optimization for Fast-Startup AC-Coupled Baseband Amplifiers in Motion-Sensing Radar
abstract: Microwave radar has been widely adopted as a wireless sensor to accurately detect μm-scale motions. Low-cost sensors often use ac-coupled baseband amplifiers to increase the signal level for digitization, but these can increase startup times for low-frequency sensing. Recent architectures have shown that startup times can be improved using commercial diodes but have not been tested in a wide range of use cases to evaluate potential limitations. This work presents an in-depth analysis of diode-based ac-coupled fast-startup amplifiers to quantify the impacts of 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup> order effects on amplifier performance. The closed-form solutions are verified using SPICE software, with experimental results confirming the effects of nonidealities in realistic radar applications.

articleTitle: Graphene/Silver-fused Nanocomposites for Strain Sensing Applications
abstract: The paper discusses the fabrication and implementation of novel graphene/silver composite-based sensors. The need for low-cost, printed sensors that can be applied in multiple strain-induced applications has been a need in the current scenario. Both graphene and silver have shown exceptional sensing capabilities due to their enhanced electrical and mechanical properties. Although they have been individually used in pure and composite forms, their integration in forming electrodes improves the performance to a great extent. The conjugation of two nanomaterials to form efficient, sensitive, flexible sensors is shown here. The results shown here form a podium for the sensors to be used for real-time strain-sensing applications.

articleTitle: High-Precision Prediction of NOx, NO2 and C6H6 by Multiple Gas Sensors Using a Novel Cascaded MLP-LSTM Model
abstract: Gas sensing applications provide real-time, accurate monitoring crucial for public health and environmental sustain ability, especially outdoors. Outdoor gas sensing faces challenges from sensor distortions due to temperature, humidity, and cross-sensitivity interference. This study employs a sensor array with a machine learning algorithm that combines a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model, tailored for edge applications to compensate for cross-sensitivity and temperature-humidity variations. The features of MLP stacked with LSTM highlight the breakthrough growth of such network models in gas concentration estimation. In the Experimental results showed significant improvement in gas estimation accuracy with the proposed MLP-LSTM model, achieving R2 values of 0.812, 0.803, 0.644, and 0.997 for CO, NOx, N02, and C6H6, respectively.

articleTitle: Potassium and Sodium Ion Concentration Sensors for Intracranial Monitoring Based on Solid-State Electrode
abstract: Craniocerebral injury is a medical problem that has attracted global attention. Intracranial K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>and Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>concentrations are crucial indicators of intracranial status. Real-time monitoring of craniocerebral parameters is helpful in the diagnosis and treatment of craniocerebral injury. In this study, we developed a flexible sensor that can be used to monitor intracranial K<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>and Na<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>concentrations, and we verified the performance of the sensor through animal implantation experiments. Thus, a new option for minimally invasive real-time monitoring of intracranial parameters is provided.

articleTitle: Low Noise Temperature Compensation Strategy for North-finding MEMS Gyroscope
abstract: This work analyzes the influence of different temperature compensation strategies on the bias instability (BI) of MEMS gyro for north-finding. Three temperature sources are involved, namely, conventional CMOS sensor and two virtual sensors based on the gyro's drive frequency and gain control voltage. We show that virtual measurement based on drive frequency is immune to the 1/f noise in CMOS readout circuit, and the measurement instability improved from 20m°C to 1.2m°C. Although virtual measurement based on gain control voltage still suffers from 1/f noise disturbance, its larger temperature sensitivity results in a better instability of 7m°C. The selection criteria of temperature sensor for mass-produced MEMS gyro with different temperature coefficients (TCOs) is proposed. Applying the virtual compensation strategies to a 4-position Maytagging procedure, the azimuth accuracy is increased from 0.47° to 0.26° and 0.35° within 5min.

articleTitle: Sense-Based User Interface (SUI) Platforms to Detect Children's Physical and Emotional Behaviors
abstract: With the rapid development of digital entertainment and educational content, young children of five or under are exposed to digital input/output devices. Their social skills are essential in physical and emotional development and can be acquired through cooperative activities with peers of the same age. However, with the increase in digital input/output devices, social isolation of young children is a critical problem, resulting in a lack of social, language, and self-regulation skills. This study introduces sense-based user interface (SUI) platforms that can seamlessly interact with young children to collect and analyze children's physical and emotional behaviors through flexible sensors. Specifically, we designed SUI platforms by integrating flexible pressure and touch sensors into a toy drum, a familiar and engaging object for young children. Synchronous systems are developed to collect data instantaneously when the child strikes the drum in response to the teacher's instruction, and the collected data in real-time can be visualized to analyze children's physical and emotional behaviors. The synchronous SUI platform can compare the characteristic development status between exceptional and regular children. The proposed SUI platforms are expected to evaluate early childhood development characteristics like motor, interaction, and self-regulation skills.

articleTitle: Enhanced Magneto-Mechanical Coupling with FeGaB/AlN Thin Films in Mesoscopic Silicon-Free Coupled-Structure Magnetoelectric Resonators
abstract: In conventional MEMS magnetoelectric (ME) sensors, the presence of a silicon substrate introduces extra mechanical stress and energy dissipation, hindering the direct and efficient coupling between the magnetostrictive and piezoelectric layers. In this case, we developed a silicon-free ME resonator design, featuring an asymmetric coupled cantilever beam structure, where one beam has a 200 nm FeGaB magnetic layer on a 1 μm AIN piezoelectric layer, while the other beam has only the piezoelectric layer. The hysteresis loop further indicates stable magnetic performance with a low energy loss of 83.56 J/m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. Dynamic characterization using laser Doppler interferometry reveals enhanced magneto-mechanical coupling of 367 ppm/Oe, especially at resonant frequencies around 65.35 kHz with a quality factor of 602 under atmospheric conditions. The absence of the Si substrate minimizes mechanical losses, amplifying the magneto-mechanical coupling, marking an improvement over Si-based counterparts. This ME design shows potential for high-precision positioning and magnetic imaging applications.

articleTitle: Biocompatible Artificial Skin with an Embedded Optical Fiber Specklegram Sensor
abstract: Artificial skins are flexible devices with multi-parameter sensing ability, mimicking the functionalities of biological structures. This work presents a biocompatible transducer made of agar gel with an embedded optical fiber sensor. A concatenated hetero-core fiber structure produces speckle patterns modulable by the applied physical or chemical stimulus, whereas the enclosing agar package conveys mechanical strength and flexibility. The sensor achieved force, bending, and temperature resolutions of 0.03 N, 0.14°, and 0.34°C, respectively, besides a spatial resolution of 0.7 mm. Furthermore, the agar structure is sensitive to surrounding liquids and moistures, endorsing possible applications in biomedical and biochemical assessments.

articleTitle: TFT Active Pixel Sensors with Organic Photoconductive Films for Flexible Sensor Applications
abstract: We demonstrate the fabrication and imaging operation of a thin-film transistor (TFT) active pixel sensor (APS) with an organic photoconductive film (OPF) on a film-laminated glass carrier. Using a three-transistor APS signal readout circuit composed of indium-tin-zinc-oxide TFTs and an ultralow-dark-current «30 pA/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>) OPF with a top transparent electrode, we successfully obtained an image output from the sensor with a pixel number of 320 x 240 and a frame frequency of 60 Hz. We also describe the sub-μm-thick thin-film encapsulation (TFE) at a low process temperature of ≤100°C with no thermal degradation of the OPFs, as a replacement for the 60-μm-thick encapsulation film used in the fabricated TFT APS. We found that there was no degradation in the OPF characteristics with TFE even after the patterning processes for the TFE layer including alkali, acid, and water immersions.

articleTitle: Parametric Physics-Based Snow Model for Automotive Cameras
abstract: Assisted and automated driving (AAD) systems rely on perception sensors such as camera and RADAR to build situational awareness. These safety critical systems have to operate robustly when subjected to environmental conditions, e.g. snow and rain, reducing the perception performance. This work proposes a novel snow model, applied to raw camera data, that considers the drop size distribution (DSD) of falling snow given specific camera parameters. The model was applied to real ‘ideal’ data and compared with and validated against real ‘snow’ data. The results demonstrate that different drop sizes affect the image differently, smaller drops create a blurring/loss of contrast in the frames, larger drops result in more significant changes in the pixel content. This model can significantly aid testing and development of robust AAD systems.

articleTitle: Lightweight Energy-Constraint Wireless Sensor Solution for Plant Monitoring
abstract: Plants are continuously in motion, and their movements change rapidly under suboptimal conditions. Tracking these movements offers a unique way to assess their physiological condition and detect stress. This paper presents a novel approach to real-time plant movement monitoring using a lightweight wearable wireless sensor system with an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU). Integrating IMU data in crop monitoring allows precise detection and analysis of plant motions, providing insights into growth patterns and environmental responses. Our sensor solution is designed to minimize weight and power consumption, supporting complete long crop cycles of various greenhouse crops without the need to recharge or replace batteries. The sensor weighs only 17.89 g without casing and has a 14-month lifespan. Its wireless capability facilitates real-time data collection and easy deployment. Initial in-situ validation confirms that this non-intrusive, cost-effective sensor solution presents a convenient approach for emerging plant sensing applications and Internet of Things (IoT)-enabled crop monitoring systems.

articleTitle: A Fully Integrated E-nose System With 256 Half-Virtual Gas-Sensitive Pixels for Gas Recognition
abstract: In this article, a fully integrated Electronic-nose (E-nose) system for gas recognition is proposed. Integrated with four Micro-Electro-Mechanical systems (MEMS) metal-oxide (MOX) gas sensors and a programmable interface circuit, the E-nose system can measure, process, analyze and output the gas types without external devices. In order to further improve the gas-sensitive feature datasets of different odors, the E-nose microsystem can also virtually expand up to 256 half-virtual gas-sensitive pixels by operating temperature modulation and measuring voltage regulation. Similar to current image sensor, this E-nose microsystem can continuously generate a gas grayscale image with 16 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\times 16$</tex> gas-sensitive pixels at a frequency of 0.0625 Hz. With a lightweight convolutional neural network (LCNN) algorithm embedded in the E-nose system, it can directly and precisely identify nine gas types based on gas-sensitive grayscale image.

articleTitle: Chinese Paper-cutting Inspired Topological Flexible Piezoresistive Pressure Sensor for Wearable Health Monitoring
abstract: Inspired by the traditional Chinese Paper-cuttings art, this paper develops a flexible piezoresistive sensor based on rhomboid topology. Non thermal cutting of carbon black polyethylene composite film is performed using high-frequency femtosecond laser to define the topological sensing unit. The resistance response sensitivity of the sensor to normal pressure can reach up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{17.5}\ \mathbf{kPa}^{-\mathbf{1}}$</tex>. After series and parallel connection and packaging, loading a grain of raw rice onto the sensor topological unit can cause approximately 1.2% of the sensor response. The effective application of the topological sensor in human pulse waveform monitoring, finger joint bending and rapid finger tapping further demonstrates the great potential of Chinese Paper-cuttings inspired topologies in flexible electronic devices.

articleTitle: Development of a Personalized Anomaly Detection Model to Detect Motion Artifacts Over PPG Data Using Catch22 Features
abstract: As remote health monitoring grows, it's crucial to distinguish high-quality biomedical signals from low-quality ones. Identifying and mitigating motion artifacts (MAs) is essential for accurate data from wearable devices. Methods: In this work, a high-performing subset of time-series features denoted as catch22 (22 CAnonical Time-series CHaracteristics) was used to detect the presence of MAs in photoplethysmogram (PPG) data acquired from the brachial and digital artery of 31 healthy subjects. Three unsupervised algorithms were employed along with catch22 to detect MAs within the dataset, these were: One-Class Support Vector Machine, Isolation Forest, and Local Outlier Factor. Results: Aggregated precision, recall, and F1-score were computed per each method to assess the detection performances according to a variety of features and anomalies' distribution. These metrics resulted respectively equal to 0.5, 0.64, and 0.55 for OC- SVM, 0.91, 0.94, and 0.92 for IF, and 0.74, 0.75, and 0.74 for LOF. Conclusion: Experimental findings illustrate that by employing the catch22 feature subset, it is viable to discern the presence of MAs in beat-to-beat pulse waveforms without recurring to prior knowledge or data-driven PPG features.

articleTitle: The Patchkeeper: An Integrated Wearable Electronic Stethoscope with Multiple Sensors
abstract: Many parts of human body generate internal sound during biological processes, which are rich sources of information for understanding health and wellbeing. Despite a long history of development and usage of stethoscopes, there is still a lack of proper tools for recording internal body sound together with complementary sensors for long term monitoring[1]. In this paper, we show our development of a wearable electronic stethoscope, coined “Patchkeeper” (PK), that can be used for internal body sound recording over long periods of time. PK also integrates several state-of-the-art biological sensors, including electrocardiogram (ECG), photoplethysmography (PPG), and inertial measurement unit (IMU) sensors. As a wearable device, PK can be placed on various parts of the body to collect sound from particular organs, including heart, lung, stomach, and joints etc. We show in this paper that several vital signals can be recorded simultaneously with high quality. As PK can be operated directly by the user, e.g. without involving health care professionals, we believe it could be a useful tool for telemedicine and remote diagnostics.

articleTitle: Plasmonic Micropillar Based SERS-Sensing Platform for Integrin Detection of Regulated Cells
abstract: Artificial extracellular matrix (ECM) has become a powerful tool to control cell behavior, but the traditional characterization method of the regulated cells has limits in sensing biocomponent changes in real time. In this work, a plasmonic micropillar was proposed by introducing gold nanorods (AuNRs) assembly on the polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) micropillar, which could serve as a surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS)-based sensing platform for integrin detection when cells were regulated by the topology of ECM. The regulated cells on the plasmonic micropillar showed contact guidance along the pattern and the amount of integrin between cells on different substrates were compared by multivariate curve resolution (MCR) analysis. The platform integrates ECM-induced cell alignment with SERS-based integrin measurement, offering opportunities to monitor biocomponents of regulated cells in real time, which may give insight into mechanisms of cell-interface response and tissue engineering.

articleTitle: Multimodal Stress and Boredom Detection via Smartwatch Sensors and Hybrid Deep Residual Network with CBAM
abstract: The prevalence of stress and boredom in contempo-rary culture substantially influences mental health and overall well-being. Identifying activities associated with these emotional states is essential to implement effective treatments and support systems. This research presents a new method for identifying stress and boredom activities using wristwatch sensor data and a hybrid deep learning model called CNN-ResBiGRU-CBAM. This model utilizes convolutional neural networks (CNN s), residual bidirectional gated recurrent units (GRUs), and a convolutional block attention module (CBAM) to acquire knowledge about spatial and temporal characteristics and comprehend intricate patterns in sensor input. The experimental results underscore the practical application of the proposed model in the field of affective computing and mental health monitoring. This model not only outperforms both traditional and state-of-the-art deep learning models in accurately identifying stress and boredom behaviors, but also demonstrates its adaptability in leave-one-subject-out validation. With an impressive accuracy of 99.47 % and an F1-score of 99.44% in 5-fold cross-validation, this model shows promise in acquiring features that are relevant to different individuals, thereby enhancing the field of affective computing and mental health monitoring through the use of wearable devices.

articleTitle: A Wireless Facemask for Ultrafast and Continuous Tracking of Breath CO2 Patterns
abstract: Respiration is a critical health indicator, necessitating affordable, portable, stable, and reliable wearable devices for monitoring exhaled carbon dioxide. We introduce a novel hydrophobic composite material, mCP/ZIF-8@COF, synthesized to create a fast-responsive (55 ms), humidity-resistant CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> sensor, significantly enhancing stability and reliability across various conditions. Integrating this sensor into a respiratory mask results in a wireless intelligent monitoring system capable of real-time analysis of breathing patterns, including normal, deep, rapid, cough, and apneic respirations. To improve COPD diagnostic accuracy, we developed an algorithm based on residual neural networks (RNN), achieving 93% accuracy in distinguishing COPD patients from healthy individuals based on respiratory waveforms. This system provides a real-time, non-invasive respiratory health monitoring solution, with data sharing capabilities for clinical use.

articleTitle: Modeling of Hall-Based Magnetoelastic Torque Sensors
abstract: Magnetoelastic torque sensors are prevalent in e-bikes. The full-scale magnetic field is typically below 1 mT and read out via discrete fluxgates in commercial sensor modules. To achieve a more compact integration, we explore in this paper Hall-based sensors. Using a multiphysics simulation model, we analyze the system design trade-off between sensitivity and robustness against mechanical misalignment. Our model shows that Gallium Arsenide Hall-based sensors can provide a noise-free resolution of 10 bits in a 500-Hz bandwidth, with a full-scale upper limit of 200 N ·m. Experimental validation confirms our simulation results. These findings establish a theoretical foundation for developing high-performance miniaturized magnetoelastic sensors for e-bikes and beyond.

articleTitle: Snowflake-Patterned CNT/LIG@SEBS-Based Dry Electrodes for Reliable Arrhythmia Diagnosis
abstract: Arrhythmia, a condition characterized by abnormal heart rhythms, can often lead to serious complications such as stroke, making early diagnosis crucial. This study aims to develop a wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) patch sensor capable of diagnosing arrhythmias by monitoring ECG in real-time. The sensor features laser induced graphene (LIG) electrode, inspired by snowflake pattern, which provided a large surface area that effectively minimizes noise from motion artifact. Furthermore, the sensor's performance was enhanced through drop casting carbon nanotubes (CNT), which improved the electrical conductivity and reduces the skin contact impedance, resulting in a value of 5. 5 x 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</sup>Ω at 100 Hz. The fabricated sensor exhibited higher signal to noise ratio (SNR) value compared to the commercial Ag/ AgCI electrodes, enabling more precise ECG waveform monitoring. The ECG sensor demonstrated SNR values of 49 dB while sitting, 25.4 dB while walking, and 20.7 dB while running. It is expected that the ECG patch sensor can be applied to wearable devices to monitor and diagnose personal health conditions in real-time.

articleTitle: Reference-Free Multi-Species Gas Detection via Unsupervised Learning
abstract: Conventional chemometric models rely heavily on reference spectra for accurate species quantification. However, the availability of reference spectra is not always guaranteed, deeming these models unreliable and impractical in many scenarios. To address this limitation, we introduce an AutoencoderBased Blind Source Separation (AE-BSS) model for multi-species detection. The AE-BSS model can infer both species concentrations and their reference spectra based solely on composite mixture spectra, eliminating the need for individual reference spectra. Initially tested with simulated mixtures of methane, ethylene, ethane, propane, benzene, toluene, o-xylene, and isoprene, the AE-BSS model demonstrated accurate quantification without requiring their reference spectra. To validate these findings experimentally, we employed a setup using a single infrared laser to train the AE-BSS model. The results showed that the model accurately predicted both the reference spectra and species concentrations. Our findings confirm the effectiveness and robustness of the AE-BSS in real-world scenarios, significantly enhancing gas sensing applications. Future work will focus on extending the application of the model to more complex environments, including high-pressure and high-temperature conditions.

articleTitle: A Data Driven Correction Algorithm for Inverse Problems with Application to Spectral Reconstruction
abstract: Plasmonic filter arrays offer a potential solution for creating compact and cost-effective spectrometers. However, they cannot filter accurately at specific wavelengths, resulting in raw outputs that do not adequately represent the spectra of measured objects. Consequently, a process is required to reconstruct the spectra from the CSS (Chip-Size Spectrometer) values. This paper presents a novel procedure for reconstruction that employs a transformation correction of the measured CSS values before approximating the spectra. The performance of this method is compared with a deep learning architecture, as well as least squares with Tikhonov regularization and Ridge regression. This evaluation is conducted using data from two different plasmonic filter arrays and a set of measurements based on transmittance foils. The results demonstrate that our method outperforms other approaches and achieves better reconstruction accuracy compared to pure learning methods, while needing significantly less data.

articleTitle: Collision-avoidance LoRaWAN Network for Intermittent Sensor Systems
abstract: This paper proposes a collision-avoidance algorithm to reduce LoRaWan communication collisions due to variability in energy harvesting (EH) time among intermittent end devices (nodes). This variability is caused by adjustment of communication parameters such as Spreading Factor (SF) and Transmitting Power <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(Tx)$</tex> as well as harvesting conditions. The proposed algorithm enhances the network's connectivity by efficiently allocating SF, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Tx$</tex>, transmission time and channel. The allocation considers network performance and introduces energy awareness into a TDMA-like collision avoidance protocol. The results revealed that the algorithm is able to synchronize intermittent nodes preventing collisions while maintaining connectivity with the network.

articleTitle: Neuromorphic Touch Sensors for Pleasantness Encoding via Spike Patterns: A Bio-Inspired Artifical Fingertip for Restoring Affective Sensations
abstract: The loss of tactile perception in individuals hinders their ability to interact with the environment. The touch sense not only allows humans to recognize textures and shapes, but also to feel pleasantness evoked by the touched surface. The perception of tactile affective sensations is essential for a person's well-being and social interactions. Hence, research in the field of bionic limbs aims at investigating how to restore the sense of touch comprehensively. In this study, the encoding of surface pleasantness by means of an artificial fingertip via neuronal-like spiking patterns is introduced. The proposed sensing system presents biomimetic features, mimicking the behavior and the distribution of the human finger's Merkel mechanoreceptors. The artificial fingertip demonstrated to capture the variations in pressure, shear, and vibration during the exploration of varied surfaces. The tactile information was then converted into spike trains through a neuromorphic approach. The outcomes of this study lay the foundations for restoring pleasantness sensations from textures through neural sensory feedback interfaces.

articleTitle: Noninvasive Glucose Estimation Using Multi-Wavelength Diffused Transmitted and Reflected NIRS in Solid Tissue Phantoms
abstract: We utilized a multi-wavelength laser proving system to study the feasibility of noninvasive glucose monitoring in soft silicon-based tissue phantoms fabricated for twelve glucose concentrations within the 0 to 420 mg/dl range. We also present results of monitoring the glucose levels in the solid tissue phantoms using concurrent diffused transmitted and reflected near-infrared detection with the simultaneous measurement of environmental factors. Our estimations using multivariate linear regression and multi-layer perceptron models resulted in 0.87 R2 and 39.65 RMS, as well as 1.0 R2 and 2.87 RMS, respectively, across 1110 frame datasets for twelve tissue samples.

articleTitle: Development of Plane Bending Fatigue Tester for Electrode Materials of Lithium-Ion Battery by Using Strain Sensors
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are used in various products. Especially in long-term use, accidents such as overheating and ignition of lithium-ion batteries often occur due to fatigue failure of electrode materials. In this study, mechanical fatigue tests were conducted on electrode materials to investigate the mechanical fatigue mechanism of the electrode materials and to establish a fatigue life prediction method. It is difficult to conduct fatigue tests on electrode materials by themselves because they are brittle thin films. Therefore, this study has developed and validated a plane bending fatigue tester to measure the fatigue life of the electrode materials coated on the metal foil by using strain sensors.

articleTitle: End-to-End Processing-on-Chip Wearable Ear EEG Device with Tiny Neural Network for Multilevel Stress Detection
abstract: The study proposes an innovative method for predicting stress levels that employs electroencephalography (EEG) data collected from behind the ear (BTE) and incorporates tiny neural networks (TNN). The system, which consists of an EEG processing device and a companion smartphone application for monitoring, is designed to: (1) collect EEG signals from behind the ear rather than the scalp, prioritizing comfort and reducing hair interference; (2) filter out irrelevant signals from the desired EEG; (3) extract relative power spectral density (PSD) features from EEG data using Fast Fourier Transform (FFT); and (4) classify stress levels using a proposed TNN. Importantly, all processing stages occur on the chip itself, rather than on external devices such as PCs or servers, providing fast and synchronized processing and preventing data loss during transmission. In addition, (5) a user-friendly smartphone app is being created for rapid and straightforward stress level monitoring. Experimental results show that the on-chip TNN is successful, with accuracy of 90.83%, precision of 90.87%, recall of 90.83%, and an F1-score of 0.9081, all verified using leave-one-subject-out cross-validation (LOOCV). This merging of BTE EEG analysis with on-chip TNNs offers the potential for enhancing mental stress detection and other health-related uses.

articleTitle: Effect of Periodic Rough Surface on Ultrasonic Pulse-echo Signal
abstract: Fluid flowing through a pipe not only reduces the pipe thickness but also creates a rough surface. In the inspection of pipes in the plant system, the pulse-echo method is used for thickness measurement. This study aims at the extension of the ultrasonic inspection and focuses on the reflected wave from a rough surface. In this paper, a simultaneous generation of plane and spherical waves by an ultrasonic probe is described. A computational simulation calculated the propagation of the ultrasonic waves in specimens with periodic flaws by the finite difference time domain method. In an experiment, a broadband frequency probe obtained ultrasonic signals in the same condition as the simulation. The simulation results were a good agreement with the experimental results.
