The frequency spectrum of the reflected wave depends on the periodic flaw parameters of the rough surface. This indicates a potential to predict the flaw parameters from the pulse-echo signal.

articleTitle: Significantly Improved Front Side Illuminated Photodiodes: Integrated in a 0.18 μm Modular CMOS Foundry Technology
abstract: Broadband reduced reflection loss of front side illuminated photodiodes realized within the restrictive environment of a standard 0.18 um CMOS production process without compromising dark current, capacitance or any other device parameter.

articleTitle: Analysis of Energy Harvesting in Beyond Diagonal-RIS-Enabled WSNs
abstract: Wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are used in many applications, especially for disaster management and surveillance in challenging terrains. The sensor nodes' energy is crucial for the network's lifetime and system performance. To address this, we investigated wireless power transfer (WPT) using radiative RF signals from the base station (BS). Since a direct link between BS and WSNs can be blocked, we consider a beyond-diagonal reconfigurable intelligent surface (BD-RIS)-enabled WPT for WSNs. We formulate the optimization problem to maximize total energy harvesting (EH) at the system's cluster head (CH) nodes, subject to BD-RIS scattering matrix constraints. We select CHs among the sensor nodes using the LEACH protocol. This work uses a low-complexity solution to the optimization problem. The proposed work is evaluated using MATLAB and compared to benchmark WPT and RIS-assisted WPT methods. We analyze the total EH versus transmit power for different BD-RIS modes and architectures. Additionally, we examine total EH for varying numbers of BD-RIS cells and CH distances. BD-RIS-enabled WPT shows a significant gain in total EH compared to WPT and RIS-assisted WPT.

articleTitle: High Dynamic Range Object Detection System with Image Fusion Network Using High-Illumination Specialized Binary Image
abstract: This study presents an object detection system combining a dual-imaging CMOS image sensor (CIS) with a fusion model to address feature loss from light saturation. The CIS captures general and binary images, with the latter providing additional information in saturated conditions. These images are fused to preserve texture details and enhance detection under high-intensity lighting. Using the PascalRaw dataset, the proposed system demonstrates robust performance across various lighting conditions, significantly outperforming traditional methods. This research highlights the effectiveness of machine-friendly sensors and fusion models in improving object detection accuracy.

articleTitle: In-Line Portable Moisture Sensor
abstract: We designed, fabricated and tested an in-line portable moisture sensor for industrial applications, which comprises a sensor array that can detect the moisture content in plastic granulates at real time as well as all the necessary readout electronics for signal processing and communication. Measurement results performed with plastic pellets showed that the in-line portable moisture sensor can detect the moisture content with a precision of 100 ppm thus providing a very important control input, which is used to reduce the amount of energy consumed by industrial drying systems and also to enable added production time by avoiding the additional drying time caused by utilizing the fixed drying time recommended in the datasheet of the plastic granulate.

articleTitle: Analysis of Piezoresistive Silicon as Sense Element for use in Flexible Tactile Sensors
abstract: This paper presents the bending analysis of stress-sensor chips of 300 µm and 100 µm thickness. Previous work on similar topics is usually heavily focused on ultra-thin chips (≤20 µm) and their reliability analysis for flexible applications. This paper aims to prove that flexible tactile sensors can be made using silicon resistors as the primary stress elements and can demonstrate good results even at intermediate thickness levels. The silicon resistors show a linear temperature response and can be oriented to have directional stress sensitivity, proving superior to other organic sensors. The motivation behind this research is to make the tactile sensor solely using CMOS circuits and, therefore, integrate both the sensor and the readout circuitry in one chip. This is extremely useful if the tactile sensors are used on a large scale and must be fabricated commercially using existing infrastructure.

articleTitle: A Gelatin/Activated Carbon Multifunctional Coating for Future Edible Diagnostic Systems
abstract: Edible electronics aims to deliver safe-to-eat devices for gastrointestinal tract monitoring constituted by food-derived materials and therefore can be metabolised by the human body. However, identifying materials and processing methods for edible sensors and electronics remains an open challenge. Here we present an edible multifunctional composite coating produced by spray-coating an ink formulation of activated carbon (conductor) and commercial gelatin-based candy (binder) in a water-ethanol dispersant. The coating exhibits advantageous electronic properties, including conductivity (~50 Ω.cm resistivity), piezoresistivity, stretchability and temperature sensitivity. To demonstrate its versatility, the same composite formulation is used to deliver functional properties to a range of relevant electronic components, namely gating material for field-effect transistors, and strain, pressure, and temperature sensors.

articleTitle: Covalent Functionalization of Violet Phosphorus Nanosheets for Room-Temperature NO2 Sensing
abstract: Violet phosphorus possesses unique band structure, making it a promising candidate for electronic device applications. This study presents covalently functionalized violet phosphorus nanosheets (VPNSs) for sensitive and selective detection of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) gases at room temperature. The modified VPNSs were facilely synthesized via liquid-phase exfoliation and subsequent covalent functionalization with nitrophenyl groups (VPNSs-PhNO2), significantly changing the intrinsic electronic properties and improving their gas-sensing performance. SEM and FTIR analyses confirmed the effective attachment of nitrophenyl groups which contributed to their enhanced sensitivity and selectivity response towards NO2 gases. The sensing results revealed that as-modified VPNSs exhibited markedly faster response and recovery times compared to conventional sensors. It is suggested that the nitro groups not only facilitated the semiconductor type transition but also improved the interaction of VPNSs with NO2 gas. These innovative designs of VPNSs-PhNO2 sensors offer a solution for highly sensitive NO2 detection.

articleTitle: Towards Fabrication of Next-Generation Physical Sensors Through Integrating Suspended Sub-Micron Silicon Nanowires with Microelectromechanical Systems
abstract: Silicon nanowires possess superior mechanical, electrical, and optical properties, making them ideal for next-generation sensors. This study presents a scalable technology for monolithic fabrication of sub-micron silicon nanowires with micro electromechanical systems, achieving integration of suspended sub-micron silicon nanowires within microelectromechanical systems up to 80 μm thick on Si substrates, with high yield and repeatability. The technological approach is validated on silicon-on-insulator substrates, followed by electromechanical characterization via electrical probe measurements and vibrational testing for performance validation. The presented technology is promising for the potential development of next-generation high-performance physical sensors such as accelerometers and gyroscopes.

articleTitle: An Inkjet-Printed Stretchable Sensor Patch for Multimodal Physiological Monitoring
abstract: Emerging wearable technologies have opened up a realm of possibilities for accessible daily health monitoring. Here, an inkjet-printed stretchable sensor patch capable of electrochemical sensing and biopotential recording is presented. The sensor adopts a multi-layer configuration embedded with horseshoe-shaped serpentines, resulting in favorable mechanical stability that can withstand 20% deformation. By employing functional surface modifications, the sensor patch enables real-time monitoring of K+ and glucose with sensitivities of 55.72 mV/decade and 688.1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{nA}/(\text{mM}\cdot \text{cm}^{2})$</tex> respectively. In vivo experiments for recording biopotentials further confirm the capability of the sensor patch for on-body continuous biological quantification, leading to enhanced possibilities for low-cost, comprehensive healthcare management.

articleTitle: A New Nonlinear Micromechanical Structure Used in MEMS Inertial Sensors
abstract: This paper presents a new MEMS design for micromechanical nonlinear springs to produce negative stiffness and reduce resonant frequency. The design incorporates a precise amount of negative stiffness, resulting in an overall softening behaviour that adjusts the structure's compliance under specific load conditions. Compared to existing nonlinear structures such as clamp-clamp curved beams, it requires much less inertial force to be pulled into a nonlinear force-displacement behaviour, resulting in a smaller mass and chip area. Additionally, it offers precise mechanism response definition and predictable system behaviour. The efficiency of the proposed design is demonstrated through its integration into a micromachined MEMS inertial sensor. Measurements on the sensor performance show a notable displacement sensitivity of ~1 μm/mg and a resonant frequency of ~16 Hz for the fabricated prototype.

articleTitle: MEMS Acetone Gas Sensors with Eu-doped SnO2/In2O3 Nanofibers Using Electrospinning and Lithography Patterning Technique
abstract: In this paper, 1 mol% europium-doped tin dioxide / indium trioxide (Eu-doped SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) nanofibers were fabricated by coaxial electrospinning device. At 300°C to 1 parts per million (ppm) of acetone, the micro electromechanical system (MEMS) gas sensor employing lithography technique to coat nanofibers showed an excellent response of 2.43 (the ratio of resistance in air and in target gas). Additionally, when compared with device using drop coating method, the sensor exhibited better response and acetone selectivity at trace concentration. Wafer-level outstanding uniformity and consistency of acetone sensing performance were exhibited. This research suggested Eu-doped SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/In<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>nanofibers prepared by such method have potential to manufacture high-throughput reliable MEMS acetone sensors.

articleTitle: Smartphone Video-Based Blood Pressure Estimation via Pulse Transit Time and Machine Learning
abstract: Blood pressure (BP) measurement is crucial for managing cardiovascular health, including conditions like hypertension, heart disease, and stroke. Traditional methods, such as auscultatory and oscillometric techniques, have limitations in terms of accessibility and convenience. Recent advancements in contactless health sensing technologies, like camera-based methods, offer promising alternatives. This study proposes a new BP estimation framework that captures facial and finger video data using the front and back cameras of an Android smartphone. By extracting photoplethysmography signals and computing Pulse Transit Time, we integrate participant height into the feature set. Pattern recognition using Chebyshev distance and 1-D Convolutional Neural Network for estimating BP. Due to the lack of existing datasets, we developed a dataset with 11 subjects engaging in different activities to induce BP changes. Our framework meets AAMI and Grade ‘A’ of BHS standards for both Systolic and Diastolic BP, with RMSE of 4.6092 and 3.3622, respectively. This innovation offers a cost-effective, user-friendly, and portable solution for BP monitoring, benefiting remote and underserved populations.

articleTitle: Plasmon-Induced Concentric Hexagonal Ring Resonator for Nanophotonic Sensing
abstract: A metal-insulator-metal waveguide-based concentric hexagonal ring resonator plasmonic nanosensor has been designed and optimized for sensing the refractive index of analytes. The sensor has been functionalized through a wide range of midIR wavelengths. In the spectral output from the sensor, the prevalent plasmonic modes (dipolar and quadrupolar) have exhibited prominent shifts in the resonance wavelengths with the changes as slight as 0.00025 RIU in the refractive index of the surrounding medium, making promises as a refractive index sensor. Further explorations have shown a systematic linear correlation of the resonance wavelengths with the refractive indices, with a sensitivity as high as 2700nm/RIU and a figure of merit ~17.5.

articleTitle: A Green and Facile Approach of Graphite Conductive Ink Preparation for Electrochemical Sensing Application
abstract: Conventionally, Graphite (GR) conductive ink is formulated by dispersing GR particles in organic solvents like N-methyl-2-Pyrrolidone(NMP), Dimethylformamide(DMF), etc.; however, these solvents are toxic and require high annealing temperatures, render them incompatible for flexible substrate. Here, we report a green and facile method to synthesize GR conductive ink by employing the eco-friendly solvent ethanol and acetone with biodegradable binder Cellulose Acetate (CA) and its subsequent use in fabricating disposable paper sensors. Characterization of paper sensors revealed uniform morphology with good conductivity. The choice of CA to GR ratio and paper grade improved the sensor's electrochemical performance. Finally, we evaluated the utility of the fabricated paper sensor in estimating bovine serum albumin (BSA) by employing the redox cycling process. Chronoamperiometry detection of BSA showed a linear range between 0-500mg/dl with a detection limit of 1.48mg/dl. This work provides a promising way to formulate a sustainable, affordable, and easily scalable method for GR conductive ink preparation for flexible electrochemical sensing applications.

articleTitle: Cytotoxicity Anlysis of Drugs Using Contrast Surface Plasmon Images in Gold Nanoslit Arrays
abstract: We have fabricated a transmission-based surface plasmon resonance (SPR) label-free sensor for assessing cell adhesion and cell-drug interaction. Changes in cell adhesion can be analyzed through transmission images of nanoslit array sensors (NAS). However, the precise cytotoxicity of anticancer drugs such as doxorubicin (DOX) remains uncertain using previous approach. In the current work, we provide a new strategy of using NAS reflectance imaging to evaluate the cytotoxicity of DOX on the CLI-O lung cancer cell line. By capturing NAS reflection images at three designated time points during cytotoxicity assessment, we can quantify the percentage of CLI-O cells attachment affected by DOX, as well as the half inhibitory concentration (IC50) value of DOX for CLI-O cells. A conventional approach, CCK-8 assay, was used to conduct a cytotoxicity test on DOX, and the results showed that the IC50 obtained by NAS was no different from the traditional method. Label-free cytotoxicity assessment using NAS is simple and time-saving approach. Furthermore, it provides quantitative analysis for anticancer drug cytotoxicity. It is a very powerful platform for developing new anti-cancer drugs in the future.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Background Odor Influence on Mold Odor Detection Using Multiple Insect Olfactory Receptor-Based Sensor Arrays
abstract: Insects possess a superior sense of smell, making them valuable for various practical applications. Given their sensitivity to mold-derived odorants in agricultural crops and food products, we aim to utilize them as biosensors to detect mold contamination. In real-world scenarios of mold contamination, the presence of background odorant components, alongside mold-derived odorant components pose a potential challenge. Therefore, our study investigated whether a sensor array using multiple cell-based sensors expressing insect olfactory receptors can effectively discriminate mold-derived components by testing a mixture of samples containing a background odorant. Our experimental findings suggested that, with appropriate selections, mold odorants can be successfully differentiated even amidst the presence of background odorant components.

articleTitle: Imaging of Sr-90 Radionuclide Sources Based on Diamond Pixel Detectors
abstract: In recent years, the demand for detectors enabling real-time monitoring of both the activity and the spatial distribution of Sr-90 radionuclides has grown significantly. This is a consequence of the increased dispersion of radiotoxic Sr-90 in the environment, but also of the recently proposed use of Sr-90 sources in space and industry applications. Here, the first example of real-time imaging of the spatial intensity profile of a low-activity (3.7 kBq) Sr-90 radionuclide source obtained with a polycrystalline diamond (PCD) pixel detector is reported. High-quality substrates are used, ensuring a 80% charge collection efficiency under irradiation with beta particles, an unprecedented result for PCD. The remarkable pixel response uniformity (relative standard deviation < 5%), along with the absence of inter-pixel cross-talk, allow for realtime measurements with no need for correction factors or pixel-by-pixel calibration. In addition, the low operating voltage (10 V) and a dedicated compact front-end/read out electronics for signal conditioning and data acquisition ensure the device portability, essential to applications requiring in-situ monitoring of Sr-90 radionuclide sources.

articleTitle: Piezoresistive Accelerometer Based on Amorphous Carbon Films
abstract: Amorphous carbon film (a-C) has many outstanding characteristics, such as low friction, anti-wear properties and chemical stability. Its preparation is low cost, simple, and can well combined with microelectromechanical system (MEMS) process. Because it has remarkable piezoresistive effect, a-C piezoresistor was integrated in accelerometer to get a high-performance sensor. Using electron cyclotron resonance (ECR) plasma sputtering and ion evaporation deposition process, a-C was integrated on the quad-beam-mass structure as piezoresistor which had high gauge factor. By adjusting process parameters, the gauge factor could be controlled. In the ECR sputtering process, bias voltage +50 V and +100 V was applied to the substrate, respectively. And the gauge factor was within the range of 3.2-6.7 and 5.5-9.6; in the other process, a negative bias voltage 2 kV was applied to the substrate, then the hydrogenated amorphous carbon films (a-C: H) was deposited, which had a higher gauge factor 40.5-54.2. A MEMS piezoresistive accelerometer based on a-C piezoresistor was designed and fabricated. The piezoresistive accelerometer which used a-C: H had higher sensitivity 0.023 mV/V/g and natural frequency 18.1 kHz. This study provided a new method to further improvement of the comprehensive performance of MEMS piezoresistive accelerometer.

articleTitle: Dual-Measurement Pitot Tube Type Airflow and Waterflow Speed Sensor for Seabird Biologging
abstract: This study reports on a Pitot tube type airflow and waterflow speed sensor for seabird biologging. Due to seabirds' remarkable ability to traverse the sea and sky, biologging method, in which sensors are attached to animals, has been used to measure their locomotion under natural conditions. To evaluate seabird locomotion, a sensor was required that could be attached to a seabird and directly measure relative air speed and water speed. Here, we propose a sensor that incorporates a Pitot tube structure and a polytetrafluoroethylene porous film with air permeability and waterproof properties. We achieved the ability to switch the measurement principle between air and water using the same sensor element, enabling the measurement of different pressure ranges. The sensor demonstrated adequate responsiveness to airflow ranging from 0–10 m/s and waterflow from 0-1.6 m/s in experiments.

articleTitle: 3D Printing of Electrically Conductive Silver Nanoparticle-Embedded Foams for Pressure Sensor Applications
abstract: Flexible pressure sensors with high sensitivity have gained considerable attention in the electronic skin, human motion control, and health monitoring fields. Porous structures strongly enhance the compressibility and sensitivity in piezoresistive sensors compared with bulk materials. However, traditional foam fabrication methods lead to poor adhesion between nanofillers and polymer matrix, instability, complexity, and low reproducibility. We report a single-step 3D printing process for silver nanoparticle-embedded foams, creating pressure sensors with controlled conductivity, shape, and stiffness. Our silver nanoparticle-embedded foam-based sensors achieve high sensitivity with a wide working range and minimal hysteresis. Additionally, these sensors demonstrated robust durability, maintaining consistent resistance signals across 250 cyclic tests, and are integrated into a pressure patch and smart shoe sole for human motion monitoring.

articleTitle: Highly Sensitive Biosensors for Chemicals of Alcohol Metabolism
abstract: The volatile organic compounds (VOCs) produced and emitted by the human body have the potential to monitor metabolism and disease in real-time. The biosensors are suitable for measuring such VOCs because of their molecular selectivity. Here, we studied the strategy for enhancing the sensitivity of enzyme-based biosensors based on the substrate recycling reaction. Alcohol metabolism was selected as a model system for evaluation, and we targeted the simultaneous detection of both ethanol (EtOH) and acetaldehyde (AcH). Substrate cycling was achieved by combining alcohol oxidase (AOD), which can catalyze EtOH by consuming oxygen, and alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH), which can catalyze AcH by consuming nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH), which has autofluorescence (ex. 340 nm, em. 490 nm). The feasibility of the AOD/ADH cycling reaction was demonstrated by oxygen sensing and NADH fluorescence sensing. The experimental results showed that the AOD/ADH cycling reaction contributed to the improvement of the lower limit of quantification by a factor of 2 and 1000 in oximetry (for EtOH, the dynamic range was 0.7-500 µM) and fluorometry (for AcH, the dynamic range was 59 pM-100 µM). The AOD/ADH substrate cycling reaction can be applied to sensors that react with important chemicals in alcohol metabolism: both EtOH and AcH.

articleTitle: Relative Measurement of Micro-UAVs Based on a Miniaturized 2D Profile Sensor System
abstract: Relative positioning serves as one of the key tech-nologies for the autonomous flight of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarms. The mainstream vision-based methods in existing studies have high demands for computing power, energy, and size. When deployed on UAVs, especially micro-UAVs of several hundred grams, their accuracy and update rate are limited. In this study, we have developed a miniaturized high-precision relative measurement system utilizing a 2D profile sensor. The system achieves a relative angle measurement accuracy of around 1°. The results are fused with onboard ultra-wideband (UWB) system. Experiment results indicate the fusion system reaches a centimeter-level relative positioning accuracy, providing accurate relative coordinates for micro-UAV swarm cooperative missions.

articleTitle: A Dual Port Low Reflection Microwave Angular Displacement Sensor Based on Transversal Signal Interference Principle
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a novel dual-port low-reflection microwave angular displacement sensor that employs the transversal signal interference (TSI) principle to achieve high-precision and large-range dual-parameter sensing. It has good linearity in the sensing range of 0°-180°, and the sensitivity accuracy can reach 0.6 MHz/deg and 0.033 dB/deg. The sensor is specially designed to minimize reflection interference, and the sensor is low-reflective by integrating absorption filter networks both at the input and output ports, which greatly improves the practicality of microwave sensors in practical applications. Simulations and implementation measurements prove that the sensor can realize excellent linearity and dynamic range with low reflection characteristics.

articleTitle: Inkjet-printed Electrohydraulic Actuator
abstract: Soft actuators have emerged as a promising field and have shown great potential to revolutionize robotics, healthcare, and other industries. Among various types of soft actuators, electrohydraulic actuators have proved to be the most versatile with their ability to produce high force and actuation strain without compromising compliance and flexibility. However, the existing fabrication methods for the development of soft actuators may not be well suited for miniature actuator development. Here, we introduced an alternating methodology for fabrication of miniature actuators utilizing inkjet printing and 3D printing. We demonstrated a three-pouch configuration actuator achieving a strain of 8.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> by optimizing design parameters.

articleTitle: Real-Time Gas-Compensated Thermal Flow Sensor
abstract: In this paper, a thermal flow sensor is presented that is compensated real-time for changes in gas composition. The sensor comprises a thermal flow meter and a velocity-independent gas properties meter. The maximum error of the gas properties meter due to velocity fluctuations is less than 1 % which enables the measurement of thermal conductivity and volumetric heat capacity under dynamic flow conditions. These two parameters are obtained using a single sensing wire with two different measurement techniques, DC excitation and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3}\omega$</tex> method. Various gases, including pure gases and binary gas mixtures (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, Ar, air, He, Ar-air, and He-air), are applied, and the flow rate is corrected for each gas simultaneously using the measured physical parameters. The obtained maximum error between the measured and applied flow rate is 8.8% for CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and less than 5 % for the other gases.

articleTitle: Modeling of Synthetic Biology-Based Plant Sensors
abstract: Synthetic biology-based plant sensors detect plant responses to either biotic or abiotic stress. The sensing can be due to the response of a promoter gene activating a reporter gene, expressing a protein that activates—directly or indirectly—a signal output mechanism. The promoter-reporter operation can be a single-stage response or a multiple-stage one, where, for example, the expressed protein of the first stage activates another promoter gene. The output signal can be optical, electrical, or electrochemical. The sensor can be a multiple-input/multiple-output device and include control elements, such as a genetic optical switch, or feedback mechanisms for reducing background noise and improving signal-to-noise ratio. Next is the transducer, converting the biological signal to an electrical signal for further signal processing, analog to digital conversion, storage, and network communication. The modeling of each of the stages: whole-cell sensing, protein expression and signal transduction, and CMOS interfacing, is presented, and a unified approach is proposed allowing for complete system modeling using Verilog-A hardware description language (HDL).

articleTitle: A Flexible Capacitive Pressure Sensor with Improved Sensitivity Over a Broad Pressure Range
abstract: This Flexible pressure sensors with high sensitivity over a broad range are essential for practical applications. However, most sensors exhibit low sensitivity when subjected to high pressure. Herein, a hierarchical hybrid dielectric layer comprising short PDMS/CNT and high PDMS cones is proposed to realize a higher sensitivity over a high-pressure range. The novel square ring arrangement of hierarchical microstructures and dielectric constants contributes to a three-fold increase in sensitivity as the pressure exceeds 20 kPa, along with a fast response of 184 ms and a detection limit of 9.2 Pa. These merits enable this sensor to monitor real-time subtle radial arterial pulses. Furthermore, the as-proposed sensor is further integrated with a homemade keyboard cover and successfully achieves finger-pressing discrimination for different individuals, paving the way for privacy protection during unlocking via passwords.

articleTitle: Quality Factor Optimization and Thermal Noise Analysis of Silicon MEMS Resonators*
abstract: Silicon MEMS resonators (SMR) are employed as high-precision sensors, covering a wide range of practical applications for sensing acceleration, angular velocity, gravity, temperature, magnetism, and gases. However, the advancements of such a technology hinge on noise performance, wherein frequency thermal noise is the physical noise limit that poses challenges. This paper focuses on the theoretical modeling of SMR, frequency thermal noise analysis, and quality factor optimization. Starting from the double- ended tuning fork (DETF) equation of motion, the linear spectral density of frequency thermal noise is analyzed by combining the phase noise and frequency noise conversion relationship. Through theoretical analysis and multi-physics simulations, the interaction of structural parameters on the Q- factor is obtained. Further, the effectiveness of the Q-factor on frequency thermal noise is investigated. By optimizing the structure of SMR, the frequency thermal noise is reduced by up to 17.88-fold, of about 2.76 µHz/Hz<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1/2</sup>, compared to the common DETF. The study of the relationship between the parameters of SMR and the frequency thermal noise reveals that the optimization route by increasing the ratio of the Q- factor to the eigenfrequency. In addition, such a method can be adapted as a universal technique to analyze the noise performance of other types of resonant sensors.

articleTitle: Composite and Stretchable Silicone for Niche Profiling Applications
abstract: In this work, we developed a silicone and polyurethane (PU)-based composite, which supports stretchable applications. Through material survey, comparison, and mechanical characterization, it was proved that the roll-to-roll manufactured product shows cohesive bonding force over <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2}\ \ \mathbf{Kg}/\mathbf{cm}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex>, outperforming existing commercialized ones. Eight composite formulations were evaluated through ASTM D5459-95 standard, which indicated outstanding elastic recovery (between 89.72% and 93.65%), permanent deformation (between 6.35% and 10.28%) and stress retention (between 68.34% and 92.32%). In addition, a three-dimensional profiling that incorporated the developed composite further demonstrated its supportiveness on advanced sensing systems that require material stretchability.

articleTitle: A Wearable EEG Band Based on Spray-Coated Textile Bioelectrodes
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) is a non-invasive electrophysiological measurement that plays a pivotal role in diagnosing neurological disorders. Apart from the clinical use, EEG gained progressive attention in the assessment and recognition of emotional states, the development of non-invasive human-machine interfaces, and for biofeedback. In such contexts, the development of innovative bioelectrodes, able to improve comfort and unobtrusiveness, fabricated by means of scalable, large-area fabrication techniques, is an important research goal. Herein, we present a novel approach for the fabrication of EEG textile bioelectrodes, which are based on large-area, spray coated poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate conductive polymer, mixed with an ionic additive. The bioelectrodes exhibit comparable performance with a commercial wearable device for EEG signal acquisition (i.e., the Muse™ headset), when analyzing the EEG power spectral density during both eyes closed and eyes open conditions. These results suggest that the proposed textile electrodes could be an efficient alternative to state-of-the-art EEG electrodes, particularly in applications where unobtrusive and comfortable sensing is required.

articleTitle: A Wafer-level Package Design with Symmetrical Out-plane Electrodes for 3D-MEMS Devices
abstract: This paper describes a three-layer wafer-level package (WLP) scheme with lateral feedthrough signals and double-sided symmetrical out-plane electrodes for 3D MEMS devices. The WLP usually adopts the lateral signal routing scheme under the insulating layer or the vertical routing scheme based on TGV and TSV processes. SOI processes cannot easily place out-plane electrodes under the device layer. Therefore, a WLP scheme based on the SOG process and lateral signal routing is proposed and verified. The fabrication sequentially adopts anodic bonding and Au-Sn solid-liquid interdiffusion (SLID) bonding to realize the encapsulation of a stack of three layers and gap control of symmetrical out-plane electrodes by anchors and standoffs on device layer. Considering that the signal leads arranged under the insulation will face the risk of failure due to bonding pressure, this paper designs a novel signal lateral feedthrough scheme to improve the process yield. Shear strength test shows an average shear strength of 18.5MPa. Capacitance measurement is done to evaluate fabrication accuracy of out-plane electrodes. 8 dies from first fabrication flow have an average capacitance dispersion of 8.9%.

articleTitle: Powering Wireless Sensors Using Magnetoelectric Wireless Power Transfer
abstract: This paper presents a method to wirelessly power sensors using magnetoelectric (ME) structures as receivers. ME receivers consist of composites of magnetostrictive (MS) and piezoelectric material. Using ME receivers, as opposed to inductively coupled coils, is useful when a combination of small size and low frequency are desirable. Most ME receivers require a large DC magnetic field bias for high-performance operation. We present magnetization grading approach with multiple layers of MS material that results in high-performance structures with no DC magnetic field bias required. Our device produces 600 microwatts when excited by a 100 microtesla AC magnetic field at 192.3 kHz. The device is 12.4 mm X 5 mm X 1 mm. The corresponding normalized power density is 10.71 mWcm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−3</sup>Oe<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−2</sup>, which is the highest reported to our knowledge.

articleTitle: Smart Mattress Cover for Unobtrusive Monitoring of Sleep-Quality Correlates in Real-Life
abstract: This paper presents the design, development, and preliminary testing of the Smart Mattress Cover (SMC), a non-obtrusive, mass-production suitable system for real-world data acquisition of physiological sleep parameters correlates. The SMC integrates a fabric-based pressure sensor matrix and two accelerometers within a flexible, user-friendly design. Preliminary laboratory tests demonstrates the system's capability to detect sleep-related physiological parameters, including respiratory activity, heart rate and subject's movement.

articleTitle: Size-Resolved Concentration Estimation of Nano- and Micro-Plastics for Different Water Salinity with Nanoelectrode Array Sensors
abstract: The need for accurate monitoring of nanoplastics and microplastics in water is increasing as global plastic production and waste continue to rise. In this context, this work explores the use of capacitance spectroscopy at nanoelectrode arrays for pollutant monitoring in water. This technology offers benefits such as portability, high parallelization, scalability, single particle detection, and measurement automatization. However, challenges arising from the dependence of the measurement on the ionic strength of the solution and the size of the nanopollutants must be carefully addressed. In this work, a size-resolved concentration estimation method for nanoplastics monitoring in water is investigated, extending the validity of previous preliminary results to a wide range of polydisperse particles' size and water salinity; hence, more realistic scenarios.

articleTitle: Thin Film Strain Sensors with Significantly Improved Piezoresistive Stability at High Temperatures by Introducing Insulating Phase
abstract: In this work, we propose a strategy to significantly enhance the piezoresistive stability of indium tin oxide (ITO) thin film strain sensors (TFSSs) at high temperatures. Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, known for its excellent thermal stability in harsh environments, was introduced into ITO matrices to form composite films. The effect of doping concentration on the crystal structure, surface morphology, electrical stability, and piezoresistive stability of ITO TFSSs were systematically investigated. Results reveal that the addition of Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>plays an important role in restraining recrystallization and reducing growth defects in ITO films at high temperatures, which leads to a remarkable improvement in piezoresistive stability by one order of magnitude. The idea disclosed in this work is of great significance for the design, fabrication, and enhancement of micro/nano piezoresistive sensors that operate in harsh environments.

articleTitle: Tactile Zero-Shot Sensing of Breast Tumors: Recognition of Human Data from Phantom Data
abstract: One of the biggest challenges of biomedical research is not having enough human data. This paper explored Tactile Attributes-based Zero-Shot Learning to recognize human data results from phantom data. Using this machine learning method, we trained a Multilayer Perceptron and a Support Vector Machine with the phantom data and estimated the malignancy level of the human data. The method showed that despite using phantom data for training, we successfully applied the knowledge to human data, achieving a malignancy level calculation accuracy of 74.42%, a sensitivity of 73.68%, and a specificity of 75.00%.

articleTitle: Solving Relative Measurements on Finite Graphs
abstract: Sensor networks often rely on relative, or differential, measurements between sensing nodes due to the absence of an absolute reference at each node. This distributed measurement model can be represented as a graph, where each node denotes an absolute “potential” to be estimated and each edge corresponds to a measurement of the relative potential difference between the two incident nodes. Solving for the absolute node potentials can be formulated as a matrix equation involving the graph's Laplacian matrix. For finite graphs where all of the relative measurement processing is handled by a single node, we propose a modified iterative Jacobi algorithm with a priority queue to solve for the node potentials. Using the eigendecomposition of the Laplacian matrix, we then derive an expression for the error variance of the estimated node potentials and show how it can be adapted for different boundary conditions.

articleTitle: Companding Curve Optimization to Maximize SNDR for High Dynamic Range Image Sensors
abstract: The demand for automotive image sensors with high dynamic range(HDR) and increased resolution has prompted significant advancements in their development. Due to the demands of High Dynamic Range (HDR), modern automotive image sensors require up to 28 bits per pixel, surpassing the capacity of existing image transmission protocols. Hence, automotive image sensors employ a PieceWise Linear (PWL) companding, which offers efficient computation, albeit with the trade-off of data loss. In order to mitigate data loss, we propose a method to optimize the companding curve by leveraging sensor characteristics, including Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) profile and SNR drop at transition. Our method achieves higher Signal-to-Noise-and-Distortion (SNDR) up to 5.2 dB and image quality compared to conventional companding curves.

articleTitle: Wearable Sensors and Electronic Skin in Digital Driven Diagnostics, Prognostics, and Therapeutics for Sustainable Health Care
abstract: Public health systems worldwide rely on limited resources and are under great pressure for the increased costs of diagnostic and therapeutic paths. The direction to mitigate these critical issues is the adoption of value-based healthcare (VBH) procedures. Moving forward to a VBH approach, in line with 5P guidelines (preventive, precision, participated, personalized & predictive medicine), requires the single patient-tailored assessment of a correct diagnosis, prediction of disease prognosis, response to standard of care treatment, including assessment of adverse side effects. The fulfillment of this need requires a high dimensional data integration approach, based on clinical data collection, storage and analysis, artificial intelligence (AI)-based solutions and wearable sensor technologies for a continuous collection of patients' relevant health and day-life information. In an ideal scenario, provided the possibility to retrieve multiparametric and multimodality data, the ability to use digital simulation, such as digital and biological twins, to predict prognostic and/or therapy response outcomes for each single patient would be desirable. Within this contest, the advent of manufacturing smart sensors has revolutionized the development of wearable devices, especially electronic skin (e-skin), opening the route to the creation of systems that mimic the sensory capabilities of human skin. These sensors, fabricated using advanced techniques on flexible and stretchable substrates, are crucial for enabling wearable sensors to detect a wide range of stimuli, including pressure, temperature, and humidity, enabling the creating of the patient's digital twin. The production of these sensors involves the integration of nanomaterials, such as graphene and other conductive polymers, which offer high sensitivity and durability while maintaining flexibility. Moreover, with advancements in flexible substrates and the miniaturization of electronic components, these systems have evolved from healthcare and robotic applications to next-generation wearable devices for humans. This talk will explore the latest advancements in the production and application of wearable graphene-based sensors, addressing the challenges of achieving high performance in flexibility, wearability and sensibility, and discussing the potentiality of this technology for the patient's digital twin, in the context of a “Digital Driven Diagnostics, prognostics, and therapeutics for sustainable Health care”.

articleTitle: Ex-Vivo Testing of Smart Ureteral Stent Toward Hydronephrosis Monitoring via Standard Stenting
abstract: This work presents a telemetric “smart” ureteral stent that offers, for the first time, compatibility with the standard stenting procedure to enable real-time sensing of ureteral obstruction and resultant kidney swelling at an early stage. This advanced ureteral stent integrates micro pressure sensors and a radiofrequency antenna to configure a resonant circuit for noninvasive kidney pressure monitoring via the indwelling stent. The stent prototype, electrically and biologically passivated by Parylene C, is tested in a harvested swine kidney-ureter model filled with artificial urine, demonstrating wireless pressure tracking with a response of 1.3 kHz/mmHg in cycled pressure variations up to 37 mmHg representing a reported average pressure rise due to chronic occlusion. The successful measurement enabled via prototype's placement into the model using today's stenting method and tools indicates potential clinical compatibility of the technology.

articleTitle: Enhancing Port Automation: A Novel Object Detection Pipeline for Container Ship Bays
abstract: In port automation, efficiency and safety can be significantly increased by autonomous container handling of ship-to-shore cranes. A crucial aspect of achieving this autonomy involves accurately detecting common objects as well as the state of the bay. Previous research has primarily focused on detecting specific types of containers or hatches, which falls short in meeting the demands of complex automated operations. We propose a novel object detection pipeline specifically tailored for this application. In this pipeline the 3D point cloud data is initially transformed into a 2D representation, then fed into the Deformable DETR (Detection Transformer) model to detect objects of interest. Our pipeline successfully detects the positions and sizes of containers, hatch covers, open hatches, and bay areas. Notably, container detection achieves both precision and recall of 0.97. The mean absolute error of the container positions is smaller than 5 cm in all directions. The bay width can be predicted correctly in 99.8 % of the cases. These results are highly promising and pave the way for the automation of ship-to-shore cranes, leading to improved efficiency and enhanced safety.

articleTitle: Wearable Temperature Sensing Bandages Based on Fano Resonance
abstract: LC wireless sensors are excelling in wearable devices with the advantages of wireless interrogations and compatibility with multiple processes. However, the high intrinsic loss of LC resonance hinders the improvement of sensitivity. To overcome the limitation, we propose a wearable temperature sensing bandages based on LC Fano resonance. A wirelessly powered negative impedance is integrated into the LC temperature sensor to generate a discrete spectrum, while the external readout coil, driven by signal analyzer, provides a continuum spectrum. The asymmetric Fano resonance is formed via mutual coupling between the readout circuit and the LC sensor, which results in high resolution. We fabricate the sensing system on PI embedded in bandages with polyethylene-glycol-based temperature sensitive capacitor. To imitate human applications, we conduct the experiments by ranging the temperature from 36°C to 42°C. The results show that Fano-resonant temperature sensor achieves a resolution of 0.04°C.

articleTitle: Fruity Twin – A Digital Platform for Processing Sensor Data in Food Cool Chains
abstract: The storage and transport of fresh fruits require dense sensor monitoring to preserve high food quality by adaptive control of cooling parameters. Digital Twins are the method of choice for the integration of services for sensor measurement forwarding, data conversion and predictive modelling. Further resampling services compensate for deviating and non-synchronized sensor intervals. The Digital Twin platform was demonstrated for monitoring and predicting condensation on the fruit surface in a cooling chamber with apples.

articleTitle: Enhancing Ozone Gas Sensor Performance with Polypyrrole-Coated Metal-Oxide Semiconductors
abstract: The development of practical gas sensors necessitates the fulfillment of several fundamental requirements, including ultra-high sensitivity, rapid response time, and exceptional gas selectivity. Metal oxide semiconductors, such as Indium Gallium Zinc Oxide (IGZO), exhibit commendable adsorption capacity for ozone (O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) gas; however, their application is often limited by prolonged response times and the necessity for external heating to enhance performance. This study addresses these limitations by integrating the conductive polymer polypyrrole (PPy) with IGZO to fabricate advanced O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> gas sensors. Experimental results demonstrate a significant enhancement in response time upon the incorporation of PPy, as compared to the pristine IGZO material. The polypyrrole coverage facilitates faster electron transport and improved gas interaction dynamics, thereby markedly reducing the response time and energy requirements for effective O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> detection.

articleTitle: Fully Automated Rapid Immunofludic Device by Use of Microfibrous Reactor for Human Saliva Sample
abstract: Given the growing need for rapid measurement for health monitoring, small sized automated analysis devices from human sample directly are required. We developed fully automated immunofluidic device for rapid biomarker detection from human saliva sample directly. The total system detects human cortisol in 15 minutes with high sensitivity <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(0.5\sim 30 \text{ng}/\text{mL}$</tex>) and a limit detection of 0.36 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{ng}/\text{mL}$</tex>, integrating pretreatment, immunoreaction, and analysis efficiently.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Description and Detection of Sparse Features for Deformable Intraoperative Bladder Environments*
abstract: Robust feature extraction is fundamental for locating abnormalities in the urinary bladder, ensuring precise orientation within the hollow organ, despite the limited field of vision in endoscopic surgeries. This paper addresses intraoperative challenges such as a lack of prominent features and continuous underlying deformations. Robust approaches that simultaneously perform feature detection and extraction, which are effective in rigid environments, are adapted for the intraoperative setting via transfer learning. As a first step, a dataset is created using endoscopic monocular images to accurately mimic the bladder's deformable environment and define ground truth assignments between images. Subsequently, an existing Convolutional Neural Network is fine-tuned with loss functions tailored to this new dataset. The simultaneous detection and description approach outperforms pixel-based methods in feature detection for intraoperative environments, showing a reduction in the distance between predicted and actual positions to less than 20 %. This approach lays the foundation for creating a digital representation of the bladder based on monocular endoscopic camera videos, enabling precise localization and storage of collected data during surgery.

articleTitle: Sensitivity-enhanced Planar Microwave Sensor for Rapid Human Fibrinogen Concentration Monitoring
abstract: Fibrinogen is essential for the formation of clots in the body and is crucial to maintaining hemostasis and recovering from trauma. Here, we present a highly sensitive portable planar microwave sensor for rapid detection of dissolved human fibrinogen. The proposed sensor will facilitate monitoring in pre-surgical evaluations and management of clotting disorders in clinical settings without physical contact with the sample under test using coupled reader-tag-based structure. The chipless tag, which is a planar split-ring resonator (SRR), is the main sensing element energized through electromagnetic (EM) coupling via a microstrip gap-coupled transmission line reader. As the sample solution changes in fibrinogen concentration, the dielectric properties of it will be impacted and the variation can be monitored using the tag. The sensor, with the designed resonance frequency of 876 MHz, demonstrates the capability to detect human fibrinogen concentrations with 0.1 mg/mL resolution, well below the thresholds considered clinically relevant. The sensitivity of the sensor is enhanced using interdigitated capacitive structures in the gap area of the SRRs allowing for the differentiation of concentrations at and around clinically relevant values.

articleTitle: The Development of Rumen Bacteria Microbial Fuel Cell in Anaerobic Environments
abstract: Long term diagnostics and health monitoring of inaccessible sensors require strenuous power management or alternate power generation methods. Intraruminal devices can be powered with green energy using a microbial fuel cell (MFC). However, issues concerning poor steady-state power generation in anaerobic environments must be addressed. In this study, we propose a new type of structure of MFC for power generation in the rumen of cattle. Steady-state performance is evaluated with electrodes of 3 different materials. Using our proposed structure, the MFC's voltage drop in anaerobic environments is minimized, and each material electrode displayed a maximum power generation characteristic as follows: 0.4 µW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for gold, 0.15 µW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for platinum, and 0.002 µW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for carbon.

articleTitle: VelObPoints: a Neural Network for Vehicle Object Detection and Velocity Estimation for Scanning LiDAR Sensors
abstract: LiDAR sensors are crucial sensors for highly automated vehicles. Relevant information about the vehicle's sur-roundings can be obtained from 3D point clouds, which serves as a basis for decision-making for further control of the vehicle. For this purpose, information about the type and position of objects in the vehicle's environment and their velocity and movement direction is essential. In this paper, we present VelObPoints, a neural network architecture that estimates the longitudinal and lateral velocity and performs object detection on a single LiDAR point cloud. Compared to existing tracking methods, the neural network allows this information to be extracted from a single LiDAR frame. We propose a simulated dataset for training and testing, containing motion distortion effects. The neural network achieves a mean Intersection over Union of 0.863 and a mean average velocity error of 0.332 m s<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−l</sup>. Based on a single point cloud, this information, consisting of the object's scaling, position, and rotation, as well as its velocities in the longitudinal and lateral directions, is immediately available for the driving function. For subsequent motion prediction, and object tracking, leading to more quickly available velocity and motion direction information and higher redundancy in sensor data fusion.

articleTitle: Design Aspects for Eddy Current Displacement Sensors in High Temperature Environments
abstract: The application of eddy current displacement sensors (ECDSs) for monitoring industrial processes has been studied. Industrial processes often present challenges due to harsh operating conditions. For example, sensors can be affected by high temperatures, dirt, dust, and humidity. These effects cause significant deviations in the measurement signal, necessitating the development of robust sensors. In this study, we present an approach for designing an ECDS suitable for high temperature environments with high temperature variations and varying humidity levels. Our approach addresses various aspects, including the selection of former materials, suitable winding techniques, and measurement frequencies, to develop a sensor system capable of accurately measuring large distances in such environments. We present lab measurements showing the feasibility of the proposed approach. The results provide a basis for reliable position measurement with ECDS in harsh environments.

articleTitle: Enhancing Bioimpedance Tissue Classification with Elastography Sensor Data via Multimodal Learning
abstract: Multimodal data from intraoperative sensors has the potential to support surgeons in deciding subsequent action steps by characterizing tissue in real time. There are several challenges when it comes to multimodal systems, such as limited measurement time and tissue deformation, making some modalities unreliable. To address this, a Stronger Enhancing Weaker framework is applied to bioimpedance and Water-Flow Elastography sensor data. This framework uses cross-modal translation and feature alignment, aiming for knowledge transfer from a strong to a weak modality during training to enhance unimodal performance of the weak modality at inference. Using a specialized experimental setup with porcine samples, the mechanical and electrical properties of tumorous and healthy urinary bladder are replicated. This approach achieves significant improvements in classification performance, improving the bioimpedance sensor's unimodal classification accuracy by 7.2 %. Further improvements of 6.8 % are observed when combining both modalities. This multimodal fusion method shows promise in improving tissue classification accuracy during surgery, potentially reducing recurrence rates.

articleTitle: An Ultra-high Bandwidth Piezoelectric MEMS Accelerometer Towards Condition-based Monitoring
abstract: MEMS accelerometers often encounters a trade-off between sensitivity and bandwidth. To overcome this limitation and achieve a high bandwidth without compromising sensitivity, we have transitioned the spring-mass design from conventional bending paradigm to tensile-compressive paradigm, resulting in a significant increase in the spring stiffness. This paper introduces a piezoelectric MEMS accelerometer with an unprecedented bandwidth exceeding 100 kHz. The device exhibits a resonant frequency of 165 kHz and a sensitivity of 0.2 mV/g. To the best of our knowledge, this is the highest bandwidth reported for a piezoelectric MEMS accelerometer, demonstrating its exceptional potential for condition-based monitoring (CbM) applications.

articleTitle: In Situ Raman Multi-Gas Sensing During Formation and Residual Gas Impact on Cycling Performance of Pouch Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Understanding the impact of residual gases on battery performance after the formation process is crucial for pouch cells. In this study, we investigate the evolution of gases during the formation of pouch batteries and their effects on the cycling performance of the cells after formation. It is found that C2H4, CH4, and CO are generated during the formation process. During battery cycling studies, rapid capacity decay is observed, accompanied by significant gas generation. The findings suggest that residual gases exacerbate internal reactions in the battery, leading to increased gas production and accelerated deterioration of battery performance.

articleTitle: High Speed SPAD Active Quenching and Reset Chipset in 55nm BCDLite Process for Quantum Applications
abstract: This paper presents a high-speed single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) active quenching and reset chipset for quantum applications. This chipset includes a low voltage current sensing chip and a high-voltage (HV) driver chip which can be scaled up to a multi-channel SPAD system. Both chips are implemented in a 55nm BCDLite process. The measurement results show that the current sensing chip can detect picoampere avalanche current with less than 1ns response time and generate tunable pulse width quench and reset signals using an on-chip digital process unit (DPU). On-chip programmable clock generator provides tuning range between 2ns - 1000ns with step size of 1ns. For HV driver chip, with a high-speed HV half bridge driver and associated level shifter, this circuit can drive 20pF load using 15V quenching signal with nanosecond delay.

articleTitle: Monolithic Vacuum Packaging for a CMOS MEMS Resonator Oscillator
abstract: The paper presents a monolithic vacuum packaging methodology specifically tailored for a CMOS MEMS resonator oscillator. The chip fabrication follows standardized CMOS MEMS process, ensuring measurement consistency and yielding dies with stable frequencies. We designed a 0.18µm CMOS MEMS resonator oscillator integrated with a tunable transimpedance amplifier (TIA). The oscillator operates at 36 kHz and is sealed within a ceramic dual in-line package using adhesive encapsulation under a vacuum pressure of 20 mTorr. After five months of vacuum maintenance testing, deviations in the resonator oscillator's quality factor, amplitude, and resonant frequency remain consistently below 0.1%. The oscillator achieves a signal-to-noise ratio of 100 dbc/sqrt(Hz) and a phase jitter of 8.2 ns with an integration bandwidth from 100 Hz to 16 kHz. Experimental results demonstrate that this vacuum packaging for the resonant oscillator can successfully achieve medium vacuum sealing (20 mTorr) over a long period and maintain stable component characteristics.

articleTitle: Pipelines Leak Localization Through Acoustic Emission and Deep Learning
abstract: This work develops a Deep Learning (DL) model to detect pipeline leaks, pointing out their localization. Early detection of leaks allows us to anticipate maintenance actions to mitigate environmental damage and material and financial losses. The developed model has as input the acoustic signal's Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) from piezoelectric sensors distributed along the pipe. A MultiHeadAttention layer is used for feature extraction-the other model's layers process such features, out-putting the presence (or not) of leaks for all pipe segments. A real testbed is built with a pressurized pipeline and acoustic emission sensors, allowing data acquisition. Several DL models are trained and compared. The best-detecting DL model showed accuracy and Fl-Score of over 97%, validating the technique.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Assembly of All-quartz Integrated Resonant Accelerometer with High Stability
abstract: Drift degrades stability of MEMS accelerometer a lot, in terms of temperature and long-term impacts. This study proposed an integrated resonant accelerometer with an all-quartz sensitive structure, which was designed to achieve resistance to temperature and long-term drift. Processes such as wet etching, quartz-on-quartz direct bonding, and femtosecond laser micro welding were utilized to fabricate and assemble the prototype. Experimental platforms were built up to characterize its stability, and results demonstrated that the stability at full-temperature range was 34.64 µg/oC, and the long-term stability was less than 100 µg. Combined with stability performances already measured, the accelerometer is comparable to, or even better than, state-of-the-art counterparts without compensation.

articleTitle: Fostering Sparsity in Sparse Convolution Networks for Efficient 3D Perception via Feature-Guidance
abstract: 3D Point clouds have unique computational challenges due to their unstructured sparse nature and non-uniform density. Recent 3D object detectors usually apply sparse convolutional networks for feature extraction owing to its efficiency. However, sparse CNNs suffer from the submanifold dilation problem of regular sparse convolutions yielding more and more active sites in feature maps. Thus, leading reduced feature sparsity and higher computational burden. We find that 3D object detector's learned underlying geometric and spatial distributions in deeper feature maps can serve as an important cue to determine crucial areas at runtime to eliminate the extra computations in sparse convolution networks. A Bayesian feature selection approach is proposed which adds zero training overhead while streamlining active sites at the inference stage. We reveal inherent divergences between object and background distributions in high-dimensional feature space and exploit this to classify features and prune non-essential regions. It is demonstrated that solely leveraging these learned distributions, our approach achieves significant memory savings with only minor performance drawbacks.

articleTitle: Fast Crosstalk Compensation in Resistive Sensor Arrays Using Feed-Forward Neural Networks
abstract: Resistive sensor arrays (RSAs) are a type of sensor arrangement in which all resistances are connected sharing conductive rows and columns. It means, the same electrical path is shared between all resistances that belong to the same row/column. This manufacturing method is optimal due to its simplicity and low cost, but the crosstalk effect arises. Due to this effect, when a sensor is measured, its resistance is not correctly obtained. To solve this problem, several solutions have been proposed, from complex readout circuits to post-processing algorithms. In this work, crosstalk is compensated for the first time on the entire RSA at once using Feed-Forward Neural Networks (FFNNs), which leads to high computational speed. This paper concludes that FFNN offer a good trade-off between speed and accuracy, being able to increase accuracy with more training.

articleTitle: Digital Magnetic Proximity Extension RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a-Assisted Immunoassay with Attomolar Sensitivity
abstract: Accurate detection of protein biomarkers is essential in biomedical applications due to their association with various diseases. The detection and quantification of these biomarkers facilitate early diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment interventions. Among the available methods, proximity extension assays (PEA) are notable for using pairs of antibodies linked with oligonucleotides, where the extension of these oligonucleotides creates unique sequences for each protein target. Traditionally, quantification in PEA has relied on polymerase chain reaction (PCR). However, the emergence of isothermal nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) offers a promising alternative, particularly suited for clinical and point-of-care applications. In response to these advancements, we propose a novel digital magnetic proximity extension RP A-CRISPRlCas12a-assisted immunoassay system. Our assay demonstrates a limit of detection (LOD) of 314 attomolar (aM) for the IL-8 protein target, which is 6,400 times more sensitive than ELISA, 76 times more sensitive than traditional PEA, and 5 times more sensitive than MagPEA. Additionally, the construction of a smartphone-based detection device highlights the potential for our assay's application in point-of-care settings.

articleTitle: Unobtrusive Spatial Localization of Impact Induced Soundwaves using 2D Beamforming Algorithm
abstract: Runtime localization of surface wear zones in industrial machines has been a daunting problem in the domain of predictive maintenance. Wear occurs due to the percussive impact and dynamic contact of a surface by another solid body. Spatial localization of impact sounds generated due to this phenomenon can help to locate the wear zones. Furthermore, most of these machines are rotating (e.g. grinding mills) / moving (e.g. crushers) in nature. This necessitates non-contact sensing outside the machine. In this work, a novel approach using a modified 2D beamforming algorithm has been presented that can localize non-coherent impact sound sources with RMSE localization error less than 10%.

articleTitle: A Novel System Design of Eddy Current Testing Robot for Metal Defect Detection
abstract: We present an novel robotic system that seamlessly integrates with multichannel Eddy Current Testing (ECT). The ECT system is developed on a Zynq-7020 Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), which facilitates rapid data acquisition. The system aims to achieve highly accurate defect localization by leveraging real-time robotics control and efficient data syn-chronization. To enhance the precise positioning of the detected defects, our system employs the Robot Operating System (ROS) for exact and real-time control, alongside Kalman filtering (KF) sensor fusion for robust pose estimation. Additionally, the robot pose is tightly coupled with the ECT data through an innovative synchronization strategy which achieves a mean delay of 11.77 ms. The system's efficacy is assessed on both aluminum and ferromagnetic specimens, demonstrating the ability to localize defects with precision up to 0.18 cm.

articleTitle: Experimental Analysis of Wind Effect in Acoustic Hail Sensors
abstract: Hail is a particularly threatening climatic phenomenon that causes significant economic losses. Currently, acousto-electric sensors for local measurement of hail impacts can be found on the market. These sensors acquire electrical signals from impacts using piezoelectric transducers and estimate the energy of the impacts by relating it to the energy of the signals. Given that wind is always present during storms, it is crucial to assess how it affects the obtained signals due to the deviation in the trajectory of hailstones, which causes them to impact obliquely. In this study, we conduct an experiment to evaluate the significance of oblique incidences on the sensor's collecting surface. We designed a custom experimental platform, which we present along with the results. The findings indicate that the energy of the signals is linearly related to the angle of incidence.

articleTitle: IoT Based Smart Spectacles Integrated with Mobile App for Tech-Neck Posture Correction
abstract: ‘Techneckal’ is a smart spectacles along with a mobile application built for analyzing the user's posture to help with tech-neck in a cost-effective solution, a common medical condition which causes soreness in the neck muscles. While the mobile application as a stand-alone entity is capable of indicating improper posture while using mobile phones, its integration with the smart spectacles shall help users correct their posture while using non-electronic gadgets as well. The mobile application notifies the user instantly to correct their posture when the user's device surpasses the specified angle to avoid straining in their neck. While using their mobile phone, it uses the orientation sensor of the user's mobile to check the device's orientation and thereby predicting the posture. The smart spectacles measures the angle of the user's neck with the help of an accelerometer sensor and communicates the data to the mobile application through a WiFi module micro controller embedded within its frame.

articleTitle: A Conductivity-Compensated Liquid Film Thickness Measurement Scheme Using Segmented Electrode Arrays
abstract: The measurement of circumferential film thickness, mainly during core annular flow is important in many industrial applications. The thickness of the film is often non-uniform and changes randomly over time. Moreover, the continuous fluctuation of conductivity during the flow due to changes in temperature and other parameters makes the measurement challenging. This article introduces an array of innovative coplanar five-electrode conductivity probes that can measure liquid film thickness (LFT) by compensating for the random fluctuation of the conductivity. The array provides simultaneous measurement at twelve different angular locations. The results from a static test reveal that the voltage ratio obtained from each set of measuring electrodes remains consistently stable, even when evaluating water samples with varying conductivities. The useful measuring range of the proposed sensor is found to be up to 3 mm. The conductivity probe would be useful for assessing the non-uniform distribution of circumferential LFT by employing an array of such sensors.

articleTitle: Enhancing Non-Invasive Electroanatomical Mapping with Dynamic Sensor Arrays
abstract: Electroanatomical mapping (EAM) is an essential tool for diagnosing and treating cardiac arrhythmias. Traditional non-invasive EAM methods, especially those based on magnetocardiography (MCG), face challenges due to the limited amount of sensors. This paper introduces a dynamic sensor array approach designed to overcome these limitations. Unlike traditional static sensor arrays, our approach leverages sensor repositioning between heartbeats, enabling enhanced spatial res-olution and more accurate current density estimation without increasing the sensor count. Our simulations demonstrate that the dynamic sensor array significantly enhances the performance of the EAM algorithm, achieving better estimations of current densities and improved separation of healthy and pathological regions. Specifically, the dynamic array with six motion steps per axis improved the Dice score from 0.82 to 0.95, precision from 0.95 to 0.98, and recall from 0.73 to 0.92 compared to a static array. These findings suggest that dynamic sensor arrays could substantially reduce the cost and improve the performance of non-invasive EAM, potentially transforming cardiac diagnostics.

articleTitle: Screen-Printed Graphene-Ink on a Fitted Sheet for Pressure Sensing and Sleeping Posture Recognition by Machine Learning Techniques
abstract: This paper presents the development and characterization of an innovative piezoresistive fabric-based sensor system, enhanced with graphene nanoplatelets (GNPs) for pressure sensing applications. Utilizing a screen-printing technique, an ink modified with GNPs is applied directly onto a crib-size fitted sheet (FS). The coated fabric underwent extensive characterization to evaluate its morphological, electrical, mechanical, and electromechanical properties. Results revealed a piezoresistive sensitivity (gauge factor) of approximately 9.9 in the wale direction and 1.2 in the course direction at an applied strain (ε) of 2.7%. Subsequently, data collected via an electrical resistance tomography (ERT)-inspired strategy were processed using machine learning (ML) classification techniques to detect pressure on the mattress covered with the piezoresistive coated fitted sheet (CFS). Experimental results demonstrate the proposed sensor system's capability for high-precision pressure sensing over large areas, achieving 96.3 % accuracy in recognizing compressed regions and 94.4% accuracy in identifying different sleeping positions on various zones of the sensorized mattress surface.

articleTitle: SiC Micro-Hot Wires for Flow Measurement in Harsh Environments
abstract: The present study reports developments in the process of fabricating and characterizing silicon carbide suspended hot wires for the measure of turbulent air flow in harsh environments, with substrate current leakage suppression. The fabrication process involves silicon thinning, polishing and bonding to a glass substrate, SiC etching and Si under-etching to create the suspended wire structure. The resistivity dependance relative to temperature was measured and Joule heating was applied to the wire. Flush mounting on a NACA 0018 airfoil was achieved and first characterizations under air flow on a tabletop wind tunnel were conducted on both constant current and constant temperature operating modes, showing the device sensitivity under air flow.

articleTitle: Harvesting Kinetic Energy from Rain Gauge Tipping Motion Using Electromagnetic Induction
abstract: Measuring rainfall is crucial for making well-informed decisions across various sectors, including agriculture, infrastructure, flood monitoring and warnings, and climate research. This paper presents a self-powered tipping bucket rain gauge (TBRG) designed to transmit data when most needed-during stormy, dark conditions when solar energy is unavailable. It leverages the mechanical motion of the internal tipping bucket to harvest and convert kinetic energy into electrical energy. The theoretical analysis and design choices confirmed the feasibility of harnessing the TBRG's kinetic energy from its tipping bucket motion. Experimental results highlight the harvester's potential to accumulate charge over time and support real-time data transmission.

articleTitle: Hot Microtube Flowmetry with Heater-Integrated Microchannel Resonators
abstract: Accurate flow measurement on a microscale is essential for process monitoring in MEMS fabrication and semiconductor industries. However, traditional flow sensors such as ultrasonic, Coriolis, and hot-wire anemometers are challenging to implement with microchannels due to their physical size, difficulty to measure low flow rate, and fragility, respectively. This study introduces a novel hot-microtube anemometer for liquid flow speed measurement by using a heater-integrated microchannel resonator, HMR. The HMR operates by forced convection cooling within a heated channel, measuring flow velocity using a resistive thermometer. This technique not only measures fluid flow but also determines density via resonance frequency. Additionally, it measures dynamic viscosity through the vibration amplitude of the liquid sample. We experimentally demonstrate the feasibility of accurate microscale flow measurements, showing that HMR well follows to King's Law, a fundamental equation in anemometry studies.

articleTitle: A High-Performance Mode-Localized Vacuum Gauge Based on FPGA Closed-Loop Control
abstract: Vacuum gauges are widely used in semiconductor and industrial equipment. Sensitivity, resolution, and accuracy are the key characteristics of these gauges. The performance of traditional gauge is limited by the size and thickness of the diaphragm, but the thin and large silicon diaphragm is difficult to fabricate. In this paper, mode-localized gauges are developed and operated in a closed-loop configuration. The gauge senses vacuum pressure by a silicon diaphragm, and a weak-coupling resonator is used to measure the deformation of the diaphragm, which can increase the sensitivity compared with traditional resonators. In addition, FPGA-based closed-loop control of the proposed gauge is developed, which is reported for the first time. Three devices are tested from 0.5 to 100 Pa, which can prove the reliability of the design and control strategy. The results show that the performance of the above three devices is improved compared to those of other studies.

articleTitle: Grating-coupled silver nanoparticle arrays for point-of-care PCR platform
abstract: Point-of-care (POC) polymerase chain reaction (PCR) devices are essential for rapid and cost-effective infectious disease diagnostics, overcoming the limitations of traditional laboratory PCR, which requires trained personnel.
